summary: Perfectoid rings and spaces in the generality of perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1: characteristic 0 and p, no perfectoid base field), layers P0–P7, planned at declaration granularity on the carriers of the Tau Ceti anchor and AdicSpacesPartII and within the RS-05 narrowing. P0 builds almost mathematics over an abstract basic setup (V, m): the almost category as Mathlib's Serre-class localization, Hom, tensor and the adjoints, almost algebras, almost flat, projective, finite projective and finite étale objects, the almost cotangent complex over DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 with deformation theory, faithfully flat descent, and completion and inversion of a pseudouniformiser. P1 builds perfectoid Tate rings and fields, the tilt with its sharp map, Fontaine's θ with its primitive kernel, the classification of untilts by primitive ideals of degree one and the tilting equivalence over any perfectoid base, compared with Mathlib's PreTilt, untilt and fontaineTheta, with BMS integral perfectoid rings and with the anchor's Layer 6. P2 proves the tilting homeomorphism with its rational subsets, perfectoid rational localisation, stable uniformity, the sheaf theorem with almost acyclicity of O⁺, and builds perfectoid spaces as a full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces with glued tilting, the slice equivalence and fibre products. P3 proves the three conclusions of almost purity, Fontaine–Wintenberger, and the étale site of a perfectoid space with its tilting equivalence, with the henselian finite étale approximation as an early algebraic prefix. P4 decomposes ECD §5 (injections, immersions, Zariski closed immersions, separatedness); P5 cofiltered limits and ECD 6.4 (o)–(iii); P6 κ-small spaces, the assembly of ECD 6.4(iv) and ECD 7.8–7.11; P7 perfectoid tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers. Sources are public (Scholze's Perfectoid spaces, Étale cohomology of diamonds v4 and torsion paper, the Berkeley lectures, Kedlaya–Liu I and II, Kedlaya's AWS notes, Bhatt's notes, Gabber–Ramero, BMS, Scholze–Weinstein) with source locators recorded for independent checking. P1 remains partial at the general-base mod-pseudouniformizer comparison; inputs owned by other roadmaps are requests and unread proof inputs are gaps. The independent review does not certify the remaining stages or all source excerpts.

nodes.title: Basic setup (V, m): an idempotent ideal with flat m ⊗ m
nodes.statement: A basic setup is a pair S = (V, m) of a commutative ring V and an ideal m ⊆ V such that (i) m is idempotent, m·m = m (Mathlib `IsIdempotentElem m` in the semiring `Ideal V`), and (ii) the V-module m̃ := m ⊗_V m is flat. Condition (i) is Gabber–Ramero's basic setup (GR (2.1.1)); condition (ii) is the flatness GR assume from (2.5.14) on, imposed here once for all almost mathematics of this roadmap. Pinned conventions: a V-module M is almost zero if m·M = 0; a V-linear map is an almost isomorphism if its kernel and cokernel are almost zero; m̃ always denotes the tensor product m ⊗_V m (it maps onto m·m = m, isomorphically when m is flat); the classical limit is m = V. A basic setup is data, not a type class, because one ring carries several setups (for a perfectoid Tate ring R, (R°, R°°) and (R⁺, the root ideal of a pseudouniformiser), compared in PerfectoidSpaces:P1). Condition (A): m is a filtered union of principal ideals; condition (B): for every k ≥ 1 the k-th powers of elements of m generate m. (A) implies (B), and (A) together with m·m = m implies (ii) (P0/filtered-principal-union-tilde-flat).
hypotheses: V is a commutative ring (Lean: `[CommRing V]` in universe u); m is an ideal of V.
m·m = m. This is the only hypothesis GR use before (2.5.14); it makes almost zero modules closed under extensions.

m ⊗_V m is V-flat. GR impose it from (2.5.14) on (cotangent complex and deformation theory) and use it earlier in Corollary 2.2.22 (exactness of M ↦ M_!); every instance used in this atlas satisfies it: root ideals and maximal ideals of valuation rings with non-finitely-generated maximal ideal satisfy condition (A), and m = V is flat.
proofSteps: Structure `Almost.BasicSetup V` with fields `ideal : Ideal V`, `isIdempotentElem : IsIdempotentElem ideal` and `flat_tilde : Module.Flat V (ideal ⊗[V] ideal)`.

The predicate `S.IsAlmostZero M := ∀ ε ∈ S.ideal, ∀ x : M, ε • x = 0` on V-modules and `S.IsAlmostIso f` := kernel and cokernel almost zero; `S.almostZero : ObjectProperty (ModuleCat V)` is the first predicate on objects.

Conditions (A) and (B) as `Prop`-valued definitions on S (not fields), with (A) → (B) routine: if m = ⋃ V·x_α is directed then every finite set of k-fold products of elements of m lies in some (V·x_β)^k = V·x_β^k, so m = m^k is the union of the principal ideals V·x_β^k and is generated by k-th powers.
Base change along a ring map V → W is the setup (W, mW) (P0/basic-setup-base-change).
Examples: the classical setup (V, V); the zero setup (V, 0); root setups (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup); valuation rings (P0/valuation-ring-basic-setup).

nodes.title: Almost zero modules and almost isomorphisms are detected by m̃ ⊗ −
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. For a V-module M the following are equivalent: (a) m·M = 0; (b) m ⊗_V M = 0; (c) m̃ ⊗_V M = 0. A V-linear map f : M → N is an almost isomorphism if and only if 1 ⊗ f : m̃ ⊗_V M → m̃ ⊗_V N is an isomorphism. If m is flat, the multiplication map m̃ → m is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: S a basic setup (m·m = m, m̃ flat).
proofSteps: (a)⇒(b): if mM = 0 then m ⊗_V M ≅ (m ⊗_V V/m) ⊗_{V/m} M ≅ (m/m²) ⊗_{V/m} M = 0 because m² = m.
(b)⇒(c): m̃ ⊗_V M ≅ m ⊗_V (m ⊗_V M) by associativity.
(c)⇒(a): the map m ⊗ m ⊗ M → M, x ⊗ y ⊗ z ↦ xyz, has image m²M = mM, so m̃ ⊗ M = 0 forces mM = 0.
Almost isomorphisms: m̃ ⊗_V − is exact (m̃ flat), so ker(1 ⊗ f) = m̃ ⊗ ker f and coker(1 ⊗ f) = m̃ ⊗ coker f; apply (a)⇔(c) to both.
If m is flat, m ⊗_V m → m ⊗_V V = m is injective, and its image is m·m = m.
acceptance: For V = valuation ring of ℂ_p, m maximal, M = V/m: m ⊗_V M = m/m² = 0, while for m = (p) in ℤ_p (not a basic setup) m ⊗ ℤ_p/p = (p)/(p²) ≠ 0.
The inclusion m ↪ V is an almost isomorphism (cokernel V/m), and 1 ⊗ (m ↪ V) : m̃ ⊗ m → m̃ is an isomorphism (P0/tilde-ideal-idempotent).

nodes.title: m̃ ⊗ m ≅ m̃ and m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃; symmetric tensors of m
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. The map m̃ ⊗_V m → m̃, x ⊗ y ⊗ z ↦ x ⊗ yz, is an isomorphism; consequently the multiplication m̃ ⊗_V m̃ → m̃ is an isomorphism (m̃ is an idempotent V-module). For every k ≥ 2 the symmetric group S_k acts trivially on ⊗^k_V m; in particular x ⊗ y = y ⊗ x in m̃.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Trivial S_k-action: reduce to a transposition and k = 2; for x, y, z ∈ m one computes x ⊗ yz = xy ⊗ z = y ⊗ xz = yz ⊗ x, and elements yz span m because m = m².

The inclusion m ↪ V is an almost isomorphism (kernel 0, cokernel V/m almost zero), so 1 ⊗ (m ↪ V) : m̃ ⊗ m → m̃ ⊗ V = m̃ is an isomorphism by P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero; this composite is x ⊗ y ⊗ z ↦ x ⊗ yz.
m̃ ⊗ m̃ = (m̃ ⊗ m) ⊗ m ≅ m̃ ⊗ m ≅ m̃ by applying the previous step twice.
acceptance: For the classical setup m = V the isomorphism is V ⊗ V ⊗ V ≅ V ⊗ V, the multiplication.
For a root setup with ϖ a nonzerodivisor, m is flat, m̃ ≅ m and the isomorphism is the multiplication m ⊗ m ≅ m.

nodes.title: Base change of a basic setup along a ring map V → W
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and V → W a ring homomorphism. Then S_W := (W, mW) is a basic setup: (mW)·(mW) = mW, and the natural map W ⊗_V m̃ → (mW) ⊗_W (mW) is an isomorphism, so (mW)~ is W-flat. Flatness of m alone does not pass to mW; this is why the setup requires m̃, not m, to be flat.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; V → W any ring homomorphism.
proofSteps: Idempotence: (mW)² = m²W = mW.
Let m_W := W ⊗_V m; the sequence 0 → K → m_W → mW → 0 has K = Tor_1^V(V/m, W), killed by m, so m ⊗_V K = 0 (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero).
Applying m_W ⊗_W − and − ⊗_W mW to this sequence gives m_W ⊗_W m_W ≅ m_W ⊗_W (mW) ≅ (mW) ⊗_W (mW), i.e. W ⊗_V m̃ ≅ (mW)~.
W ⊗_V m̃ is W-flat because flatness is stable under base change (Mathlib `Module.Flat.baseChange`).
acceptance: For V → V[1/ϖ] with ϖ ∈ m, mV[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] and S_W is the classical setup of V[1/ϖ].
For V → V/I, S_{V/I} = (V/I, (m + I)/I); for the root setup of V the base change is the root setup of the images of the roots.

nodes.title: Condition (A) implies that m ⊗ m is flat
nodes.statement: Let V be a commutative ring and m ⊆ V an ideal with m·m = m which is a filtered union of principal ideals (condition (A)). Then m̃ = m ⊗_V m is a flat V-module; hence (V, m) is a basic setup.
hypotheses: m = m², and m = ⋃_α V·x_α for a directed family of elements x_α ∈ m (α ≤ β iff V·x_α ⊆ V·x_β).
proofSteps: Write m = colim_α V·x_α; since tensor products commute with filtered colimits, m̃ = colim_α (V·x_α) ⊗_V (V·x_α), and V·x_α ≅ V/Ann(x_α) ≅ (V·x_α) ⊗_V (V·x_α) via π_α : V → (Vx_α) ⊗ (Vx_α), v ↦ v·x_α ⊗ x_α.

Given α, choose β with x_α ∈ V·x_β² (possible because m = m²), say x_α = y·x_β², and set z = y·x_β, so that x_α = z·x_β. Then Ker π_α ⊆ Ker(μ_{z²}) and there is λ_{αβ} : (Vx_α) ⊗ (Vx_α) → V with π_β ∘ λ_{αβ} = j_{αβ} ⊗ j_{αβ} and λ_{αβ} ∘ π_α = μ_{z²}.

Hence every transition map (Vx_α)⊗(Vx_α) → (Vx_β)⊗(Vx_β) factors through the free module V, so m̃ is a filtered colimit of free modules of rank one, hence flat (equational criterion: a relation in m̃ comes from some stage and dies after factoring through V; Mathlib `Module.Flat.iff_forall_exists_factorization`).
acceptance: For a valuation ring V with non-principal maximal ideal m, m is the directed union of its principal ideals, so m̃ is flat (here m itself is torsion-free, hence flat, and m̃ = m).
For a root setup m = ⋃_n ϖ_n V (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup) the lemma applies without assuming ϖ to be a nonzerodivisor.

nodes.title: The basic setup of an element with compatible p-power roots
nodes.statement: Let V be a commutative ring, p ≥ 2 an integer and (ϖ_n)_{n≥0} a sequence in V with ϖ_{n+1}^p = ϖ_n for all n; put ϖ := ϖ_0 and m := ⋃_n ϖ_n V = Ideal.span {ϖ_n}. Then (V, m) is a basic setup, the root setup of (ϖ_n): m is the increasing union of the principal ideals ϖ_n V, m·m = m, and m̃ is flat by condition (A). A V-module M is almost zero for it iff ϖ_n M = 0 for all n. If ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of V then every ϖ_n is a nonzerodivisor, each ϖ_n V is free of rank one, m is flat and countably generated, and the multiplication m̃ → m is an isomorphism. Replacing (ϖ_n) by the shifted sequence (ϖ_{n+k})_n, or by any sequence (ϖ'_n) with ϖ'_n V = ϖ_{n+c} V for all large n, gives the same setup. This is the input PerfectoidSpaces:P1 instantiates with a pseudouniformiser admitting compatible p-power roots (ECD Definition 3.21).
hypotheses: V commutative; p ≥ 2; ϖ_{n+1}^p = ϖ_n for all n ≥ 0.
No topology and no perfectoid hypothesis: the construction is purely algebraic; the nonzerodivisor hypothesis is used only for the flatness of m itself and m̃ ≅ m.
proofSteps: Increasing chain: ϖ_n = ϖ_{n+1}^p ∈ ϖ_{n+1}V, so ϖ_n V ⊆ ϖ_{n+1} V and m is a directed union of principal ideals.
Idempotence: ϖ_n = ϖ_{n+1}·ϖ_{n+1}^{p−1} ∈ m·m because p ≥ 2.
m̃ is flat by P0/filtered-principal-union-tilde-flat.
Almost zero: mM = 0 iff ϖ_n M = 0 for all n, because the ϖ_n generate m.

If ϖ is a nonzerodivisor: ϖ_n^{p^n} = ϖ, so ϖ_n is a nonzerodivisor; ϖ_n V ≅ V; m is a filtered colimit of free modules, hence flat, and m ⊗ m → m is injective with image m² = m (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero, last clause).
acceptance: For V = 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}] and ϖ_n = t^{1/p^n}: m = (t^{1/p^∞}), V/m = 𝔽_p is almost zero, V/t is not.
For V = 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and ϖ_n = p^{1/p^n} (a compatible system of roots of p), m is the maximal ideal of V.

nodes.title: The basic setup (K°, K°°) of a valuation ring with non-principal maximal ideal
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring (a domain in which the ideals are totally ordered; Mathlib `ValuationRing V` with `IsDomain V`) whose maximal ideal m is not finitely generated (equivalently not principal; for a rank-one valuation: the valuation is nondiscrete, e.g. V = K° for a perfectoid field K). Then (V, m) is a basic setup: m·m = m, m is torsion-free hence flat, and m̃ ≅ m. A V-module is almost zero iff it is killed by m, iff it is a vector space over the residue field k = V/m; in particular k is almost zero. This is the setup of Sch12 §4 and of GR Example 2.1.2(i).
hypotheses: V a valuation domain; m = maximal ideal not finitely generated.
No completeness, no rank-one hypothesis: every valuation ring with non-principal maximal ideal qualifies; the rank-one nondiscrete case is GR Example 2.1.2(i).
proofSteps: Idempotence: let x ∈ m; since m ≠ xV there is y ∈ m ∖ xV; as ideals of V are totally ordered, x ∈ yV, x = yz; z ∈ m, otherwise z is a unit and y ∈ xV; so x ∈ m·m.

m is the directed union of its principal ideals (totally ordered), so condition (A) holds; moreover m is torsion-free, hence flat over the Bezout domain V (Mathlib `Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout`), and m̃ ≅ m (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero).
Almost zero modules are killed by m, i.e. are k-vector spaces.

For K perfectoid with pseudouniformiser ϖ having compatible p-power roots, the ideal equals that of the root setup (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup).

nodes.title: Almost zero modules form a Serre class
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. The property S.almostZero of V-modules (m·M = 0) is a Serre class in the abelian category ModuleCat V (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`): it contains 0 and is closed under submodules, quotients and extensions. It is moreover a tensor ideal: M almost zero implies M ⊗_V N, Hom_V(M, N) and Hom_V(N, M) almost zero for all N.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; only m·m = m is used.
proofSteps: Zero, submodules and quotients: immediate from the definition.
Extensions: for 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 with mM' = mM'' = 0 one has mM ⊆ M' and hence m·mM ⊆ mM' = 0, so m²M = 0, and m² = m.
Tensor ideal: ε ∈ m acts on M ⊗ N, Hom(M, N), Hom(N, M) through its action on M, which is zero.
acceptance: The extension 0 → k → V/m² ... for V = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}: V/m² = V/m = k, consistent with idempotence; for ℤ_p (not a setup) ℤ/p² is an extension of almost zero modules not killed by (p).
Mathlib's `SerreClassLocalization` API applies to S.almostZero (instance found by type class inference).

nodes.title: Products, limits, lim¹, colimits, Tor and Ext of almost zero modules are almost zero
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. If (M_i)_{i∈I} is any family of almost zero V-modules then ∏_i M_i and ⊕_i M_i are almost zero; the colimit of any diagram of almost zero modules is almost zero; for an inverse system (N_n)_{n∈ℕ} of almost zero modules, lim_n N_n and lim¹_n N_n = coker(∏ N_n → ∏ N_n, (x_n) ↦ (x_n − φ_n(x_{n+1}))) are almost zero; and for M almost zero, Tor_i^V(M, N) and Ext^i_V(M, N), Ext^i_V(N, M) are almost zero for all i and N. Consequently a map of inverse systems of V-modules whose kernels and cokernels are termwise almost zero induces almost isomorphisms on lim and on lim¹.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; no finiteness or Mittag-Leffler hypothesis: the product is killed elementwise.
proofSteps: Products: for ε ∈ m, ε·(x_i)_i = (ε x_i)_i = 0. Direct sums, lim (a submodule of the product), colimits (a quotient of a direct sum) and lim¹ (a quotient of a product) follow.
Tor and Ext: multiplication by ε on Tor_i(M, N) and Ext^i(M, N) is induced by multiplication by ε on M, which is zero; similarly in the second variable.

For a map of inverse systems with almost zero kernels K_n and cokernels Q_n: split into 0 → K → N → I → 0 and 0 → I → N' → Q → 0 and use the six-term lim–lim¹ sequences; the error terms lim K_n, lim¹ K_n, lim Q_n, lim¹ Q_n are almost zero and almost zero modules form a Serre class.
acceptance: For S = (𝒪_{ℂ_p}, 𝔪) and N_n = k for all n with zero transition maps: lim N_n = 0, lim¹ N_n = ∏ k / (image) is almost zero though nonzero.
This is the special case ε_n = m of GR Lemma 2.4.2(i),(ii) (a constant sequence of ideals converging to V^a).

sources.match: GR's lemma for colimits, limits and lim¹ of systems killed by ideals converging to V^a; the constant sequence m is the case needed here.

nodes.title: Firm modules: a small-hom model of the almost category
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup (m̃ = m ⊗_V m flat). A V-module M is firm if the multiplication map m̃ ⊗_V M → M is an isomorphism; firm modules form a full subcategory S.Firm of ModuleCat V, closed under kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts (hence abelian, with exact inclusion j_!). The functor j^* : ModuleCat V → S.Firm, M ↦ m̃ ⊗_V M, is well defined (m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃), exact, right adjoint to j_!, and has a fully faithful right adjoint j_* : N ↦ Hom_V(m̃, N); its kernel {M : m̃ ⊗ M = 0} is exactly S.almostZero. By Mathlib's `Abelian.isLocalization_isoModSerre_kernel_of_leftAdjoint`, j^* is a localization functor for the almost isomorphisms S.almostZero.isoModSerre. This yields the instance `MorphismProperty.HasLocalization.{u} S.almostZero.isoModSerre` whose localized category has Hom-types in the universe u of the V-modules; the almost category P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base is defined through it. The categories S.Firm and Almost.Module S are equivalent; firm modules are the modules of the form M_! (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; flatness of m̃ is used for exactness of m̃ ⊗ − and for closure of firm modules under kernels.
Universe convention: V : Type u, ModuleCat.{u} V, so S.Firm : Type (u+1) with Category.{u}, matching `HasLocalization.{u}`.
proofSteps: Firm modules are closed under kernels and cokernels: m̃ ⊗ − is exact, so the multiplication maps of ker f, coker f are the restrictions/quotients of isomorphisms; biproducts are clear.
m̃ ⊗ M is firm because m̃ ⊗ m̃ → m̃ is an isomorphism (P0/tilde-ideal-idempotent).

Adjunctions: Hom_V(j_! F, M) ≅ Hom_Firm(F, m̃ ⊗ M) for F firm (Bhatt Construction 4.1.5, using I ⊗^L R/I ≃ 0, i.e. m̃ ⊗ V/m... = 0 and m̃ flat), and Hom_Firm(m̃ ⊗ M, N) = Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N) ≅ Hom_V(M, Hom_V(m̃, N)) (tensor–hom).
Counit j^* j_* N = m̃ ⊗ Hom_V(m̃, N) → N is an isomorphism for N firm (Bhatt: tensoring the triangle RHom(V/m, N) → N → RHom(m̃, N) with m̃ kills the first term), so j_* is fully faithful.
Kernel: m̃ ⊗ M = 0 iff mM = 0 (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero); hence (Mathlib) j^* is a localization functor for S.almostZero.isoModSerre, and the HasLocalization instance is ⟨j^*⟩.
acceptance: m̃ is firm, and for the classical setup every module is firm and j^* ≅ 𝟭.
For m ≠ V the module V is not firm, while j^*(V) = m̃ is.

uses.how: supplies the HasLocalization.{u} instance, so Hom-types of almost modules are V-modules in the same universe

nodes.title: Almost modules over a basic setup: the Serre quotient V^a-Mod
nodes.statement: For a basic setup S = (V, m), the category of almost V-modules V^a-Mod := Almost.Module S is the localization of ModuleCat V at the almost isomorphisms S.almostZero.isoModSerre (maps with almost zero kernel and cokernel), i.e. the Serre quotient of V-modules by the almost zero modules, realised with Mathlib's Serre-class localization: the carrier is `MorphismProperty.Localization'` for the `HasLocalization.{u}` instance of P0/firm-module-model, so Hom-types are V-modules in the universe of V-modules. The localization functor M ↦ M^a (`Almost.toAlmost S`) is exact and essentially surjective; M^a ≅ 0 iff M is almost zero; f^a is an isomorphism iff f is an almost isomorphism; V^a-Mod is abelian (Mathlib `SerreClassLocalization.abelian`); a functor G out of V^a-Mod to an abelian category is exact iff G ∘ (−)^a is, and an exact functor out of ModuleCat V factors (uniquely up to unique isomorphism) through (−)^a iff it kills almost zero modules. For a perfectoid field K and S = (K°, K°°) this is Sch12's K°a-mod; for a perfectoid Tate ring R, PerfectoidSpaces:P1 instantiates S with (R°, R°°) and (R⁺, root ideal) (ECD Definition 3.23). All almost-vanishing statements in consumers ("H^i(X, O⁺) is almost zero", "R⁺/ϖ is almost the equalizer") are statements in this category.
hypotheses: S a basic setup (P0/almost-basic-setup): m·m = m and m̃ flat.
The setup is general: no valuation, no perfectoid field. The perfectoid instances are tests here and theorems in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup.
proofSteps: S.almostZero is a Serre class (P0/almost-zero-serre-class).
The HasLocalization.{u} instance from the firm model (P0/firm-module-model) fixes the carrier `S.almostZero.isoModSerre.Localization'` and the functor `Q'`.

Abelian structure: the localized category is preadditive with additive localization functor (calculus of fractions, Mathlib `Localization.preadditive`) and abelian by `SerreClassLocalization.abelian`; exactness of (−)^a by `SerreClassLocalization.preservesFiniteLimits`/`preservesFiniteColimits`.
Zero objects and isomorphisms: `SerreClassLocalization.isZero_obj_iff`, `SerreClassLocalization.isIso_map_iff`.
Universal property for exact functors: `SerreClassLocalization.exactFunctor_comp_iff` and `SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft`.
acceptance: For S = (K°, K°°), K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}): (K°/K°°)^a ≅ 0, and Hom_{K°a}(K°a, (K°/ϖ)^a) ≅ Hom_{K°}(K°°, K°/ϖ) contains the sums Σ_i ϖ^{1−1/p^i} x_i that are not in the image of K°/ϖ (Sch12 Remark 4.8).
For the classical setup (V, V), (−)^a is an equivalence ModuleCat V ≌ Almost.Module S.

nodes.title: Hom(M^a, N^a) = Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N)
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. For V-modules M, N there is a natural V-linear bijection Hom_{Almost.Module S}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Hom_V(m̃ ⊗_V M, N). In particular Hom-types of Almost.Module S are V-modules, functorially in both variables, and they contain no nonzero almost zero elements (if m·f = 0 then f = 0). With M = V: Hom(V^a, N^a) ≅ Hom_V(m̃, N).
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Calculus of fractions: Hom(M^a, N^a) = colim over almost isomorphisms φ : P → M of Hom_V(P, N) (GR (2.2.3)).

The multiplication m̃ ⊗ M → M is an initial object of the category of almost isomorphisms over M: for φ : P → M an almost isomorphism, m̃ ⊗ P → m̃ ⊗ M is an isomorphism (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero), giving ψ : m̃ ⊗ M → P over M; two such ψ differ by a map with image in Ker φ (almost zero) from m̃ ⊗ M = m·(m̃ ⊗ M), hence agree.
So the colimit is Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N); in the firm model this is Hom_{Firm}(m̃ ⊗ M, m̃ ⊗ N) ≅ Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N) because m̃ ⊗ N → N is an almost isomorphism and m̃ ⊗ M is firm.
No almost zero elements: if ε·f = 0 for all ε ∈ m then f vanishes on m·(m̃ ⊗ M) = m̃ ⊗ M.
acceptance: For S = (K°, K°°), M = K°, N = K°/ϖ: Hom(K°a, (K°/ϖ)^a) = Hom_{K°}(K°°, K°/ϖ) (Sch12 Proposition 4.4 and Remark 4.8).

nodes.title: Almost elements M_* and the left adjoint M_! of almostification
nodes.statement: For a basic setup S = (V, m): (i) the functor of almost elements (−)_* : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V, M_* := Hom_{V^a}(V^a, M) with its V-module structure, is right adjoint to M ↦ M^a, with counit (M_*)^a → M an isomorphism (so (−)_* is fully faithful) and (N^a)_* ≅ Hom_V(m̃, N) naturally; (ii) (−)_! : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V, M_! := m̃ ⊗_V M_*, is left adjoint to M ↦ M^a with unit M → (M_!)^a an isomorphism (so (−)_! is fully faithful), and it is exact because m̃ is flat; (iii) for every V-module N the unit N → (N^a)_* and the natural map (N^a)_! → N are almost isomorphisms, and M_! → M_* is an almost isomorphism; (iv) (−)^a preserves all limits and colimits, (−)_* preserves limits and injective objects (not infinite direct sums), (−)_! preserves colimits and tensor products; Almost.Module S is complete, cocomplete, satisfies AB5, has the generator V^a and enough injectives; (v) preimages of almost elements exist only up to m: for an epimorphism φ : M_1 → M_2, x ∈ (M_2)_* and ε ∈ m there is y ∈ (M_1)_* with φ_*(y) = ε·x.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; m̃ flat is used for exactness of (−)_!.
proofSteps: (i) By P0/almost-hom-formula Hom(M^a, N) ≅ Hom(M^a, (N_*)^a) ≅ Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N_*) ≅ Hom_V(M, Hom_V(m̃, N_*)) ≅ Hom_V(M, N_*) (GR proof of Proposition 2.2.13(ii)); the counit is an isomorphism (GR 2.2.13(iii), or Gabriel [38, Ch.III Prop.3]). In the firm model (−)_* is j_* = Hom_V(m̃, −).

(ii) Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M_*, N) ≅ Hom(M, N^a) by (2.2.4) (GR Proposition 2.2.21); exactness: right exact as a left adjoint, left exact as m̃ ⊗ − is exact and (−)_* left exact (GR Corollary 2.2.22(i)). In the firm model (−)_! is the inclusion j_!.
(iii) The kernel and cokernel of N → Hom_V(m̃, N) are killed by m (from the exact sequence 0 → m̃-torsion ...; GR 2.2.9 via (2.2.4)).

(iv) Adjoint functors preserve limits/colimits; (−)^a has both adjoints; limits and colimits of almost modules are computed as (lim M_*)^a and (colim M_*)^a (GR Corollary 2.2.15); injectives: (−)_* is right adjoint to an exact functor (GR Corollary 2.2.17), and (−)^a is right adjoint to the exact (−)_! (GR Corollary 2.2.22(ii)), so injective V-modules give injective almost modules.
(v) For ε ∈ m, ε·x is in the image because the cokernel of (M_1)_* → (M_2)_* is almost zero (GR Remark 2.2.14(ii)).
acceptance: For S = (K°, K°°) and N torsion-free: (N^a)_* = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : εx ∈ N for all ε ∈ m} (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii)); e.g. ((K°°)^a)_* = K°.
((K°/ϖ)^a)_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ) strictly contains K°/ϖ (Sch12 Remark 4.8).

uses.how: M_* = Hom(m, M_*) has no ϖ-torsion; (N^a)_* = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : εx ∈ N}; A_* = R° for a perfectoid algebra

nodes.title: Almost isomorphisms are stable under tensor products
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup. The class S.almostZero.isoModSerre of almost isomorphisms of V-modules is multiplicative, and for every V-module X and almost isomorphism f, X ⊗ f and f ⊗ X are almost isomorphisms; that is, it is a monoidal morphism property for Mathlib's monoidal structure on ModuleCat V (`MorphismProperty.IsMonoidal`). Equivalently, almost zero modules form a tensor ideal.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Multiplicativity is Mathlib's (isoModSerre of a Serre class is multiplicative and has the two-out-of-three property).

f is an almost isomorphism iff m̃ ⊗ f is an isomorphism (P0/almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero); then m̃ ⊗ (X ⊗ f) ≅ X ⊗ (m̃ ⊗ f) is an isomorphism, so X ⊗ f is an almost isomorphism; symmetrically for f ⊗ X.
acceptance: For f : m ↪ V (an almost isomorphism) and X = V/m: X ⊗ f : m/m² = 0 → V/m has almost zero cokernel V/m, as the lemma predicts.

nodes.title: The closed symmetric monoidal structure on almost modules
nodes.statement: For a basic setup S = (V, m), Almost.Module S carries the symmetric monoidal structure localized from ModuleCat V (Mathlib `LocalizedMonoidal` for the monoidal class of almost isomorphisms, P0/almost-isomorphisms-are-monoidal), with unit V^a (≅ m^a): the localization functor M ↦ M^a is symmetric monoidal, M^a ⊗ N^a ≅ (M ⊗_V N)^a, and M ⊗ N ≅ (M_* ⊗_V N_*)^a ≅ (M_! ⊗_V N_!)^a. The tensor product is right exact in each variable. The internal hom is alHom(M, N) := (Hom_{V^a}(M, N))^a, the almostification of the V-module of P0/almost-hom-formula; there is a natural isomorphism Hom(L ⊗ M, N) ≅ Hom(L, alHom(M, N)), so Almost.Module S is closed, and alHom(M^a, N^a) ≅ (Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N))^a. The functor (−)_! is strong monoidal on nonempty tensor products (M ⊗ N)_! ≅ M_! ⊗_V N_!, and (−)_* is lax symmetric monoidal.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Monoidal structure: Mathlib `LocalizedMonoidal (toAlmost S) S.almostZero.isoModSerre (Iso.refl _)` gives the monoidal category and makes toAlmost monoidal; Mathlib's Braided file upgrades it to a symmetric monoidal structure because ModuleCat V is symmetric.

nodes.title: Almost algebras (commutative monoids in V^a-Mod) and their modules
nodes.statement: For a basic setup S = (V, m), an almost V-algebra is a commutative unital monoid object in the symmetric monoidal category Almost.Module S: Almost.Algebra S := CommMon (Almost.Module S) (Mathlib), with monoid morphisms. For an almost algebra A, A_* = Hom(V^a, A) is a commutative V-algebra (a·b := μ ∘ (a ⊗ b) ∘ ν⁻¹); R ↦ R^a from commutative V-algebras to almost algebras is left adjoint to A ↦ A_*, with counit A ≅ (A_*)^a, so (−)_* is fully faithful and Hom_{Alg}(A, B) ≅ Hom_{V-alg}(A_*, B_*); every almost algebra is R^a for R = A_*. An A-module is a module object over A (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mod`); A-modules form an abelian, complete and cocomplete category A-Mod, closed symmetric monoidal with M ⊗_A N := (M_* ⊗_{A_*} N_*)^a, and A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_*) (P0/change-of-basic-setup). An A-algebra is a morphism A → B. Pinned convention: module-theoretic notions for A-modules (flat, almost projective, almost finitely generated and presented) are those of P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness and P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented, evaluated through this equivalence on the A_*-module M_*.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: CommMon (Almost.Module S) for the symmetric monoidal structure of P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom.
A_* is a commutative V-algebra: (−)_* is lax symmetric monoidal (Bhatt Remark 4.2.8) and End(V^a) = V (GR 2.2.8).

Adjunction and counit: toAlmost is symmetric monoidal, so it maps commutative V-algebras to almost algebras; its right adjoint (−)_* on modules lifts to monoids (lax monoidal right adjoint of a strong monoidal functor), with counit the isomorphism of P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (GR Proposition 2.2.13 for algebras).

A-Mod: kernels are A-submodules and, ⊗ being right exact, cokernels carry A-module structures, so A-Mod is abelian (GR 2.2.6); limits and colimits via (−)_* (GR Corollary 2.2.15); A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_*) by P0/change-of-basic-setup (i).

nodes.title: Change of basic setup: (W, mW)^a-Mod ≃ W^a-Mod, and invariance under almost isomorphic base rings
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and V → W a ring homomorphism, S_W = (W, mW) the base-changed setup (P0/basic-setup-base-change). (i) Restriction of scalars gives a functor Almost.Module S_W → (modules over the almost V-algebra W^a in Almost.Module S), and it is an equivalence with quasi-inverse M ↦ (M_*)^a; it commutes with (−)_* and (−)_!, and the analogous statement holds for almost algebras. (ii) If V → W is an almost isomorphism of V-modules (kernel and cokernel killed by m), then W^a ≅ V^a as almost V-algebras and restriction of scalars Almost.Module S_W → Almost.Module S is an equivalence. The case R⁺ ⊆ R° (R°/R⁺ almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii)) is the comparison R°a-mod ≃ R⁺a-mod stated in ECD after Definition 3.23 and Berkeley after Definition 7.4.3, proved in PerfectoidSpaces:P1 from this lemma.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; V → W any ring map for (i); for (ii) its kernel and cokernel are killed by m.
proofSteps: (i) GR Remark 2.2.12: the obvious functor (W, mW)^a-Mod → W^a-Mod and the quasi-inverse M ↦ M_*; the unit and counit are the isomorphisms of P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints over the two setups (almost zero W-modules for mW are the W-modules killed by m).
Compatibility with (−)_* and (−)_!: GR Remark 2.2.28(ii).
(ii) (V → W)^a is an isomorphism of almost algebras, so W^a-modules are V^a-modules, i.e. objects of Almost.Module S; compose with (i).
acceptance: For V = R⁺ ⊆ W = R° with R perfectoid Tate, (ii) gives Almost.Module (R⁺, ϖ^{1/p^∞}R⁺) ≃ Almost.Module (R°, ϖ^{1/p^∞}R°).
For W = V/I, (i) identifies almost V/I-modules with almost V-modules killed by I.

nodes.title: The left adjoint B ↦ B_!! of almostification on algebras
nodes.statement: For a basic setup S = (V, m) and an almost V-algebra B, B_! = m̃ ⊗_V B_* is a non-unital V-algebra; B_!! := (V ⊕ B_!)/I, where I is the V-submodule spanned by the elements (xy, −x ⊗ y ⊗ 1) for x, y ∈ m, is a unital commutative V-algebra with B ≅ (B_!!)^a, and B ↦ B_!! is left adjoint to R ↦ R^a from A_!!-algebras to A-algebras (for any almost algebra A with B an A-algebra). B is exact if 0 → m̃ → V ⊕ B_! → B_!! → 0 is exact; every almost algebra is exact when m̃ → m is an isomorphism (e.g. m flat), and V^a × B is always exact. B ↦ B_!! commutes with all colimits, in particular with tensor products; the natural map B_!! → B_* is an almost isomorphism. B ↦ B_!! preserves faithful flatness of morphisms but not flatness (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness).
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Ring structure on V ⊕ B_!: (v, b)(v', b') = (vv', vb' + v'b + bb'); I is an ideal (GR 2.2.23).
Adjunction: an A-algebra map φ : B → C^a gives B_! → C (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints) and with V → C a ring map V ⊕ B_! → C killing I; conversely localize (GR Proposition 2.2.27).
B ≅ (B_!!)^a: the kernel of V ⊕ B_! → B_!! is the image of m̃, which is almost isomorphic to m ⊂ V (GR Remark 2.2.26).
Colimits: left adjoint; tensor products are pushouts (GR Remark 2.2.28(i)); B_!! → B_* almost isomorphism (Bhatt Remark 4.2.8).
acceptance: (V^a)_!! ≅ V: (V^a)_! = m̃ and (V ⊕ m̃)/I ≅ V via (v, x ⊗ y) ↦ v + xy.
For m flat (valuation or root setups with ϖ a nonzerodivisor), every almost algebra is exact.

nodes.title: Almost finitely generated, uniformly almost finitely generated and almost finitely presented modules
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module, M = N^a over A = R^a. N^a is almost finitely generated if for every finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m there are n and an R-linear φ : Rⁿ → N with m₀·coker φ = 0; uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n if one n works for all m₀; almost finitely presented if for every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m there is a complex R^k →ψ Rⁿ →φ N with m₀·coker φ = 0 and m₀·ker φ ⊆ im ψ. These conditions depend only on N^a (not on the representative N), and agree with GR's definitions through the uniform structure on isomorphism classes (GR Definition 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.10); under condition (A) (e.g. root and valuation setups) they are equivalent to Sch12's ε-formulation: for every ε ∈ m there is a finitely generated (presented) R-module N_ε and N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion). For an arbitrary almost algebra A they are applied to M_* over A_* (P0/almost-algebras). Pinned: our uniform notion (maps from Rⁿ with small cokernel) implies GR's U_n(A) in general and is equivalent to it under (A) (GR Remark 2.3.9).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; R a V-algebra; N an R-module.
proofSteps: Definitions as stated, with finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m (Mathlib `Submodule.FG`).

Independence of the representative: if N → N' is an almost isomorphism, replace m₀ by m₁ with m₀ ⊆ m₁² ... using m = m²: generators of N' multiplied by elements of m lift to N (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); the kernel condition for presentations is handled as in GR Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12.
Comparison with GR 2.3.8: GR Proposition 2.3.10(i) and (ii)(c) are exactly our conditions for almost finitely generated and presented modules.
acceptance: Sch12 Example 4.9 / Bhatt Example 4.2.7: for K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): L°a is almost finitely presented and uniformly almost finitely generated with bound 2 over K°a.

nodes.title: Flat, faithfully flat, almost projective and almost finite projective almost modules
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. M is flat if M ⊗_A − : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact, faithfully flat if moreover M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 implies N ≅ 0, almost projective if alHom_A(M, −) : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact (GR Definition 2.4.4), and almost finite projective if it is almost projective and almost finitely generated (P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented); 'uniformly almost finite projective' adds a uniform bound. Pinned convention: categorical projectivity (Hom(M, −) exact) is never used — Almost.Module S has no nonzero projective objects when V is local and m ≠ V (GR Example 2.4.5). For a V-algebra R and an R-module N: N flat (faithfully flat, projective) implies N^a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) over R^a (GR 2.4.8). Characterisations: Tor and Ext criteria (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion), ε-factorisation (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), finite projective = flat + almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A an almost V-algebra; A-Mod as in P0/almost-algebras.
proofSteps: Define the three predicates on objects of A-Mod through the functors M ⊗_A − and alHom_A(M, −) (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom for A-Mod).

Compatibility with honest modules: if N is R-flat then N ⊗_R − preserves almost zero modules and exact sequences, so it induces an exact functor on the Serre quotient (GR 2.4.8); faithfulness from m ⊗ (N ⊗ X) = 0 ⇔ m ⊗ X = 0 for N faithfully flat; projective N is a summand of a free module and alHom(R^{(I)}, −) = ∏ is exact.
Almost projective ⇒ flat: multiplication by ε factors through a free module (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)).
Stability: tensor products and base change preserve flatness and almost projectivity (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii)); transitivity along almost algebra maps (GR Lemma 2.4.7).
acceptance: Over S = (K°, K°°): M is flat over K°a iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)); K°a is flat, (K°/ϖ)^a is not.
V^a is almost projective and flat but not a projective object when V is local and m ≠ V.

nodes.title: Tor and Ext criteria for almost flatness and almost projectivity
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module. (i) For R-modules M, N and i ≥ 0 there are natural isomorphisms Tor_i^{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Tor_i^R(M, N)^a and alExt^i_{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Ext^i_R(M, N)^a, where Tor^{R^a} and alExt are the derived functors of ⊗ and alHom on R^a-Mod (computed by flat resp. injective resolutions). (ii) N^a is flat over R^a iff Tor_i^R(N, X) is almost zero for all R-modules X and all i > 0; (iii) N^a is almost projective iff Ext^i_R(N, X) is almost zero for all X and i > 0; (iv) N^a is faithfully flat iff it is flat and, for every R-module X, N ⊗_R X almost zero implies X almost zero. (v) An almost projective module is flat.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; R a V-algebra.
proofSteps: Derived functors on R^a-Mod exist: enough injectives and enough flat and almost projective objects (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints; GR 2.4.8, 2.4.10); bounded above exact complexes of flat (almost projective) objects are acyclic for ⊗ (alHom(−, M)).

(i): the exact functor (−)^a takes a flat resolution of M to a flat resolution of M^a (GR 2.4.8), whence (2.4.11); for Ext use the adjunction between (−)_! and (−)^a on derived categories (GR 2.4.9, Lemma 2.4.14(i)).
(ii)-(iii): M is flat (almost projective) iff all higher Tor (alExt) vanish (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)); combine with (i) and P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (vanishing of M^a iff M almost zero).
(iv): faithfulness of N^a ⊗ − means N^a ⊗ X^a ≅ 0 ⇒ X^a ≅ 0.
(v): multiplication by ε ∈ m on an almost projective M factors through a free module (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).
acceptance: Over S = (K°, K°°): M^a flat iff Tor_1(M, K°/ϖ) = M[ϖ] is almost zero, iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).
Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.9.11: A°/ϖ → B°/ϖ almost faithfully flat means Tor_i^{A°/ϖ}(M, B°/ϖ) almost zero for i > 0; by (ii) this is flatness of (B°/ϖ)^a over (A°/ϖ)^a.

nodes.title: Almost projectivity via ε-factorisations through free modules
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and M an A-module. (i) M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there is a set I and A-linear maps M →u A^{(I)} →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M. (ii) If M is almost finitely generated, M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there are n(ε) ∈ ℕ and M →u Aⁿ →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M; M is uniformly almost finite projective with bound n iff n can be taken independent of ε (Kedlaya–Liu's definition of (uniformly) almost finite projective).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; M an A-module.
proofSteps: ⇐: applying alExt^i(−, N) to M → A^{(I)} → M shows that ε kills alExt^i(M, N) for i > 0; as ε ∈ m is arbitrary these are almost zero, hence zero in A-Mod (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion).

⇒ (finitely generated case, GR proof of Lemma 2.4.15): choose φ_ε : Aⁿ → M with ε·coker φ_ε = 0, factor through its image M_ε; almost projectivity makes alHom(M, Aⁿ) → alHom(M, M_ε) an epimorphism, so for δ ∈ m the map δ·γ_ε (with ε·1_M = j_ε ∘ γ_ε) lifts to u_{εδ} : M → Aⁿ; then φ_ε ∘ u_{εδ} = εδ·1_M; products εδ span m.
⇒ (general case): the same argument with a free module A^{(I)} surjecting onto M.
acceptance: For P = L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): the maps L° → (K°)² → L° with composite p^{1/p^{n−1}} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7) exhibit P as uniformly almost finite projective with bound 2.
KL Definition 5.5.8 takes (ii) as the definition of almost finite projective.

nodes.title: The ε-criterion for almost finite generation and presentation under condition (A)
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup satisfying condition (A) (m is a filtered union of principal ideals; e.g. root setups and valuation setups), R a V-algebra and N an R-module. Then N^a is almost finitely generated (resp. almost finitely presented) iff for every ε ∈ m there are a finitely generated (resp. finitely presented) R-module N_ε and an R-linear map N_ε → N whose kernel and cokernel are killed by ε; and N^a is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n iff for every ε ∈ m there is Rⁿ → N with cokernel killed by ε. In a general basic setup the same equivalences hold with ε replaced by finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m, which is the definition of P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented.
hypotheses: S a basic setup with condition (A).
proofSteps: Under (A) every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m lies in a principal ideal εV ⊆ m, and every ε ∈ m generates a finitely generated subideal; so the m₀-conditions and the ε-conditions are equivalent for generation (take N_ε := image, kernel 0).

Presentation: GR Proposition 2.3.10(ii), equivalence of (a), (b), (c), with (b) the ε, δ-formulation; from a complex R^k → Rⁿ → N with ε-small cokernel and δ-small homology one builds N_ε := Rⁿ/im ψ and conversely (Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12).
Uniform bound: GR Remark 2.3.9.
acceptance: For S = ofValuationRing K°, Sch12 Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii) is this ε-formulation.

nodes.title: Flat + almost finitely presented ⟺ almost projective + almost finitely generated
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. (i) If M is almost projective and almost finitely generated, M is almost finitely presented (and flat). (ii) If M is flat and almost finitely presented, M is almost projective. Hence 'finite projective' in Sch12's sense (flat and almost finitely presented) coincides with almost finite projective (almost projective and almost finitely generated). (iii) If A → B is a monomorphism of almost algebras and M is an almost finitely generated flat A-module with B ⊗_A M almost finitely presented over B, then M is almost finitely presented.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: (ii) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(ii): for ε, δ ∈ m pick A^m →ψ Aⁿ →φ M with ε·coker φ = 0 = δ·(ker φ/im ψ); P := coker ψ_* is a finitely presented A_*-module; flatness and Lemma 2.4.17 (Tor_1 of the transposed presentation) give γ·φ = w ∘ v through a free module for every γ ∈ m; assemble α, β with β ∘ α = εδγ·1_M and conclude by P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation.

(i) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(i): for a finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m pick φ : A^r → P with m₀·coker φ = 0; ε_i·1_P lifts to P → A^r/ker φ and, P being almost projective, ε_jψ_i lifts to A^r; Claim 2.3.11 gives finitely generated submodules of ker φ containing ε_iε_j ker φ, so m₀²·ker φ lies in a finitely generated submodule.
(iii) GR Proposition 2.4.19.
acceptance: For the classical setup this is the statement that finitely presented flat modules are projective and finitely generated projective modules are finitely presented.
Sch12 Proposition 4.10 is the case S = (K°, K°°).

nodes.title: E ⊗ alHom(F, N) → alHom(F, E ⊗ N) is an isomorphism for almost finite projective E or F
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and E, F, N A-modules. The natural map E ⊗_A alHom_A(F, N) → alHom_A(F, E ⊗_A N) is (i) an isomorphism if E or F is almost finite projective, if E is flat and F almost finitely presented, if F is almost projective and E almost finitely presented, or if E is almost projective and F almost finitely generated; (ii) a monomorphism if E is flat and F almost finitely generated, or if E is almost projective; (iii) an epimorphism if F is almost projective and E almost finitely generated. Consequences: for P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism, P is reflexive (P ≅ P**), and B ⊗_A alHom_A(P, N) ≅ alHom_B(B ⊗_A P, B ⊗_A N) for every A-algebra B.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Free finite case: alHom(Aⁿ, N) ≅ Nⁿ and the map is an isomorphism.

Almost finite projective F: for ε ∈ m apply the natural transformation to F →u_ε A^{I(ε)} →v_ε F (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation) with I(ε) finite; a diagram chase shows that kernel and cokernel are killed by ε, hence almost zero, hence zero (GR proof of Lemma 2.4.29).

The remaining cases reduce, via almost elements and ε-approximations, to classical statements for finitely generated (presented) modules and free modules (Bourbaki Algèbre commutative I §2 Prop. 10), as in GR.
ω_{P/A} is the case E = P, N = A; reflexivity and base change: GR Lemma 2.4.31.
acceptance: For P = (Rⁿ)^a free: ω_{P/A} is the usual identification Rⁿ ⊗ (Rⁿ)^∨ ≅ End(Rⁿ) after almostification.

nodes.title: Duals, traces of endomorphisms and the trace form of an almost finite projective algebra
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. For an A-module M, the dual is M* := alHom_A(M, A) with evaluation ev_{M/A} : M ⊗_A M* → A. For P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism (P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective) and the trace is tr_{P/A} := ev_{P/A} ∘ ω_{P/A}⁻¹ : End_A(P)^a → A. For an A-algebra B which is almost finite projective as an A-module, μ : B → End_A(B)^a (b ↦ multiplication by b, defined on almost elements) gives the almost trace Tr_{B/A} := tr_{B/A} ∘ μ : B → A, the trace form t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A, and τ_{B/A} : B → B*; t_{B/A} is a perfect pairing if τ_{B/A} is an isomorphism. Properties: tr(ψ∘φ) = tr(φ∘ψ); tr(φ ⊗ ψ) = tr(φ)·tr(ψ); additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules; Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}; Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}; τ is B-linear and compatible with base change. Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` (zero on non-free modules) is not used for almost finite projective modules; it agrees with tr on free modules.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; P almost finite projective; B an A-algebra, almost finite projective as A-module.
proofSteps: Define P*, ev and ω on almost elements (GR Definition 2.4.23, 2.4.26); ω iso by P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective; tr := ev ∘ ω⁻¹ and ζ_P := ω⁻¹(1_P) (GR Definition 4.1.1).
Cyclicity: reduce by A-linearity to rank-one maps x ↦ n·α(x), then compute (GR Lemma 4.1.2); multiplicativity (Lemma 4.1.3); additivity via the ε-split pullback trick (Proposition 4.1.4).
Algebra traces: μ is a B-linear monomorphism (GR 4.1.7); base change and transitivity (Proposition 4.1.8); τ_{B/A} and base change (Lemma 4.1.13).
Compatibility with free modules: for P = (Rⁿ)^a, ω and ev are almostifications of Mathlib's `dualTensorHom` and evaluation, so tr = (LinearMap.trace)^a.
acceptance: For B = (Rⁿ)^a with R-algebra structure free of rank n: Tr_{B/A} = (Algebra.trace R Rⁿ)^a.
For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)): Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2 and t_{L°a/K°a} is perfect, while the honest trace form on R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K° has discriminant 4p^{1/p^n} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7).

nodes.title: Rank decomposition of uniformly almost finite projective modules
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup satisfying condition (B) (k-th powers generate m; implied by (A)), A an almost V-algebra and P a uniformly almost finite projective A-module. Then P has finite rank: Λ^r_A P = 0 for some r. For P almost projective with Λ^r_A P = 0 there is a unique decomposition A ≅ A_0 × A_1 × ⋯ × A_{r−1} such that P_i := P ⊗_A A_i has constant rank i over A_i: Λ^{i+1}_{A_i} P_i = 0 and Λ^i_{A_i} P_i is an invertible A_i-module (P_i ⊗ P_i* ≅ A_i). The decomposition is compatible with base change A → A'.
hypotheses: S a basic setup with condition (B) (used for uniform continuity of Λ^r, GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi), and for Proposition 4.3.4); root and valuation setups satisfy (A) hence (B).
Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 4.11 cites GR Proposition 4.3.27 and Remark 4.3.10(i) in book numbering; the arXiv v3 statements with these numbers are the ones quoted here.
proofSteps: Finite rank: a uniformly almost finitely generated module with bound n lies in the closure U_n(A) of the modules generated by n almost elements; under (B) the operation Λ^{n+1} is uniformly continuous (GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi)) and vanishes on modules generated by n elements, so Λ^{n+1}P = 0 (GR Remark 4.3.10(i)).

Formal rank: χ_P(X) = Σ_i tr(Λ^i 1_P) X^i defines an endomorphism of Ĝ_m (GR Corollary 4.3.8, from Proposition 4.3.4 whose proof uses (B)); for finite rank it is (1 + X)^α for a locally constant α (Remark 4.3.10(ii)).
Decomposition: induction on r, the case r = 2 being GR Lemma 4.3.12, the inductive step using Lemma 4.3.26 (Λ²(Λ^{r−1} P) = 0) (GR Proposition 4.3.27).
Uniqueness and base change: the idempotents are determined by χ_P, which is compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.3.2(i)).
acceptance: For L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): r = 3, A = A_2 (constant rank 2).
For A = K°a × K°a and P = K°a × 0: A_1 = first factor, A_0 = second factor.

nodes.title: Flat, unramified, étale and finite étale morphisms of almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost V-algebras; view B as a B ⊗_A B-algebra through the multiplication μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B, with kernel I_{B/A}. Following GR Definition 3.1.1: φ is flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) if B is a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) A-module; (uniformly) almost finite if B is a (uniformly) almost finitely generated A-module; weakly unramified (unramified) if B is a flat (almost projective) B ⊗_A B-module; weakly étale (étale) if flat and weakly unramified (unramified). φ is finite étale if it is étale and B is an almost finitely presented A-module (Sch12 Definition 4.13; GR's A-Ét_afp; Kedlaya–Liu's and Bhatt's 'almost finite étale'); then B is almost finite projective over A (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff). A_fet denotes the full subcategory of A-algebras that are finite étale over A. Equivalent descriptions: unramified iff there is a diagonal idempotent e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with μ(e) = 1 and I_{B/A,*}·e = 0 (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation, Sch12's definition); for B almost finite projective over A, étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} is perfect (P0/trace-form-criterion). Pinned: 'finite étale' always means étale and almost finitely presented; in the classical setup it is Mathlib's finite étale (P0/finite-etale-localizes), while GR's 'étale' without finiteness is more general than EGA étale (GR Remark 3.1.3(i)).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras; module notions as in P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness and P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented, applied to B as an A-module and as a B ⊗_A B-module.
proofSteps: Define the predicates on morphisms of Almost.Algebra S through the module structures of B over A and over B ⊗_A B (μ_{B/A} a morphism of almost algebras).
A_fet := full subcategory of Under A on the finite étale morphisms.
The characterisations are P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation (GR Proposition 3.1.4), P0/trace-form-criterion (GR Theorem 4.1.14) and P0/etale-morphisms-stability (GR Lemma 3.1.2).

nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. φ is unramified (B almost projective over B ⊗_A B) iff there is an almost element e_{B/A} ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with e² = e, μ_{B/A}(e) = 1 and x·e = 0 for every x ∈ (I_{B/A})_*. The element e is unique, and B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B as B ⊗_A B-algebras (I_{B/A} with unit 1 − e). More generally, for an ideal I of an almost algebra A, A/I is almost projective over A iff I is generated by an idempotent of A_*, which is then unique.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: ⇒: for ε ∈ m almost projectivity gives an ε-splitting u_ε : B → B ⊗_A B of μ with μ ∘ u_ε = ε·1_B (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation); e_ε := u_ε(1) satisfies e_ε² = ε e_ε, μ(e_ε) = ε and I_*·e_ε = 0 by B ⊗_A B-linearity.
δ e_ε = ε e_δ for ε, δ ∈ m, so ε ⊗ δ ↦ δ·e_ε is a well defined map m ⊗_V m → (B ⊗_A B)_*, i.e. an almost element e (GR (3.1.7)), with the required properties.
⇐: u(b) := e·(1 ⊗ b) is B ⊗_A B-linear by the annihilation property and splits μ, so B is a direct summand, hence almost projective (GR Lemma 2.4.15).
Uniqueness and the product decomposition: GR Corollary 3.1.9 and Remark 3.1.8.
acceptance: For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the idempotent is Bhatt's e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1).
In the classical setup with B finite étale over A, ker μ is a finitely generated idempotent ideal, generated by the idempotent 1 − e (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`).

nodes.title: Stability of flat, unramified and étale morphisms of almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B, ψ : B → C morphisms of almost algebras. (i) Flatness, almost projectivity, faithful flatness, almost finiteness, weak unramifiedness, unramifiedness, weak étaleness and étaleness are stable under base change A → A' and (ii) under composition. (iii) If φ is flat and ψ ∘ φ faithfully flat then φ is faithfully flat. (iv) If φ is weakly unramified and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly étale) then ψ is flat (weakly étale). (v) If φ is unramified and ψ ∘ φ étale then ψ is étale. (vi) φ is faithfully flat iff it is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (vii) If φ is almost finite and weakly unramified then φ is unramified. (viii) If ψ is faithfully flat and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly unramified) then φ is flat (weakly unramified). Finite étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: (i), (ii), (iii), (viii): the module-theoretic stability of P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii), Lemma 2.4.7) applied to B over A and over B ⊗_A B.
(vi): Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0.
(vii): B is an almost finitely presented B ⊗_A B-module (I_{B/A} is a quotient of (B ⊗_A B) ⊗_A B), so flat implies almost projective (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).
(iv), (v): μ_{B/A} is étale when φ is unramified; Γ_ψ := 1_C ⊗_B μ_{B/A} is étale by (i), p := (ψ∘φ) ⊗_A 1_B is flat (étale), and ψ = Γ_ψ ∘ p; apply (ii).
Finite étale: base change and transitivity of almost finite presentation (GR Lemma 2.4.7, 2.3.7(v)).
acceptance: In the classical setup (vi) is the usual criterion 'faithfully flat iff injective with flat cokernel'.
Base change of L°a/K°a along K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a gives a finite étale (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

nodes.title: Almost finite projective algebras are étale iff the trace form is perfect
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras with B almost finite projective as an A-module. Then φ is étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A is a perfect pairing, i.e. τ_{B/A} : B → B* = alHom_A(B, A) is an isomorphism. In that case (1_B ⊗ τ_{B/A})(e_{B/A}) = ζ_B, where e_{B/A} is the diagonal idempotent and ζ_B = ω_{B/A}⁻¹(1_B). In particular, for B almost finitely presented, φ is finite étale iff B is flat over A and t_{B/A} is perfect.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; B almost finite projective over A.
proofSteps: τ_{B/A} is B-linear and compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.1.13), giving the B ⊗_A B-linear diagram (4.1.15).

⇒: for φ étale, B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation), so τ_{B⊗B/B} = τ_{B/B} ⊕ τ_{I/B} and after B ⊗_{B⊗_A B} − all arrows of (4.1.15) are isomorphisms, in particular τ_{B/A}.
⇐: put e := (1_B ⊗ τ⁻¹)(ζ_B); Claim 4.1.16 (I_{B/A}·ζ_B = 0 and σ(ζ_B) = Tr_{B/A}) gives I_{B/A}·e = 0 and μ(e) = 1, hence e is the diagonal idempotent (GR Proposition 3.1.4).
acceptance: For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the trace form is perfect on the almost level (the discriminants 4p^{1/p^n} of the approximations R_n tend to a unit up to m).
In the classical setup with B finite free: the classical criterion 'finite free étale iff discriminant is a unit'.

nodes.title: Inverting an element of m: almost modules become honest modules over V[1/ϖ]
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and ϖ ∈ m. The localisation M ↦ M[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] ⊗_V M is exact and kills almost zero modules (ϖM = 0), so it factors, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, through an exact functor Almost.invert ϖ : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V[1/ϖ] with invert(M^a) ≅ M[1/ϖ] and invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ] ≅ M_![1/ϖ]. Consequences: almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms and almost exact complexes become exact after inverting ϖ; the setup S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical (m·V[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ]), so Almost.Module over it is ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]; invert is symmetric monoidal and sends almost algebras to V[1/ϖ]-algebras. The ϖ-adic completion side of this passage — completeness of M versus M_*, and exactness of complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ, with the lim¹ term kept — is P0/almost-completeness-via-almost-elements and P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m (so ϖ kills almost zero modules; ϖ need not be a nonzerodivisor).
proofSteps: M ↦ M[1/ϖ] is exact (Mathlib localisation is exact) and kills almost zero modules; by Mathlib `SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft` it factors through toAlmost as an exact functor.
invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ]: apply the factorisation to M ≅ (M_*)^a (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).

S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical because ϖ ∈ m becomes a unit (P0/basic-setup-base-change); invert is then the composite of change of setup (P0/change-of-basic-setup) and Almost.Module.classicalEquiv (GR 5.2.17: 'A[ε^{-1}] is a usual V-algebra').
Monoidality: localisation commutes with tensor products, so invert is symmetric monoidal and carries commutative monoids to commutative V[1/ϖ]-algebras.
acceptance: S = (K°, K°°): invert((K°/ϖ)^a) = 0, invert(K°a) = K, invert(R°a) = R for a perfectoid K-algebra R.

PerfectoidSpaces:P2 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D2: H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for i > 0 gives H^i(X, O) = H^i(X, O⁺)[1/ϖ] = 0 (cohomology on quasicompact sites commutes with the filtered colimit defining O = O⁺[1/ϖ]).

nodes.title: Comparison of finite étale almost algebras with Mathlib's finite étale algebras
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and R → R' a map of commutative V-algebras. (i) If R' is finite étale over R in Mathlib's sense (`Algebra.Etale R R'` and `Module.Finite R R'`), then R^a → R'^a is finite étale in the almost sense. (ii) In the classical setup (m = V) the converse holds, so A_fet for A = R^a is equivalent to Mathlib's category of finite étale R-algebras. (iii) For ϖ ∈ m, if R'^a is finite étale over R^a then R'[1/ϖ] is finite étale over R[1/ϖ] in Mathlib's sense (inverting ϖ turns almost statements into honest ones, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion). (iv) GR-étale morphisms in the classical setup are exactly the absolutely flat (weakly étale) maps whose diagonal is almost projective; they need not be of finite presentation, and a classical étale map in EGA's sense is étale in GR's sense.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; R → R' a map of V-algebras.
proofSteps: (i) R' is a finitely presented projective R-module (finite étale ⇒ finite, flat, finitely presented), so R'^a is almost finite projective (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness); the kernel J of R' ⊗_R R' → R' is finitely generated with J = J² (Ω_{R'/R} = 0), hence generated by an idempotent (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`), whose image is the diagonal idempotent (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation).

(ii) In the classical setup almost notions are honest: almost finitely presented = finitely presented, the diagonal idempotent gives Ω_{R'/R} = 0 (formally unramified), and a flat, finitely presented, formally unramified algebra is étale (GR 3.4.44: étale = absolutely flat and finitely presented).
(iii) Apply the exact monoidal inversion functor (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and (ii) for the classical setup (V[1/ϖ], V[1/ϖ]).
(iv) GR Remark 3.1.3(i) and digression 3.4.44.
acceptance: For K a perfectoid field and L/K finite separable: L°a is finite étale over K°a (ECD/Sch12), while L° need not be finite étale over K° in Mathlib's sense (it is not finitely presented in general); (i) is strictly weaker than the almost statement.
For R → R' = R × R the diagonal idempotent is (1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1).

nodes.title: Almost Kähler differentials Ω_{B/A} and almost derivations
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras, I_{B/A} = ker(μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B). The module of almost differentials is the B-module Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}², with the A-derivation δ : B → Ω_{B/A}, b ↦ 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 on almost elements. For a B-module M, an A-derivation B → M is an A-linear ∂ with ∂(b₁b₂) = b₁∂(b₂) + b₂∂(b₁) on almost elements; they form a V-module Der_A(B, M), and f ↦ f ∘ δ is an isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M). Properties: Ω_{C⊗_A B/C} ≅ C ⊗_A Ω_{B/A}; for A → B → C an exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0; for C = B/I an exact sequence I/I² → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → 0; Ω commutes with colimits; (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}; for V-algebras R → R', Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (Ω_{R'/R})^a (Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras.
proofSteps: Define I_{B/A}, Ω_{B/A} and δ in B ⊗_A B-Mod (P0/almost-algebras).
Universal property (2.5.24) and Proposition 2.5.25 as for rings, working on almost elements (GR 2.5.23 leaves them as exercises).
(Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}: compare derivations B_!! → M with almost derivations B → M^a (GR Lemma 2.5.28).
Comparison with Mathlib: (−)^a is exact and monoidal, so it carries the kernel of R' ⊗_R R' → R' and its square to I_{B/A} and I_{B/A}².

nodes.title: The almost cotangent complex L_{B/A}
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras. Put Ã := V^a × A and B̃ := V^a × B (exact almost algebras). The almost cotangent complex is L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗_{B̃_!!} L_{B̃_!!/Ã_!!}, an object of the derived category of B_!!-modules, where L_{−/−} is the classical cotangent complex of the ring map Ã_!! → B̃_!! (simplicial polynomial resolution; supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0); its almostification L^a_{B/A} ∈ D(B-Mod) is the object used in deformation theory. Properties: H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}; Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M) (GR (3.2.8)), Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M) (P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison); transitivity triangle (P0/cotangent-transitivity); Tor-independent base change (P0/cotangent-flat-base-change); L_{colim B_λ/colim A_λ} ≅ colim L_{B_λ/A_λ} for filtered systems; vanishing for weakly étale maps (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale); for V-algebras R → S, L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a (P0/almost-cotangent-comparison-classical), so 'the almost cotangent complex depends only on R^a → S^a' (Sch12 §5).

nodes.title: Transitivity triangle for almost cotangent complexes
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and A → B → C morphisms of almost algebras. There is a natural distinguished triangle C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A}[1] in D(C_!!-Mod), and hence C ⊗_B L^a_{B/A} → L^a_{C/A} → L^a_{C/B} → in D(C-Mod); on H_0 it extends the exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Apply the classical transitivity triangle (Illusie II.2.1.2, from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) to Ã_!! → B̃_!! → C̃_!! and base change to C_!! (GR Theorem 2.5.32).
Almostify (exact functor) for the L^a version; H_0 by P0/almost-differentials.
acceptance: For A → A[X] → A (X ↦ 0): the triangle A ⊗ L_{A[X]/A} → L_{A/A} ≃ 0 → L_{A/A[X]} → gives L^a_{A/A[X]} ≃ (X)/(X²)[1] ≅ A[1], the conormal module in homological degree 1.
Used in Sch12's proof of Theorem 5.10 for A → A_n → A_{n−1} (with base change).

sources.match: The triangle.

nodes.title: The almost cotangent complex of R^a → S^a is the almostified classical one
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and f : R → S a map of V-algebras. (i) If f^a : R^a → S^a is an isomorphism, then (L_{S/R})^a ≃ 0 in D(S^a-Mod). (ii) The natural map L^a_{S^a/R^a} → (L_{S/R})^a is an isomorphism in D(S^a-Mod). Hence the almost cotangent complex of a morphism of almost algebras coming from V-algebras is computed by the classical cotangent complex, and it depends only on R^a → S^a.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; L_{S/R} the classical cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).
proofSteps: (ii) from (i) by transitivity applied to (R^a)_!! → R and (S^a)_!! → S, whose almostifications are isomorphisms.

(i) by induction on q of H_q(L^a_{S/R}) = 0: transitivity for R → f(R) → S reduces to f injective or surjective; replace S by its standard free simplicial resolution S_• and R by R_• := S_• ×_S R (levelwise almost isomorphisms) and use the spectral sequence H_j(L_{S[i]/R[i]}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ_{S_•/R_•}); for S = V[T] free: if f surjective use a section; if f injective, compare with Sym(m̃ ⊗ F) ⊆ R ⊆ Sym(F) using flatness of m̃ and F (GR proof of Proposition 8.1.7).
acceptance: For R = V and S = V × k (k = V/m): f^a is an isomorphism (cokernel k almost zero), and L_{S/V} ≅ 0 × L_{k/V} has homology consisting of k-modules, hence almost zero, as (i) predicts.
Sch12 §5 uses (ii) implicitly when stating that L^a_{S/R} depends only on R^a → S^a.

sources.match: The comparison, located in GR §8.1 (simplicial almost algebras).
Part (ii).
Sch12's statement that L^a depends only on the almost morphism.

nodes.title: Tor-independent base change for almost cotangent complexes
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A → B and A → A' morphisms of almost algebras, B' := B ⊗_A A', and suppose the natural map B ⊗^L_A A' → B' is an isomorphism (Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0 for i > 0; e.g. B or A' flat over A). Then B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'} and (B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A}) ⊕ (B'_!! ⊗_{A'!!} L_{A'/A}) → L_{B'/A} are quasi-isomorphisms. This is the result Sch12 cites as 'Theorem 2.5.36 of [14]' (LNM 1800 book numbering) in the proof of Theorem 5.10; in arXiv v3 it is Theorem 2.5.35 (arXiv Theorem 2.5.36 is the vanishing statement of P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).
hypotheses: S a basic setup (m̃ flat, used in Proposition 2.5.34).
proofSteps: Proposition 2.5.34: if A, B, C, B ⊗_A C are exact, m̃ ⊗ Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) → Tor_i is an isomorphism for i > 0, and Tor^A_i(B, C) = 0 implies Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) = 0 (uses m̃ flat).

Replace algebras by V^a × (−) (commutes with tensor products) so that everything is exact, then apply the classical Tor-independent base change (Illusie II.2.2.1, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) (GR proof of Theorem 2.5.35).
acceptance: Sch12 proof of Theorem 5.10: for A_n flat over (K°/ϖ^n)^a the square (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, A_n → A_{n−1} is Tor-independent, so L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ≅ A_{n−1} ⊗ L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}; with transitivity this gives the triangle used there.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the almost cotangent complex when the diagonal is Tor-trivial
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and R → S' a morphism of almost algebras with Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 and Tor^{S'⊗_R S'}_i(S', S') = 0 for all i > 0 (S' ⊗_R S'-module structure via μ). Then L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 in D(S'_!!-Mod). In particular L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 for every weakly étale (hence every étale, every finite étale) morphism R → S'.
hypotheses: S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 gives, by P0/cotangent-flat-base-change, (S'⊗S')_!! ⊗ L_{S'/R} ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/S'} and (…⊗L) ⊕ (…⊗L) ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/R}.
Transitivity for R → S' ⊗_R S' → S' (P0/cotangent-transitivity): S'_!! ⊗ L_{S'⊗S'/R} ≅ L_{S'/R}; combined, L ⊕ L → L is an isomorphism that is the sum map, so L ≃ 0 (GR Theorem 2.5.36).
Weakly étale: S' is flat over R and over S' ⊗_R S', so both Tor conditions hold.
acceptance: Every idempotent quotient A → A/eA is weakly étale, so L_{(A/eA)/A} ≃ 0.
For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra the vanishing L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0 is of a different nature (Frobenius; Sch12 Proposition 5.13, PerfectoidSpaces:P1).

nodes.title: Square-zero extensions of almost algebras are classified by Ext¹ of the almost cotangent complex
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A → B a morphism of almost algebras and M a B-module. (i) Almostification Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) → Exal_A(B, M) is an equivalence of categories of square-zero extensions, inducing a group isomorphism on isomorphism classes, functorial in all arguments. (ii) There are natural isomorphisms Ext⁰_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Exal_A(B, M) ≅ Ext¹_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext¹_B(L^a_{B/A}, M). (iii) For an epimorphism A → B with kernel I, Hom_B(I/I², M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M) via pullback of 0 → I/I² → A/I² → B → 0.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A-extensions of B by M are short exact sequences 0 → M → E → B → 0 in A-Mod with E an A-algebra, M a square-zero ideal with its given B-module structure (GR 2.5.2–2.5.7).
proofSteps: (i): send X = (0 → I → E → B → 0) to X_! = (0 → I_! → E_!! → B_!! → 0), right exact, and push out along I_! → I_* (GR Lemma 2.5.17, Remark 2.5.19); the category is additive by the Baer-sum construction on ExalC (GR 2.5.5–2.5.6) and (2.5.15).

(ii): Ext⁰ via Illusie II.1.2.4.2 and Lemma 2.5.28 (GR Proposition 2.5.29); Ext¹ via Illusie III.1.2.3 applied to Ã_!! → B̃_!! and (i) (GR Theorem 2.5.30); the almost form via (3.2.8), which uses GR Proposition 2.5.42 and Lemma 2.4.14(i).
(iii): GR Lemma 3.2.1 (factor the structure map through A/I²).
acceptance: For the trivial extension B ⊕ M, the class is 0; for A → B = A/I with I² = 0 the extension A itself corresponds to 1_{I}.
In Sch12 Theorem 5.11 these groups classify deformations of perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras.

nodes.title: Local flatness criterion for square-zero thickenings, honest and almost
nodes.statement: (i) (classical) Let R be a ring, J ⊆ R an ideal with J² = 0, R' = R/J, and M an R-module; put M' = M/JM. Then M is R-flat iff M' is R'-flat and the natural map u(M) : J ⊗_{R'} M' → JM (x ⊗ m' ↦ xm) is an isomorphism. (ii) (almost) Let S be a basic setup and f̃ : B̃ → C̃ a morphism of A-extensions 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0 and 0 → J → C → C₀ → 0 (I² = J² = 0) whose square is cofibred (C₀ ≅ C ⊗_B B₀). Then B → C is flat iff B₀ → C₀ is flat and C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: J² = 0 (nilpotent of order two; the general nilpotent case follows by induction).
proofSteps: (i) Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 22.3 ((1)⇔(3) for a nilpotent ideal), as recalled by GR (3.2.19): ⇒ tensor 0 → J → R → R' → 0 with M; ⇐ show Tor_1^R(N, M) = 0 for all N by dévissage 0 → JN → N → N/JN → 0 to R'-modules N', where Tor_1^R(N', M) is controlled by u(M) and flatness of M'.

(ii) Apply (i) to the ring map B_!! → C_!! and almost elements, using exactness of (−)^a, (−)_! and the Tor comparison of P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion (GR Lemma 3.2.6: 'the almost version of the local flatness criterion').
acceptance: For R = k[ε]/(ε²), M = R: M' = k flat and u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → εR bijective; for M = k: u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → 0 not injective, and k is not flat over R.
Used in P0/almost-deformation-theory to identify flat deformations with extensions by C₀ ⊗ I.

nodes.title: Flat square-zero deformations of almost algebras: obstruction, torsor, automorphisms
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ = (0 → I → B → B₀ → 0) an A-extension (I² = 0) and f₀ : B₀ → C₀ a flat morphism of almost algebras. Let ω(B̃, f₀) := ∂(I → C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ∈ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I), ∂ the boundary of the transitivity sequence for B → B₀ → C₀. Then (i) ω(B̃, f₀) = 0 iff there is a flat deformation of C₀ over B, i.e. a B-extension C̃ = (0 → C₀ ⊗ I → C → C₀ → 0) with C flat over B and C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀; (ii) if ω = 0, the isomorphism classes of flat deformations form a torsor under Exal_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext¹_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I); (iii) the automorphism group of a flat deformation (acting trivially on C₀ and on C₀ ⊗ I) is Der_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I). More generally (GR Proposition 3.2.9) for any B₀-linear u : I → J the obstruction ω(B̃, f₀, u) = v_! ∘ ω(B̃, f₀) governs extensions C̃ with kernel J.
hypotheses: S a basic setup (m̃ flat); I² = 0; f₀ flat.
Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 5.11 cites GR Proposition 3.2.9 (same number in arXiv v3).
proofSteps: Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀ gives Exal_{B₀}(C₀, J) → Exal_B(C₀, J) → Hom_{B₀}(I, J) →∂ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, J) (P0/cotangent-transitivity, P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison, GR Lemma 3.2.1).
Obstruction, torsor and automorphisms as in Illusie III.2.1.2.3, applied through the almost Exal/Ext dictionary (GR Proposition 3.2.9).

Flatness of the deformation: by P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion, C is flat over B with C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀ iff its kernel is C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I via (3.2.5), which is the choice u = (I → C₀ ⊗ I) (GR 3.2.10, Corollary 3.2.11).
acceptance: If L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ 0 (e.g. C₀ étale over B₀, or a perfectoid (K°/ϖ)^a-algebra over (K°/ϖ)^a) then a flat deformation exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; Sch12 Theorem 5.10 applies this over (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a.
For A = B = B₀ ⊕ I trivial and C₀ = B₀[X] (almost polynomial), the trivial deformation C₀ ⊕ C₀ ⊗ I exists and deformations form a torsor under Ext¹(L^a, −) = 0.

nodes.title: Lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions of almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ an A-extension 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0, and C̃ⁱ = (0 → Jⁱ → Cⁱ → C₀ⁱ → 0), i = 1, 2, A-extensions with morphisms f̃ⁱ : B̃ → C̃ⁱ, together with v : J¹ → J² and g₀ : C₀¹ → C₀² such that u² = v ∘ u¹ and f₀² = g₀ ∘ f₀¹. The class v_* e(C̃¹) − e(C̃²) ∗ g₀ ∈ Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) is the obstruction to a morphism of A-extensions g̃ : C̃¹ → C̃² over v and g₀ with f̃² = g̃ ∘ f̃¹; when it vanishes, such g̃ form a torsor under Der_{B₀}(C₀¹, J²) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀²}(C₀² ⊗ L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²). In particular, if C and C' are flat over B with reductions C₀, C₀' and f₀ : C₀ → C₀', the obstruction to lifting f₀ lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I) and lifts form a torsor under Hom(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; I² = 0.
proofSteps: The classes e(C̃ⁱ) ∈ Ext¹(L^a_{C₀ⁱ/B}, Jⁱ) come from P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison; the problem is solvable iff v_*C̃¹ and C̃² ∗ g₀ coincide.
Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀¹ shows the difference lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) (GR (3.2.15)); conclude as in Illusie III.2.2.2 (GR Proposition 3.2.16).
acceptance: Sch12 Theorem 5.12 (almost version) is the flat case; with L^a ≃ 0 it gives unique lifting of morphisms, the full faithfulness in Sch12 Theorem 5.10.
For C₀ étale over B₀: morphisms lift uniquely (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (i)).

nodes.title: Étale almost algebras lift uniquely along nilpotent ideals
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a nilpotent ideal, A' := A/I. (i) For B weakly étale over A, C any A-algebra and J ⊆ C nilpotent, Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C) → Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C/J) is bijective. (ii) B ↦ A' ⊗_A B is an equivalence from weakly étale A-algebras to weakly étale A'-algebras; (iii) it restricts to an equivalence of étale algebras A-Ét ≃ A'-Ét and (iv) to an equivalence of finite étale algebras A_fet ≃ A'_fet (étale and almost finitely presented).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; I nilpotent (induction reduces to I² = 0).
proofSteps: (i): I² = 0 by induction; lifts of morphisms are governed by Ext^{1,0}(L^a_{B/A}, −) (P0/almost-morphism-lifting), and L_{B/A} ≃ 0 for B weakly étale (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).

(ii): a weakly étale B' over A' has a unique flat lift B (P0/almost-deformation-theory with L ≃ 0); B is weakly étale: μ_{B'/A'} is weakly étale, lifts to a flat μ̃ : B ⊗_A B → C, and by (i) C ≅ B compatibly, so B is B ⊗_A B-flat (GR proof of Theorem 3.2.18(ii)).
(iii): if B' is étale, I_{B'/A'} is an étale B' ⊗ B'-algebra (Corollary 3.1.9), lifts, and B ⊗_A B ≅ C ⊕ B, so B is almost projective over B ⊗_A B.
(iv): an étale B with A' ⊗_A B almost finitely presented is almost finitely presented (GR Lemma 3.2.25(iii), Tor^A_1(A', B) = 0 by flatness) (GR Theorem 3.2.28(ii)).
acceptance: A = (K°/ϖ^n)^a, I = ϖ^{n−1}A: finite étale (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a-algebras lift uniquely to (K°/ϖ^n)^a; this is the finite-level step of GR Theorem 5.3.27.
In the classical setup (iii) is SGA 1 I.8.3 in GR's generality of étale (not necessarily finitely presented) algebras.

nodes.title: B ↦ B_!! preserves and reflects faithful flatness, but not flatness
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is faithfully flat iff φ is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (ii) φ is a monomorphism iff φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is injective, and B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! is flat over A_!! iff B/A is flat over A. (iii) Hence φ is faithfully flat iff φ_!! is a faithfully flat ring map. (iv) Flatness is not preserved: for S = ofValuationRing V with residue field k, the flat projection V^a × V^a → V^a becomes V ×_k V → V under (−)_!!, which is not flat.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; m̃ flat is used in (ii) through GR Proposition 2.4.35.
proofSteps: (i): GR Lemma 3.1.2(vi), Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0 in A-Mod.

(ii): the kernel of φ_!! is (ker φ)_! and (−)_! reflects zero; B_!!/Im A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! (both are cokernels of V ⊕ (−)_! modulo the same ideal); (−)_! takes flat modules to flat modules and back (GR Proposition 2.4.35, Remark 3.1.3(ii)).
(iii): apply (i) to φ and the classical criterion to φ_!!.
(iv): (V^a × V^a)_!! = V ×_k V (fibre product of rings over the residue field) and V ×_k V → V is not flat (GR Remark 3.1.3(ii)).
acceptance: For φ = identity, φ_!! is the identity.
Bhatt Remark 4.2.8(2): (−)_!! preserves faithful flatness but may not preserve flatness.
