nodes.title: Faithfully flat descent for almost modules and almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is of effective descent for modules: M ↦ (B ⊗_A M, can) is an equivalence from A-Mod to the category Desc(B/A) of B-modules N with a B ⊗_A B-linear isomorphism β : p₂*N ≅ p₁*N satisfying the cocycle condition p₁₂*(β) ∘ p₂₃*(β) = p₁₃*(β); (ii) the same holds for A-algebras; (iii) both statements are stable under base change A → A' (universal effective descent); (iv) under (i) the full subcategories of flat, almost finitely generated, almost finitely presented and almost finite projective modules correspond, and under (ii) those of weakly étale, étale and finite étale algebras correspond; (v) almost projectivity descends when B is almost finitely presented over A (for general faithfully flat φ this is not asserted: GR Remark 3.2.26(iii) leaves it open).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness).
proofSteps: φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is a faithfully flat ring map (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness).

Classical descent: extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`); the identification of comonad coalgebras with descent data (cocycle and uniqueness), and descent for algebras, is Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 0E (request).

Transport: a descent datum (N, β) over B/A gives (N_!, β_!) over B_!!/A_!! because (−)_! commutes with tensor products (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom) and (B ⊗_A B)_!! ≅ B_!! ⊗_{A_!!} B_!!; descend to an A_!!-module and almostify; A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_!!) via A ≅ (A_!!)^a (P0/change-of-basic-setup).

(iv): descent of flatness, almost finite generation and presentation (GR Remark 3.2.26(ii)), of almost finite projectivity (Remark 3.2.26(iii) with P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), of (weakly) étale algebras (GR 3.4.1, P0/etale-morphisms-stability (viii)).
(v): GR Remark 3.2.26(iv) via Lemma 2.4.31(i) and Proposition 2.4.18(ii).
acceptance: For V-algebras R → R' with R' faithfully flat, the almostification of Grothendieck's descent is (i) for R^a → R'^a.
DiamondsAndVStacks:D3: with (S⁺/ϖ)^a faithfully flat over (R⁺/ϖ)^a (automatic flatness), the descent datum on (S̃⁺/ϖ)^a descends to an almost (R⁺/ϖ)^a-algebra.

nodes.title: The Amitsur complex of an almost faithfully flat map is exact
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras and M an A-module. The augmented Amitsur complex 0 → M → M ⊗_A B → M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B → ⋯ (differentials the alternating sums of the coface maps) is exact in A-Mod. In honest terms: for V-algebras R → R' such that R'^a is faithfully flat over R^a (e.g. Tor_i^R(X, R') almost zero for i > 0 and X ⊗_R R' almost zero only if X is), and any R-module N, the cohomology of 0 → N → N ⊗_R R' → N ⊗_R R' ⊗_R R' → ⋯ is almost zero; in particular N^a is the equalizer of (N ⊗ R')^a ⇉ (N ⊗ R' ⊗ R')^a.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat.
proofSteps: After base change along φ the complex acquires a contracting homotopy (the extra degeneracy from the multiplication B ⊗_A B → B).
B ⊗_A − is exact and faithful on A-Mod, hence reflects exactness of complexes.

Honest form: (−)^a is exact, so cohomology of the honest complex almostifies to the cohomology of the almost complex; P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion translates the Tor hypotheses into faithful flatness of R'^a.
acceptance: DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions: R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ ⇉ S⁺/ϖ ⊗ S⁺/ϖ is almost exact (ECD Proposition 8.8 uses the honest faithfully flat version for totally disconnected X).
For A → A × A (faithfully flat, split) the Amitsur complex is split exact.

nodes.title: Tight ideals, the Jacobson radical and henselian pairs of almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. An ideal I ⊆ A is tight if there are a finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m and n ∈ ℕ with Iⁿ ⊆ m₀·A (GR Definition 5.1.5); for ϖ ∈ m the ideal ϖA is tight. The Jacobson radical of A is rad(A) := rad(A_*)^a (GR 5.1.1); for a V-algebra R and an ideal J ⊆ R, J^a ⊆ rad(R^a) iff mJ ⊆ rad(R) (GR Lemma 5.1.2). A pair (A, I) with I ⊆ rad(A) is henselian if (A_*, m·I_*) is a henselian pair (Mathlib `HenselianRing A_* (m·I_*)`), and tight henselian if moreover I is tight (GR Definition 5.1.8); (R^a, J^a) is henselian iff (R, mJ) is (GR Lemma 5.1.10). If A is I-adically complete (A → lim A/Iⁿ an isomorphism), (A, I) is henselian (GR Remark 5.3.7).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; ideals of A are subobjects I ↪ A stable under multiplication, with powers Iⁿ the images of I^{⊗n}.
proofSteps: Define IsTight via Submodule.FG subideals of m and the ideal m₀·A.

nodes.title: Almost Nakayama lemma for tight ideals
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ rad(A) a tight ideal. (i) If M is an almost finitely generated A-module with IM = M, then M = 0. (ii) If φ : N → M is a morphism of almost finite projective A-modules such that φ ⊗_A A/I is an isomorphism, then φ is an isomorphism. (iii) If M is almost finitely generated and M ⊗_A A/I = 0 then M = 0.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; I tight (Iⁿ ⊆ m₀A) and I ⊆ rad(A).
proofSteps: (i): pick a finitely generated Q with m₀M ⊆ Q ⊆ M; then M = IⁿM ⊆ m₀M ⊆ Q, so M = Q is finitely generated; for a finitely generated A_*-submodule M₀ with M₀^a = M one gets m₀M₀ ⊆ mI_*·m₀M₀, and mI_* ⊆ rad(A_*) (GR Lemma 5.1.2), so m₀M₀ = 0 by Nakayama, whence mM₀ = 0 and M = 0 (GR proof of Lemma 5.1.6).

(ii): Coker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 and Coker φ almost finitely generated (GR Lemma 2.3.17(i)) give Coker φ = 0; then Ker φ is almost finitely generated (Lemma 2.3.17(ii), M almost finitely presented) and Ker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 by flatness of M, so Ker φ = 0 (GR Corollary 5.1.7).
(iii) is (i) since M ⊗ A/I = M/IM.
acceptance: For A = K°a (K perfectoid), I = ϖA: an almost finitely generated M with M = ϖM is zero; the hypothesis 'almost finitely generated' is needed, since K = K°[1/ϖ] satisfies K = ϖK.

nodes.title: Idempotents lift uniquely along tight henselian pairs
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup and (A, I) a tight henselian pair of almost algebras (e.g. A I-adically complete with I tight). Then A → A/I induces a bijection from the idempotents of A_* to the idempotents of (A/I)_*.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; (A, I) tight henselian.
proofSteps: If m̃ has homological dimension ≤ 1: (A_*, I_*) is henselian (GR Corollary 5.1.16), so idempotents of A_* and A_*/I_* correspond; an idempotent almost element of A/I lifts to an almost element of A because the obstruction in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, I) dies in Ext¹(V^a, I) coming from Ext¹(V^a, Iⁿ) for n large (Claim 5.1.19, using Ext²(V^a, −) = 0 from Lemma 2.4.14), and liftings of idempotents along nilpotent thickenings are unique (GR Proposition 2.5.13(i)).

General m: write m as a filtered union of subideals m_λ with m_λ² = m_λ and m̃_λ flat of homological dimension ≤ 1 (GR Theorem 2.1.12), apply the first case to each (V, m_λ) and glue the unique lifts (GR proof of Proposition 5.1.17).
acceptance: For A = (V⟦X⟧)^a and I = XA: idempotents of A_* and of (A/I)_* = (V^a)_* = V_*-idempotents agree.
Used with the rank decomposition to lift the decomposition A/ϖ = ∏ Ā_i to A (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).

nodes.title: Almost finite projective modules over I-adically complete almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism, A_n := A/I^{n+1}. Then M ↦ (M ⊗_A A_n)_n is an equivalence from almost finite projective A-modules to compatible systems (M_n) of almost finite projective A_n-modules (M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n), with quasi-inverse (M_n) ↦ lim_n M_n; in particular P ≅ lim_n P ⊗_A A_n for every almost finite projective P. Moreover an I-c-adic A-module whose reduction M_0 is almost finitely generated is almost finitely generated with M ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete (GR's conditions (a), (b) of Lemma 5.3.5 for A_n = A/I^{n+1}).
proofSteps: Topological modules over A∞ with I-c-adic topology correspond to compatible systems (GR Lemma 5.3.16).

Almost finite generation of lim M_n from M_0 almost finitely generated and I tight: find almost elements whose images generate modulo m₀ at level n+1, then I^{n+1}M ⊆ N and N is closed (GR Lemmas 5.3.17, 5.3.18).
Almost projectivity of lim M_n: a topologically almost split surjection from the completed free module and ε-factorisations (GR Lemma 5.3.20).

Full faithfulness: P → lim P ⊗ A_n is an isomorphism, first for P = A^r, then for P almost finite projective via ε-factorisations P → Aⁿ → P (GR Claim 5.3.25, P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).
acceptance: For A = K°a, I = ϖA: almost finite projective K°a-modules are the limits of compatible almost finite projective (K°/ϖ^n)^a-modules.

nodes.title: Unramifiedness lifts from the reduction modulo a tight ideal
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A I-adically complete (A ≅ lim_n A/I^{n+1}). (i) For ideals I, J and φ : A → B: if φ ⊗ A/I and φ ⊗ A/J are unramified then so is φ ⊗ A/IJ. (ii) If B is an almost finite projective A-algebra such that B/IB is unramified over A/I, then B is unramified over A. (iii) More generally, for I ⊆ rad(A) tight and B almost finite over A with B/IB unramified over A/I, B is unramified over A.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete for (ii).
proofSteps: (i): reduce to IJ = 0; B is B ⊗_A B-flat by the Tor base change (Claim 5.2.13), and almost projective by the 2-cartesian square of almost projective modules over B ⊗ B/(I' ∩ J') (GR Proposition 3.4.21) and Lemma 3.2.25(i) (GR proof of Theorem 5.2.12(ii)).

(ii): by (i) with J = Iⁿ, each B_n := B/I^{n+1}B is unramified over A_n; the diagonal idempotents e_n (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation) are compatible by uniqueness and define an idempotent of lim (B_n ⊗ B_n)_* = (B ⊗_A B)_* (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, Claim 5.3.25); μ = lim μ_n and I_{B/A} = lim I_{B_n/A_n} give conditions (ii), (iii) of the characterisation (GR Claim 5.3.29).

(iii): Ω_{B/A} is almost finitely generated with Ω ⊗ A/I = 0, so Ω = 0 (P0/almost-nakayama); then I_{B/A} is idempotent and locally generated by idempotents after inverting generators of m₀ and modulo m₀ (GR Corollary 5.2.15 via Theorem 5.2.12(iv) and Theorem 5.2.4).
acceptance: For A = K°a and B = L°a (L/K finite étale), unramifiedness of L°a/K°a follows from that of (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

nodes.title: Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely modulo a tight ideal of a complete almost algebra
nodes.statement: Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal such that A is I-adically complete (A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism). Then B ↦ B ⊗_A A/I is an equivalence of categories A_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet, with quasi-inverse B₀ ↦ lim_n B_n, where B_n is the unique finite étale A/I^{n+1}-algebra lifting B₀. In particular, for ϖ ∈ m and A ϖ-adically complete, A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet; this is Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over an arbitrary basic setup (Sch12 states it for S = (K°, K°°) and A flat over K°a). Complements: if A is flat over V^a then every B ∈ A_fet is flat over V^a and ϖ-adically complete (P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete); for root setups B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B/ϖB is over A/ϖ (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).
hypotheses: S a basic setup (m̃ flat, needed for the cotangent complex behind the nilpotent lifting).
I tight (e.g. I = ϖA with ϖ ∈ m) and A I-adically complete; flatness of A over V^a is not needed for the equivalence itself.
Sch12 cites GR Theorem 5.3.27 (same number in the book and in arXiv v3).
proofSteps: Finite levels: A_{n+1} → A_n has nilpotent kernel, so A_{n+1,fet} ≃ A_{n,fet} (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (iv)); hence 2-lim_n (A_n)_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet (GR proof of Theorem 5.3.27).

Passage to the limit: for a compatible system (B_n), B := lim B_n is almost finite projective over A with B ⊗ A_n ≅ B_n (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules), unramified (P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction (ii)), hence étale (almost projective ⇒ flat) and almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), i.e. B ∈ A_fet.
Full faithfulness: Hom_A(B, C) = lim_n Hom_{A_n}(B_n, C_n) because C ≅ lim C_n (Claim 5.3.25) and morphisms of finite étale algebras lift uniquely at each finite level.
acceptance: S = (K°, K°°), A = K°a, ϖ ∈ K°°: K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet, the middle link in K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet (Sch12 §4).
A finite étale (A/ϖ)-algebra has exactly one finite étale lift to A, up to unique isomorphism.

nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is ϖ-adically complete (B ≅ lim_n B/ϖⁿB), and if A is flat over V^a then so is B.

nodes.title: Uniform finite projectivity of a finite étale algebra can be checked modulo ϖ (root setups)
nodes.statement: Let S be the root setup of (ϖ_n) (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup), ϖ = ϖ_0, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is uniformly almost finitely generated over A with bound r iff B/ϖB is uniformly almost finitely generated over A/ϖ with bound r; hence B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B ⊗_A A/ϖ is uniformly finite projective over A/ϖ. (Sch12 Theorem 4.17, last sentence, over (K°, K°°); in a general basic setup no source proves the reverse implication.)
hypotheses: S a root setup (used to find, for each k, elements ϖ_{k+1} and t = ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} with ϖ = ϖ_{k+1}²·t); A ϖ-adically complete; B finite étale over A.
proofSteps: ⇒: base change preserves uniform bounds (GR Lemma 2.3.7(v)).

⇐: fix k ≥ 1 and δ := ϖ_{k+1}. Choose φ̄ : (A/ϖ)^r → B/ϖB with cokernel killed by δ, and lift δ·φ̄ to φ : A^r → B (almost elements lift up to multiplication by δ, P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); then δ²B ⊆ φ(A^r) + ϖB.
Let C := coker φ, an almost finitely generated A-module; δ²C ⊆ ϖC = t·δ²C with t := ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} ∈ m (p^{k+1} ≥ 3 for k ≥ 1), so M := δ²C satisfies M = tM.

tA is tight (t ∈ m) and contained in rad(A) because t^{p^{k+1}} ∈ ϖA and A is ϖ-adically complete; M is almost finitely generated, so M = 0 by P0/almost-nakayama; hence δ² = ϖ_{k+1}² kills coker φ, and so does ϖ_k (a multiple of ϖ_{k+1}²).

Every ε ∈ m is a multiple of some ϖ_k, so for every ε there is A^r → B with cokernel killed by ε: B is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound r (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion, condition (A)).
acceptance: Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over (K°, K°°) with ϖ having compatible p-power roots; used by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for 'S°a is uniformly finite projective over R°a'.

nodes.title: ϖ-adic completeness of an almost module and of its almost elements
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, and M an almost V-module whose almost elements M_* have no ϖ-torsion. Then: (i) (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿM_* for all n; (ii) M_*/ϖⁿM_* → (M/ϖⁿM)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel; (iii) M is ϖ-adically complete (M → lim_n M/ϖⁿM an isomorphism in Almost.Module S) iff M_* is ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) M_*`); the comparison lim M_*/ϖⁿ → lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* = (lim M/ϖⁿ)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel, the lim¹ of the almost zero cokernels being almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; M_* ϖ-torsion-free (for S = (K°, K°°) this is flatness of M, Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).
proofSteps: (i): ϖ is injective on M_* hence a monomorphism on M, so ϖⁿM ≅ M and (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿ M_*.
(ii): left exactness of (−)_* gives injectivity; the cokernel embeds in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M)[ϖⁿ], and Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M) is almost zero because V^a is almost projective (Bhatt proof of Lemma 4.4.1(3)).

(iii) ⇒: (−)_* commutes with limits, so M_* ≅ lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* ⊇ lim M_*/ϖⁿ with almost zero cokernel Q (lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero), and Q is killed by ϖ ∈ m; since M_* is ϖ-torsion-free, Bhatt Lemma 4.4.2 (for α injective between ϖ-torsion-free modules with ϖ-torsion cokernel, the source is complete iff the target is) shows M_* is complete.
(iii) ⇐: (−)^a preserves limits (it has a left adjoint (−)_! and a right adjoint), and M ≅ (M_*)^a.
acceptance: For S = (K°, K°°) this is Sch12 Lemma 5.3(iii)-(iv); for Bhatt's setup (R, I) and a finitely generated J, Bhatt Proposition 4.4.3 proves the analogue without torsion-freeness using derived completeness.
M = (K°/ϖ)^a is ϖ-adically complete but M_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ) has ϖ-torsion: the torsion-freeness hypothesis is not decorative for (i).

nodes.title: Complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ are almost exact, with the lim¹ term controlled
nodes.statement: Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m and C^• a cochain complex of V-modules (C^i = 0 for i < 0) such that every C^i is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete. If the cohomology of C^•/ϖC^• is almost zero in every degree, then: (i) H^i(C^•/ϖⁿC^•) is almost zero for all n ≥ 1 and all i; (ii) for every i there is an exact sequence 0 → lim¹_n H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) → H^i(C^•) → lim_n H^i(C^•/ϖⁿ) → 0 (Milnor sequence of the tower C^• = lim_n C^•/ϖⁿ, whose transition maps are termwise surjective), and both outer terms are almost zero, so H^i(C^•) is almost zero; (iii) C^•[1/ϖ] is exact. Neither the torsion-freeness nor the completeness can be dropped, and the lim¹ term is not discarded: it is almost zero because every H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) is.
hypotheses: S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; C^i ϖ-torsion-free (for exactness of 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} → C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0) and ϖ-adically complete (C^i = lim C^i/ϖⁿ).
proofSteps: (i): torsion-freeness makes 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} →·ϖ C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0 exact; the long exact cohomology sequence (Mathlib `ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`) and closure of almost zero modules under extensions (P0/almost-zero-serre-class) give induction on n.

(ii): completeness and surjectivity of transitions give the short exact sequence of complexes 0 → C^• → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → 0 (second map (x_n) ↦ (x_n − x̄_{n+1})); its long exact cohomology sequence, with H^i(∏_n −) = ∏_n H^i(−) for modules, is the Milnor sequence.
Products, lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), so H^i(C^•) is an extension of almost zero modules.
(iii): localisation at ϖ is exact and kills almost zero modules (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
acceptance: Non-example for completeness: C^0 = V[1/ϖ] (torsion-free, not ϖ-adically separated), C^i = 0 otherwise: C/ϖ = 0 is exact, but H^0(C) = V[1/ϖ] is not almost zero.

nodes.title: Almost sheaves, almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech complexes on a site
nodes.statement: Let (C, J) be a site and S = (V, m) a basic setup. For a sheaf F of V-modules on (C, J) (Mathlib `Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)`): F is almost zero if m·F(U) = 0 for all U; almost zero sheaves form a Serre class of the abelian category of sheaves, and the Serre localization Almost.Sheaf J S is the category of sheaves of almost V-modules (GR 3.3.1–3.3.2: a basic setup relative to the topos of (C, J)), with exact localization F ↦ F^a. For X ∈ C and n ≥ 0 the cohomology H^n(X, F) of the underlying abelian sheaf (Mathlib `Sheaf.H'`) is a V-module through the action of V on F, and its almostification H^n(X, F)^a ∈ Almost.Module S depends only on F^a (almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology); F is almost acyclic on X if H^n(X, F)^a = 0 for n > 0. For a family 𝔘 = (U_i → X) the Čech complex Č(𝔘, F) (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` on the underlying presheaf) is a complex of V-modules with almostification Č(𝔘, F)^a, and the augmented complex F(X) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact if its cohomology is almost zero. The Čech-to-derived comparison for almost acyclic bases is P0/almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion.
hypotheses: (C, J) a site whose category of sheaves of V-modules is abelian with enough injectives (Mathlib `sheafIsAbelian`, `HasSheafify`); S a basic setup.
proofSteps: Almost zero sheaves: m·F = 0 is closed under subsheaves, quotient sheaves (sheafification preserves m-torsion: m kills the presheaf quotient, hence its sheafification) and extensions (m² = m), so it is a Serre class.
V-action on cohomology: each v ∈ V acts on F by an endomorphism of sheaves, hence on H^n(X, F) by functoriality (`Sheaf.H.map`), making H^n(X, F) a V-module; if m·F = 0 then ε acts by zero on H^n.
Almost Čech complex: apply cechComplexFunctor to the presheaf of V-modules and then toAlmost S termwise.
Relative basic setup: Almost.Sheaf J S is equivalent to sheaves on (C, J) with values in almost modules computed through (−)_* (GR 3.3.2: M_* is a sheaf).
acceptance: On the one-point site, Almost.Sheaf J S ≃ Almost.Module S and almost cohomology vanishes in positive degrees.
For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and F = O⁺_X (a sheaf of R⁺-modules for the setup (R⁺, root ideal)), PerfectoidSpaces:P2 proves H^n(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for n > 0.

nodes.title: Almost Čech acyclicity on a basis implies almost acyclicity
nodes.statement: Let (C, J) be a site, S a basic setup, F a sheaf of V-modules, and 𝔅 a full subcategory of C stable under fibre products such that every covering of an object of 𝔅 is refined by a covering by objects of 𝔅 (e.g. rational subsets of an affinoid adic space with finite rational covers, or affinoid perfectoid objects of a pro-étale or v-site). If for every U ∈ 𝔅 and every covering 𝔘 of U by objects of 𝔅 the augmented Čech complex F(U) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact, then H^n(U, F) is almost zero for all U ∈ 𝔅 and n > 0 (and H^0(U, F) = F(U)).
hypotheses: S a basic setup; 𝔅 as stated; F a sheaf of V-modules.
proofSteps: Almostify DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison: the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence Ȟ^p(𝔘, H^q(F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, F) is a spectral sequence of V-modules; the exact functor toAlmost S carries it to a spectral sequence in Almost.Module S.

Induction on n (Cartan's argument, ECD proof of Proposition 8.8): suppose H^q(V, F)^a = 0 for 0 < q < n and all V ∈ 𝔅; for α ∈ H^n(U, F) and ε ∈ m choose a covering 𝔘 by objects of 𝔅 on which α dies (locality of cohomology); the spectral sequence and the almost exactness of the Čech complexes of 𝔘 and of its fibre products show ε·α = 0.
acceptance: Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4 and Sch12 Proposition 6.14: almost exact Čech complexes of O⁺ for finite rational covers of a perfectoid affinoid give H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for i > 0.
In the classical setup this is Cartan's lemma on acyclic bases (D0).

nodes.title: Perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1), perfectoid algebras and perfectoid Tate pairs
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. Let R be a commutative topological ring which is a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing), complete and Hausdorff, with power-bounded subring R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring). For a commutative ring A and ideals I, J ⊆ A with p ∈ J and x^p ∈ J for every x ∈ I, write Φ: A/I → A/J for the ring homomorphism x mod I ↦ x^p mod J (ECD §3 notational convention). R is a perfectoid Tate ring if (a) R is uniform, i.e. R° is a bounded subset of R (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded), and (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ of R (a topologically nilpotent unit, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer; necessarily ϖ ∈ R°) such that ϖ^p divides p in R° and Φ: R°/ϖR° → R°/ϖ^pR° is bijective. No perfectoid base field is fixed; characteristic 0 and characteristic p are both allowed (for pR = 0 the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous), and p may be a nonzero nonunit (e.g. in a product K × K♭). A perfectoid R-algebra is a perfectoid Tate ring S with a continuous ring homomorphism R → S; morphisms are continuous R-algebra homomorphisms. A perfectoid Tate pair is a Huber pair (R, R+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair) with R perfectoid; the condition depends only on R (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).
hypotheses: Completeness includes separatedness (anchor convention): CompleteSpace R and T2Space R, with the uniform structure of the topological additive group.
Uniformity is boundedness of R° in R (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the uniformity of anchor Layer 4.2); it is not implied by (b) (test IsPerfectoidTateRing.not_of_not_uniform).
The divisibility ϖ^p | p holds in R°, not merely in R; together with (b) it cannot be replaced by surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p alone (ℚ_p, ECD Remark 3.3).
proofSteps: Φ is well defined and additive: for i ∈ I, (x + i)^p − x^p ∈ (p, i^p) ⊆ J, and (x + y)^p − x^p − y^p ∈ pA ⊆ J by divisibility of the binomial coefficients.
A pseudo-uniformizer ϖ lies in R°, and in every ring of integral elements R+ (ECD §3 preamble; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).

The listed equivalent formulations (Berkeley 6.1.1, Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.1, Kedlaya AWS 2.1.1, BMS1 "Fontaine's sense") agree by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer and P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring.
acceptance: ℚ_p^cycl (ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1), the completed perfection of F_p((t)) (ϖ = t), ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and the non-field ring ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ECD Example 3.4) are perfectoid Tate rings (P1/perfectoid-examples).
ℚ_p is a complete uniform Tate ring whose Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective, and it is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).

nodes.title: Rings of integral elements of a complete uniform Tate ring are ϖ-adically and p-adically complete
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements; R+ = R° allowed) and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then (a) the subspace topology of R+ is the ϖ-adic topology and R+ is ϖ-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {ϖ}) R+); (b) ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R+ and R = R+[1/ϖ]; (c) if ϖ divides p in R+, then R+ is p-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+); (d) if R ≠ 0 and p is topologically nilpotent in R, then p is not a unit of R+. In particular, for R ≠ 0 perfectoid, R+ satisfies the hypotheses [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+)] and [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+] of Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta.
hypotheses: R complete and Hausdorff; uniformity is used to know that R+ ⊆ R° is bounded.
proofSteps: (a) R+ is open, hence closed, hence complete; it is bounded, so by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero (for any pair of definition (A_0, I)) the open sets ϖ^nR+ are cofinal among the neighbourhoods ϖ^nA_0 of 0; completeness plus Hausdorffness give IsAdicComplete.
(b) ϖ is a unit of R; for x ∈ R, ϖ^nx → 0, so ϖ^nx ∈ R+ for n large because R+ is open.
(c) (p) ⊆ (ϖ) are finitely generated ideals of R+, so ϖ-adic completeness implies p-adic completeness (Stacks Tag 090T; the same step in BMS1 §3.1).
(d) If p were a unit of R+, then p^{-n} ∈ R+ (bounded) and p^n → 0 would give 1 = p^{-n}p^n → 0, so 1 lies in the closure of 0 and R = 0.
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K° (or an open valuation subring K+) this is the ϖ-adic and p-adic completeness of K+ used in Sch12 Lemma 3.4.
For R = ℚ_p and R+ = ℤ_p with ϖ = p: ℤ_p is p-adically complete (the lemma needs no perfectoid hypothesis).

nodes.title: Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the pseudo-uniformizer condition kept
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ R° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in R°. The following are equivalent: (i) Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective (every element of R°/ϖ^p is a p-th power); (ii) Frobenius on R°/p is surjective; (iii) every element of R°/ϖpR° is a p-th power. The same equivalences hold for any ring of integral elements R+ in place of R° when ϖ ∈ R+ and ϖ^p | p in R+. The divisibility hypothesis is essential: surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p without any ϖ with ϖ^p | p does not give perfectoidness (ℚ_p), and surjectivity of the Frobenius endomorphism of R°/ϖ is weaker than (i) (ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p}, Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).
hypotheses: ϖ^p | p in R° is a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
R° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).
proofSteps: (iii) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (i): ϖpR° ⊆ pR° ⊆ ϖ^pR°, so surjectivity passes to coarser quotients.

(i) ⇒ (iii): by successive ϖ^p-adic approximation using (i), every x ∈ R° is a convergent sum x = x_0^p + ϖ^px_1^p + ϖ^{2p}x_2^p + ⋯ with x_i ∈ R° (R° is ϖ-adically complete); then x ≡ (x_0 + ϖx_1 + ϖ²x_2 + ⋯)^p modulo pϖR°, since every mixed term of the p-th power is divisible by p and by ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.9 (iii) ⇒ (i)).
For R+ the same argument applies to the ϖ-adically complete ring R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).
acceptance: ℚ_p: Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is surjective, but no pseudo-uniformizer ϖ has ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p, so the criterion does not apply and ℚ_p is not perfectoid.
ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p} (ϖ^p = p): Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/ϖ = F_p is surjective, but Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/p = F_p[ϖ]/(ϖ^p) is not (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).

sources.match: The successive ϖ^p-adic approximation argument (i) ⇒ (ii).
The equivalence of the three surjectivity conditions for a π-adically complete ring with π^p | p.
The three conditions verbatim.
The easy direction (ii) ⇒ (i).
Surjectivity modulo p descends to smaller quotients, and the converse fails without a condition like ϖ^p | p.
The existence of the ideal of definition I with p ∈ I^p (here ϖ with ϖ^p | p) is a genuine condition that excludes (ℚ_p, ℤ_p).

nodes.title: Injectivity of Frobenius is automatic and the perfectoid condition is independent of the pseudo-uniformizer
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. (a) For every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R°, Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is injective. (b) If R is moreover uniform, then for pseudo-uniformizers ϖ, ϖ' with ϖ^p | p and ϖ'^p | p in R°, Φ is bijective for ϖ iff it is bijective for ϖ'; equivalently R is perfectoid iff there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius on R°/p is surjective, and then Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective for every such ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; Berkeley Remark 6.1.3). (c) The same holds for a ring of integral elements R+ in place of R°: if ϖ ∈ R+, ϖ^p | p in R+ and x ∈ R+ with x^p ∈ ϖ^pR+, then x ∈ ϖR+.
hypotheses: (a) and (c) use only that R° (resp. R+) is integrally closed in R and ϖ is a unit of R; (b) uses uniformity and completeness through P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion.
proofSteps: (a) If x ∈ R° and x^p = ϖ^py with y ∈ R°, then (x/ϖ)^p = y, so x/ϖ ∈ R is integral over R° and lies in R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral), i.e. x ∈ ϖR° (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof).
(c) Same argument with the integrally closed R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
(b) By (a), bijectivity of Φ for ϖ is its surjectivity, which by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion is equivalent to surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p, a condition independent of ϖ.
acceptance: In ℚ_p^cycl, ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1 and ϖ' = ζ_{p³} − 1 both satisfy ϖ^p | p, and Φ is bijective for both.
In ℂ_p the conditions for ϖ = p^{1/p} and ϖ' = p^{1/p²} coincide.

nodes.title: Uniform (in particular perfectoid) Tate rings are reduced
nodes.statement: A Hausdorff uniform Tate ring R is reduced; in particular every perfectoid Tate ring is reduced (Sch12 Proposition 5.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6 proof).
hypotheses: Uniformity is essential: ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is a complete Tate ring that is not reduced.
proofSteps: If x ∈ R is nilpotent, then λx is nilpotent, hence power-bounded, for every λ ∈ R; for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ this gives ϖ^{-n}x ∈ R° for all n, i.e. x ∈ ⋂_n ϖ^nR°.
R° is ϖ-adically separated (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), so x = 0.
acceptance: ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is not reduced, hence not uniform, hence not perfectoid, although ϖ = p^{1/p} satisfies ϖ^p | p and Frobenius on its power-bounded subring modulo p is surjective.

nodes.title: A perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p is uniform (open mapping theorem)
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pR = 0 which is perfect (PerfectRing R p: Frobenius R → R bijective). Then R° is bounded, i.e. R is uniform.
hypotheses: R complete, Hausdorff and Tate; no uniformity is assumed.
proofSteps: Φ: R → R is a continuous bijective ring homomorphism. Make the target an R-module through Φ (a·y := a^py); then Φ is R-linear, surjective and continuous, both sides are complete, first countable (a Huber ring has a countable neighbourhood basis of 0) and nonarchimedean, the target is Hausdorff and scalar multiplication on it is continuous, so Φ is open by the open mapping theorem over a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap; ECD Proposition 3.5 proof; Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.0.3 phrases the same step with two norms).

Choose a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R_0 for a ring of definition R_0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero). Openness gives n ≥ 1 with ϖ^nR_0 ⊆ Φ(R_0); since Φ(ϖ^jR_0) = ϖ^{pj}Φ(R_0), this yields Φ^{-1}(ϖ^mR_0) ⊆ ϖ^{⌊(m−n)/p⌋}R_0 for every integer m.

If y is topologically nilpotent then y^{p^k} ∈ R_0 for some k; applying Φ^{-1} k times and the previous inclusion gives y ∈ ϖ^{-c}R_0 with c = ⌈(n + p)/(p − 1)⌉, independent of y (if m ≥ −c then ⌊(m − n)/p⌋ ≥ −c). For x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so R° ⊆ ϖ^{-c-1}R_0 is bounded. (This integral-exponent estimate replaces the chain Φ^{-k}(R_0) ⊆ ϖ^{-n/p-⋯-n/p^k}R_0 ⊆ ϖ^{-n}R_0 of ECD and Berkeley, whose last inclusion needs ϖ^{q}R_0 ⊆ R_0 for fractional q; see sourceIssues.)

nodes.title: In characteristic p, perfectoid Tate rings are exactly the perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let R be a topological ring with pR = 0. Then R is a perfectoid Tate ring iff R is a perfect complete Hausdorff Tate ring. For such R, R° and every ring of integral elements R+ are perfect, Φ: R° → R° is an automorphism, and every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ satisfies the condition of ECD Definition 3.1 (ϖ^p | p = 0 is vacuous).
hypotheses: pR = 0; completeness includes Hausdorffness.
proofSteps: (⇐) R is uniform (P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform). x is power-bounded iff x^p is, so Φ restricts to an automorphism of R°; hence Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective, and it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a).

(⇒) If Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism, so is R°/ϖ^n → R°/ϖ^{np} for all n by induction; passing to the limit with R° ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete) gives Φ: R° ≅ R°, and inverting ϖ shows R is perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5 proof).
R+ is perfect: if x^p ∈ R+ then x is integral over R+, so x ∈ R+ (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.2).

nodes.title: lim_{x↦x^p} R+ ≅ lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 ≅ lim_Φ R+/p (ECD Lemma 3.10, first part)
nodes.statement: Let R be a nonzero complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ a ring of integral elements and ϖ_0 ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer dividing p in R+. Then projection (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (x^{(n)} mod ϖ_0)_n is a multiplicative bijection lim_{x↦x^p} R+ → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0R+, and a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (R+ with its topology, R+/ϖ_0 discrete); the inverse sends (x̄_0, x̄_1, …) to (x^{(i)})_i with x^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞} x_{n+i}^{p^n} for arbitrary lifts x_j ∈ R+ of x̄_j. The same holds for p in place of ϖ_0, and the ring homomorphism lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 induced by the quotient map is an isomorphism. In Mathlib terms: Perfection.quotientMulEquiv p (span {ϖ_0}) : Perfection R+ p ≃* Perfection (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p, and Perfection (ModP R+ p) p is PreTilt R+ p.
hypotheses: R ≠ 0, so ϖ_0 and p are not units of R+ and R+/ϖ_0 has characteristic p (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (d)).
proofSteps: R+ is ϖ_0-adically and p-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a), (c)), and CharP (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p holds; Mathlib's Perfection.quotientMulEquiv applies to I = ϖ_0R+ and to I = pR+. Its inverse is built from Perfection.teichmuller, i.e. the limit x^{(i)} = lim_n x_{n+i}^{p^n}, which converges because x ≡ y mod ϖ_0^n implies x^p ≡ y^p mod ϖ_0^{n+1} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof; Perfection.teichmuller_spec).
Continuity of the inverse: x^{(i)} mod ϖ_0^{n+1} depends only on x̄_{i+n} (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
The map lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 is a ring homomorphism compatible with the two multiplicative bijections from lim R+, hence bijective (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i)).
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K°, this is Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i).
For R of characteristic p (so R+ perfect), projection to the zeroth factor identifies lim_{x↦x^p} R+ with R+.

nodes.title: Pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. A pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots is an element ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_{n≥0} of the multiplicative monoid lim_{x↦x^p} R (Mathlib Perfection R p) such that ϖ := ϖ^{1/p^0} is a pseudo-uniformizer of R lying in R° with ϖ^p | p in R°. Then every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer in R°, ϖ^q := (ϖ^{1/p^n})^m is well defined for q = m/p^n ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0} (and for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] as a unit of R), and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of the tilt R♭ with (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Attached to ϖ♭ is the spectral gauge |x|_ϖ := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°}: a power-multiplicative, submultiplicative, ultrametric norm defining the topology of R, with |ϖ^qx|_ϖ = 2^{-q}|x|_ϖ, R° = {x : |x|_ϖ ≤ 1} and R°° = {x : |x|_ϖ < 1}. Existence is P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; the normalisation |ϖ|_ϖ = 1/2 is a convention, and changing ϖ changes |·|_ϖ by a power.
proofSteps: ϖ^{1/p^n} is a unit because its p^n-th power is, topologically nilpotent because its p^n-th power is, and power-bounded because R° is integrally closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).

Gauge: |x|_ϖ is finite since R = R°[1/ϖ]; submultiplicative and ultrametric since R° is a ring; power-multiplicativity |x^n|_ϖ = |x|_ϖ^n: if x^n ∈ ϖ^{q'}R° and q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with nq ≤ q' then (x/ϖ^q)^n ∈ R°, so x/ϖ^q ∈ R° by integral closedness, and ℤ[1/p] is dense in ℚ.
Topology: the balls {|x|_ϖ ≤ 2^{-q}} = ϖ^qR° form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); R°° = ⋃_q ϖ^qR° is P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal.
acceptance: In ℂ_p, (p^{1/p^n})_n with a compatible choice of roots is such an element and |x|_ϖ = 2^{-v_p(x)} (normalised valuation v_p(p) = 1).
ℚ_p admits none: no pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p satisfies ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Every perfectoid Tate ring has a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (ECD Lemma 3.10)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ_1 a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ_1^p | p in R°. There is ϖ♭ ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R° with ϖ := ϖ♭^{(0)} ≡ ϖ_1 mod ϖ_1^pR°; then ϖ = ϖ_1·u with u ∈ (R°)^×, ϖR° = ϖ_1R°, ϖ^p | p in R°, and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). If pR = 0 every pseudo-uniformizer has unique compatible roots.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; the zero ring is allowed (then everything is 0).
proofSteps: Put ϖ_0 := ϖ_1^p, which divides p. Frobenius on R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i)), so the zeroth projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 → R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective); by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius choose ϖ♭ ∈ lim R° whose image in R°/ϖ_0 is ϖ_1 (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof).
Then ϖ = ϖ_1 + ϖ_1^py = ϖ_1(1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y) with y ∈ R°, and 1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y is a unit of the ϖ_1-adically complete ring R° (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).
All components ϖ^{1/p^n} are units and topologically nilpotent because their p^n-th power ϖ is.

nodes.title: Every ring of integral elements of a perfectoid Tate ring satisfies the Frobenius condition
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and R+ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then (a) Frobenius on R+/p is surjective, and every element of R+/ϖpR+ is a p-th power for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+; (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+ and p/ϖ^p ∈ R°° (topologically nilpotent), and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+, Φ: R+/ϖ → R+/ϖ^p is bijective; (c) consequently (R, R+) satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 with R+ in place of R°, which is the formulation of Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.1.1 and Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.3.1, and these definitions agree with ECD's: the perfectoid condition on a Huber pair (R, R+) depends on R alone.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; R+ open and integrally closed, so R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).
proofSteps: (b) existence: take ϖ_0 with compatible p-power roots and ϖ_0^p | p in R° (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), write p = ϖ_0^pu with u ∈ R°, and set ϖ := ϖ_0^{1 − 1/p²}; then p = ϖ^p·ϖ_0^{1/p}u with ϖ_0^{1/p}u ∈ R°° ⊆ R+.

(a) (BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof) For x ∈ R+ write x = y^p + pϖz with y, z ∈ R° (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (iii) for R°); ϖz ∈ R°° ⊆ R+, so y^p = x − pϖz ∈ R+ and y ∈ R+ by integral closedness; hence x ≡ y^p mod pR+. Surjectivity modulo ϖpR+ then follows from P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion applied to R+.
(b) bijectivity: surjectivity from (a) since pR+ ⊆ ϖ^pR+; injectivity from P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (c).

(c) is (b) together with P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion; conversely a Huber pair satisfying the R+-condition has R perfectoid by BMS1 Lemma 3.20 (P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison) or Kedlaya–Liu II Proposition 3.3.3.
acceptance: For K a perfectoid field and K+ ⊆ K° an open valuation subring of rank 2, Frobenius on K+/p is surjective.
Mathlib's surjective_fontaineTheta applies to R+ with hypothesis Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R+ p) p) supplied by (a) (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

nodes.title: Metric criterion: a uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff every element is a p-th power up to a fixed factor c < 1 (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c))
nodes.statement: Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ B° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in B° admitting a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ B° ((ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}, ϖ^{1/p^0} = ϖ). Let |x| := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B°} be the spectral gauge of ϖ (the formula of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, here on a ring not assumed perfectoid). Then (a) |·| is an ultrametric, submultiplicative, power-multiplicative norm defining the topology of B, with |ϖ^q x| = 2^{-q}|x| and B° = {x : |x| ≤ 1}; (b) B is a perfectoid Tate ring if and only if there is c ∈ (0, 1) such that for every x ∈ B there is y ∈ B with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|; (c) if B is perfectoid, every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) = (|ϖ|^p, 1) has this property, and y can be taken in B° when x ∈ B°. Kedlaya states the criterion for a uniform analytic Huber pair (A, A⁺) with an ideal of definition I, p ∈ I^p, and the norm attached to I; this node is its Tate-ring form with the gauge of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, which every perfectoid Tate ring has (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots) and which every Tate ring receiving a continuous map from a perfectoid Tate ring has (the image of such a ϖ). Power-multiplicativity of the norm is used: the criterion is a statement about the spectral gauge.
hypotheses: B complete, Hausdorff and uniform (B° bounded); ϖ^p | p in B° and the roots ϖ^{1/p^n} lie in B.
No perfectoid base field; B may have characteristic 0, p, or neither (then |p| may be 0 on some factors).
proofSteps: (a) Ultrametricity and submultiplicativity are inherited from B° being an additive subgroup and a subring. Power-multiplicativity: if ϖ^{-nq}x^n ∈ B° then (ϖ^{-q}x)^n ∈ B°, so ϖ^{-q}x is integral over B° and lies in B° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral); rounding exponents in ℤ[1/p] gives |x^n| = |x|^n. If |x| ≤ 1 then ϖ^{1/p^k}x ∈ B° for all k, hence x^n ∈ ϖ^{-1}B° for all n, a bounded set by uniformity, so x ∈ B°. |x| = 0 forces x ∈ ⋂_q ϖ^qB° = 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); the sets ϖ^qB° are a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero).

(c), hence ⇒ of (b): if B is perfectoid, Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion). Given c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) and x ≠ 0, choose q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with u := ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B° and 2^{-q} ≤ 2^p c|x|, choose w ∈ B° with u − w^p ∈ ϖ^pB° and put y := ϖ^{q/p}w; then |x − y^p| = 2^{-q}|u − w^p| ≤ 2^{-q-p} ≤ c|x| (Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c), second paragraph).

⇐ of (b): given c and u ∈ B°, put u_0 := u and choose inductively y_k with |u_k − y_k^p| ≤ c|u_k|, u_{k+1} := u_k − y_k^p. Then |y_k^p| ≤ |u_k| ≤ c^k, so y_k ∈ B° by (a). For c^k ≤ 2^{-p}, u − (y_0 + ⋯ + y_{k−1})^p = u_k − (mixed binomial terms), and the mixed terms lie in pB° ⊆ ϖ^pB°; as {|x| ≤ 2^{-p}} = ϖ^pB° by (a), u is a p-th power modulo ϖ^pB°. So Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective, it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a), and B is perfectoid by P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras.
Kedlaya AWS proves ⇐ through Lemma 2.8.2, whose hypothesis is that the pair is already perfectoid (recorded in sourceIssues); the successive approximation above replaces it.
acceptance: B = ℂ_p with ϖ = p^{1/p} (so |p| = 2^{-p}): every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) works, matching "any c ∈ (p^{-1}, 1)" of Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c) for the normalisation |p| = p^{-1}.

Non-example: for a perfectoid field K, B = K⟨T⟩ (Gauss norm, uniform, ϖ ∈ K with roots) fails the criterion at x = T: the reduction of y^p in (K°/K°°)[T] is a p-th power, so |T − y^p| ≥ 1 = |T| for every y; B is not perfectoid.
P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: the criterion passes along isometric continuous maps with dense image, since |x − x′| < |x| implies |x′| = |x|.

nodes.title: The tilt R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.9, Lemma 3.10)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Its tilt is R♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} R, the multiplicative monoid Perfection R p of compatible sequences (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} with (x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}, with the inverse-limit topology (induced from ∏_ℕ R), pointwise multiplication and addition (x + y)^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. The limit exists and R♭ is a topological ring of characteristic p which is perfect (ECD Lemma 3.10; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1). Concretely, for ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ_0 | p, the submonoid lim_{x↦x^p} R° is identified with the ring lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭] as monoids, and the ring structure of R♭ is that of this localisation; it is given by the limit formula and does not depend on ϖ_0 or ϖ♭. For a Huber pair (R, R+) with R perfectoid, the tilt pair is (R♭, R♭+) with R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting). If pR = 0 then x ↦ x^{(0)} is an isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; the construction of the ring structure uses ϖ_0 | p and completeness of R°.
Additivity of the zeroth projection is not asserted (P1/sharp-map).
proofSteps: Ring structure on lim R°: transport along the multiplicative bijection with lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); the resulting sum has i-th component lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} because at level i + n both reduce to x̄_{i+n} + ȳ_{i+n} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec characterises the limit), and this formula shows independence of ϖ_0.

R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭]: for x ∈ lim R, ϖ^Nx^{(0)} ∈ R° for some N; then (ϖ^{N/p^n}x^{(n)})^{p^n} ∈ R° and, R° being integrally closed, ϖ♭^N x ∈ lim R° (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof, "R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] as multiplicative monoids, and in fact as rings").
Characteristic p and perfectness: p·1 = 0 in lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 since ϖ_0 | p; Frobenius is (x^{(n)}) ↦ ((x^{(n)})^p), with inverse the shift (x^{(n)}) ↦ (x^{(n+1)}).

Topology: the inverse-limit topology on lim R° equals that of lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 with discrete factors (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); it is a ring topology (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)).
Characteristic p: R is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), so projection to the zeroth factor is bijective, and the limit formula is constant, hence the projection is additive.

nodes.title: R♭° = lim R° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ, R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (ECD Lemma 3.10)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. Then (a) R♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} R° = {x ∈ R♭ : x^{(n)} ∈ R° for all n} = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°}, and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ_0 of R dividing p in R° projection is a topological ring isomorphism R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (discrete factors) ≅ lim_Φ R°/p; (b) ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭, R♭° is an open and bounded subring whose subspace topology is the ϖ♭-adic one, and R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭]; (c) for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with 0 < q ≤ p, x ↦ x^{(0)} mod ϖ^qR° induces a ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭^qR♭° ≅ R°/ϖ^qR°, in particular R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ; (d) the kernel of R♭° → R°/ϖ^q is ϖ♭^qR♭°.
hypotheses: ϖ^p | p in R°, so ϖ^q | p for q ≤ p.
proofSteps: (c),(d) Kernel: if x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^qR°, then (x^{(n)}/ϖ^{q/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° gives x^{(n)} ∈ ϖ^{q/p^n}R° by integral closedness, i.e. x/ϖ♭^q ∈ lim R°. Surjectivity: Frobenius on R°/ϖ^q is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q → R°/ϖ^q is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective). Ring homomorphism: it is the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius).

(b) By (d), ker(pr_n: lim_Φ R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ) = ϖ♭^{p^n}R♭°, so the inverse-limit topology on lim R° is ϖ♭-adic; ϖ♭ is a unit (each coordinate is a unit of R) and topologically nilpotent; lim R° = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°} (integral closedness) is the preimage of the open R° under the continuous zeroth projection, hence open; it is bounded because (ϖ♭^My)^{(i)} = ϖ^{M/p^i}y^{(i)}; and x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NR° for i ≤ n iff x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^{Np^n}R°, so the two topologies agree; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring.

(a) lim R° is a bounded open subring, so it consists of power-bounded elements; conversely if x ∈ R♭ is power-bounded, {x^m} ⊆ ϖ♭^{-c}lim R°, so {(x^{(0)})^m} ⊆ ϖ^{-c}R° and x^{(0)} ∈ R°, and x^{(n)} ∈ R° since (x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x^{(0)} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof: lim R° "agrees with the powerbounded elements R♭°").
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K: K♭° = lim K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ and K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(iii)).
For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: R♭°/ϖ♭ = (K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}] (Sch12 Proposition 5.20 proof).

nodes.title: The tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the tilt R♭ is a complete Hausdorff uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Lemma 3.10, "a perfectoid F_p-algebra"); ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer, (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition, and R♭ ≠ 0 iff R ≠ 0.
hypotheses: R perfectoid.
proofSteps: Huber and Tate: (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)), and ϖ♭ is a topologically nilpotent unit.
Complete Hausdorff: R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 is an inverse limit of discrete rings; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] with R♭° open.
Uniform: R♭° is bounded (it is a ring of definition).
Perfect of characteristic p (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect.
1 ≠ 0 in R♭ iff 1 ≠ 0 in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ iff R ≠ 0 (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)).
acceptance: (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = ε − 1 (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
The tilt of a perfectoid ring of characteristic p is itself (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, equivOfCharP).

nodes.title: The sharp map ♯: R♭ → R (continuous, multiplicative, not additive)
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the sharp map ♯: R♭ → R, x ↦ x♯ := x^{(0)} (Mathlib Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0 on the underlying monoid Perfection R p) is continuous and multiplicative with 0♯ = 0, and is not additive in general. It satisfies (x^{1/p^n})♯ = x^{(n)}; x ∈ R♭° iff x♯ ∈ R°; x♯ = 0 iff x = 0; for x, y ∈ R♭°, (x + y)♯ ≡ x♯ + y♯ mod pR°; every element of R° is congruent modulo pR° to some y♯ with y ∈ R♭°; reduction of ♯ modulo ϖ is the ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ of P1/tilt-integral-subrings; and (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ. If pR = 0, ♯ is the ring isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.
hypotheses: R perfectoid.
proofSteps: Multiplicativity and continuity: ♯ is a coordinate projection of the inverse limit (ECD after Lemma 3.10; Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
Additivity modulo p: the reduction R♭° → R°/p, x ↦ x♯ mod p, is the zeroth projection of the ring lim_Φ R°/p (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius, P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a)).
Surjectivity modulo p: Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/p is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective).
x♯ = 0 ⇒ x = 0: x^{(n)} is nilpotent ((x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x♯) hence 0 as R is reduced (P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced).
acceptance: In (ℚ_p^cycl)♭: ε♯ = 1 while (ε − 1)♯ ≠ 0, so ♯ is not additive.
In (ℂ_p)♭: p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) has (p♭)♯ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements).

nodes.title: The spectral gauge is preserved by the sharp map: |x♯|_R = |x|_{R♭}
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, and |·|_ϖ, |·|_{ϖ♭} the spectral gauges of R and R♭ (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, the second for R♭ with its pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ and roots ϖ♭^{1/p^n}), both normalised by |ϖ| = |ϖ♭| = 1/2. Then |x♯|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭} for all x ∈ R♭ (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, "easy to check", over a perfectoid field; it is the norm Kedlaya–Liu put on the tilt by pullback along ♯).
hypotheses: None beyond the setting.
proofSteps: For q ∈ ℤ[1/p]: x ∈ ϖ♭^qR♭° iff ϖ♭^{-q}x ∈ R♭° iff (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯ ∈ R° (P1/sharp-map: membership in R♭° is detected by ♯, and ♯ is multiplicative with (ϖ♭^q)♯ = ϖ^q), so the two infima run over the same set of q.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p^cycl and ε = (ζ_{p^n})_n: |(ε − 1)♯| = lim |ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)}, which is |ε − 1| in K♭ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

nodes.title: Functoriality of tilting: f ↦ f♭
nodes.statement: A continuous ring homomorphism f: R → S between perfectoid Tate rings induces f♭: R♭ → S♭, (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (f(x^{(n)}))_n (Mathlib Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f on the underlying monoids), a continuous ring homomorphism with (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), f♭(R♭°) ⊆ S♭°, id♭ = id and (g ∘ f)♭ = g♭ ∘ f♭; on R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ it induces the reduction of f. A morphism of Huber pairs (R, R+) → (S, S+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom) with R, S perfectoid induces a morphism of the tilt pairs. Hence tilting is a functor from perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) to perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) of characteristic p, and a perfectoid R-algebra S gives a perfectoid R♭-algebra S♭.
hypotheses: f continuous; no condition on plus rings for the ring-level statement.
proofSteps: Multiplicativity is clear. Additivity: f is continuous and a ring homomorphism, so it commutes with the limit formula of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring. Continuity: coordinatewise.

f(R°) ⊆ S° for any continuous homomorphism from a Tate ring to a uniform Tate ring (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so f♭ maps lim R° into lim S° = S♭° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); similarly lim R+ into lim S+ when f(R+) ⊆ S+.
Functor laws hold coordinatewise; compatibility with ♯ is the zeroth coordinate.
acceptance: For the inclusion ℚ_p^cycl → ℂ_p, f♭ maps ε ∈ (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ to ε ∈ (ℂ_p)♭.
For g ∈ Gal(ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p) with cyclotomic character χ(g), g♭(ε) = ε^{χ(g)} (Berkeley Example 6.2.4: γ(t) = (1+t)^γ − 1).

nodes.title: The tilt B♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} B of a complete uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1)
nodes.statement: Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (B is not assumed perfectoid) and B⁺ ⊆ B° a ring of integral elements. Its tilt is B♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} B (Mathlib `Perfection B p`) with the inverse-limit topology, pointwise multiplication, x♯ := x^{(0)}, and addition (x + y)^{(i)} := lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. Then: (a) the limit exists and makes B♭ a perfect topological ring of characteristic p; ♯ is continuous and multiplicative; B♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} is an open subring and B♭° := lim_{x↦x^p} B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°}; B♭ is complete and Hausdorff; (b) for every ideal of definition I ⊆ B⁺ with p ∈ I (for instance I = (p, ϖ) for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ B⁺; Kedlaya asks p ∈ I^p), reduction x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod I)_n is an isomorphism of topological rings B♭⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I (discrete factors), and B♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt B⁺ p; (c) if B has a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in B° and compatible p-power roots, i.e. ϖ = ϖ♭♯ for some ϖ♭ ∈ B♭, then ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of B♭, B♭° is open and bounded with the ϖ♭-adic topology, B♭ = B♭°[1/ϖ♭], the spectral gauges satisfy |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ, and B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; this applies whenever there is a continuous ring homomorphism f: A → B from a perfectoid Tate ring A, with ϖ♭ := f♭(ϖ_A♭); the closure in B♭ of a perfect subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is then a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p; (d) a continuous ring homomorphism g: B → C of such rings induces g♭: B♭ → C♭, (x^{(n)}) ↦ (g(x^{(n)})), a continuous ring homomorphism with (g♭x)♯ = g(x♯), functorially; (e) there is a unique ring homomorphism θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ with θ_B([x]) = x♯ (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` for the p-adically complete ring B⁺), natural in B: θ_C ∘ W(g♭) = g ∘ θ_B; it is not surjective in general; (f) if B is perfectoid, B♭ with ♯, g♭ and θ_B is the tilt of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring with the sharp map, functoriality and θ of P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel.
hypotheses: B complete, Hausdorff, uniform, p topologically nilpotent in B; no perfectoid condition.
In (c) B♭ is Tate only because ϖ has compatible p-power roots in B; without them B♭ need not be Tate (test uniformTilt_padic).
proofSteps: (b), and the ring structure: B⁺ is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), hence I-adically complete for I = (p, ϖ) because p^N ∈ ϖB⁺ for large N; Mathlib `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` (hypotheses IsAdicComplete I B⁺ and CharP (B⁺/I) p) gives the multiplicative bijection lim B⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I, a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (the argument of P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with I in place of ϖ_0). Transport the ring structure of the perfect F_p-algebra lim_Φ B⁺/I; its sum has i-th coordinate lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} (Mathlib `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`), which does not depend on I. For I = (p) this is Mathlib `PreTilt B⁺ p` (B⁺ is p-adically complete, Stacks Tag 090T).

(a): Kedlaya's identity [x + y] = lim_m ([x^{p^{-m}}] + [y^{p^{-m}}])^{p^m} in W(F_p[x^{p^{-∞}}, y^{p^{-∞}}]) (Kedlaya AWS (2.7.1.2)), specialised to the coordinates of x, y ∈ B♭, gives existence of the limit, associativity and continuity of the addition on all of B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1(a)–(b) and proof); on B♭⁺ it is the ring structure of (b). B♭⁺ is the preimage of the open B⁺ under the continuous ♯, hence open; it is complete by (b), so B♭ is complete and Hausdorff. lim B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} and lim B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°} because B⁺ and B° are integrally closed in B (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).

(c): (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯, so {x : x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NB° for i ≤ n} = ϖ♭^{Np^n}B♭°: the topology of B♭° is ϖ♭-adic, ϖ♭ is a unit (coordinatewise) and topologically nilpotent, and |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ (same set of exponents q, as in P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp). Hence B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. For f: A → B, f(ϖ_A) = (f♭ϖ_A♭)♯ has compatible roots and f(ϖ_A)^p | p in B° (continuous homomorphisms into a uniform Tate ring preserve power-bounded elements, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A closed subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is complete and Tate, and the closure of a perfect subring is perfect because x ↦ x^{1/p} (the shift of coordinates) is continuous.
(d): g commutes with the limit formula and with the coordinates (Mathlib `Perfection.mapMonoidHom`); continuity is coordinatewise.

(e): B⁺ is p-adically complete, so θ_B exists and is unique as the Witt-vector lift of x ↦ x♯ mod p (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` on PreTilt B⁺ p, via (b)); naturality follows from uniqueness. For B = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) (p odd) the image of θ_B is ℤ_p ≠ ℤ_p[p^{1/p}].

(f): for perfectoid B the construction and the formulas are those of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (θ is determined by θ([x]) = x♯).
acceptance: Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4: for f: A → B continuous with A perfectoid and B uniform, B♭ is a uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p receiving f♭: A♭ → B♭, and the closure of f♭(A♭) is a perfectoid Tate ring (the first two steps of P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion).

For B = ℚ_p, B♭ ≅ 𝔽_p with the discrete topology: an element with compatible p-power roots has valuation 0, and the only units of ℤ_p with p^n-th roots for all n are the Teichmüller representatives (p odd).

nodes.title: The integral tilt R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p, and ♯ is PreTilt.untilt
nodes.statement: Let R be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements (e.g. R°). Then R+ satisfies Mathlib's standing hypotheses Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+) and IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), and: (a) the subring R♭+ = lim_{x↦x^p} R+ of R♭ is isomorphic as a topological ring to Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p = Perfection (ModP R+ p) p via x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod p)_n, with inverse built from Perfection.teichmuller / Perfection.quotientMulEquiv; (b) under this isomorphism x ↦ x♯ on R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt : PreTilt R+ p →* R+, and PreTilt.coeff 0 is ♯ mod p (PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero); (c) R♭ ≅ (PreTilt R+ p)[1/ϖ♭] (Localization.Away). Mathlib's PreTilt is thus the integral tilt of this layer; Mathlib has no ring structure on lim_{x↦x^p} R and no tilt of a non-field Tate ring, which this layer supplies (the field case, Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val, is compared in P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).
hypotheses: R ≠ 0 (otherwise p is a unit of R+ = 0 and Mathlib's hypothesis fails).
proofSteps: (a) Both rings are lim_Φ R+/p: PreTilt R+ p by definition, R♭+ by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with ϖ_0 replaced by p, and both ring structures are the inverse-limit ones (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a) for R+ = R°, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting in general).
(b) PreTilt.untilt is defined as teichmuller p (span {p}), the zeroth coordinate of the inverse of the reduction map (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv), i.e. x ↦ x♯.
(c) R♭ = R♭+[1/ϖ♭] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b), since ϖ♭R♭° ⊆ R♭+).
acceptance: For R = ℂ_p, PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ (ℂ_p)♭° and PreTilt.untilt p♭ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements realises 𝒪_{C}♭ through PreTilt).
WittVector p (PreTilt R+ p) is Mathlib's A_inf(R+), the source of WittVector.fontaineTheta (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

nodes.title: Rings of integral elements correspond under tilting: R+ ↦ R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. (a) R+ ↦ R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ = {x ∈ R♭ : x♯ ∈ R+} is an inclusion-preserving bijection from rings of integral elements of R to those of R♭; the inverse sends R♭+ to the preimage in R° of the image of R♭+ in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (b) R♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ R+/ϖ compatibly with R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (c) On both sides, rings of integral elements correspond to integrally closed subrings of the common quotient R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ (equivalently of R°/R°° ≅ R♭°/R♭°°). Hence a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R+) has tilt pair (R♭, R♭+), and R° ↦ R♭°.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained in R°.
proofSteps: An open integrally closed R+ ⊆ R° contains R°° ⊇ ϖR° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn), so R+ is the preimage of R+/ϖR° ⊆ R°/ϖR°; R+ is integrally closed in R iff R+/ϖR° is integrally closed in R°/ϖR° (lift, resp. reduce, a monic equation; ϖR° ⊆ R+), and R+ is open iff it contains ϖR° (ECD before Lemma 3.11).

The same holds for R♭, and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)) transports integrally closed subrings; x ∈ R♭+ iff x♯ mod ϖ ∈ R+/ϖ iff x♯ ∈ R+, and then x^{(n)} = (x^{1/p^n})♯ ∈ R+ by integral closedness, so R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.5).
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K and an open valuation subring K+ ⊆ K°, K♭+ is the open valuation subring of K♭ with the same image in the common residue field K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (Sch12 Proposition 3.6 proof).

nodes.title: R°° = ⋃ ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is an idempotent flat ideal
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n a pseudo-uniformizer of R with compatible p-power roots (for R perfectoid, P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). Then the ideal R°° of topologically nilpotent elements of R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal) equals ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ⋃_{q∈ℤ[1/p]_{>0}} ϖ^qR°; it satisfies (R°°)² = R°° and is flat as an R°-module (a filtered union of the free rank-one modules ϖ^{1/p^n}R°). For every ring of integral elements R+, R°° ⊆ R+ and R°° = ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R+. Hence (R°, R°°) and (R+, R°°) satisfy the hypotheses of P0/root-ideal-basic-setup.
hypotheses: Uniformity is used through P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0).
proofSteps: ⊇: ϖ^{1/p^n} is topologically nilpotent and R° is power-bounded, so ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R°° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul).

⊆: for x ∈ R°°, x^N ∈ ϖR° for N large because ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); for p^n ≥ N, x^{p^n} ∈ ϖR°, so (x/ϖ^{1/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° and x/ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R° by integral closedness (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).
Idempotence: ϖ^{1/p^n} = (ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p ∈ (R°°)². Flatness: ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ≅ R° since ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R°, and a filtered colimit of flat modules is flat.
R+: R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}·ϖ^{1/p^n − 1/p^{n+1}}R° ⊆ ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R+.
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K, K°° = m_K with m_K² = m_K (Bhatt notes Lemma 3.1.3(2)).
For ℚ_p, ℤ_p°° = pℤ_p and (pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p: without p-power roots the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements is not idempotent.

nodes.title: The almost setup (R°, R°°) of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD 3.21–3.23)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. The pair (R°, R°°) is a basic setup for almost mathematics (P0/almost-basic-setup: R°° idempotent and R°° ⊗_{R°} R°° ≅ R°° flat), and so is (R+, R°°) for every ring of integral elements R+. For an R+-module M the following are equivalent: (i) M is almost zero, R°°M = 0; (ii) ϖ'M = 0 for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ' of R; (iii) ϖ^{1/p^n}M = 0 for all n, for one (equivalently any) pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with compatible p-power roots (ECD Definition 3.21; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.9.4). The almost-zero modules form the Serre class of P0/almost-zero-serre-class, the almost categories R°a-Mod and R+a-Mod are the Serre quotients of P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (ECD Definition 3.23), and restriction of scalars along R+ → R°, which is injective with almost zero cokernel (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), induces an equivalence R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod. The construction depends only on R. For a perfectoid field K it is the classical setup (K°, m_K), with K°/m_K almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(i)).
hypotheses: R perfectoid (compatible roots exist, P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).
proofSteps: Basic setup: R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is idempotent and flat (P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal), so P0/root-ideal-basic-setup applies to R° and to R+.
(i) ⇔ (ii) ⇔ (iii): every pseudo-uniformizer lies in R°°, every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer, and R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R°.
R°/R+ is almost zero: for x ∈ R° and ϖ' a pseudo-uniformizer, ϖ'x is topologically nilpotent, hence in R+ (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod: R+ → R° is an almost isomorphism of rings, so extension and restriction of scalars induce inverse equivalences of the Serre quotients (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K: the residue field K°/m_K is almost zero, and every almost zero K°-module is a k-vector space (ECD Example 3.22(i)).
Theorem-level consumers: H^i(Spa(R, R+), O+) is almost zero for i > 0 (ECD Theorem 3.24; P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity).

nodes.title: Perfectoid fields (ECD Definition 3.6)
nodes.statement: A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring K (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) whose underlying topological ring is a nonarchimedean field: K is a field, complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| defining its topology (ECD Definition 3.6). Equivalently (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation; ECD Proposition 3.8; the original definition Sch12 Definition 3.1): K is a nonarchimedean field which is not discretely valued, |p| < 1, and Frobenius is surjective on K°/p. Its value group is p-divisible (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible). In characteristic p a perfectoid field is the same as a complete perfect nonarchimedean field. A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is automatically a perfectoid field (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field). ℚ_p and all discretely valued fields are not perfectoid.
hypotheses: Nonarchimedean field: in Lean, NontriviallyNormedField K with IsUltrametricDist K and CompleteSpace K; its Tate structure has ring of definition K° (closed unit ball) and any 0 < |ϖ| < 1 as pseudo-uniformizer.
Residue characteristic p is forced by |p| < 1.
proofSteps: The Tate structure of a nonarchimedean field (API isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField) is routine: K° is open and bounded, and the ϖ-adic topology on K° is the norm topology.
Uniformity is automatic (K° is the closed unit ball), so the definition reduces to condition (b) of ECD Definition 3.1.
acceptance: ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and the completed perfection of F_p((t)) are perfectoid fields (P1/perfectoid-examples); ℚ_p is not.

nodes.title: Characterisation of perfectoid fields (ECD Proposition 3.8)
nodes.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean field. Then K is a perfectoid field iff (i) K is not discretely valued, (ii) |p| < 1, and (iii) Frobenius Φ: K°/p → K°/p is surjective (ECD Proposition 3.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9). Condition (i) cannot be dropped (ℚ_p and its unramified extensions satisfy (ii) and (iii)). Hence Sch12 Definition 3.1 agrees with ECD Definition 3.6, and a nonarchimedean field is a perfectoid ring in Kedlaya's sense iff it is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).
hypotheses: K complete with a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value.
proofSteps: K is uniform (K° is the closed unit ball) and Tate.

(⇒) (ii): ϖ^p | p with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 gives |p| ≤ |ϖ|^p < 1. (iii): P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i) ⇒ (ii). (i): if K were discretely valued with uniformizer π and ϖ = uπ^k (k ≥ 1), then K°/ϖ and K°/ϖ^p are Artin local rings of lengths k and pk, so Φ could not be bijective (ECD Remark 3.3).

(⇐) A nondiscrete subgroup of ℝ_{>0} is dense, so there is ϖ ∈ K with |p|^{1/p} ≤ |ϖ| < 1, i.e. ϖ^p | p in K° (Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9 proof); then P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion and P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer give bijectivity of Φ: K°/ϖ → K°/ϖ^p.
acceptance: ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) satisfy (i)–(iii) (P1/perfectoid-examples).
ℚ_p satisfies (ii) and (iii) (Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective) but not (i); Sch12 notes that nondiscreteness is needed to exclude unramified extensions of ℚ_p.

nodes.title: The value group of a perfectoid field is p-divisible (Sch12 Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with value group Γ = |K^×| ⊆ ℝ_{>0}. Then Γ is p-divisible, and it is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 (in characteristic 0).
hypotheses: K perfectoid; in characteristic p the statement follows from perfectness.
proofSteps: Characteristic p: every x has a p-th root x^{1/p}, so |x| = |x^{1/p}|^p.

Characteristic 0 (Sch12 Lemma 3.2): Γ ≠ |p|^ℤ by nondiscreteness (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), so Γ is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1; for such x choose y with |x − y^p| ≤ |p| (Frobenius surjective on K°/p); then |y|^p = |y^p| = |x|.
acceptance: |ℂ_p^×| = |p|^ℚ is p-divisible; |ℚ_p^×| = |p|^ℤ is not, consistently with ℚ_p not being perfectoid.

nodes.title: A uniform Banach field over a nondiscretely valued field is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean field whose value group |F^×| is dense in ℝ_{>0}, and let A be a uniform Banach F-algebra (complete, with topology defined by a power-multiplicative norm; equivalently the spectral seminorm |·|_sp is a norm defining the topology) whose underlying ring is a field. Then |·|_sp is multiplicative, so A is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 3.7). The criterion used: a uniform Banach field A is a nonarchimedean field iff |t|_sp |t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ∈ A^× (Remark 3.3), because then |x|_sp = |xy·y^{-1}|_sp ≤ |xy|_sp/|y|_sp.
hypotheses: |F^×| dense in ℝ_{>0}; the discretely valued case is not covered by the proof (Kedlaya, Remark 3.9).
Uniformity is essential: Kedlaya's Example 2.15 is a Banach field that is not a nonarchimedean field.

The proof uses the Berkovich spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms: M(A) ≠ ∅ for A ≠ 0, f is a unit iff α(f) ≠ 0 for all α, and |x|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x) (Berkovich, Theorems 1.2.1 and 1.3.1), requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0.
proofSteps: Criterion (Remark 3.3): if |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ≠ 0 then |·|_sp is multiplicative; conversely a multiplicative norm satisfies it.

Lemma 3.6: if A is not a nonarchimedean field, there are t ∈ A with |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp > 1 and an interval [γ, δ] meeting |F^×| such that |λ|·|(t − λ)^{-1}|_sp ≤ c² for all λ ∈ F with |λ| ∈ [γ, δ]; the proof builds a convergent sequence μ_n = Σλ_i in F by contradiction.

Theorem 3.7: with ρ_n ↑ δ and polynomials P_n(t) = ∏(t − λ_{n,i}) whose roots have norms in [ρ_n^-, ρ_n^+], set x_n = (Σ_{j<m_n} P_{n,j}t^j)/P_n(t) and y_n = x_1⋯x_n; estimate α(y_n − y_{n−1}) for every α ∈ M(A) with α(t) = ρ, pass to |·|_sp = max_α α, and obtain a limit y which is neither zero nor a unit, a contradiction.
acceptance: Applied with F the completed perfection of F_p((z)) (value group dense) to a perfect uniform Banach field of characteristic p (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field).
Kedlaya Example 2.15 (Gauss norm on F(T_1, T_2, …)): the completion is a Banach field whose norm is not multiplicative, and it is not uniform.

nodes.title: A perfectoid Tate ring is a field iff its tilt is (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, general base)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Then R is a perfectoid field (a nonarchimedean field) iff its tilt R♭ is; in that case the absolute values satisfy |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R when normalised by |ϖ♭|_{R♭} = |ϖ|_R (Sch12 Lemma 5.21 over a perfectoid base field; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.5.2 and Example 3.3.8 in characteristic 0; Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).
hypotheses: R perfectoid with ϖ♭ with compatible roots; the spectral gauges are those of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.
proofSteps: A uniform Tate ring R is a nonarchimedean field iff R is a field and its spectral gauge |·|_ϖ is multiplicative (then |·|_ϖ is an absolute value defining the topology).

(⇒) |·|_{R♭} = |·♯|_R (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp) is multiplicative because ♯ is. R♭ is a field: for x ≠ 0, every x^{(n)} ≠ 0 (P1/sharp-map: x♯ = 0 iff x = 0, applied to x^{1/p^n}), and ((x^{(n)})^{-1})_n ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R is a multiplicative inverse (the argument of Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2).

(⇐) (Sch12 Lemma 5.21) Scale x, y ≠ 0 by powers ϖ^{k/p} into R° ∖ ϖ^{1/p}R°, choose x♭, y♭ ∈ R♭° with x − (x♭)♯, y − (y♭)♯ ∈ ϖR° (P1/sharp-map); then |x| = |x♭|, |y| = |y♭|, |xy| = |x♭y♭|, so multiplicativity transfers. x is a unit: |1 − x·((x♭)^{-1})♯| < 1 and R is complete.
acceptance: (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ is the field F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
For a perfectoid field K, the product K × K♭ is perfectoid but not a field, and its tilt K♭ × K♭ is not a field.

nodes.title: A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya; ECD Remark 3.7)
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field. Then the topology of A is defined by a multiplicative absolute value, so A is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 4.2; answers ECD Remark 3.7; Berkeley Remark 6.1.8; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.1).
hypotheses: A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field (Kedlaya, Remark 4.3: such A need not be an algebra over any perfectoid field).
proofSteps: Characteristic p: A is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) and uniform; for a pseudo-uniformizer z, A is a uniform Banach algebra over the completed perfection of F_p((z)), whose value group is dense (Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2 proof; Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.1.8), so P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field applies.

General case: A♭ is a field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field, (⇒) argument for fields: coordinatewise inverses in lim_{x↦x^p} A) and a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence a perfectoid field by the characteristic-p case; so A is a perfectoid field by P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field (⇐). This replaces Kedlaya's appeal to the homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(A♭) of Berkovich spectra by the spectral-gauge comparison P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp.
acceptance: Every perfectoid Tate ring that is a field, e.g. ℚ_p^cycl or ℂ_p with their Tate topologies, is a perfectoid field; the theorem is needed when the topology is given only by a ring of definition.

Kedlaya Remark 4.3 constructs a perfectoid ring over ℚ_p admitting quotients ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), which is not an algebra over any perfectoid field; the theorem applies to its field quotients.
