nodes.title: Tilt of a perfectoid field; comparison with Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field. Its tilt K♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) is a perfectoid field of characteristic p with absolute value |x|_♭ := |x♯|; K♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ is its valuation ring for any ϖ ∈ K with |p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1; |K♭^×| = |K^×|; K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ and K♭°/m♭ ≅ K°/m; K♭ = K if char K = p. Replacing ϖ by (ϖ♭)♯ one may assume ϖ has compatible p-power roots (Sch12 Lemma 3.4, Remark 3.5). For v : Valuation K ℝ≥0 the absolute value, O = K° and hv : v.Integers O, the tilt is isomorphic to Mathlib's Tilt K v O hv p = FractionRing (PreTilt O p), and Mathlib's valuation PreTilt.val K v O hv p satisfies PreTilt.val x = v(x♯) for x ∈ PreTilt O p ≅ K♭°.
hypotheses: K perfectoid; ϖ | p in K° for the identification with lim_Φ K°/ϖ.
proofSteps: K♭ is a perfectoid Tate ring (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) and a nonarchimedean field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field) with absolute value |x♯| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp).
K♭° = lim K° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings) is a valuation ring: x or x^{-1} lies in it according as |x♯| ≤ 1 or ≥ 1.

Value groups: |K♭^×| ⊆ |K^×|; conversely for x ∈ K° with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 there is y ∈ K♭° with x ≡ y♯ mod pK° (P1/sharp-map), so |x| = |y♯|, and such |x| generate |K^×| (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible, proof).
Residue fields: K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings), and m, m♭ are the nilradicals of these rings.

Mathlib: K♭° ≅ PreTilt O p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt) and K♭ = Frac(K♭°) = FractionRing (PreTilt O p); PreTilt.val x = preVal(x_n)^{p^n} for n with x_n ≠ 0, and a lift z of x_n satisfies z^{p^n} ≡ x♯ mod p^{n+1} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec), so for v(z) > v(p) both sides equal v(x♯).
acceptance: For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = (p, p^{1/p}, …) and t♯ = p.
For K = ℚ_p^cycl, |(ε − 1)♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

nodes.title: Continuous valuations of K and K♭ correspond (Sch12 Proposition 3.6)
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, |·| ↦ |·|♭, |x|♭ := |x♯|, is a bijection between continuous valuations of K up to equivalence and continuous valuations of K♭ up to equivalence (points of Spa(K, K°) ∪ … of higher rank included); it is the field case of the tilting homeomorphism P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets.
hypotheses: K perfectoid; continuity in Huber's sense (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont): continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m.
proofSteps: |·|♭ is a valuation: only the ultrametric inequality is nontrivial and follows from |x + y|♭ = lim |(x^{1/p^n})♯ + (y^{1/p^n})♯|^{p^n} ≤ max(|x♯|, |y♯|).

Continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m, hence to valuation subrings of K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting); this bijection is the one described.
acceptance: The rank-one valuation of K maps to the rank-one valuation of K♭ of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; higher-rank continuous valuations correspond to valuation subrings of the common residue field K°/m.

nodes.title: A_inf = W(R+) for a perfectoid pair of characteristic p: strict p-ring, (p,[ϖ])-adically complete
nodes.statement: Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then R+ is perfect, ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free, and A_inf(R, R+) := W(R+) satisfies: (a) W(R+) is p-torsion free and p-adically complete with W(R+)/p = R+ (a strict p-ring; Mathlib WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP); (b) every element is uniquely Σ_{n≥0} p^n[x_n] with x_n ∈ R+; (c) [ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor, W(R+) is [ϖ]-adically and (p,[ϖ])-adically complete and separated, and W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ; (d) Σ p^n[x_n] is a unit iff x_0 is a unit of R+; (e) the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology does not depend on ϖ; (f) W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] is the ring W^b(R) of Witt vectors with bounded Teichmüller coordinates, independent of ϖ and of R+ up to the evident inclusions; (g) for every p-adically complete ring S and ring homomorphism R+ → S/p there is a unique ring homomorphism W(R+) → S lifting it; Frobenius W(Φ) is an automorphism.
hypotheses: pR = 0 and R perfectoid, so R and R+ are perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
proofSteps: (a), (b), (g): R+ is perfect, so W(R+) is the strict p-ring with residue ring R+ (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.2.1, Corollary 2.2.6, Lemma 2.2.7; Mathlib WittVector, WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP).

(c): [ϖ]·Σp^n[x_n] = Σp^n[ϖx_n] and ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (b)); completeness from W_r(ϖ^{p^{r−1}}R+) ⊆ [ϖ]W_r(R+) ⊆ W_r(ϖR+) and ϖ-completeness of R+ (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(ii); Bhatt Example 6.1.6).

(d): reduction modulo p is R+ and W(R+) is p-adically complete; (e): two pseudo-uniformizers divide powers of each other in R+; (f): [ϖ]^{-n}Σp^m[x_m] = Σp^m[ϖ^{-n}x_m] (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.2, Remark 2.3.3).
acceptance: For R = F the perfect field of anchor Layer 6 and R+ = 𝒪_F, this is the (p,[ϖ])-adic completeness of A_inf = W(𝒪_F) packaged in anchor Layer 6.1 (P1/anchor-layer-6-compatibility).
For R+ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}, A_inf = W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) is (p,[p♭])-adically complete; Mathlib's BDeRhamPlus 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p is built on W(PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p) ≅ this ring.

nodes.title: Primitive (distinguished) elements and ideals of degree 1 in W(R+) (ECD Definition 3.15)
nodes.statement: Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. An element ξ = Σ_{n≥0} p^n[ξ_n] ∈ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 (distinguished) if ξ_0 is topologically nilpotent and ξ_1 is a unit of R+; equivalently ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u with u ∈ W(R+)^× (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.2.3). An ideal J ⊆ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 if it is principal with a primitive generator. Equivalently (ECD Definition 3.15), J is generated by an element p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W(R+): every such element is primitive, and every primitive element is a unit multiple of one of this form, because a topologically nilpotent element of R+ is divisible by a pseudo-uniformizer (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2; Kedlaya AWS Exercise 2.3.6). ξ = p is primitive (ξ_0 = 0): it corresponds to the untilt R itself. In the notation of an untilt S, R = S♭ and R+ = S♭+.
hypotheses: ξ_0 = 0 is allowed (Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.2.5); p² and [ϖ] are not primitive.
proofSteps: p + [ϖ]α = [ϖα_0] + p(1 + [ϖ]α') with α − [α_0] = pα'; 1 + [ϖ]α' is a unit because its reduction 1 + ϖα'_0 is a unit of the ϖ-adically complete R+ (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)).
Conversely ξ = [ξ_0] + pu with u a unit: u^{-1}ξ = p + [ξ_0]u^{-1}, and ξ_0 = ϖc for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2), so u^{-1}ξ = p + [ϖ]([c]u^{-1}).
acceptance: In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): p − [p♭] and Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p} are primitive (Kedlaya AWS Examples 2.3.7–2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.5).

nodes.title: Primitive elements are nonzerodivisors and divide each other only up to units (ECD Lemma 3.16)
nodes.statement: Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. (a) Every primitive element ξ ∈ W(R+), in particular every p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer of R+ and α ∈ W(R+), is a nonzerodivisor (ECD Lemma 3.16; in ECD's notation α ∈ W(R♭+), the printed "W(R+)" being a misprint; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.10). (b) If ξ, ξ' are primitive and ξ' = yξ with y ∈ W(R+), then y is a unit (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.5); so two primitive elements generating comparable ideals are associate.
hypotheses: R+ perfect, ϖ-adically separated and ϖ-torsion free (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring).
proofSteps: (a) Reduce to ξ = p + [ϖ]α (P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals). If ξ·Σ_n[c_n]p^n = 0, then modulo [ϖ] this reads Σ[c_n]p^{n+1} ≡ 0, so all c_n ∈ ϖR+; divide all c_n by ϖ and induct; since R+ is ϖ-adically separated, all c_n vanish (ECD Lemma 3.16 proof).

(b) Comparing Witt coordinates (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.2.8), ξ'_1 − y_0ξ_1 is topologically nilpotent; ξ_1, ξ'_1 are units, so y_0 is a unit of R+, and y is a unit (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)).
acceptance: p − [p♭] ∈ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) is a nonzerodivisor (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).

With p♭ a compatible system of p-power roots of p and ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, p − [p♭] and ξ_cyc = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} both generate ker θ in W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}); hence they are associates and each divides the other by a unit (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel; Scholze 2013 Lemma 6.3).

Negative example: μ = [ε] − 1 = ([ε]^{1/p} − 1)·ξ_cyc lies in ker θ but does not generate it. The factor [ε]^{1/p} − 1 is not a unit: its zeroth Witt coefficient ε^{1/p} − 1 lies in the maximal ideal of 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭} (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)). Regularity of ξ_cyc implies (μ) is strictly smaller than (ξ_cyc), so μ is not primitive. Membership in ker θ alone does not imply primitivity.

nodes.title: W(R+)/ξ is [ϖ]-torsion free and [ϖ]-adically complete (the facts ECD Lemma 3.14 uses)
nodes.statement: Let ξ ∈ W(R+) be primitive, (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then A+ := W(R+)/ξ satisfies: (a) the image of [ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor; (b) A+ is [ϖ]-adically complete and separated, and its [ϖ]-adic and (p,[ϖ])-adic topologies coincide; (c) A+/[ϖ] ≅ W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ; (d) A+ is p-adically complete; (e) ξW(R+)[1/[ϖ]] ∩ W(R+) = ξW(R+). These are the two properties ECD Lemma 3.14 uses without proof ("W(R♭+)/ξ is [ϖ♭]-torsion free and [ϖ♭]-adically complete").
hypotheses: ξ primitive; by P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals we may take ξ = p + [ϖ]α.
proofSteps: (a) If [ϖ]x = ξy, then modulo p: ϖx_0 = ϖα_0y_0, so x_0 = α_0y_0 and x − αy = pz; then p[ϖ]z = [ϖ](x − αy) = ξy − [ϖ]αy = py, so y = [ϖ]z (W(R+) is p-torsion free) and x = ξz ([ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor, P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (c)). (e) is (a) iterated.
(c) (ξ, [ϖ]) = (p, [ϖ]) since ξ ≡ p mod [ϖ]; W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ.

(b),(d) ξW(R+) is closed for the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology (by (a), ξW ∩ [ϖ]^nW = [ϖ]^nξW), so A+ is complete for the finitely generated ideal (p,[ϖ]); since p = ξ − [ϖ]α ∈ ([ϖ]) + (ξ), the topology on A+ is [ϖ]-adic; p-adic completeness follows as (p) ⊆ ([ϖ]) in A+ (Stacks Tag 090T).
acceptance: For ξ = p − [p♭] in W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): W/ξ ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p} is p-torsion free and p-adically complete.
For ξ = p: W(R+)/p = R+ is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free.

nodes.title: ECD's θ is Mathlib's WittVector.fontaineTheta; surjectivity from surjective_fontaineTheta
nodes.statement: Let R be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements. Mathlib's WittVector.fontaineTheta R+ p : 𝕎(PreTilt R+ p) →+* R+ (defined under [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+)] and [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+], both supplied by P1/integral-elements-adically-complete) corresponds, under R♭+ ≅ PreTilt R+ p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt), to ECD's θ: W(R♭+) → R+, Σ_n p^n[r_n] ↦ Σ_n p^n r_n♯. In particular θ([x]) = x♯ (WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller) and θ mod p is x ↦ x♯ mod p (WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta). Mathlib's surjective_fontaineTheta applies because Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring), so θ is surjective. θ is the unique ring homomorphism W(R♭+) → R+ lifting x ↦ x♯ mod p (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7, Definition 2.7.3). Mathlib's fontaineThetaInvertP and BDeRhamPlus R+ p are built on this θ.
hypotheses: R ≠ 0 and R perfectoid.
proofSteps: Both maps are ring homomorphisms W(R♭+) → R+ sending [x] to x♯ (Mathlib fontaineTheta_teichmuller with PreTilt.untilt = ♯, P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt); a ring homomorphism out of the strict p-ring W(R♭+) into a p-adically complete ring is determined by its reduction mod p, which is x ↦ x♯ mod p for both (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7).
Surjectivity: Mathlib surjective_fontaineTheta with hypothesis Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R+ p) p) from P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (a).
ECD's check that θ is a ring map modulo ϖ^m through the m-th ghost map factoring over W(R+/ϖ) is Mathlib's construction fontaineThetaModPPow (ghost component factoring over W(R/p)).
acceptance: For R = ℂ_p: fontaineTheta sends [p♭] to p and [ε] to 1 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).
For R of characteristic p (R♭ = R): θ is reduction modulo p, W(R+) → R+ (Bhatt Proposition 6.1.8 proof).

nodes.title: Fontaine's θ: W(S♭+) → S+ is surjective with kernel generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor (ECD Lemma 3.14)
nodes.statement: Let (S, S+) be a perfectoid Tate pair (any characteristic) with tilt (S♭, S♭+). (a) θ: W(S♭+) → S+, Σ[r_n]p^n ↦ Σ r_n♯p^n, is a surjective ring homomorphism (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib). (b) ker θ is generated by a primitive element of degree 1, which can be taken of the form ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ ∈ S♭+ a pseudo-uniformizer such that (ϖ♭♯)^p | p in S+, and α ∈ W(S♭+); ξ is a nonzerodivisor. (c) An element of ker θ generates ker θ iff it is primitive (BMS1 Remark 3.11). (d) θ extends to a surjection W(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]] → S with kernel ξW(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]], and W(S♭+)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = S♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ S+/ϖ♭♯. If pS = 0 then ker θ = (p). (ECD Lemma 3.14; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.8; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.5; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.6.3 in characteristic 0.)
hypotheses: (S, S+) perfectoid; no perfectoid base field.
proofSteps: (a) P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib.

Construction of ξ: choose ϖ♭ with compatible roots (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots) and ϖ := ϖ♭♯ with ϖ^p | p in S+ (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); put α_0 := p/ϖ ∈ S+, choose β ∈ S♭+ with β♯ ≡ α_0 mod pS+ (P1/sharp-map, surjectivity of ♯ mod p on S+), so f := ϖ♭β has f♯ ≡ p mod pϖS+; write p = f♯ + pϖ Σ_n r_n♯p^n with r_n ∈ S♭+ (θ surjective) and put ξ := p − [f] − [ϖ♭]Σ_n[r_n]p^{n+1} ∈ ker θ, of the form p + [ϖ♭]α (ECD Lemma 3.14 proof).

Generation: θ induces a surjection W(S♭+)/ξ → S+, which is an isomorphism modulo [ϖ♭] because W(S♭+)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = W(S♭+)/(p, [ϖ♭]) = S♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ S+/ϖ (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting (b)); W(S♭+)/ξ is [ϖ♭]-torsion free and complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element) and S+ is ϖ-torsion free, so the map is an isomorphism (a surjection of such modules that is injective modulo ϖ has kernel in ⋂ϖ^n = 0).
Nonzerodivisor: P1/distinguished-element-criterion (a). (c): a primitive ξ' ∈ ker θ is yξ with y a unit by P1/distinguished-element-criterion (b); a generator is associate to ξ, hence primitive.
(d) Invert [ϖ♭], θ([ϖ♭]) = ϖ being a unit of S. Characteristic p: S♭ = S and θ is reduction mod p.
acceptance: For S = ℂ_p: ker θ = (p − [p♭]), and Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} is another generator (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).
For S a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, ker θ = (p).

nodes.title: ker θ is compatible with base change: ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭+)
nodes.statement: Let f: (R, R+) → (S, S+) be a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs with tilt f♭. Then θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R and ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭+); every generator ξ of ker θ_R maps to a generator of ker θ_S. nodes.title: Euclidean division by a primitive element and approximation by sharp elements (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.7, 2.6.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7)
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no base field), ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯, and |·| the spectral gauges |·|_ϖ of A and |·|_{ϖ♭} of A♭ (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), so that |y♯| = |y| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp). Let z = [z̄_0] + p·z_1 (z_1 ∈ W(A♭°)^×) be a primitive generator of ker(θ: W(A♭°) → A°) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), extend θ to W^b(A♭) := W(A♭°)[1/[ϖ♭]] → A, and give W^b(A♭) the Gauss norm |Σ_n p^n[x_n]| := sup_n |x_n|. An element x = Σ_n p^n[x_n] is prepared if |x_0| ≥ |x_n| for all n ≥ 1. Then: (a) (Euclidean division) for x ∈ W^b(A♭) put x′ := p^{-1}(x − [x_0]) and r(x) := x − z_1^{-1}x′z = [x_0] − [z̄_0]z_1^{-1}x′; if x ∉ zW^b(A♭), the terms of the sequence x, r(x), r(r(x)), … are congruent to x modulo z and are prepared from some term on; no nonzero element of zW^b(A♭) is prepared; (b) (norms) |θ(x)| ≤ |x| for every x, with equality when x is prepared; hence the quotient norm of the Gauss norm on W^b(A♭)/(z) ≅ A is the spectral gauge, and |z̄_0| = |p| (|p| < 1, and |p| = 0 iff pA = 0); (c) (sharp approximation) for every a ∈ A there is y ∈ A♭ with |a − y♯| ≤ |p|·|a|, so |y| = |a|; for a ∈ A° one can take y ∈ A♭°; (d) (pointwise form) α ↦ α ∘ ♯ maps the Gel'fand spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms on (A, |·|) into M(A♭), and for every a ∈ A and ε > 0 there is y ∈ A♭ with α(a − y♯) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a), ε} for all α ∈ M(A) simultaneously; with |·| = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α (Berkovich; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21) this refines (c) up to ε; (e) (quasi-additivity of ♯) |(x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯| ≤ |p|·max{|x|, |y|} for x, y ∈ A♭.
hypotheses: A perfectoid; z any primitive generator of ker θ (all differ by units of W(A♭°), P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals).
Part (d) uses the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring and the maximum formula for the spectral seminorm, requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0; parts (a)–(c) and (e) do not.
proofSteps: Gauss norm: Witt vector arithmetic is homogeneous in the Teichmüller coordinates (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.2.8; Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.1.4), so the Gauss norm is ultrametric and submultiplicative, |p·w| = |w| (a shift of coordinates), |[c]w| ≤ |c||w|, and units of W(A♭°) have norm 1 (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (b), (d), (f)). As |z̄_0| < 1, |zw| = |w| for all w (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.6.2).

(a): r(x) ≡ x mod z by construction and |r(x) − [x_0]| ≤ |z̄_0||x|. If |r^{m+1}(x)| > |z̄_0||r^m(x)| for some m, the zeroth coordinate of r^{m+1}(x) carries its norm and r^{m+1}(x) is prepared, and so are all further terms; otherwise |r^m(x)| ≤ |z̄_0|^m|x| and the Euclidean quotients sum to q with x = qz. A nonzero prepared zw would satisfy |zw| = |w| ≥ |w_0| > |z̄_0w_0|, the norm of its zeroth coordinate, contradicting preparedness (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.6, 2.6.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(a)).

(b): θ(Σp^n[x_n]) = Σp^n x_n♯ (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (a)), so |θ(x)| ≤ sup_n |x_n♯| = |x|. If x is prepared, θ(x) = x_0♯ + p·θ(x′) with |p·θ(x′)| ≤ |p||x_0| < |x_0| = |x_0♯| unless pA = 0, so |θ(x)| = |x|. Every class has a prepared representative by (a) (θ is surjective onto A, P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (d)), which gives the quotient norm (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.7, Corollary 2.6.10). θ(z) = 0 gives z̄_0♯ = −p·θ(z_1) with θ(z_1) a unit of A°, so |z̄_0| = |p| (the constant c := |z̄_0| of the proof of Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3).

(c): for a prepared representative x of a, a − x_0♯ = p·θ(x′) with |θ(x′)| ≤ |x_0| = |a|; take y := x_0. If |a| ≤ 1 then |x_0| ≤ 1, so x_0 ∈ A♭° (gauge ≤ 1 characterises A♭°, P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).

(d): α ∘ ♯ is multiplicative, bounded by |·| on A♭, and ultrametric by continuity of α and the limit formula for the addition of A♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring). Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(b): after enough Euclidean steps the representative y of a satisfies β(y_n) ≤ max{ε, β(y_0)} for all β ∈ M(A♭) and n ≥ 1. For α ∈ M(A) and β = α ∘ ♯, α(a − y_0♯) ≤ sup_{n≥1} α(p)^n α(y_n♯) ≤ α(p)·max{ε, α(y_0♯)}; if α(y_0♯) > ε this bound is < α(y_0♯) (α(p) ≤ |p| < 1), so α(a) = α(y_0♯). The maximum formula is TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0 (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21).

(e): choose q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with ϖ♭^{-q}x, ϖ♭^{-q}y ∈ A♭° and 2^{-q} arbitrarily close to max{|x|, |y|}; ♯ is multiplicative and (x′ + y′)♯ − x′♯ − y′♯ ∈ pA° for x′, y′ ∈ A♭° (P1/sharp-map), so (x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯ ∈ ϖ^q·pA°, of gauge ≤ 2^{-q}|p|.
acceptance: A = ℂ_p, z = p − [p♭]: every a ∈ ℂ_p is y♯ up to |p||a|, i.e. O_{ℂ_p}/p ≅ O_{ℂ_p♭}/p♭ lifted along ♯; a − y♯ need not vanish.
Characteristic p: z = p, z̄_0 = 0 and |p| = 0; r(x) = [x_0] is prepared after one step and a = y♯ exactly.

Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3 ("only if", with c = |z̄_0|) and Lemmas 2.8.5–2.8.6 use (c)–(e): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings and P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting.

nodes.title: The untilt of (R, R+) along a primitive ideal J: (W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R+)/J)
nodes.statement: Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p, J ⊆ W(R+) a primitive ideal of degree 1 and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. The untilt of (R, R+) along J is the pair (A, A+) with A+ := W(R+)/J and A := A+[1/π], π the image of [ϖ], topologised so that A+ is open with its π-adic (equivalently (p,[ϖ])-adic) topology; equivalently A = W^b(R)/J·W^b(R) with W^b(R) = W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]. A is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer π and ring of definition A+, independent of ϖ; the construction is functorial for morphisms of pairs f with W(f)(J) ⊆ J' (then J' = W(f)(J)·W(R'+)), and comes with the multiplicative map ♯_J: R → A, x ↦ θ_J([x]) (θ_J the quotient map), with ♯_J(ϖ) = π. That (A, A+) is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R, R+) is P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.
hypotheses: J primitive of degree 1; the choice of ϖ does not matter.
proofSteps: A+ is [ϖ]-torsion free and [ϖ]-adically complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element), so (A+, πA+) is a pair of definition of the complete Hausdorff Huber ring A = A+[1/π], and π is a topologically nilpotent unit.
Independence of ϖ: two pseudo-uniformizers of R+ divide powers of each other.
W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] = W^b(R): [ϖ]^{-n}Σp^m[x_m] = Σp^m[ϖ^{-n}x_m] (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.2).
Functoriality: W(f) induces the map; J' = W(f)(J)W(R'+) by P1/distinguished-element-criterion (b).
acceptance: J = (p) returns (R, R+) (Berkeley Lemma 6.2.8 remark).
For R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, J = (p − [t]) gives the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7).

nodes.title: The tilt of W(R+)/J is R+, and θ for W(R+)/J is the quotient map
nodes.statement: In the situation of P1/untilt-construction, let A+ = W(R+)/J and θ_J: W(R+) → A+ the quotient map. Then (a) A+/p ≅ R+/ξ_0R+ for a generator ξ (ξ_0 its zeroth Witt coordinate), Frobenius on A+/p is surjective, and x ↦ (θ_J([x^{1/p^n}]))_n is a multiplicative bijection R+ → lim_{x↦x^p} A+ whose composite with reduction is a ring isomorphism R+ ≅ lim_Φ A+/p = PreTilt A+ p; (b) under this identification Mathlib's θ for A+ (WittVector.fontaineTheta A+ p) is θ_J, so ker θ_{A+} = J; (c) R = R+[1/ϖ] ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A as monoids (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.3.7; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.14: ♯ = θ ∘ [·]).
hypotheses: J = ξW(R+) primitive; A+ is p-adically complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element (d)).
proofSteps: (a) W(R+)/(ξ, p) = R+/ξ_0 with ξ_0 topologically nilpotent; lim_Φ R+/ξ_0 = R+ because R+ is perfect and ξ_0-adically complete (ξ_0 ∈ ϖ'R+ for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ', Stacks Tag 090T; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.4.2); Frobenius on R+/ξ_0 is surjective.

lim_{x↦x^p} A+ ≅ lim_Φ A+/p multiplicatively (Mathlib Perfection.quotientMulEquiv for the p-adically complete A+), and the composite of x ↦ (θ_J[x^{1/p^n}])_n with it is x ↦ (x^{1/p^n} mod ξ_0)_n, the isomorphism R+ ≅ lim_Φ R+/ξ_0.
(b) θ_J and Mathlib's θ for A+ are ring maps W(R+) → A+ with [x] ↦ θ_J([x]) = x♯; uniqueness (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7) gives equality. (c) invert ϖ and π = θ_J([ϖ]).
acceptance: For J = (p): A+ = R+ and the identification is the identity.
For J = (p − [p♭]) ⊆ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): A+ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and this is PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}.

nodes.title: An integral perfectoid ring with a nonzerodivisor π gives a perfectoid Tate ring R_0[1/π] (BMS1 Lemma 3.21)
nodes.statement: Let R_0 be π-adically complete and π-torsion free for some π with π^p | p, with Frobenius surjective on R_0/p and Φ: R_0/π → R_0/π^p bijective (equivalently R_0 is integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5, with π a nonzerodivisor: BMS1 Lemma 3.10). Then R := R_0[1/π], with R_0 open and π-adic, is a complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring; after replacing π by a unit multiple with compatible p-power roots π^{1/p^n} ∈ R_0 (BMS1 Lemma 3.9), R° = {x ∈ R : π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0 for all n} (the almost elements of R_0), R_0 ⊆ R° and πR° ⊆ R_0; R°/R_0 is killed by every π^{1/p^n}.
hypotheses: π a nonzerodivisor; π^p | p in R_0.
proofSteps: Roots: BMS1 Lemma 3.9 gives a unit u with uπ admitting compatible p-power roots in R_0; replace π.
Topology: (R_0, πR_0) is a pair of definition; R is complete Hausdorff and Tate with pseudo-uniformizer π.
Let R_0* := {x ∈ R : π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0 ∀n}. Φ: R_0*/π^{1/p} → R_0*/π is injective, and x ∈ R, x^p ∈ R_0* ⇒ x ∈ R_0* by descending induction on k with π^{k/p}x ∈ R_0* (Sch12 Lemma 5.7).

R° = R_0*: R_0* ⊆ π^{-1}R_0 is bounded; if x is power-bounded then π^{1/p^n}x is topologically nilpotent, so (π^{1/p^n}x)^{p^N} ∈ R_0 for large N, hence π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0* by p-root closedness, for all n, so x ∈ R_0* (Sch12 Lemma 5.6).

R is uniform, π^p | p in R°, and Frobenius on R°/π is surjective (almost surjectivity from R_0 plus the Sch12 Lemma 5.6 argument with z = y/π^{1/p²}); so R is perfectoid (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
acceptance: R_0 = ℤ_p^cycl, π = ζ_{p²} − 1: R = ℚ_p^cycl and R° = R_0.
R_0 = the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]: R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with R° = R_0 (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).

nodes.title: The untilt along a primitive ideal is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R, R+) (converse construction of ECD 3.17)
nodes.statement: For (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and J ⊆ W(R+) primitive of degree 1, the untilt (A, A+) of P1/untilt-construction is a perfectoid Tate pair: A is a perfectoid Tate ring, A+ = W(R+)/J is a ring of integral elements of A (open, integrally closed, contained in A°), A°/A+ is almost zero, and the identification R+ ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A+ of P1/untilt-tilt-identification extends to an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (R, R+) ≅ (A♭, A♭+) under which ker θ_A = J (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.14 and 2.7.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.8; the converse functor of ECD Theorem 3.17 and Berkeley Theorem 6.2.11 "with its topology and plus ring").
hypotheses: J primitive.
proofSteps: A+ is integral perfectoid: π-adically complete and π-torsion free for π := θ_J([ϖ^{1/p}]) (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element), π^p | p (p = ξ − [ϖ]α maps to −θ_J([ϖ])θ_J(α)), Frobenius surjective on A+/p, and θ for A+ has principal kernel J (P1/untilt-tilt-identification (b)); Φ: A+/π → A+/π^p is bijective by BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i).
By P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid, A = A+[1/π] is a perfectoid Tate ring with A+ ⊆ A° and πA° ⊆ A+ (A°/A+ almost zero).

Tilt: A♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} A ≅ R compatibly with the ring structures (P1/untilt-tilt-identification (a), (c); the ring structure of A♭ is transported from lim_Φ A+/π, which is R+ as a ring), and ker θ_A = J.

A+ is a ring of integral elements: it is open (it contains πA°) and it is the preimage of its image in A°/π ≅ A♭°/ϖ ≅ R°/ϖ, which is R+/ϖ, integrally closed in R°/ϖ; so A+ is the ring of integral elements corresponding to R+ under P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.
acceptance: (the completed perfection of F_p((t)), J = (p − [t])) gives (ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7).
J = (p) returns (R, R+).

nodes.title: Untilts are classified by primitive ideals of degree 1 (ECD Theorem 3.17)
nodes.statement: (ECD Theorem 3.17; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.8; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.3.9; Berkeley Theorem 6.2.11) The functors (S, S+) ↦ (S♭, S♭+, ker θ_S) and (R, R+, J) ↦ (W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R+)/J) are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between (i) perfectoid Tate pairs (S, S+) with morphisms of Huber pairs and (ii) triples (R, R+, J) with (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and J ⊆ W(R+) primitive of degree 1, a morphism being a morphism f of pairs with W(f)(J) ⊆ J' (then J' = W(f)(J)W(R'+)). The unit is induced by θ_S: W(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ker θ ≅ S, the counit is the identification of P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair, and both are natural. Characteristic-p pairs correspond to J = (p).
hypotheses: No perfectoid base field; both characteristics.
proofSteps: Forward functor: P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, P1/tilt-functoriality; ker θ is primitive (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel) and morphisms respect kernels (P1/theta-kernel-base-change).
Backward functor: P1/untilt-construction and P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.
Unit: θ_S induces W(S♭+)/ker θ ≅ S+ and, after inverting [ϖ♭], S, compatibly with topologies and plus rings (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (d)). Counit: P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.
Naturality: θ is natural (θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R, P1/theta-kernel-base-change).
acceptance: For (K♭, K♭°) with K a perfectoid field and J = ker θ, the construction returns (K, K°).
Over F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: J = (p) gives the field itself, J = (p − [t]) the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), J = (Σ_{i<p}[1+t]^{i/p}) the field ℚ_p^cycl; φ(J) gives Frobenius-twisted markings.

nodes.title: Marked untilts of a perfectoid pair of characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. A marked untilt of (R, R+) is a triple (S, S+, ι) with (S, S+) a perfectoid Tate pair and ι: (S♭, S♭+) ≅ (R, R+) an isomorphism of Huber pairs; a morphism (S, S+, ι) → (S', S'+, ι') is a morphism f of Huber pairs with ι' ∘ f♭ = ι. By P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, (S, S+, ι) ↦ W(ι)(ker θ_S) is an equivalence from marked untilts to the discrete category of primitive ideals J ⊆ W(R+): a marked untilt has no nontrivial automorphisms and isomorphic marked untilts are uniquely isomorphic. Marked untilts pull back along morphisms of pairs (R, R+) → (R', R'+) (J ↦ J·W(R'+)); marked untilts of (R, R+) and of (R, R°) correspond (plus rings correspond, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting); pS = 0 iff J = (p), the marked untilt (R, R+, id).
hypotheses: (R, R+) of characteristic p; the marking ι is part of the data.
proofSteps: Equivalence: fully faithful because morphisms of untilts over (R, R+) are determined by their tilts (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals); the primitive ideal is an invariant, and ofPrimitive realises every J.
No automorphisms: an automorphism of (S, S+, ι) has f♭ = id, hence f = id.
acceptance: (ℂ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p}, can) is the marked untilt of (ℂ_p♭, 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) with ideal (p − [p♭]).

nodes.title: Strict inclusions correspond under tilting (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2)
nodes.statement: A continuous ring homomorphism f: A → B of complete Hausdorff Tate rings is a strict inclusion if it is injective and a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology (equivalently, as A is complete, a topological ring isomorphism onto a closed subring). Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯, and f: A → B continuous. (a) If B is a perfectoid Tate ring, f is a strict inclusion if and only if f♭: A♭ → B♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality) is (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2). (b) More generally, let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and B♭ its tilt (P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring; f(ϖ) = (f♭ϖ♭)♯ has compatible roots and f(ϖ)^p | p in B°). For the spectral gauges |·|_ϖ, |·|_{f(ϖ)}, |·|_{ϖ♭}, |·|_{f♭ϖ♭}: f is a strict inclusion iff |f(a)| = |a| for all a ∈ A; f♭ is a strict inclusion iff it is isometric; and f is a strict inclusion iff f♭ is. The analogous statement for injections that are not strict is Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.9.13 and is not part of this node.
hypotheses: A perfectoid; in (b) B only complete, Hausdorff and uniform (p is topologically nilpotent in B because it is in A).
Strictness is a topological condition; injectivity alone does not suffice (acceptance).
proofSteps: Strict ⇔ isometric: f(A°) ⊆ B° (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) gives |f(a)| ≤ |a|. If f is a strict inclusion, {a : f(a) ∈ B°} is bounded in A, so it lies in ϖ^{-N}A° and |a| ≤ 2^N|f(a)|; applied to a^{p^n} with power-multiplicativity (P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion (a)) this gives |a| ≤ 2^{N/p^n}|f(a)| for all n, so |a| ≤ |f(a)|. Conversely an isometry is injective and a homeomorphism onto its image, because the gauges define the topologies. The same applies to f♭ between the perfect uniform Tate rings A♭ and B♭.

f isometric ⇒ f♭ isometric: |f♭(x)| = |(f♭x)♯| = |f(x♯)| = |x♯| = |x| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp for A; P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c) for B; (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (d)). This is the direction "obvious from the definition of A♭ as a topological space" in Kedlaya's proof.

f♭ isometric ⇒ f isometric: for a ≠ 0 take y ∈ A♭ with |a − y♯| ≤ |p||a| (P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c)). If pA = 0 then a = y♯ and |f(a)| = |f♭(y)| = |y| = |a|. Otherwise |y| = |a|, |f(y♯)| = |f♭(y)| = |a|, and |f(a) − f(y♯)| ≤ |a − y♯| < |a|, so |f(a)| = |a|.

Kedlaya's proof of ⇐ in (a) untilts instead: A = W^b(A♭)/(z) and B = W^b(B♭)/(z) for a primitive generator z of ker θ_A (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, P1/theta-kernel-base-change), and zW(B♭⁺) ∩ W(A♭⁺) = zW(A♭⁺) by [z̄_0]-adic successive approximation (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.1; its second displayed equality has a misprint, recorded in sourceIssues). The gauge argument above covers the uniform target of (b), which the untilting argument does not.
acceptance: A finite extension K ⊆ L of perfectoid fields is a strict inclusion, and so is K♭ ⊆ L♭ (absolute values extend).

Non-example of strictness: for a perfectoid field K, the continuous injection K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{1/p^n} ↦ (ϖT)^{1/p^n}, is not strict (|T^N| = 1 while |(ϖT)^N| = 2^{-N}), and its tilt T ↦ ϖ♭T is not strict either.
Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4: the untilt B₀ of the closure of f♭(A♭) maps to a uniform B by a strict inclusion because B₀♭ → B♭ is one, by (b) (P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion).

nodes.title: R perfectoid Tate ⇔ R+ integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.20)
nodes.statement: (BMS1 Lemma 3.20) Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements. If R is a perfectoid Tate ring, then R+ (and R°) is an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5 (π-adically complete for some π with π^p dividing p up to a unit, Frobenius surjective on R₀/p, and the kernel of θ : A_inf(R₀) → R₀ principal). Conversely, if R+ is integral perfectoid and bounded in R, then R is a perfectoid Tate ring. Together with P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.21) this is the comparison between the integral notion of BMS1 Definition 3.5, on which PerfectoidQuotients Q0 builds, and the Tate-ring notion of this layer; the Q0 node records it as unproved in its own sources and imports it from here.
hypotheses: R Tate; boundedness of R+ is needed for the converse (a non-bounded R+ cannot occur inside a uniform R).
proofSteps: (⇒) R+ is ϖ-adically complete for ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete, P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (a)); ker θ is principal (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel, or BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii) from bijectivity of Φ: R+/ϖ → R+/ϖ^p and ϖ a nonzerodivisor).

(⇐) ϖR° ⊆ R+ for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, so R° is bounded; a pseudo-uniformizer π with π^p | p in R° exists by the BMS1 argument (a unit multiple of a pseudo-uniformizer is θ([π♭]), and a high p-power root works); then Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (write πx = y^p + pπz with y, z ∈ R+ and y/π^{1/p} ∈ R°).
acceptance: ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}] are integral perfectoid (BMS1 Example 3.6), and ℚ_p^cycl, ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ are perfectoid Tate rings.
Perfect F_p-algebras are integral perfectoid with π = 0, but with the discrete topology they are not Tate: the comparison needs R Tate.

nodes.title: Perfectoid R-algebras are equivalent to perfectoid R°a-algebras (Sch12 §5, over an arbitrary perfectoid base)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, and (R°, R°°) its almost setup (P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). Call an R°a-algebra A perfectoid if A_* (P0 almost elements) is ϖ-torsion free, A is ϖ-adically complete, and Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ is an isomorphism; for R = K a perfectoid field, ϖ-torsion freeness is flatness over K°a and this is Sch12 Definition 5.1(ii). Then: (a) for a ϖ-torsion-free R°-module N, (N^a)_* = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : ϖ^{1/p^n}x ∈ N for all n}; for M with M_* ϖ-torsion free and q ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}: (ϖ^qM)_* = ϖ^qM_*, M_*/ϖ^qM_* ⊆ (M/ϖ^qM)_* and every ε ∈ R°° maps (M/ϖ^qM)_* into M_*/ϖ^qM_*, and M is ϖ-adically complete iff M_* is (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii)–(iv)); (b) for a perfectoid R-algebra S, S°a is a perfectoid R°a-algebra and Φ: S°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ S°/ϖ (Sch12 Proposition 5.5); (c) for a perfectoid R°a-algebra A, S := A_*[1/ϖ] with A_* open and ϖ-adic is a perfectoid R-algebra with S° = A_* and Φ: A_*/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A_*/ϖ (Sch12 Lemmas 5.6–5.7); (d) S ↦ S°a and A ↦ A_*[1/ϖ] are inverse equivalences R-Perf ≃ R°a-Perf.
hypotheses: Over a general base R°, flatness over R°a is not the right condition (perfectoid quotients R → R/I are not flat); ϖ-torsion freeness of A_* replaces it, and coincides with flatness when R° is a valuation ring.
proofSteps: (a) (N^a)_* = Hom(R°°, N) = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : εx ∈ N ∀ε ∈ R°°} with R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R° (P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal); (ϖ^qM)_* = ϖ^qM_* as ϖ^qM_* is ϖ-torsion free; left exactness of (·)_* (right adjoint of (·)^a, P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints) gives the inclusion, and the ε-image statement is Sch12 Lemma 5.3(iii)'s argument; completeness transfer: (·)_* and (·)^a commute with inverse limits (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

(b) Φ is surjective on S°/ϖ^{1/p} → S°/ϖ (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion) and injective: x^p/ϖ power-bounded ⇒ x/ϖ^{1/p} power-bounded (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a)); S° is ϖ-complete and ϖ-torsion free (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete); apply (a).

(c) Sch12 Lemma 5.7: x ∈ S, x^p ∈ A_* ⇒ x ∈ A_*, by descending induction with ϖ^{k/p}x, using injectivity of Φ on A_* and ϖ-torsion freeness. Sch12 Lemma 5.6: a power-bounded x has (εx)^{p^N} ∈ A_* for large N, so εx ∈ A_* for all ε ∈ R°°, so x ∈ A_* by (a); Φ surjective on A_*/ϖ: from almost surjectivity ϖ^{1/p}x ≡ y^p mod ϖA_*, z := y/ϖ^{1/p²} satisfies z^p ≡ x mod ϖ^{(p−1)/p}A_*, z ∈ A_* by Lemma 5.7. S is uniform (S° = A_* bounded) and perfectoid.
(d) The two constructions are inverse by (b), (c) and A = (A_*)^a.
acceptance: For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over a perfectoid field, R° is the ϖ-adic completion of K°[T^{1/p^∞}] and R°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra (Sch12 Proposition 5.20).
The non-surjectivity of M_*/xM_* → (M/xM)_* (Sch12 Remark 5.4) shows that (a) cannot be strengthened to an equality.

nodes.title: Frobenius criterion for vanishing of the (almost) cotangent complex; perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ
nodes.statement: (a) (Gabber–Ramero, arXiv Lemma 6.5.9(i) = LNM 1800 Lemma 6.5.13(i); Sch12 Proposition 5.13(ii); Bhatt Proposition 6.1.4) Let A_0 → B be a map of F_p-algebras such that the relative Frobenius A_0(Φ) ⊗^L_{A_0} B → B(Φ) is an isomorphism in D(A_0). Then L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0. In particular L_{B/F_p} ≃ 0 for B perfect, and L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0 whenever A_0 → B is flat and relatively perfect. (b) The almost version holds over any basic setup (V, m) with V an F_p-algebra: if the relative Frobenius of a map of almost algebras is an isomorphism in the almost derived category, then the almost cotangent complex L^a (P0/almost-cotangent-complex) vanishes. (c) Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ with compatible roots, and A a (R°/ϖ)^a-algebra which is (almost) flat over (R°/ϖ)^a with Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A. Then L^a_{A/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0. For R = K a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Corollary 5.16.
hypotheses: OPTIONAL ALTERNATIVE ROUTE (Scholze 2012's deformation-theoretic proof). No node outside this optional two-node route depends on it (the optional deformation node still uses the optional cotangent lemma): the tilting equivalence (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) and the mod-ϖ equivalence (P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence) are derived from P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals. Keep the node and its sources, but do not schedule it as a prerequisite (RT-AREA-padic-1/5).
The hypothesis in (a) is on the derived relative Frobenius, not on Ω¹ alone.

The classical cotangent complex, its simplicial description, transitivity and Tor-independent base change are requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0; the almost version is P0/almost-cotangent-complex.
proofSteps: (a) Take a simplicial resolution P• of B by free A_0-algebras; the relative Frobenius A_0(Φ) ⊗_{A_0} P• → P•(Φ) sends X_i ↦ X_i^p and is by hypothesis a quasi-isomorphism of simplicial A_0(Φ)-algebras, hence induces A_0(Φ) ⊗^L L_{B/A_0} ≃ L_{B(Φ)/A_0(Φ)} ≃ L_{B/A_0}; on differentials it sends dX_i ↦ d(X_i^p) = 0, so the isomorphism is the zero map and L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0 (GR Lemma 6.5.9 proof; Sch12 Proposition 5.13 proof).
(b) The same argument with almost algebras (Sch12 before Corollary 5.16, "the previous theorems stay true in the almost world"), or apply (a) to B_!! as in Sch12 Corollary 5.16 proof.

(c) A_0 := R°/ϖ is an F_p-algebra (ϖ | p); A_0(Φ) ≅ R°/ϖ^{1/p} as A_0-module via Φ: R°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ R°/ϖ; by flatness A_0(Φ) ⊗^L A = A/ϖ^{1/p}, and the relative Frobenius is the given isomorphism Φ; apply (b).
acceptance: Ω¹_{R/F_p} = 0 for perfect R, since dx = d(y^p) = py^{p−1}dy = 0 (Sch12 Remark 5.14); the degree 0 and 1 parts are Mathlib's KaehlerDifferential and Algebra.H1Cotangent, which vanish for perfect R.
W(R) is the unique flat p-adically complete deformation of a perfect R (Sch12 Remark 5.14; Bhatt Example 6.1.6).

nodes.title: Unique flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ (Sch12 Theorem 5.10, over a perfectoid Tate base)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots. Reduction modulo ϖ, A ↦ A/ϖ, is an equivalence between (i) ϖ-adically complete R°a-algebras A that are (almost) flat over R°a with Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ, and (ii) (almost) flat (R°/ϖ)^a-algebras B with Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B. Concretely B lifts uniquely, through the square-zero extensions (R°/ϖ^n)^a → (R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, to a compatible system of flat (R°/ϖ^n)^a-algebras B_n with B_n/ϖ^{n−1} ≅ B_{n−1}, and A = lim B_n. For R = K a perfectoid field every perfectoid K°a-algebra is flat and this is Sch12 Theorem 5.10, the step K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf of Sch12 Theorem 5.2. Over a general base the flat objects form full subcategories; the full categories are compared, without deformation theory, in P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence.
hypotheses: OPTIONAL ALTERNATIVE ROUTE (Scholze 2012's deformation-theoretic proof). No node outside this optional two-node route depends on it (the optional deformation node still uses the optional cotangent lemma): the tilting equivalence (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) and the mod-ϖ equivalence (P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence) are derived from P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals. Keep the node and its sources, but do not schedule it as a prerequisite (RT-AREA-padic-1/5).
Flatness is over R°a (resp. (R°/ϖ)^a); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R° and ϖ^{n−1}R°/ϖ^nR° ≅ R°/ϖ is square-zero in R°/ϖ^n for n ≥ 2.
Illusie–Gabber–Ramero deformation theory (obstructions in Ext², torsor under Ext¹, automorphisms Hom; lifting of morphisms) in the almost setting is P0/almost-deformation-theory.
proofSteps: L^a_{B/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0 (P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi (c)).

For a flat lift B_{n−1} over (R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, flat base change gives L^a_{B_{n−1}/(R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ⊗^L (R°/ϖ)^a ≃ L^a_{B/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0, so L^a_{B_{n−1}} ≃ 0 by derived Nakayama for the nilpotent ideal (Bhatt Corollary 6.1.5; Sch12 Theorem 5.10 proof via the transitivity triangle for 0 → B → B_n → B_{n−1} → 0).

All obstructions and ambiguities for lifting B_{n−1} to a flat (R°/ϖ^n)^a-algebra, and for lifting morphisms, lie in Ext groups of this vanishing complex (P0/almost-deformation-theory; Sch12 Theorems 5.11–5.12), so lifts exist and are unique up to unique isomorphism.
A := lim B_n is ϖ-adically complete with A/ϖ^n = B_n, flat, and Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ is inherited from B (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

nodes.title: In characteristic p, perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ lift explicitly by the inverse limit along Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let T be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, t = (t♭)♯ a pseudo-uniformizer (its p-power roots are unique) and (T°, T°°) its almost setup. Let Λ := F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) with x ↦ t. (a) For a (T°/t)^a-algebra B that is almost flat over Λ for the root ideal (equivalently, for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] ∩ (0, 1), the kernel of t^q on B_* is t^{1−q}B_* up to almost zero) with Φ: B/t^{1/p} → B an isomorphism, the inverse limit B̃ := lim_Φ B (in almost T°a-algebras) is perfect, t-adically complete and t-torsion free with B̃/t ≅ B; (b) conversely lim_Φ(B̃/t) ≅ B̃ for such B̃; (c) hence reduction mod t is an equivalence between perfect, t-adically complete, t-torsion-free T°a-algebras (the perfectoid T°a-algebras, Bhatt Example 6.2.4(1)) and Λ-flat (T°/t)^a-algebras with Φ: B/t^{1/p} ≅ B; (d) with P1/almost-integral-dictionary, T-Perf ≃ these categories (Sch12 Remark 5.18: the lifting "can be made explicit by means of the inverse limit over the Frobenius").
hypotheses: pT = 0; Λ-flatness replaces flatness over (T°/t)^a, which fails for quotients.
proofSteps: (b) For B̃ perfect and t-adically complete, lim_Φ B̃/t = lim_{x↦x^p} B̃ = B̃ (Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.4.2 and Remark 3.4.10; Mathlib Perfection.quotientMulEquiv, the ring structures agreeing as p = 0).

(a) The transition maps Φ: B → B are surjective with kernel t^{1/p}B (Φ factors through B/t^{1/p} ≅ B), so B̃ → B is surjective; its kernel is {(b_n) : b_0 = 0}, and Λ-flatness gives unique compatible b_n/t^{1/p^n} (well defined modulo t^{1−1/p^n}B, whose p-th powers vanish), so the kernel is t♭B̃; t-torsion freeness and completeness follow in the same way (Sch12 Proposition 5.17 proof; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.3.7).
(c),(d) Bhatt Example 6.2.4(1) and P1/almost-integral-dictionary.
acceptance: For B = T°/t: lim_Φ B = T°.

nodes.title: Tilting equivalence Perf_R ≃ Perf_{R♭} over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring, with the explicit tilt
nodes.statement: (ECD Theorem 3.13; Berkeley Theorem 6.2.7; Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.17; Sch12 Theorem 5.2 over a perfectoid field) Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ and J_R := ker(θ_R: W(R♭°) → R°), a primitive ideal (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel). The tilting functor S ↦ S♭ (R♭ → S♭ the tilt of R → S, P1/tilt-functoriality) is an equivalence from perfectoid R-algebras to perfectoid R♭-algebras, with quasi-inverse T ↦ T♯ := W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]/J_R·W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]], the untilt along J_R·W(T°) (P1/untilt-construction); the unit S ≅ (S♭)♯ is induced by θ_S and the counit (T♯)♭ ≅ T by P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair, both natural. Explicitly S♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} S, S♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} S° ≅ lim_Φ S°/ϖ and S♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ S°/ϖ; the functor is independent of choices, extends to pairs (S, S+) ↦ (S♭, S♭+), and S is a perfectoid field iff S♭ is (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field). For R = K a perfectoid field, T♯ = W(T°) ⊗_{W(K♭°)} K°[1/ϖ] (Sch12 Remark 5.19; Bhatt Remark 6.2.8), and the functor agrees with Sch12's chain K-Perf ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf ≃ K♭°a-Perf ≃ K♭-Perf.
hypotheses: No perfectoid base field; continuous homomorphisms between Tate rings preserve power-bounded elements into uniform targets (API of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so R-algebras are pairs over (R, R°).
proofSteps: Slice categories: perfectoid R-algebras are perfectoid pairs (S, S°) with a morphism from (R, R°); under P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals they correspond to triples (T, T°, J) with a morphism from (R♭, R♭°, J_R), i.e. J = J_R·W(T°) (P1/theta-kernel-base-change), i.e. to perfectoid R♭-algebras T (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.17).
Explicit tilt: P1/tilt-integral-subrings applied to S; field case: P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field.
Consistency with Sch12 for R = K: both functors send S to the unique T with (T°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (S°/ϖ)^a over K°/ϖ ≅ K♭°/ϖ♭ (Bhatt Corollary 6.2.6; P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence).
acceptance: (Sch12 Proposition 5.20; Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15) The tilt of R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ is R♭⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ with T_i♯ = T_i (P1/perfected-tate-algebra).

nodes.title: Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with them (Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let J be a small filtered category and j ↦ R_j a functor from J to perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms φ_a: R_i → R_j (no injectivity, flatness or density assumed; characteristic 0, p or neither; no perfectoid base field). Fix j₀ ∈ J and a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ ∈ R_{j₀}♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯ (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots); on the tail J_{j₀} = Under j₀ (final in J, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`) the images of ϖ and of its roots are pseudo-uniformizers with compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in every R_j° (a compatible pseudo-uniformizer). Put A := colim_j R_j° (filtered colimit of rings, Mathlib `CommRingCat.FilteredColimits`), R_0 := its ϖ-adic completion lim_n A/ϖ^nA, and R := R_0[1/ϖ], topologised with R_0 open carrying its ϖ-adic topology. Then: (a) R is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and ring of definition R_0; ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R_0 and R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = colim_j R_j°/ϖ^n; the canonical maps ι_j: R_j → R are continuous and compatible, and the image of colim R_j is dense; for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring S and compatible continuous ring homomorphisms ψ_j: R_j → S there is a unique continuous ψ: R → S with ψ ∘ ι_j = ψ_j; R is independent of j₀ and ϖ, and replacing R_j° by rings of integral elements R_j⁺ (compatible under the φ_a) gives the same R, since ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j⁺ ⊆ R_j°; (b) R is a perfectoid Tate ring; R_0 is ϖ-adically complete and integral perfectoid, R_0 ⊆ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R_0 for all n; so R, with the ι_j, is the colimit of the R_j in perfectoid Tate rings and in complete Hausdorff uniform Tate rings; (c) tilting commutes with completed filtered colimits: the R_j♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality) form a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p with compatible pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭, and the continuous homomorphism from their completed colimit T (as in (a), with ring of definition the ϖ♭-adic completion of colim R_j♭°) to R♭ induced by the ι_j♭ is an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings, compatible with ♯; dually, for a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and a filtered system of perfectoid R′♭-algebras T_j, the untilt over R′ (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) of their completed colimit is the completed colimit of the untilts T_j♯. PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs builds the same ring from plus rings along a cofiltered diagram of pairs and P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid adds the statements about the plus ring.
hypotheses: J small and filtered (hence nonempty); every R_j a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1; transition maps continuous.

The R_j must be perfectoid: a completed colimit of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid (ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})) without its tilt being the colimit of the tilts (test completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower); such limits are tilde-limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P7).
proofSteps: Compatible pseudo-uniformizer: continuous ring homomorphisms map units to units, topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent ones and R_{j₀}° into R_j° (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so the images of ϖ♭'s coordinates are compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in R_j°; parallel morphisms j₀ ⇉ j may give different images, which agree in A. Restricting to Under j₀ does not change the colimit (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget).

(a) A exists (mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A as it is a unit in each R_j. The ϖ-adic completion R_0 is ϖ-adically complete with R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = A/ϖ^nA (Stacks Tag 05GG for the finitely generated ideal ϖA; mathlib:AdicCompletion) and ϖ-torsion free (if ϖ·(x_n)_n = 0 in lim A/ϖ^n then x_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^nA, so x_n = 0). R := R_0[1/ϖ] with basis {ϖ^nR_0} is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. R_j° is open and bounded in R_j with its ϖ-adic topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero), so R_j° → A → R_0 is continuous and extends to ι_j on R_j = R_j°[1/ϖ]. Universal property: ψ_j(R_j°) ⊆ S° (S uniform), S° is open, bounded and ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so the induced A → S° extends uniquely to R_0 and to R; uniqueness from density of A in R_0. Independence: two compatible pseudo-uniformizers define cofinal filtrations on A (at a common stage each divides a power of the other), and colim R_j⁺ ⊆ A ⊆ ϖ^{-1}·colim R_j⁺ because ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j°° ⊆ R_j⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), so both completions give the same R.

(b) ϖ^p | p in A, hence in R_0. Φ: A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is the filtered colimit of the bijections Φ_j: R_j°/ϖ → R_j°/ϖ^p (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer, P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), hence bijective, and so is Φ: R_0/ϖ → R_0/ϖ^p since R_0/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n. By the successive-approximation argument of P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion ((i) ⇒ (ii), which uses only ϖ-adic completeness) Frobenius on R_0/p is surjective. So R_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii), P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison), and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes R = R_0[1/ϖ] a perfectoid Tate ring with R_0 ⊆ R° and R°/R_0 killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}. The colimit statement is (a) together with perfectoidness.

(c) The R_j♭ are perfectoid of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) with transition maps φ_a♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality); by (a) and (b) their completed colimit T is perfectoid, with ring of definition T_0 and T_0/ϖ♭ = colim_j R_j♭°/ϖ♭. The ι_j♭ induce χ: T → R♭ (universal property (a); R♭ is uniform). Modulo ϖ♭, T_0/ϖ♭ = colim R_j♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ colim R_j°/ϖ = R_0/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c), compatibly with the φ_a), and R_0/ϖ → R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ is an almost isomorphism (its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, by (b)); likewise T_0/ϖ♭ → T°/ϖ♭. So χ induces an isomorphism (T°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (R♭°/ϖ♭)^a of perfectoid (R_{j₀}♭°a/ϖ♭)-algebras, and χ is an isomorphism by P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence over the base R_{j₀}♭ (Sch12 Theorem 5.2: perfectoid algebras are determined by their reduction modulo ϖ; Bhatt Remark 6.2.9). Compatibility with ♯ holds coordinatewise.
(c) dual form: apply (c) to the system T_j♯, whose tilts are the T_j (counit of P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), and use full faithfulness of untilting.
acceptance: Sch12 proof of Theorem 3.7 and Bhatt, proof of almost purity over a field: for M the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭, M is the completed colimit of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ and the union of the L♯ is dense in M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 4.6: the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebras is perfectoid; here without a base field.
Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22: the completion of a filtered direct limit of Fontaine perfectoid Banach rings, for the infimum of the spectral norms, is perfectoid.

uses.how: the Krasner step: the untilt of the completed algebraic closure M of K♭ is the completed colimit of the untilts of the finite extensions of K♭ in M, (c)
the completed colimit of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings, with ring of definition the completed colimit of the R_j°, is perfectoid, (a)–(b)
perfectoidness and tilt of the completed direct limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces; P5 adds the plus rings

uses.where: Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2 and proof of Theorem 3.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22
uses.how: filtered colimits of perfectoid algebras and their tilts in the sources

tests.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_const
tests.statement: For J with a terminal object j (in particular a one-object J), completedFilteredColimit F ≃+* F.obj j as topological rings, compatibly with ι_j.

tests.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_locallyConstant
tests.statement: For a perfectoid field K and a profinite set S = lim S_i (finite S_i), the completed colimit of the perfectoid rings K^{S_i} = C(S_i, K) is C^0(S, K) with the sup norm, and its ring of definition is C^0(S, K°).

tests.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_tilt_algebraicClosure
tests.statement: For a perfectoid field K, tiltEquiv identifies (completion of an algebraic closure of K♭) with the tilt of the completed colimit of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L of K♭ inside it; the union of the L♯ is dense in the untilt.

tests.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower
tests.statement: For p odd, the fields ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n}) are not perfectoid and their tilts in the sense of P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring are 𝔽_p, while the completion ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ is perfectoid with tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: tilting does not commute with completed colimits of non-perfectoid rings, so the hypothesis that every R_j be perfectoid cannot be dropped.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit
api.statement: completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ : Type, for F : J ⥤ (perfectoid Tate rings, continuous homomorphisms) with J filtered and ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with roots of F.obj j₀; CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition
api.statement: R_0 = AdicCompletion (span {ϖ}) (colim (F ⋙ powerBoundedSubring)), an open bounded subring with its ϖ-adic topology; R = Localization.Away ϖ R_0; R_0 ⧸ ϖ^n ≃+* colim (R_j° ⧸ ϖ^n).

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ι
api.statement: ι j : F.obj j →+* completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, continuous, with (ι j).comp (F.map a) = ι i for a : i ⟶ j in Under j₀.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.lift
api.statement: For S complete Hausdorff uniform Tate and compatible continuous ψ j : F.obj j →+* S: lift ψ continuous with (lift ψ).comp (ι j) = ψ j (lift_comp_ι), and hom_ext for two continuous maps agreeing on all ι j.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing
api.statement: IsPerfectoidTateRing (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭).

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition_almostEq
api.statement: R_0 ≤ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n} • R° ≤ R_0 for all n (R°/R_0 is almost zero for P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.denseRange
api.statement: The ring homomorphism colim F → completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ has dense range.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.tiltEquiv
api.statement: tilt (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭) ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (F ⋙ tiltFunctor) ϖ♭.toTilt, a homeomorphism commuting with sharp and sending tilt.map (ι j) to ι j.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv
api.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and G : J ⥤ perfectoid R′♭-algebras: the untilt over R′ of completedFilteredColimit G is isomorphic to completedFilteredColimit (G ⋙ untiltFunctor R′), naturally in G.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.equivOfChoice
api.statement: Changing (j₀, ϖ♭) or restricting along a final functor J′ ⥤ J gives canonically isomorphic rings, compatibly with ι and lift; using compatible rings of integral elements instead of R_j° gives the same ring.

api.name: Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isColimit
api.statement: The cocone (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, ι) is a colimit in the category of perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms.

sources.match: Filtered colimits of perfectoid algebras are completions of the uncompleted colimit, (a)–(b).

nodes.title: Perfected Tate algebras R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ in any set of variables over any perfectoid Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (ϖ^p | p in R°) and Σ an arbitrary set, possibly infinite. The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is A_0[1/ϖ], where A_0 is the ϖ-adic completion of the monoid algebra R°[T^a : a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}] (AddMonoidAlgebra over the finitely supported exponent vectors Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}, T^a = Π_s T_s^{a(s)}), topologised with A_0 open and ϖ-adic; equivalently the completion of the perfect polynomial ring R[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] for the topology in which R°[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] is open with its ϖ-adic topology (the Gauss norm). It is a perfectoid Tate ring with R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩° = A_0 = {Σ_a c_aT^a : c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on exponents}; R⁺⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a ring of integral elements for every R⁺. Universal property: for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and every family, indexed by s ∈ Σ, of compatible systems (t_s^{(m)})_{m≥0} in S° with (t_s^{(m+1)})^p = t_s^{(m)}, there is a unique continuous R-algebra map R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ t_s^{(m)}; for S perfectoid such families are families (x_s) in S♭°, via t_s^{(m)} = (x_s^{1/p^m})♯. Its tilt is R♭⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, so T_s♯ = T_s. The construction is functorial in Σ, and R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is the completed filtered colimit (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings) of the algebras in finitely many of the variables. For Σ = {1, …, n} it is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩, which contains Tau Ceti's R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ as the closed subring of series with exponents in ℕ^n, with a continuous R-linear retraction σ(Σ x_aT^a) = Σ_{a ∈ ℕ^n} x_aT^a; the Laurent variant R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid as well (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12 for arbitrary index sets).
hypotheses: R perfectoid with no base field; Σ any set (Σ = ∅ gives R).
Infinite Σ is used: P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base takes Σ = C♭° (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21), and Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7 takes Σ = C♭⁺.
proofSteps: A_0 is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (a completed free R°-module on the monomials, with c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter), with A_0/ϖ = (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ]; Φ: A_0/ϖ → A_0/ϖ^p is bijective coefficientwise (R° perfectoid) and on monomials (a ↦ pa is bijective on ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}), and Frobenius on A_0/p is surjective; so A_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)) and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes A_0[1/ϖ] perfectoid with A_0 ⊆ A° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_0.
A° = A_0: if ϖ^{1/p^m}x ∈ A_0 for all m then every coefficient c_a satisfies ϖ^{1/p^m}c_a ∈ R° for all m, hence c_a ∈ R° (R° = its own almost elements, P1/almost-integral-dictionary (a)).

Universal property: T^a ↦ Π_s (t_s^{(m)})^{k_s} for a = (k_s/p^m)_s is a well-defined R°-algebra map R°[T^a] → S° (compatibility of the systems; continuous maps into the uniform S send R° into S°, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); it is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, and S° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so it extends uniquely to A_0 and to A_0[1/ϖ]; uniqueness from density of R[T_s^{1/p^∞}].

Tilt: the ring map R♭°⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → lim_{x↦x^p} A_0, T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, reduces modulo ϖ♭ to the identity of (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] = (R♭°/ϖ♭)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); both sides are ϖ♭-adically complete and torsion free, so it is an isomorphism; invert ϖ♭ (P1/sharp-map for T_s♯ = T_s).

Finitely many variables: for finite Σ_0 ⊆ Σ, A_0(Σ_0) ⊆ A_0(Σ), the union is dense and A_0(Σ)/ϖ^n = colim_{Σ_0} A_0(Σ_0)/ϖ^n, which is the description of the completed colimit in P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (a). A map g: Σ → Σ′ induces T_s ↦ T_{g(s)} by the universal property.
The subring R⟨T⟩ and σ for Σ = {1, …, n}: σ is continuous and R-linear and splits the inclusion (it is not multiplicative).
acceptance: ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = A[1/p] with A the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}] (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).
The tilt of K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (Sch12 Proposition 5.20).

For perfectoid B, C over a Tate ring A, P := B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩ with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ inr((s^{1/p^m})♯) maps to the uniform completed tensor product with dense image (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21; P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base).

uses.how: R̃⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over an arbitrary perfectoid R̃ with ι and σ is a perfectoid frame of R⟨T⟩ (Σ = {1, …, n})
the perfectoid relative ball B^{N,perf}_X = Spa(A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, A+⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)
the perfectoid polydisc
the perfectoid ring B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩ in infinitely many variables and its universal property, mapping densely to B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21)

uses.where: Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13
uses.how: C̃ = A⟨T_s^{p^{-∞}} : s ∈ C♭⁺⟩ surjecting onto C, for completed tensor products of perfectoid rings

uses.where: ECD Example 3.4(iii); Sch12 Proposition 5.20; Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12
uses.how: the example in the sources

tests.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_empty_test
tests.statement: perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R as topological rings.

tests.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X_pow
tests.statement: (X s (1/p^{m+1}))^p = X s (1/p^m), and Frobenius on A_0/ϖ sends the class of X s (1/p) to that of X s 1; for Σ = ℕ the series Σ_k ϖ^k X k 1 converges while Σ_k X k 1 does not.

tests.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tilt_cyclotomic
tests.statement: tilt (ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≃+* (tilt ℚ_p^cycl)⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (ECD Example 3.4(iii); Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).

tests.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_fin_test
tests.statement: For Σ = Fin n, perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ of the AdicSpacesPartII request, restrictedIncl embeds TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R with retraction σ, and for Fin n ⊆ ℕ the map perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) → perfectedTateAlgebra R ℕ is a strict inclusion.

tests.name: Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_restricted
tests.statement: For n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0, R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is not perfectoid: T_1 is not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc).

tests.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift_one
tests.statement: lift with t_s^{(m)} = 1 for all s, m is evaluation at T = 1, a continuous R-algebra map to R; two continuous R-algebra maps agreeing on all X s (1/p^m) are equal.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra
api.statement: perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ : Type for Σ : Type*, with CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances and an R-algebra structure.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.isPerfectoidTateRing
api.statement: IsPerfectoidTateRing (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ).

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X
api.statement: X s a = T_s^a for s : Σ and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}; X s (a + b) = X s a * X s b, (X s (a/p))^p = X s a, X s a ∈ A°.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.powerBoundedSubring_eq
api.statement: (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ)° = {Σ c_a T^a | c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}}.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift
api.statement: For a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and a family t : Σ → Perfection S° p (compatible p-power roots in S°), the unique continuous R-algebra map with X s (1/p^m) ↦ coeff m (t s); lift_X and uniqueness (hom_ext).

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.liftTilt
api.statement: For S perfectoid: continuous R-algebra maps perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ → S correspond to maps Σ → (tilt S)°, x ↦ lift (fun s ↦ x s), with sharp (tilt.map (liftTilt x) (X s 1)) = sharp (x s).

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tiltEquiv
api.statement: tilt (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ) ≃+* perfectedTateAlgebra (tilt R) Σ, a homeomorphism with sharp (X s a) = X s a.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.mapIndex
api.statement: For g : Σ → Σ′, the continuous R-algebra map with X s a ↦ X (g s) a; mapIndex id = id, mapIndex (g′ ∘ g) = mapIndex g′ ∘ mapIndex g.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.equivCompletedColimit
api.statement: perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (Σ₀ ↦ perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ₀) over finite subsets Σ₀ ⊆ Σ (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings).

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.restrictedIncl
api.statement: For Σ = Fin n: the continuous injective R-algebra map from TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R (R⟨T⟩) with closed image, T_i ↦ X i 1.

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.retraction
api.statement: For Σ = Fin n: the continuous R-linear map σ onto integral exponents with σ ∘ restrictedIncl = id (the frame of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings).

api.name: Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.plus

nodes.title: The completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field; its tilt and primitive ideal
nodes.statement: The completion ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is a perfectoid field: its valuation ring is the p-adic completion ℤ_p^cycl of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}], its value group |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)} is nondiscrete and Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective. Its tilt is the completed perfection of F_p((t)) with t = ε − 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …), with |t♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (Berkeley Example 6.2.4), and it is the untilt of (F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^) along the primitive ideal generated by Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[1 + t]^{i/p} (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.8). ℤ_p^× acts compatibly, by γ(t) = (1 + t)^γ − 1 on the tilt.
hypotheses: p any prime; ζ_{p^n} a compatible system of primitive p^n-th roots of unity.
proofSteps: ℤ_p[ζ_{p^n}] is the valuation ring of ℚ_p(ζ_{p^n}) with |ζ_{p^n} − 1| = |p|^{1/(p^{n−1}(p−1))}, so the value group is nondiscrete and |p| < 1.

Every element of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}] is Σa_iζ^i with a_i ∈ ℤ_p and ζ ∈ μ_{p^n}, and Σa_iζ^i ≡ (Σa_iζ'^i)^p mod p for ζ'^p = ζ, as a^p ≡ a mod p for a ∈ ℤ_p; so Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.5.12: "trivial to check") and P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation applies.
Tilt: ε ∈ lim ℤ_p^cycl, t = ε − 1 has |t♯| = lim|ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)} < 1, is a pseudo-uniformizer, and K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
Primitive generator: z = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} maps to p under W(K♭°) → W(F_p), so z_1 is a unit, and θ(z) = Σ_{i<p}ζ_p^i = 0; hence ker θ = (z) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c)).
acceptance: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}) is the finite extension K·ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p^cycl, perfectoid by stability of perfectoid fields under finite extension (Sch12 Theorem 3.7(i), Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.5.6), the P3 node P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.
v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1) in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements.

nodes.title: Examples and non-examples of perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Remark 3.3, Example 3.4)
nodes.statement: The following are perfectoid Tate rings, each a declaration of the library: (1) ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p), a perfectoid field whose tilt contains p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) with (p♭)♯ = p; (2) the completion K_1 of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), a perfectoid field with valuation ring the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}] and tilt F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t♯ = p, the untilt along (p − [t]) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7); (3) the completed perfection F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, a perfectoid field of characteristic p equal to its own tilt; (4) ℚ_p^cycl (P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); (5) ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (P1/perfected-tate-algebra); (6) the ring R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ϖ^p = T divides p in R°), which does not contain a nonarchimedean field (ECD Example 3.4(iv); Berkeley Example 6.1.5(4)); (7) products such as K × K♭ for a perfectoid field K, where p is a nonzero nonunit. Non-examples: ℚ_p and every discretely valued nonarchimedean field (ECD Remark 3.3), F_p((t)) (not perfect), ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) (not uniform), R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ for n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0 (T_1 not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p).
hypotheses: Each example is checked against ECD Definition 3.1 through the criteria of this layer.
proofSteps: (1) ℂ_p is algebraically closed with value group |p|^ℚ, so every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(2)); P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation.

(2) K_1° = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^ is generated by the p^{1/p^n}, whose classes are p-th powers modulo p (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(1)); its tilt is computed by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field and it is the untilt along (p − [t]) (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals).
(3) P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. (4) P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field. (5) P1/perfected-tate-algebra.

(6) R° is the displayed ring (bounded); ϖ = T^{1/p} has ϖ^p = T and p = T·(p/T) with p/T ∈ R°; Frobenius R°/T^{1/p} → R°/T is surjective as all topological generators T^{1/p^n}, (p/T)^{1/p^n} and ℤ_p^cycl have p-th roots modulo p (ECD Example 3.4(iv)).

(7) API IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras. Non-examples: P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation, P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced, P1/perfected-tate-algebra.
acceptance: These realise the tests of the stage: completed F_p((t^{1/p^∞})), cyclotomic and compatible-root mixed-characteristic fields, perfected Tate balls and tori, and a non-field perfectoid Tate ring.

nodes.statement: Let F be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of characteristic p with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, as in anchor Layer 6.1. Then (a) F is a perfectoid field of characteristic p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), its tilt is F itself with ♯ the identity (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), and (F, 𝒪_F) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p; (b) the anchor's A_inf = W(𝒪_F), with pair of definition (A_inf, (p, [ϖ])), is the ring W(F♭+) = W(𝒪_F) of this layer, and the anchor's (p, [ϖ])-adic completeness and separatedness of W(𝒪_F) is P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring for (F, 𝒪_F); (c) the untilts of F are the pairs (W(𝒪_F)[1/[ϖ]]/(ξ), W(𝒪_F)/(ξ)) for primitive ξ ∈ A_inf (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). The anchor's curve 𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf) and its Frobenius windows are not re-planned; P1 only identifies the input objects.
hypotheses: F as in anchor Layer 6 (no algebraic closedness).
proofSteps: (a) A complete nontrivially valued perfect field is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid; its value group is p-divisible (perfectness), so not discrete.

nodes.title: The tilting map x ↦ x♭ from Spa(R, R⁺) to Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺) and sharp map ♯ : R♭ → R (continuous and multiplicative, not additive), X = Spa(R, R⁺), X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺). For x ∈ X with valuation v_x : R → Γ_x ∪ {0}, the composite v_x ∘ ♯ : R♭ → Γ_x ∪ {0} is a continuous valuation of R♭ with v_x(f♯) ≤ 1 for all f ∈ R♭⁺; its class is a point x♭ ∈ X♭, characterised by |f(x♭)| ≤ |g(x♭)| ⟺ |f♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)| for all f, g ∈ R♭ (written |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|). The tilting map τ_R : X → X♭, x ↦ x♭, satisfies: (a) supp(x♭) = {f ∈ R♭ : f♯ ∈ supp(x)}; (b) τ_R is continuous: if f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭ and some f_i is a unit of R♭ (for instance f_n = (ϖ♭)^N), then f₁♯, …, f_n♯ generate the unit ideal of R and τ_R⁻¹(U(f₁, …, f_n / g)) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯); every rational subset of X♭ has a presentation with f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺ and f_n = (ϖ♭)^N for some N; (c) τ is natural: for a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with tilt φ♭, τ_R ∘ Spa(φ) = Spa(φ♭) ∘ τ_S; (d) if pR = 0 then (R♭, R♭⁺) = (R, R⁺) with ♯ = id and τ_R = id. That τ_R is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets; here only the map and its first properties are constructed.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) a perfectoid Tate pair (stage conventions); no base field.

For (b): some numerator f_i is a unit of R♭, which makes f_i♯ = (f_i)♯ a unit of R because ♯ is multiplicative with 1♯ = 1; without such a normalisation the unit-ideal condition on f♯ is not automatic before the homeomorphism is known.
For (c): φ continuous, φ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺, and φ♭ its tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), so that φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭.
proofSteps: Valuation axioms: v_x(0♯) = 0, v_x(1♯) = 1 and multiplicativity come from ♯ being multiplicative with 0♯ = 0, 1♯ = 1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).

Strong triangle inequality: by the addition law of the tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) (f + g)♯ = lim_n z_n with z_n = ((f^{1/p^n})♯ + (g^{1/p^n})♯)^{p^n}; v_x(z_n) ≤ M := max(v_x(f♯), v_x(g♯)). If M ≠ 0, continuity of v_x makes {w : v_x(w) < M} an open neighbourhood of 0, so v_x((f + g)♯ − z_n) < M for large n and v_x((f + g)♯) ≤ M; if M = 0 then all z_n lie in supp(v_x), which is closed (an intersection of the open, hence closed, subgroups {v_x < γ}), so (f + g)♯ ∈ supp(v_x) (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.12; Sch12 proof of Proposition 3.6).

Continuity of v_x ∘ ♯: {f : v_x(f♯) < γ} = ♯⁻¹{v_x < γ} is open because ♯ is continuous; v_x(f♯) ≤ 1 on R♭⁺ because (R♭⁺)♯ ⊆ R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting: R♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺). Hence x♭ ∈ X♭ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff`); equivalent valuations give equivalent composites, so τ_R is well defined on classes, and (a) is the definition of the support.

(b): if f_i is a unit of R♭ then f_i♯ is a unit of R, so f♯ generates the unit ideal and U(f♯/g♯) is rational; x ∈ τ⁻¹U(f/g) iff |f_j♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)| ≠ 0 for all j, i.e. x ∈ U(f♯/g♯). Normalisation: on the quasi-compact rational U = U(f/g) the function g is a unit of O(U), so |(ϖ♭)^N(y)| ≤ |g(y)| on U for N large, and adding (ϖ♭)^N to the numerators does not change U (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`; Sch12 Remark 2.8); multiplying all parameters by a power of ϖ♭ puts them into R♭⁺ (`rationalSubset_image_mul_right`). Continuity follows because rational subsets form a basis of X♭ (Tau Ceti `isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`).

(c): φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), so for y ∈ Spa(S, S⁺) both composites send y to the class of v_y ∘ φ ∘ ♯_R. (d): in characteristic p the tilt of (R, R⁺) is (R, R⁺) with ♯ = id (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
acceptance: For K = Q_p^cycl (the completion of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}), a perfectoid field) and R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, the point x of evaluation at T^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n} tilts to the point of R♭ = K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ given by evaluation at T ↦ ϖ♭, and τ⁻¹{|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|} = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}.
The map is not Spa of a morphism of Huber pairs: for K = Q_p^cycl there is no ring homomorphism K♭ → K at all (K♭ has characteristic p, K characteristic 0).
