nodes.title: Rational localisations of perfectoid Tate pairs of characteristic p are perfect, with an explicit almost integral model
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with pR = 0 (so R is a perfect complete Tate ring and R⁺ is perfect; ECD Proposition 3.5), ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudo-uniformizer, X = Spa(R, R⁺), f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R⁺ with f_n = ϖ^N, and U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g). Then: (i) the rational localisation (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) (anchor Layer 3.1) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p: Frobenius is bijective on O_X(U) and on O_X⁺(U); (ii) let A_U be the ϖ-adic completion of the subring R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^m} : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0] of R[1/g]; then A_U is perfect and ϖ-torsion free, A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)° inside O_X(U) = A_U[1/ϖ], and both quotients O_X(U)°/A_U and O_X⁺(U)/A_U are almost zero (killed by ϖ^{1/p^k} for all k); (iii) the surjection ψ : R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^∞}], T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i/g)^{1/p^m}, has kernel containing the ideal I generated by the elements g^{1/p^m} T_i^{1/p^m} − f_i^{1/p^m} (i ≤ n, m ≥ 0), and ker ψ / I is almost zero; (iv) consequently every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p is stably uniform.
hypotheses: pR = 0; (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair (equivalently R perfect, complete, Tate: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
f_i, g ∈ R⁺ and f_n = ϖ^N: every rational subset has such a presentation (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b), applied with R = R♭).
Almost zero is with respect to the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); in a perfect R⁺ it is generated by the ϖ^{1/p^k}.
proofSteps: (i) Frobenius: the composite R → R → O_X(U) of Φ⁻¹ with the structure map is continuous, sends g to g^{1/p}, a unit of O_X(U), and f_i/g to (f_i/g)^{1/p}, which is power-bounded; by the universal property of the rational localisation (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`) it extends uniquely to σ : O_X(U) → O_X(U). Φ ∘ σ and σ ∘ Φ are continuous and restrict to the structure map on R, so both are the identity by uniqueness (Kedlaya AWS proof of Theorem 2.5.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.1.7). A perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid, in particular uniform (ECD Proposition 3.5). O_X⁺(U) is perfect because it is integrally closed in the perfect ring O_X(U).

(iii) The ideal I is stable under p-th roots of its generators, so P := R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]/I is perfect; ψ induces a surjection P → R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}] which becomes an isomorphism after inverting ϖ, because inverting ϖ inverts g (g · (f_n/g) = ϖ^N), so that R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}][1/ϖ] = R[1/g] and P[1/ϖ] = R[1/g] as well; hence its kernel is ϖ^∞-torsion in the perfect ring P, and ϖ^k x = 0 implies (ϖ^{k/p^m} x)^{p^m} = 0, so ϖ^{k/p^m} x = 0 since perfect rings are reduced (Sch12 proof of Lemma 6.4(i) in characteristic p; Bhatt Lemma 9.2.3(2)).

(ii) A_U is perfect and ϖ-torsion free as the ϖ-adic completion of a perfect ϖ-torsion-free ring. The cokernel of R⁺[f/g] → R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}] is killed by ϖ^{nN} (Bhatt Lemma 9.2.3(3): a product ∏(f_i/g)^{a_i} with a_i ∈ [0,1) times ϖ^{nN} lies in R⁺[f/g] because ϖ^N/g = f_n/g), so both ϖ-adic completions give the same Tate ring after inverting ϖ, and R⁺⟨f/g⟩[1/ϖ] = O_X(U) because R⁺ is a ring of definition of R (R uniform) and f₁, …, f_n generate the unit ideal. A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) since its generators have absolute value ≤ 1 on U = Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) and O_X⁺(U) is closed. Since A_U is open and bounded, O_X(U)° ⊆ ϖ^{-c}A_U for some c; for y ∈ O_X(U)° and k ≥ 0, (ϖ^{c/p^k} y)^{p^k} ∈ A_U, and A_U contains the p-th roots (unique in O_X(U)) of its elements, so ϖ^{c/p^k} y ∈ A_U: O_X(U)°/A_U is almost zero.
(iv) By (i) every rational localisation of (R, R⁺) is perfectoid, hence uniform (ECD Definition 3.1).
acceptance: For K = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ (t-adic completion) and R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, U = {|T| ≤ |t|}: O_X(U) = K⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_U = K°⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_X(U)° exactly; for the annulus U = {|t| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}, O_X(U) = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (t/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfect.

nodes.title: Almost exactness lifts from reduction modulo ϖ for torsion-free complete complexes
nodes.statement: Let V be a ring, m ⊆ V an ideal with m² = m, ϖ ∈ V an element, and call a V-module almost zero if it is killed by m (these form a Serre class, closed under arbitrary products and filtered colimits; PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class). (a) Let C be a bounded complex of V-modules whose terms are ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete and separated. If every cohomology module of C/ϖC is almost zero, so is every cohomology module of C. (b) Conversely, if the terms of C are ϖ-torsion free and every cohomology module of C is almost zero, so is every cohomology module of C/ϖC. (c) Let α : M → N be V-linear with M ϖ-adically separated, N ϖ-torsion free, coker α almost zero, and α ⊗ V/ϖ with almost zero kernel and cokernel. Then ker α and coker α are almost zero.
hypotheses: m² = m (basic setup ideal, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup); in the application V = R⁺ for a perfectoid Tate pair and m its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements, with ϖ ∈ m.
Completeness and separatedness are ϖ-adic; the inverse limit C = lim_n C/ϖ^n C has surjective transition maps.
proofSteps: (a) Termwise torsion-freeness gives short exact sequences of complexes 0 → C/ϖ^n → C/ϖ^{n+1} → C/ϖ → 0 (first map multiplication by ϖ); by induction and the long exact cohomology sequence all H^q(C/ϖ^n) are almost zero (the class is closed under extensions because m² = m).

Since C = lim_n C/ϖ^n with surjective transition maps, the Milnor sequence 0 → lim¹_n H^{q−1}(C/ϖ^n) → H^q(C) → lim_n H^q(C/ϖ^n) → 0 is exact. lim_n of almost zero modules is almost zero (a submodule of the product), and lim¹_n is a quotient of ∏_n H^{q−1}(C/ϖ^n), which is killed by m; so the derived-limit term is controlled, not discarded, and H^q(C) is almost zero. This is Sch12's 'by flatness and completeness'.
(b) The long exact sequence of 0 → C → C → C/ϖ → 0 places H^q(C/ϖ) between H^q(C) and H^{q+1}(C).

(c) (Bhatt, footnote in the proof of Lemma 9.2.5) Replace N by the image of α (its quotient is almost zero); L = ker α satisfies L/ϖL ⊆ ker(α ⊗ V/ϖ) because N is ϖ-torsion free, so L is almost ϖ-divisible, while L ⊆ M is ϖ-adically separated; an almost ϖ-divisible separated module is almost zero.
acceptance: Completeness cannot be dropped: for V = Z_p, m = 0 (so almost zero means zero) and C = [Q_p → 0], C/pC = 0 is exact while C is not; Q_p is p-torsion free but not p-adically separated.
In PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity, (b) is applied to the characteristic-p integral Čech complex and (a) to the characteristic-0 one after identifying both modulo ϖ.

nodes.title: Untilted rational localisations: explicit almost integral model, perfectoidness and tilt
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺) and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ as in the stage conventions. Let f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g) ⊆ X♭ and U♯ := τ_R⁻¹(U) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) ⊆ X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b)). Then: (i) the ϖ-adic completion A of the subring R⁺[(f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯ : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0] of R[1/g♯] is ϖ-torsion free and Frobenius induces an almost isomorphism A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ, i.e. A^a is a perfectoid R⁺ᵃ-algebra; (ii) O_X(U♯) = A[1/ϖ] is a perfectoid Tate ring and A ⊆ O_X⁺(U♯) ⊆ O_X(U♯)° with almost zero quotients; (iii) the map R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → A, T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯, is surjective modulo ϖ with kernel modulo ϖ almost equal to the image of the ideal generated by (g^{1/p^m})♯ T_i^{1/p^m} − (f_i^{1/p^m})♯; (iv) (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) is the untilt over (R, R⁺) of (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)): there is a unique isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) compatible with the structure maps from (R♭, R♭⁺) and with ♯.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; no base field; ϖ♭ with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R°.
The normalisation f_n = (ϖ♭)^N makes f₁♯, …, f_n♯ generate the unit ideal of R, so U♯ is a rational subset with the displayed presentation.

The untilt of (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) over (R, R⁺) exists by the tilting equivalence over the perfectoid base R (ECD Theorem 3.13; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt); no base field is used.
proofSteps: Characteristic p: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p applied to (R♭, R♭⁺) and U gives O_{X♭}(U) perfectoid, the model A♭ = R♭⁺⟨(f/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩ almost equal to O_{X♭}⁺(U), and the presentation P♭ = R♭⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]/I♭ with almost zero kernel onto R♭⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}].

Untilt and comparison map: let (S, S⁺) be the perfectoid (R, R⁺)-algebra with (S, S⁺)♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting). By naturality of τ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (c)) every point of Spa(S, S⁺) maps to τ⁻¹(U) = U♯, so the universal property of the rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`) gives (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) → (S, S⁺) over (R, R⁺); composing, R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}] →a A →d S⁺.

Modulo ϖ: since ♯ induces ring isomorphisms R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ and S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ natural in the pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings), the reduction of d ∘ a modulo the ideal (I, ϖ) is identified with the characteristic-p map P♭/ϖ♭ → O_{X♭}⁺(U)/ϖ♭, which is an almost isomorphism by the first step; the generators (g^{1/p^m})♯T^{1/p^m} − (f^{1/p^m})♯ reduce to g^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m} − f^{1/p^m} because ♯ is additive modulo ϖ.

Lifting: a is surjective (surjective before completion); the ϖ-adic completion of P is ϖ-adically separated and S⁺ is ϖ-torsion free, so d ∘ a, being an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ, is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer (b); Bhatt, footnote in the proof of Lemma 9.2.5). With a surjective, a and d are almost isomorphisms; A is ϖ-torsion free (a completion of a torsion-free ring), so the almost zero kernel of d vanishes and A ⊆ S⁺ with almost zero cokernel. This gives (i) and (iii), since S⁺ᵃ is a perfectoid R⁺ᵃ-algebra (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary).

(ii): as in the characteristic-p case the cokernel of R⁺[f♯/g♯] → R⁺[(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}] is killed by ϖ^{nN} (1/g♯ = ϖ^{-N} f_n♯/g♯), so A[1/ϖ] = R⁺⟨f♯/g♯⟩[1/ϖ] = O_X(U♯); hence O_X(U♯) ≅ S is perfectoid, A ⊆ O_X⁺(U♯) (generators of absolute value ≤ 1 on U♯) and O_X(U♯)°/A ≅ S°/A is almost zero (S°/S⁺ is almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii)).

(iv): the map μ : (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) → (S, S⁺) is an isomorphism of topological rings by (ii); on plus rings, tilting the inclusion (A[1/ϖ], A) → (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) shows that g divides f_i in the tilt of O_X⁺(U♯), so the tilt of Spa(O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) maps into U and the universal property over (R♭, R♭⁺) gives (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) → (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭, whose untilt inverts μ; uniqueness holds because the structure maps from (R, R⁺) are epimorphisms of complete Tate pairs (Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5(4); Sch12 Lemma 6.4(iii)).
acceptance: For a perfectoid Tate ring R₀ and the perfected Tate algebra R = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), g ∈ R♭⁺ homogeneous and U_c = {|g| ≤ |ϖ♭|^c} (c ∈ Z[1/p]_{≥0}), the lemma gives O_X(U_c♯)°ᵃ = R°⟨(g♯/ϖ^c)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ, the formula consumed by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc.

Over a perfectoid field K this is Sch12 Lemma 6.4 (i)-(iii) and Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5; for R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}, O_X(U♯) = Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ with tilt Q_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩.
The model is almost, not exactly, integral: for R⁺ ≠ R° (e.g. R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) and U = X, A = R⁺ while O_X(X)° = R°.

nodes.title: Approximation of homogeneous functions on a perfectoid polydisc over a perfectoid Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let R₀ be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R₀♭, ϖ♭ ∈ R₀♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R₀°, and let P = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ be the perfected Tate algebra, with P° = R₀°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ graded by total degree in T with values in Z[1/p]_{≥0} (R₀° in degree 0), and tilt P♭ = R₀♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, where T_i♯ = T_i. Let f ∈ P° be homogeneous of degree d. Then for every rational c ≥ 0 and every ε ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε < 1 there is g ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d such that for all x ∈ Spa(P, P°): |f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|). In particular max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) for all x.
hypotheses: R₀ a perfectoid Tate ring (no base field; Sch12 Lemma 6.5 is the case R₀ = K a perfectoid field).
P is perfectoid with P° = R₀°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and tilt R₀♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12).
Homogeneity refers to the Z[1/p]-grading of R₀°[T^{1/p^∞}] by total T-degree, extended to the completion as convergent sums of homogeneous terms of one degree.
proofSteps: Fix ε ∈ Z[1/p] ∩ (0, 1) and f; prove by induction on c, in steps c → c' = c + a with a fixed a ∈ Z[1/p], 0 < a < ε, that there are ε(c) ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε(c) ≤ ε − a and g_c ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d with |f − g_c♯| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε+ε(c)}| max(|f|, |ϖ^c|) on Spa(P, P°); c = 0 holds with ε(0) = ε and g₀ ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d with g₀♯ ≡ f modulo ϖP° (lift f coefficientwise through R₀♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R₀°/ϖ), since then |f − g₀♯| ≤ |ϖ| and max(|f|, |ϖ^0|) = 1 on Spa(P, P°); each induction step loses a small constant through almost mathematics.

On U_c♯ = {|g_c♯| ≤ |ϖ^c|} = {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} (the two agree by the induction hypothesis), h := f − g_c♯ ∈ ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c)} O⁺(U_c♯); by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization, O(U_c♯)°ᵃ = P°⟨(g_c♯/ϖ^c)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ, and homogeneity puts h almost into the ϖ-adic completion of ⊕_{i ∈ Z[1/p] ∩ [0,1]} ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c)} (g_c♯/ϖ^c)^i P°_{deg = d − di}; choose 0 < ε(c') < ε(c) and write h = Σ_i ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c')} (g_c♯/ϖ^c)^i r_i with r_i ∈ P° homogeneous of degree d − di, r_i → 0.

Choose s_i ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d − di with s_i → 0 and ϖ | r_i − s_i♯: coefficientwise lifting through R₀♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R₀°/ϖ, using that ♯ is additive modulo ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Put g_{c'} = g_c + Σ_i (ϖ♭)^{c+1−ε+ε(c')} (g_c/(ϖ♭)^c)^i s_i.

Estimate: where |f(x)| > |ϖ^c(x)|, |g_c♯(x)| = |f(x)| and each correction term has absolute value ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε+ε(c')}(x)||f(x)| (maximal at i = 1); where |f(x)| ≤ |ϖ^c(x)|, f − g_{c'}♯ ≡ f − g_c♯ − h = 0 modulo ϖ^{c+1} O(U_c♯)°, and c + 1 > c' + 1 − ε + ε(c'). This is Sch12's proof of Lemma 6.5 with K replaced by R₀; it uses only the grading, the model of O(U_c♯) and ♯ modulo ϖ.
acceptance: Field case (Sch12 Lemma 6.5, Bhatt Lemma 9.2.6): R₀ = K perfectoid field, P = K⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩.

For f = T₀ one may take g = T₀ for every c. For f = T₀ + ϖT₁ (homogeneous of degree 1), g = T₀ + ϖ♭T₁ satisfies f ≡ g♯ modulo ϖP° because ♯ is additive modulo ϖ, which gives the estimate for c = 0; for c > 0 the locus {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} requires the inductive corrections.

nodes.title: Approximation lemma: every function on a perfectoid affinoid is approximated by a sharp
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺), ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ as in the stage conventions, X = Spa(R, R⁺). (i) For every f ∈ R, every rational c ≥ 0 and every ε ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε < 1 there is g ∈ R♭ such that for all x ∈ X: |f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|); in particular max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|). (ii) For f, h ∈ R and an integer c ≥ 0 there are a, b ∈ R♭ with {x ∈ X : |f(x)| ≤ |h(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |h(x)|} = {x ∈ X : |a♯(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|}. The field version is Sch12 Corollary 6.7(i); the general version holds with the same proof over the base R, and independently by Witt-vector Euclidean division (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.17).
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; no base field.
The estimate is pointwise in the value group Γ_x ∪ {0} of each x ∈ X, with |ϖ^r(x)| := |((ϖ♭)^r)♯(x)| for r ∈ Z[1/p].
proofSteps: Reduction to R⁺ = R°: every point of X has a unique rank-one generization, which lies in Spa(R, R°); if the estimate holds at rank-one points with ε' < ε, it holds strictly there, and a strict inequality |u(y)| < |v(y)| with v(y) ≠ 0 at the rank-one generization y of x gives |u(x)| ≤ |v(x)| (u/v is topologically nilpotent in the completed residue field of y) (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(i)).

Reduction to f ∈ R° and c an integer: replace f by ϖ^k f and c by c + k; enlarging c only weakens the bound. Write f = g₀♯ + ϖg₁♯ + … + ϖ^c g_c♯ + ϖ^{c+1} f_{c+1} with g_j ∈ R♭° (successive approximation through R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); the term ϖ^{c+1}f_{c+1} does not affect the estimate, so assume f_{c+1} = 0.

Universal case: the continuous R-algebra map μ : P = R⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_c^{1/p^∞}⟩ → R, T_j^{1/p^m} ↦ (g_j^{1/p^m})♯ (universal property of the perfected Tate algebra, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples) sends the homogeneous degree-one element F = Σ ϖ^j T_j to f; its tilt μ♭ sends T_j to g_j (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality). PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc (base R₀ = R) gives G ∈ P♭° with the estimate for F on Spa(P, P°); pull it back along Spa(μ) : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(P, P°) using μ(G♯) = (μ♭(G))♯, and set g = μ♭(G).

(ii) (Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(2)): choose b with |h − b♯| < max(|h|, |ϖ^c|) and a with max(|f|, |ϖ^c|) = max(|a♯|, |ϖ^c|) by (i) (with ε < 1, the strict form following from ε < 1 and ε(c) > 0); the equality of the two sets is a case distinction with the strong triangle inequality: where |ϖ^c| ≤ |h|, |b♯| = |h|, and conversely.

Alternative proof without the polydisc: write R⁺ = W(R♭⁺)/(ξ) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals) and approximate a lift of f by a prepared Witt vector via Euclidean division by ξ (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(b); Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.9, 2.6.17).
acceptance: Sch12 Corollary 6.7(i) and Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(1) are the case of a perfectoid affinoid algebra over a perfectoid field K.

For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and f = T + ϖ, g = T + ϖ♭ satisfies f ≡ g♯ modulo ϖR°, which is the estimate for c = 0; for c ≥ 1 the lemma provides g with {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} = {|g♯| ≤ |ϖ^c|} (Sch12 Remark 6.6), a rational subset of X that is a preimage from X♭.
Consequence consumed by the tilting homeomorphism: every rational subset of X is the preimage of a rational subset of X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, step 2).

nodes.title: The tilting homeomorphism Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) identifies rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; no perfectoid base field) with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺). Then the tilting map τ_R : X = Spa(R, R⁺) → X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra), is a homeomorphism, natural in morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs. A subset U ⊆ X is rational if and only if τ_R(U) ⊆ X♭ is rational; explicitly, for f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, τ_R(U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)) = U(f₁, …, f_n / g), and every rational subset of X can be written as U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) for such f_i, g. Consequently τ_R preserves the specialisation order, quasi-compact opens and rank-one (maximal) points, and restricts, for every rational U ⊆ X, to a homeomorphism U ≅ τ_R(U) identifying rational subsets of U and of τ_R(U).
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; characteristic 0, p, or mixed (ECD Example 3.4(iv)).

Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) and Corollary 6.7(iii) prove the statement over a perfectoid field; ECD Theorem 3.12 states it for perfectoid Tate rings, with the remark after Theorem 3.13 that the proof works in general; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.16 and Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.1 prove it for Fontaine perfectoid (Tate, resp. analytic) rings.
proofSteps: Continuity and the preimage formula: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b).

Every rational subset of X is a preimage: normalise U = U(h₁, …, h_n / h) with h_i, h ∈ R⁺ and h_n = ϖ^c (Tau Ceti `rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`, `rationalSubset_image_mul_right`); then U = ⋂_{i<n} {|h_i| ≤ |h|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |h|} (Tau Ceti `rationalSubset_inter`), and each set in the intersection is {|a_i♯| ≤ |b_i♯|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |b_i♯|} = τ⁻¹U(a_i, (ϖ♭)^c / b_i) by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma (ii) (Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(3)).

Injectivity: X is spectral (Tau Ceti instance `SpectralSpace (spa Aplus)`), hence T₀, and its rational subsets form a basis; since every rational subset is τ-saturated, two points with the same image lie in the same open sets and coincide (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(iii)).

Surjectivity: for y ∈ X♭ the completed residue affinoid field (k(y)^, k(y)^+) is perfect (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p: the O_{X♭}(V), V ∋ y, are perfect) and complete, hence a perfectoid field of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation). Untilt R♭ → k(y)^ over R: the tilting equivalence over R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) gives a perfectoid R-algebra L with L♭ ≅ k(y)^, a perfectoid field, and the open valuation ring L⁺ corresponding to k(y)^+ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting); the point x : R → L → Γ ∪ {0} lies in X and x♭ = y by naturality of ♯ (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(iii): untilt the field, then the valuation).

Openness and rational images: by bijectivity and the preimage formula, τ(U(f♯/g♯)) = U(f/g); since every rational subset of X has this form, τ maps a basis of opens to opens and is a homeomorphism; a subset U ⊆ X is rational iff τ(U) is. The remaining assertions (specialisation, maximal points, restriction to rational U) are formal consequences of being a homeomorphism that preserves rational subsets, together with Tau Ceti's description of rational subsets of a rational subset (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2)).
Naturality: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (c).
acceptance: Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) (perfectoid affinoid K-algebras over a perfectoid field) is a special case.
For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: τ({|T| ≤ |ϖ|}) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}, the Gauss point goes to the Gauss point, and the classical point T ↦ ϖ goes to T ↦ ϖ♭.

The theorem applies to ECD Example 3.4(iv), R = Z_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p}, which lives over no field: its spectrum contains points with |p(x)| = 0 and points with |p(x)| ≠ 0, and both kinds are matched with points of the characteristic-p space X♭.

Without the approximation lemma one only obtains that rational subsets of X are preimages of quasi-compact opens of X♭ (Bhatt Remark 9.2.8); the statement that images of rational subsets are rational needs the approximation lemma.

nodes.title: Rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are perfectoid, with tilt the rational localisation of the tilt
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; no perfectoid base field), X = Spa(R, R⁺), X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) and τ_R : X ≅ X♭ the tilting homeomorphism. For every rational subset U ⊆ X, the rational localisation (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) of the anchor (Layer 3.1: O_X(U) = R⟨T/s⟩ for any presentation U = U(T/s), O_X⁺(U) the integral closure of the image of R⁺[T/s]; Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `completedPlusSubring`) is a perfectoid Tate pair, and there is a unique isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(τ_R U), O_{X♭}⁺(τ_R U)) compatible with the structure maps from (R♭, R♭⁺) and with ♯; equivalently (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the untilt over (R, R⁺) of the rational localisation of the tilt at τ_R(U). For a presentation U = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) with f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺ and f_n = (ϖ♭)^N (which exists for every U), O_X⁺(U)ᵃ = (R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩)ᵃ. The construction U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the rational localisation in the category of perfectoid Tate pairs: every morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) to a perfectoid Tate pair whose Spa lands in U factors uniquely through it; and tilting gives an equivalence between the rational localisations of (R, R⁺) and those of (R♭, R♭⁺). In characteristic p the tilt identification is the identity.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; characteristic 0, p or mixed; this is the AdicSpacesPartII request (R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation, R5/sousperfectoid-stably-uniform): no perfectoid base field.

The universal property among perfectoid pairs is the anchor's universal property of rational localisation (all complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with a ring of integral elements) restricted to perfectoid targets; it needs no argument beyond the anchor's, but the tilt of the localisation is characterised only after perfectoidness is known (Kedlaya AWS proof of Theorem 2.5.3: the universal property quantifies over all Huber pairs).

The anchor's structure presheaf on rational subsets must be presentation independent (anchor Layer 3.1); at the pin Tau Ceti has the localisation for each presentation and the comparison isomorphisms between presentations, not the presheaf.
proofSteps: Every rational U ⊆ X is U(f♯/g♯) for some f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, and τ_R(U) = U(f/g) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets).

PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization (ii) and (iv) for U(f/g) ⊆ X♭: O_X(U) is perfectoid, its almost integral model is R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩, and (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the untilt of (O_{X♭}(U(f/g)), O_{X♭}⁺(U(f/g))), uniquely.

Independence of the presentation: two presentations of U give canonically isomorphic rational localisations (anchor Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.presentationRingEquivOfEq_coe_comp_toCompletionLoc`), and the tilt isomorphisms are compatible because both are the unique isomorphisms compatible with the structure maps (Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5(4)).

Universal property among perfectoid pairs: restriction of the anchor's (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`). Equivalence of rational localisations under tilting: a morphism of rational localisations over (R, R⁺) is determined by the inclusion of rational subsets, and τ_R preserves inclusions (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.3(b)).
Characteristic p: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (d).
acceptance: Sch12 Corollary 6.8 (perfectoid affinoid K-algebras over a perfectoid field) and Berkeley Theorem 6.2.6 are special cases; Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 3.8 and Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(i) are the same statement for perfectoid (Tate) rings.
For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}: O_X(U) = Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ R via T ↦ ϖT, and its tilt is Q_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_{X♭}({|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}).

For R of ECD Example 3.4(iv) (no base field; R⁺ = R°) and U = U(T, p / p) = {|T| ≤ |p|}: on X one has |p| ≤ |T| (p/T ∈ R°), so |p| = |T| ≠ 0 on U and p is a unit of O_X(U); O_X(U) is a perfectoid Tate ring in which p is invertible, obtained as a rational localisation of a ring in which p is not invertible — a case covered neither by Sch12 nor by Kedlaya–Liu I §3.6.

nodes.title: The presheaf of perfectoid pairs on rational subsets: restriction maps, plus rings, and tilting as a natural isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(R, R⁺), τ = τ_R. On the poset Rat(X) of rational subsets of X, the assignment U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) with the anchor's restriction maps ρ_{U,V} (V ⊆ U) is a functor Rat(X)^op → {perfectoid Tate pairs} (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), with: (a) transitivity: for V ⊆ U rational, V is rational in U ≅ Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) and ρ_{U,V} is the rational localisation of (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) at V; (b) plus rings: O_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U}, O_X(U)°°  ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)°, and O_X(U)°/O_X⁺(U) is almost zero, so O_X⁺(U)ᵃ = O_X(U)°ᵃ; (c) tilting is a natural isomorphism: the isomorphisms tiltEquiv_U of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids satisfy tiltEquiv_V ∘ (ρ_{U,V})♭ = ρ_{τU,τV} ∘ tiltEquiv_U, i.e. the functor U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ is isomorphic to U ↦ (O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU)); (d) consequently the ring isomorphisms O_{X♭}⁺(τU)/ϖ♭ ≅ O_X⁺(U)/ϖ induced by ♯ are natural in U, and are R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ-semilinear; (e) the homeomorphisms Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U and Spa(O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU)) ≅ τU (anchor Layer 3.1) intertwine τ_{O_X(U)} and τ|_U.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ as in the stage conventions.

The anchor supplies restriction maps satisfying the identity and composition laws (Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.restrictionRingHomOfSubset` for a numerator enlargement, general inclusions through presentation changes) and the homeomorphism Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U with rational subsets identified.
Almost zero refers to the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), which is also that of O_X⁺(U) for U ≠ ∅.
proofSteps: (a): rational subsets of a rational subset are rational in X (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2)), and the composite of the rational localisations R → O_X(U) → O_X(U)_V has the universal property of R → O_X(V) (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset` applied twice).

(b): Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U and Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`) give the description of O_X⁺(U); topologically nilpotent elements lie in O_X⁺(U) because it is open and integrally closed (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`); for y ∈ O_X(U)° and a pseudo-uniformizer π, πy is topologically nilpotent, so πy ∈ O_X⁺(U) (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).

(c): both composites are morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ → (O_{X♭}(τV), O_{X♭}⁺(τV)) over (R♭, R♭⁺); the source is a rational localisation of (R♭, R♭⁺) (via tiltEquiv_U), so they agree by the uniqueness in its universal property.
(d): ♯ modulo ϖ is a ring isomorphism S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ natural in the perfectoid pair (S, S⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings; ECD Lemma 3.11); apply it to ρ_{U,V} and use (c).
(e): PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (c) applied to the structure map (R, R⁺) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) and to its tilt.
acceptance: For U = X, (d) is ECD Lemma 3.11: R♭⁺/ϖ♭ = R⁺/ϖ.

For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|²} ⊆ U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}: ρ_{U,V} : Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ → Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^∞}⟩ sends (T/ϖ)^{1/p^m} to ϖ^{1/p^m}(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^m}, and its tilt is the same formula with ϖ♭.

nodes.title: Completed residue fields of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid and tilt to those of the tilt
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(R, R⁺), x ∈ X, and (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) the completed residue affinoid field of x (the completion of the residue field of the stalk O_{X,x} for the topology of v_x, with the completion of the valuation ring of v_x; anchor Layer 3.3), with its canonical morphism (R, R⁺) → (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺). Then k(x)^ is a perfectoid field and (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair. Moreover its tilt is canonically (k(x♭)^, k(x♭)^⁺), compatibly with the canonical morphisms from (R, R⁺) and (R♭, R♭⁺) and with ♯; in particular the value groups Γ_x and Γ_{x♭} coincide and x has rank one if and only if x♭ has. Explicitly, k(x)^⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of the image in k(x) of colim_{U ∋ x} O_X⁺(U), the colimit running over the rational neighbourhoods of x (an element h of the stalk with |h(x)| ≤ 1 lies in O_X⁺ of the rational neighbourhood {|h| ≤ 1} of x).
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair (no base field).

k(x)^ is a complete nonarchimedean field whose topology is that of the rank-one generization of x (x is analytic because R is Tate); the anchor supplies stalks, residue fields and the completed residue affinoid field (requested from anchor Layer 3, as AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres also does).
proofSteps: The completion F of colim_{U ∋ x} O_X(U) (for the topology in which colim O_X⁺(U) is open with ϖ-adic topology) is a completed filtered colimit of perfectoid Tate rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), hence perfectoid (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22).

The map F → k(x)^ has dense image (the residue field of the stalk is a quotient of the colimit) and k(x)^ is uniform, being a nonarchimedean field; a uniform Tate ring receiving a morphism with dense image from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid (Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18, case (ii)); a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field is a perfectoid field (ECD Definition 3.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation). Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7.

k(x)^⁺ is an open valuation subring of k(x)^ contained in k(x)^°, hence a ring of integral elements, so (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair; the description of k(x)^⁺ follows from O_X⁺(U) = {|f| ≤ 1 on U} (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (b)) and the fact that the ϖ-adic topology of the valuation ring of a microbial valuation is its valuation topology.

Tilt: the rational neighbourhoods of x correspond to those of x♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), so F♭ is the completed colimit of the O_{X♭}(τU) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (c); tilting commutes with completed filtered colimits through R♭° = lim_Φ R°/ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). The dense-image map F → k(x)^ tilts to a dense-image map F♭ → k(x)^♭ (Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(b), case (ii)) through which v_{x♭} = v_x ∘ ♯ factors; hence k(x)^♭ is the completed residue field of x♭, and valuation rings correspond (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting). Value groups of a perfectoid field and its tilt agree (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).
acceptance: Sch12 Corollary 6.7(ii) is the case of a perfectoid affinoid algebra over a perfectoid field.

For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: at the Gauss point k(x)^ is the completion of Q_p^cycl(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm, a perfectoid field whose tilt is the analogous completion of Q_p^cycl♭(T^{1/p^∞}); at the classical point T ↦ a (a ∈ Q_p^cycl, |a| ≤ 1) k(x)^ = Q_p^cycl.
The uncompleted residue field is not perfectoid in general: Q_p^cycl(T^{1/p^∞}) is not complete.

nodes.title: Perfectoid Tate pairs are stably uniform and sheafy, with Čech-acyclic structure sheaf
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; no base field), X = Spa(R, R⁺). Then (a) (R, R⁺) is stably uniform: O_X(U) is uniform for every rational U ⊆ X (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 3.13; anchor Layer 4.2); (b) (R, R⁺) is sheafy: the structure presheaf O_X is a sheaf of complete topological rings on X (anchor `Huber.IsSheafyPair`), and O_X⁺ is a sheaf; the same holds for (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) for every rational U; (c) for every rational U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by rational subsets the augmented Čech complex 0 → O_X(U) → ∏ O_X(U_i) → ∏ O_X(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact in every degree, and H^i(U, O_X) = 0 for i > 0, H⁰(U, O_X) = O_X(U); (d) (a)-(c) depend on R only, not on the choice of R⁺.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; the sheaf property is that of the anchor's structure presheaf on the adic spectrum (Layer 3.3-3.5), which must be presentation independent.
Sheaf cohomology is that of the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on the topological space U (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`).
proofSteps: (a) O_X(U) is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), and perfectoid Tate rings are uniform by definition; in characteristic p this is already PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p (iv).

(b) Buzzard–Verberkmoes: a stably uniform complete Tate pair is sheafy (anchor Layer 4.2); O_X⁺ is a sheaf because O_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 on U} (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (b)) is a pointwise condition; rational subsets are again perfectoid, so the statement holds on each U. The sheaf condition may be checked on rational covers (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`).
(c) AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity (Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 2.4.23) applied to the sheafy complete Tate pair (R, R⁺).

(d) Stable uniformity and sheafiness of the rational localisations do not depend on R⁺ (Hansen–Kedlaya remark after Definition 3.9; the rational localisation O_X(U) for U = U(T/s) is R⟨T/s⟩ whatever R⁺ is).
acceptance: Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.6.15 (perfectoid Q_p-algebras), Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.19 (Fontaine perfectoid rings), Berkeley Theorem 6.1.10/7.1.1, Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 3.15 and Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.4 are this theorem.
In characteristic p the proof needs only perfectness: F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is stably uniform because each rational localisation is perfect and complete (ECD Proposition 3.5).

The uniform non-sheafy Huber rings of Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara are not perfectoid; perfectoid rings are never noetherian unless finite products of perfectoid fields (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.9.3), so Huber's strongly noetherian sheafiness theorem does not apply to them.

nodes.title: Integral Čech cohomology of a stably uniform sheafy Tate pair is killed by a bounded power of ϖ
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair which is stably uniform and sheafy, ϖ ∈ A⁺ a pseudo-uniformizer, X = Spa(A, A⁺), U ⊆ X rational and 𝔘 = (U₁, …, U_m) a finite covering of U by rational subsets. Let C⁺ be the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → O_X⁺(U) → ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ → O_X⁺(U₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_m) → 0. Then C⁺[1/ϖ] is the augmented Čech complex of O_X, which is exact, C⁺ is exact at its first two terms, and there is N ≥ 0 such that ϖ^N annihilates every cohomology module of C⁺. The same bound holds for the Čech complex of V ↦ O_X(V)°, whose terms are also open and bounded.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff, Tate, stably uniform (every O_X(V) uniform) and sheafy; no perfectoid or noetherian hypothesis.
Exactness of the O_X-Čech complex in all degrees is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity (Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 2.4.23).
proofSteps: C⁺[1/ϖ] is the O_X-complex because O_X⁺(V) is open in the Tate ring O_X(V); it is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity). Exactness of C⁺ at O_X⁺(U) and at ∏ O_X⁺(U_i) holds because O_X⁺ is a sheaf when O_X is (pointwise condition |f| ≤ 1; Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

Each term C^q = ∏ O_X(V) is a complete metrisable topological A-module (a finite product of complete Tate rings) and C⁺^q is open and bounded in it (stable uniformity: O_X⁺(V) ⊆ O_X(V)° bounded), so the ϖ^k C⁺^q form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0; the differentials d^q are continuous and A-linear and map C⁺^q to C⁺^{q+1}.

By exactness, im d^{q−1} = ker d^q is closed, hence complete, and d^{q−1} : C^{q−1} → ker d^q is surjective; by the open mapping theorem over the Tate ring A (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`) it is open, so d^{q−1}(C⁺^{q−1}) contains ϖ^{N_q}(ker d^q ∩ C⁺^q) for some N_q (the quotient and subspace topologies on ker d^q agree).
Hence ϖ^{N_q} kills H^q(C⁺) = (ker d^q ∩ C⁺^q)/d^{q−1}(C⁺^{q−1}); take N = max_q N_q over the finitely many degrees (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.10(iii); Berkeley proof of Theorem 7.4.4).
acceptance: For S = K⟨T⟩ over a complete nonarchimedean field K with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and the Laurent covering {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|ϖ| ≤ |T|} of the closed disc, C⁺ = [K°⟨T⟩ → K°⟨T/ϖ⟩ × K°⟨T, ϖ/T⟩ → K°⟨T/ϖ, ϖ/T⟩] is exact (N = 0): every Laurent series Σ_{k∈Z} d_k(T/ϖ)^k with d_k → 0 in K° splits into its parts of non-negative and negative degree.
The lemma gives only a bounded power of ϖ; almost vanishing needs Frobenius (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity).

nodes.title: From almost Čech acyclicity on the rational basis to almost vanishing of sheaf cohomology
nodes.statement: Let V be a ring and m ⊆ V an ideal with m² = m; call a V-module almost zero if m kills it. Let X be a topological space with a basis ℬ of quasi-compact open subsets closed under finite intersections, and F a sheaf of V-modules on X. Suppose that for every U ∈ ℬ and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by members of ℬ the Čech cohomology Ȟ^q(𝔘, F) is almost zero for all q ≥ 1. Then the sheaf cohomology H^q(U, F) is almost zero for every U ∈ ℬ and q ≥ 1; equivalently H^q(U, Fᵃ) = 0 for the associated sheaf of almost modules (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology). For m = V (almost zero = zero) this is Cartan's criterion (Stacks Tag 01EW; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison). It applies to X = Spa(A, A⁺) for a Huber pair with ℬ the rational subsets (Tau Ceti: a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersections, with finite rational refinements of every covering of a rational subset).
hypotheses: m² = m, so almost zero modules form a Serre class closed under products and filtered colimits (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class).
Every open covering of U ∈ ℬ is refined by a finite covering by members of ℬ (quasi-compactness and ℬ a basis; Tau Ceti `exists_finite_spaRationalFamily_refinement`).
Sheaf cohomology is derived-functor cohomology of the underlying sheaf of abelian groups (equivalently of V-modules); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.
proofSteps: Embed F into an injective sheaf I and put G = I/F. For U ∈ ℬ, H¹(U, F) = coker(I(U) → G(U)). Given s ∈ G(U), choose a finite covering 𝔘 of U by members of ℬ with lifts t_i ∈ I(U_i); the differences t_i − t_j form a Čech 1-cocycle of F on 𝔘, and for ε ∈ m, ε times it is a coboundary (f_i − f_j) because Ȟ¹(𝔘, F) is almost zero; then the εt_i − f_i glue to t ∈ I(U) mapping to εs. Hence H¹(U, F) is almost zero.

For q ≥ 1 and 𝔘 ⊆ ℬ, the sequence of Čech complexes 0 → C(𝔘, F) → C(𝔘, I) → C(𝔘, G) has termwise cokernel a finite product of H¹(V, F), V ∈ ℬ, hence almost zero; it is a short exact sequence in the almost category, and Ȟ^q(𝔘, I) = 0 for q ≥ 1 gives Ȟ^q(𝔘, G) almost isomorphic to Ȟ^{q+1}(𝔘, F), so G satisfies the hypothesis.

Induction on q: H^q(U, F) ≅ H^{q−1}(U, G) for q ≥ 2 because I is acyclic; conclude by the previous two steps (the argument of Stacks Tag 01EW, run modulo the Serre class of almost zero modules; Kedlaya–Liu I proof of Proposition 2.4.21).
acceptance: m = V recovers Cartan's criterion as used for O_X in AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity (2).

With V = R⁺, m the topologically nilpotent elements and F = O_X⁺ on a perfectoid affinoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity supplies the hypothesis and the conclusion is ECD Theorem 3.24.
The hypothesis must hold for all U ∈ ℬ and all finite coverings, not only for coverings of X: Čech acyclicity for the coverings of X alone does not control H^q(X, F).

nodes.title: Almost exactness of the integral Čech complex of O⁺ on rational coverings of a perfectoid affinoid
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; no base field), X = Spa(R, R⁺). For every rational U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 = (U₁, …, U_m) of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex C⁺(𝔘): 0 → O_X⁺(U) → ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is almost exact: each of its cohomology modules is killed by every topologically nilpotent element of R⁺ (equivalently by ϖ^{1/p^n} for all n; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). It is exact at its first two terms. The same holds for the complex of the O_X(V)°, which is almost equal to C⁺(𝔘) termwise; in the almost category, C⁺(𝔘)ᵃ is exact. Consequently H^i(U, O_X⁺)ᵃ = 0, i.e. H^i(U, O_X⁺) is almost zero, for every rational U ⊆ X and every i > 0 (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis).
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; U rational; 𝔘 finite and consisting of rational subsets (all finite intersections are then rational).
Almost zero: killed by the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of R⁺, which is idempotent (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
proofSteps: Characteristic p, bounded torsion: (R, R⁺) is stably uniform and sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion gives N with ϖ^N H^q(C⁺(𝔘)) = 0 for all q.

Characteristic p, Frobenius: every O_X⁺(V) is perfect (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p (i)); Frobenius Φ is a bijective additive endomorphism of each term commuting with the differentials (alternating sums of ring homomorphisms), so it induces bijections on H^q(C⁺(𝔘)) with Φ(ax) = a^pΦ(x). For a class c and k ≥ 0, ϖ^{N/p^k} c = Φ^{-k}(ϖ^N Φ^k(c)) = 0; so H^q is killed by all ϖ^{N/p^k}, and every topologically nilpotent t ∈ R⁺ satisfies t^{p^k} ∈ ϖ^N R⁺ for k large, hence t ∈ ϖ^{N/p^k}R⁺ by perfectness (Berkeley proof of Theorem 7.4.4).

General case, transport: the tilting homeomorphism identifies 𝔘 with the rational covering τ𝔘 of τU, intersections included (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), and the natural isomorphisms O_{X♭}⁺(τV)/ϖ♭ ≅ O_X⁺(V)/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (d)) give an isomorphism of complexes C⁺(τ𝔘)/ϖ♭ ≅ C⁺(𝔘)/ϖ compatible with R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ, under which ϖ♭^{1/p^n} acts as ϖ^{1/p^n}.

General case, lifting: C⁺(τ𝔘) is almost exact by the characteristic-p case and has ϖ♭-torsion-free terms, so C⁺(τ𝔘)/ϖ♭ is almost exact (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer (b)); hence C⁺(𝔘)/ϖ is almost exact; the terms of C⁺(𝔘) are ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete and separated (O_X⁺(V) is open and bounded in the complete uniform O_X(V)), so C⁺(𝔘) is almost exact by (a) of the same lemma (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.14 in characteristic 0).

Exactness at the first two terms: O_X⁺ is a sheaf (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy (b)). Comparison with O°: O_X(V)°/O_X⁺(V) is almost zero (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (b)).

Sheaf cohomology: the Čech statement holds for all finite rational coverings of all rational subsets, which form a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersections; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis with V = R⁺ and m its topologically nilpotent elements gives almost vanishing of H^i(U, O_X⁺).
acceptance: Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Proposition 6.14 (proved there through p-finite algebras and Tate's acyclicity theorem; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate keeps that route).
For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and the Laurent covering {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|ϖ| ≤ |T|}, C⁺ is exact (as for the tft disc, the Laurent decomposition of Σ_{k ∈ Z[1/p]} d_k (T/ϖ)^k splits exactly).

The conclusion is about O⁺ up to almost zero modules, not only about O: after inverting ϖ it recovers the exactness of the O-Čech complex, but C⁺ itself need not be exact when R⁺ ≠ R°, only almost exact.

nodes.title: The sheaf theorem: O_X is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology and H^i(X, O_X⁺) is almost zero
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1: any perfectoid Tate ring, of characteristic 0, p or mixed, with no perfectoid base field) and X = Spa(R, R⁺). Then: (i) O_X and O_X⁺ are sheaves on X; (ii) for every rational U ⊆ X, (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (O_{X♭}(U♭), O_{X♭}⁺(U♭)), U♭ the image of U in X♭; (iii) H⁰(X, O_X) = R and H^i(X, O_X) = 0 for i > 0; (iv) H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺ and, for i > 0, the R⁺-module H^i(X, O_X⁺) is almost zero, i.e. killed by every topologically nilpotent element of R⁺ (equivalently H^i(X, O_X⁺ᵃ) = H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0 in the almost category, Sch12 Remark 6.12); (v) (i)-(iv) hold for every rational U in place of X.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; sheaf cohomology of sheaves of abelian groups on the topological space X.

This is ECD Theorems 3.18 and 3.24 in their stated generality; the ECD citations [Sch12], [KL15] cover perfectoid algebras over a perfectoid field and over Q_p (with characteristic p), and the case where p is neither zero nor invertible is Kedlaya–Liu II §3.3 (source issue recorded).
proofSteps: (i) and (iii): PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy.
(ii): PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids.

(iv), degree 0: H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = O_X⁺(X) = {f ∈ R : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ X} = R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (b); Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1), Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

(iv), degrees i > 0: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity gives almost exactness of the O⁺-Čech complexes for all finite rational coverings of all rational subsets and, through PerfectoidSpaces:P2/cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis (with V = R⁺, m the topologically nilpotent elements, ℬ the rational subsets), almost vanishing of H^i(U, O_X⁺). The almost-category reformulation: the localisation functor to almost modules is exact and O_X⁺ᵃ = O_X°ᵃ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction (b)).
(v): rational subsets of X are affinoid perfectoid (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) with Spa ≅ U, so (i)-(iv) apply to them.
acceptance: Sch12 Theorem 6.3(iii)-(iv) and Proposition 6.14 (perfectoid affinoid K-algebras over a perfectoid field), Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.20, Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4, Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 6.14 and Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.5 are instances.

For K a perfectoid field and X = Spa(K, K°): H^i(X, O_X⁺) = 0 for i > 0 because X is a point with the trivial covering only; H⁰ = K°; almost zero cannot be improved to zero in general (Sch12 Remark 6.12 states the result as m-torsion).
For R of ECD Example 3.4(iv) (no base field) the theorem applies; the Tate-ring proofs of the ingredients do not use a base field.

nodes.title: Almost acyclicity for p-finite perfectoid affinoids via Tate's acyclicity theorem
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ. A perfectoid affinoid K-algebra (R, R⁺) is p-finite if it is the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid K-algebra (S, S⁺) of topologically finite type in Sch12 Definition 2.6(iii), including S⁺ = S°: R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_Φ S⁺ and R = R⁺[ϖ⁻¹] (Sch12 Definition 6.9). For such (S, S⁺) and Y = Spa(S, S⁺): (i) S° is open and bounded (S is uniform); (ii) for every rational V ⊆ Y, O_Y(V) is again a reduced affinoid K-algebra of topologically finite type; (iii) for every finite covering of a rational V ⊆ Y by rational subsets, every cohomology module of the augmented Čech complex of the O_Y(·)° is killed by a power of ϖ. Consequently, for X = Spa(R, R⁺): (iv) the projection X → Y is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets; (v) for rational U ⊆ X corresponding to V ⊆ Y, (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the completed perfection of (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)); (vi) for every finite rational covering of X the augmented Čech complex 0 → O_X(X)°ᵃ → ∏ O_X(U_i)°ᵃ → ∏ O_X(U_i ∩ U_j)°ᵃ → ⋯ is exact, so O_X is a sheaf and H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0 for i > 0, equivalently H^i(X, O_X⁺) is almost zero (Sch12 Proposition 6.11, Remark 6.12).
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic p; every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p is a perfectoid affinoid algebra over the perfectoid field F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ via t ↦ ϖ, with R⁺ an algebra over its ring of integers (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.14; stated as AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field (a)), so the notion covers all characteristic-p perfectoid Tate pairs that arise as completed perfections.
(S, S⁺) is reduced and topologically of finite type over K in the source convention: S is a quotient of a Tate algebra and S⁺ = S°. An arbitrary smaller plus ring is not part of Sch12 Definition 6.9.

The route through Tate's acyclicity is an alternative to the Frobenius route of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity; it is kept because Sch12 §7 (Lemma 7.5(ii), Propositions 7.6, 7.7, 7.13) reduces étale statements to p-finite algebras and hence to noetherian adic spaces.
proofSteps: (i) Reduced K-affinoid algebras are uniform: the supremum norm is equivalent to any residue norm (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm; BGR 6.2.4 Theorem 1 in Sch12's citation).
(ii) O_Y(V) is a K-affinoid algebra (a quotient of S⟨T⟩) and is reduced (BGR 7.3.2 Corollary 10, via Huber [19] Proposition 4.3; recorded as a request to AdicSpacesPartII:R0 and a gap).

(iii) (S, S⁺) is strongly noetherian (anchor Layer 0.5), so the O_Y-Čech complex is exact in all degrees (anchor Layer 4.1, all-degree Tate acyclicity) and (S, S⁺) is stably uniform by (i)-(ii); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion in its O° form (the O_Y(V)° are open and bounded by (i)-(ii)) gives the bounded torsion (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.10(iii)).

(iv)-(v) Perfection does not change the adic spectrum or the rational subsets (Frobenius is a homeomorphism on Spa and preserves rational subsets), and completion does not change them either (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48; Huber [19] Proposition 2.11 in Sch12); the completed perfection of (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) is perfectoid and has the universal property of (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p).

(vi) The O°-Čech complex for X is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_Φ of the complex for Y; along Frobenius, a bound ϖ^M on the complex for Y becomes ϖ^{M/p^k} at the k-th stage, so the colimit is almost exact, and completion preserves almost exactness (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer). The sheaf-cohomology form follows by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis.
acceptance: For S = K⟨T⟩ and the covering by {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|ϖ| ≤ |T|}, R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is p-finite, X ≅ Y, and the O°-Čech complex is exact both for Y and for X.
Remark 6.12: almost exactness of the O°ᵃ-complex is equivalent to m-torsion of H^i(X, O_X⁺).

nodes.title: Perfectoid affinoid algebras in characteristic p are completed direct limits of p-finite ones
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, and (R, R⁺) a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra such that R⁺ is a K°-algebra. Then: (i) (R, R⁺) is the completion of a filtered direct limit of p-finite perfectoid affinoid K-algebras (R_I, R_I⁺), indexed by the finite subsets I ⊆ R⁺: S_I is the image of K⟨T_i : i ∈ I⟩ → R with the quotient topology, S_I⁺ the integral closure in S_I of the image of K°⟨T_i : i ∈ I⟩, and (R_I, R_I⁺) the completed perfection of (S_I, S_I⁺); precisely R⁺/ϖ^n = colim_I R_I⁺/ϖ^n for all n; (ii) Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ lim_I Spa(R_I, R_I⁺), and every rational U ⊆ X is the preimage of a rational U_I ⊆ X_I = Spa(R_I, R_I⁺) for some I; (iii) (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the completion of colim_{J ⊇ I} (O_{X_J}(U_J), O_{X_J}⁺(U_J)), U_J the preimage of U_I; (iv) if U_I ⊆ X_I is a quasi-compact open containing the image of X, then the image of X_J lies in U_I for some J ⊇ I.
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic p and R⁺ a K°-algebra. Every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p satisfies this for K = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ with t ↦ ϖ (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.14); that reduction is stated for consumers as AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field (a), which cites this node for (i).

The choice S_I⁺ = integral closure of the image of K°⟨T_i⟩ makes S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺ automatic (R⁺ is integrally closed and contains the images of the T_i); Sch12 instead takes S_I⁺ = S_I° and uses Tate's theorem (power-bounded elements of a reduced affinoid algebra are integral over K°⟨T⟩, [31] Theorem 5.2) to get S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺. S_I⁺ is in general not the preimage of R⁺ in S_I.
proofSteps: (i) S_I is a reduced quotient of K⟨T_i⟩ (R is reduced, being perfect), S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺, and (R_I, R_I⁺) → (R, R⁺) exists by the universal property of the completed perfection. R⁺/ϖ^n = colim_I R_I⁺/ϖ^n: surjectivity is clear; for injectivity, if f₁, f₂ ∈ R_I⁺ satisfy f₁ − f₂ = ϖ^n g with g ∈ R⁺, then for J ⊇ I containing g, f₁ − f₂ ∈ ϖ^n R_J⁺. Hence R⁺ is the completed direct limit of the R_I⁺.

(ii) For the uncompleted direct limit (L, L⁺) with the ϖ-adic topology, Spa(L, L⁺) ≅ lim Spa(R_I, R_I⁺) compatibly with rational subsets (a continuous valuation of L is a compatible family, and a rational subset is defined by finitely many elements, which live at a finite stage); completion does not change Spa or rational subsets (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48). Cofiltered limits of spectral spaces along spectral maps are spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

(iii) The completed colimit of the (O_{X_J}(U_J), O_{X_J}⁺(U_J)) is perfectoid and satisfies the universal property of (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p).

(iv) Let A_I be the closed complement of U_I and A_J its preimage in X_J: constructible, hence spectral and compact in the constructible topology, with continuous transition maps; their inverse limit is the preimage of A_I in X, which is empty, so some A_J is empty (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets; Tychonoff).
acceptance: For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I = {T}, S_I = K⟨T⟩ and R_I = R: the system stabilises at a finite stage.
Part (iv) lets a finite rational covering of X, and finite étale covers over it, descend to a finite stage X_J (Sch12 Propositions 6.14 and 7.6).

nodes.title: Affinoid perfectoid spaces: adic spectra of perfectoid Huber pairs
nodes.statement: An adic space X (an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces, Layer 5: an object of Huber's category 𝒱 locally isomorphic to the adic spectrum of a sheafy Huber pair) is *affinoid perfectoid* if there are a complete Hausdorff Huber pair (R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`: R⁺ ⊆ R° open and integrally closed) with R a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective) and an isomorphism of adic spaces X ≅ Spa(R, R⁺). Here Spa(R, R⁺) is an adic space because perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy). For such X the global sections recover the pair: (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) ≅ (R, R⁺) as topological rings with plus rings (anchor Layer 3.5, and O_X⁺(X) = {f : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} = R⁺ by Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)), so X is affinoid perfectoid iff X is affinoid in the anchor's sense and O_X(X) is a perfectoid Tate ring, and then X ≅ Spa(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) canonically. By Wedhorn Proposition 8.25, Spa is an anti-equivalence from complete perfectoid Huber pairs with morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`: continuous ring maps carrying plus ring into plus ring) to the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Pinned conventions: (1) the predicate asks for a presentation by a perfectoid ring (Berkeley Remark 7.1.3); it is not the conjunction 'affinoid and a perfectoid space', the two agree in characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion), and their agreement in characteristic 0 is not asserted; (2) no perfectoid base field is fixed, R⁺ is an arbitrary ring of integral elements, and the zero ring is allowed, so the empty adic space is affinoid perfectoid; (3) morphisms are morphisms of adic spaces. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidPerfectoid X`.
hypotheses: X is an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces (Layer 5).
(R, R⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair and R is a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1).
proofSteps: Spa(R, R⁺) is an adic space: rational localisations of (R, R⁺) are perfectoid, hence uniform, so (R, R⁺) is stably uniform and sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy, which uses the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem of anchor Layer 4.2).

Global sections: for a complete Hausdorff sheafy pair O_X(X) ≅ R as topological rings (anchor Layer 3.5), and O_X⁺(X) = {f ∈ R : v(f) ≤ 1 for all v ∈ Spa(R, R⁺)} = R⁺ (anchor Layer 2.3, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)); ECD Theorem 3.24 (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity) gives the same for H⁰(X, O_X⁺).

Anti-equivalence: morphisms Y → Spa(R, R⁺) from an adic space Y correspond to morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25, requested from anchor Layer 5); with the previous step, Spa is fully faithful on complete perfectoid Tate pairs, and essentially surjective onto affinoid perfectoid spaces by definition.
Closure under isomorphisms and the analytic and spectral properties of |X| follow from the Tau Ceti results on Spa of a Tate Huber ring (every point analytic; Spa spectral).
acceptance: Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) is affinoid perfectoid, and it has exactly one point.
Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is an affinoid adic space that is not affinoid perfectoid, because O(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)) = ℚ_p is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
For the perfectoid Tate ring R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] of ECD Example 3.4(iv), which does not live over a perfectoid field, Spa(R, R°) is affinoid perfectoid.

nodes.title: Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory Perfd of adic spaces, and Perf in characteristic p
nodes.statement: A *perfectoid space* is an adic space X (anchor Layer 5) covered by open subspaces that are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space): every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U such that the open adic subspace (U, O_X|_U, (v_y)_{y ∈ U}) is isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring and R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements (ECD Definition 3.19). The category Perfd of perfectoid spaces is the full subcategory of the anchor's category of adic spaces on these objects (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`): morphisms are morphisms of adic spaces; open subspaces, gluing and the sheaf property of morphisms are the anchor's, and no second carrier (no separate locally ringed space and no second gluing theory) is introduced. Perf ⊆ Perfd is the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p, those with p = 0 in O_X(X); equivalently, X admits a morphism (necessarily unique) to the discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p), which is an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy) but not a perfectoid space, and which Perf does not contain. Properties pinned with the definition: every point of a perfectoid space is analytic, so every morphism of adic spaces into a perfectoid space is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism); an adic space with p = 0 in its structure sheaf is perfectoid iff it is covered by open subspaces Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfect complete Tate ring (ECD Proposition 3.5). Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsPerfectoidSpace X`, the category `PerfectoidSpace`, and `PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.
hypotheses: X is an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces.
p is a fixed prime.
proofSteps: The predicate is local on X and invariant under isomorphisms; Perfd := ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory IsPerfectoidSpace with the fully faithful inclusion ObjectProperty.ι (Mathlib).

Analyticity: an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R⁺) has R Tate, so all its points are analytic (Tau Ceti ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing); being analytic is local, so every perfectoid space is analytic and every morphism into it is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus).

Characteristic p: p = 0 in O_X(X) iff p = 0 in O_X(U) for all U (restriction maps are ring maps and O_X is a sheaf), iff there is a morphism of Huber pairs (𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) (continuity is automatic from the discrete topology and 𝔽_p is integral over ℤ), iff X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) exists (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25); uniqueness because 𝔽_p has only one ring map to a ring of characteristic p.

Perfect-ring criterion: ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) identifies perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p with perfect complete Tate rings, chart by chart.
acceptance: Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}), Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl) and the perfectoid closed disc Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) are perfectoid spaces; Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) lies in Perf.
Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), the closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and the discrete Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) are adic spaces that are not perfectoid.

nodes.title: Rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid opens are affinoid perfectoid, and affinoid perfectoid opens form a basis
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space. (i) If V ⊆ X is an open subspace with an isomorphism V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid, then for every rational subset W = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, T·R open) the open subspace W ⊆ X is affinoid perfectoid: W ≅ Spa(R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺), where (R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) is the rational localisation of anchor Layer 3.1, a perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), and (O_X(W), O_X⁺(W)) ≅ (R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) compatibly with restriction from V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction). (ii) The affinoid perfectoid open subspaces of X form a basis of the topology of |X|; every quasi-compact open subset of X is a finite union of them. (iii) For affinoid perfectoid opens V, V' ⊆ X and x ∈ V ∩ V' there is an open W with x ∈ W ⊆ V ∩ V' that is a rational subset of V and of V' (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3)), hence affinoid perfectoid by (i). (iv) For every affinoid perfectoid open V ⊆ X, O_X(V) is a perfectoid Tate ring and V ≅ Spa(O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) canonically (the observation in the proof of Sch12 Proposition 6.17). The intersection of two affinoid perfectoid opens need not be affinoid, nor quasi-compact.
hypotheses: X a perfectoid space; V ⊆ X an open subspace with V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid.
W = R(T/s) a rational subset of Spa(R, R⁺) with T·R open (for R Tate: T generates the unit ideal).
proofSteps: (i) The open subspace W ⊆ V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) is isomorphic to Spa of the rational localisation (anchor Layer 3.1: Spa(R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) ≅ W matching valuations and rational subsets, Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph` on underlying spaces), and the rational localisation of a perfectoid Tate pair is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

(ii) Rational subsets form a basis of Spa(R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`) and are quasi-compact (`isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`); combine with the affinoid perfectoid cover of X from the definition and (i).
(iii) Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3) for the open affinoid subspaces V, V' of the adic space X, then (i).
(iv) By definition V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) for some perfectoid Tate pair; global sections give (O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) ≅ (R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space, `spaGlobalSectionsIso`).

nodes.title: Open subspaces of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid; open immersions in Perfd
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space and U ⊆ |X| open. The open adic subspace X|_U = (U, O_X|_U, (v_x)_{x ∈ U}) of anchor Layer 5.1 (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(2)) is a perfectoid space, and the inclusion j : X|_U → X is an open immersion of perfectoid spaces with the universal property in Perfd and in adic spaces: a morphism f : Y → X from an adic space Y factors through j, uniquely, iff f(|Y|) ⊆ U. Conversely: (a) the source of an open immersion of adic spaces into a perfectoid space is perfectoid; (b) an adic space covered by open subspaces that are perfectoid spaces is perfectoid; (c) for open U' ⊆ U, (X|_U)|_{U'} = X|_{U'}. Consequently Perfd is closed under open subspaces, the open immersions in Perfd are the anchor's open immersions between perfectoid spaces, and Perf is closed under open subspaces.
hypotheses: X a perfectoid space; U ⊆ |X| open.
proofSteps: Every x ∈ U has an affinoid perfectoid open neighbourhood inside U: take an affinoid perfectoid V ∋ x and a rational W ⊆ V ∩ U containing x; W is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (i)); hence X|_U is perfectoid.
The universal property of open subspaces is the anchor's (Layer 5.1); since Perfd is a full subcategory (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) it holds in Perfd.
(a) An open immersion V → X is an isomorphism onto X|_U, U its image; apply the first step and closure under isomorphisms. (b) The perfectoid property is local by definition. (c) Anchor Layer 5.1.
Characteristic p passes to open subspaces because restriction O_X(X) → O_X(U) is a ring map.
acceptance: For X = Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) the punctured disc {T ≠ 0} is an open perfectoid subspace of X in Perf, which is not quasi-compact and so not affinoid.

nodes.title: Characteristic p: perfectoid spaces are adic spaces locally Spa of perfect Tate rings, and affinoid perfectoid spaces are the affinoid ones
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space with p = 0 in O_X(X). (i) X is a perfectoid space iff X is covered by open subspaces isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfect complete Tate ring. (ii) If X is a perfectoid space, then O_X(U) is a perfect ring (Mathlib `PerfectRing (O_X(U)) p`) for every open U ⊆ X. (iii) (Mihara; Bhatt, Exercise 9.3.12) If X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺) for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺) with A Tate, and X is a perfectoid space, then A is perfect, hence a perfectoid Tate ring, and X is affinoid perfectoid. The analogue of (iii) in characteristic 0 is not asserted: whether an affinoid adic space that is a perfectoid space is affinoid perfectoid is recorded as unclear in Bhatt, Remark 9.3.11.
hypotheses: X an adic space with p = 0 in O_X(X).
(iii): (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff, sheafy, A Tate, X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺).
proofSteps: (i) Chart by chart, ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect): a topological ring of characteristic p is a perfectoid Tate ring iff it is a perfect complete Tate ring.

(ii) Cover U by affinoid perfectoid opens V_i and each V_i ∩ V_j by affinoid perfectoid opens V_ijk (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis); O_X(V_i) and O_X(V_ijk) are perfectoid of characteristic p, hence perfect. By the sheaf property O_X(U) is the equalizer of ∏ O_X(V_i) ⇉ ∏ O_X(V_ijk); Frobenius commutes with the restriction maps, so it is injective on O_X(U), and p-th roots, unique in each O_X(V_i), agree on the V_ijk and glue. Hence O_X(U) is perfect.

(iii) A ≅ O_X(X) for the complete Hausdorff sheafy pair (anchor Layer 3.5), which is perfect by (ii) with U = X; a perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5, uniformity being automatic by the open mapping argument of Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6), so X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺) is affinoid perfectoid.
acceptance: X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: X is a perfectoid space and A is perfect.
For A = 𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩ (not perfect), Spa(A, A°) is not a perfectoid space, by (iii).

nodes.title: The glued tilt X ↦ X♭ of a perfectoid space
nodes.statement: For every perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space; any characteristic, no base field) there is a perfectoid space X♭ of characteristic p, the *tilt* of X, with a homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭|, x ↦ x♭, constructed by gluing (ECD, the sentence after Definition 3.19; Sch12 Definition 6.16 and Proposition 6.17 over a perfectoid field). Affinoid case: for X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid, X♭ := Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), where (R♭, R♭⁺) is the tilt of the pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring: R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting: R♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R⁺), and x ↦ x♭ is the tilting homeomorphism |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), which matches rational subsets U ↔ U♭ and satisfies (O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭ compatibly with restrictions (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids). General case: X♭ is glued (anchor Layer 5.3) from the tilts V♭ of all affinoid perfectoid open subspaces V ⊆ X, along the tilts of their common rational refinements (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)); since this family is canonical, X♭ is defined up to unique isomorphism, and |X♭| = |X| as sets with the same open subsets. A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces gives f♭ : Y♭ → X♭, affinoid-locally Spa of the tilt of the corresponding morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), glued because morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf; this makes X ↦ X♭ a functor Perfd ⥤ Perf with |f♭| = |f| under the homeomorphisms. Properties: (a) for U ⊆ X open, (X|_U)♭ = X♭|_{U♭}, where U♭ is U viewed in |X♭|; U is affinoid perfectoid iff U♭ is, and then (O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭; (b) the sharp maps glue to a continuous multiplicative map of sheaves of topological monoids O_{X♭} → O_X on |X| = |X♭|, f ↦ f♯, with |f♯(x)| = |f(x♭)|, carrying O⁺_{X♭} into O⁺_X; it is not additive; (c) for X of characteristic p, projection to the zeroth coordinate R♭ → R is a ring isomorphism, giving a natural isomorphism X♭ ≅ X; (d) X is not determined by X♭ (the tilt forgets the untilt); the equivalence of slice categories, and with it the description of maps into X♭ by untilts, is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.tilt : PerfectoidSpace ⥤ PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid spaces; f : Y → X a morphism of adic spaces.
Perfectoid pairs are complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (R, R⁺) with R perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1).
proofSteps: Affinoid case: X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) is affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, ECD Lemma 3.10: R♭ is a perfectoid 𝔽_p-algebra); the homeomorphism and the matching of rational subsets are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets (ECD Theorem 3.12), and the identification of the rational localisations of the tilt with the tilts of the rational localisations is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids (ECD Theorem 3.18).

Transition data: for affinoid perfectoid opens V, V' ⊆ X and W ⊆ V ∩ V' rational in both (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)), the two open embeddings W♭ → V♭, W♭ → V'♭ are Spa of the tilts of the restriction maps O_X(V) → O_X(W) and O_X(V') → O_X(W) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality); they agree with the identification of |W| inside |V| and |V'|, and the cocycle condition holds because it holds after composing with the homeomorphisms to |X| (the tilting maps are compatible with restriction).

Glue with the anchor's gluing of adic spaces (Layer 5.3; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GlueData` underneath) to obtain X♭, a perfectoid space of characteristic p covered by the V♭, with |X♭| identified with |X|.

Morphisms: given f : Y → X, cover Y by affinoid perfectoid V with f(V) ⊆ U, U affinoid perfectoid; f|_V corresponds to a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) → (O_Y(V), O⁺_Y(V)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25); tilt it (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality) and glue the resulting morphisms (Wedhorn Remark 8.24); functoriality and |f♭| = |f| are checked on affinoids, where they are the naturality of the tilting homeomorphism.
(b): the sharp map R♭ → R is continuous and multiplicative and compatible with rational localisations (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map); it glues as a map of sheaves of sets.
(c): for R of characteristic p, (x^{(i)})_i ↦ x^{(0)} is a ring isomorphism R♭ → R with inverse x ↦ (x^{1/p^i})_i, natural in R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring); glue.
acceptance: Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) with t = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) − 1 (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
For a perfectoid Tate ring R, Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa(R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with T ↦ (T, T^{1/p}, …) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).
Affinoid perfectoid open subspaces of X are exactly the U with U♭ ⊆ X♭ affinoid perfectoid (Sch12 Proposition 6.17).

nodes.title: Tilting is an equivalence between perfectoid Tate pairs over (A, A⁺) and over (A♭, A♭⁺), compatible with rational localisation
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete perfectoid Tate pair (A perfectoid Tate ring, A⁺ ⊆ A° a ring of integral elements) with tilt (A♭, A♭⁺). Let Perfd_{(A,A⁺)} be the category of complete perfectoid Tate pairs (B, B⁺) with a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), morphisms being morphisms of Huber pairs under (A, A⁺); define Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)} likewise. Then the tilt (B, B⁺) ↦ (B♭, B♭⁺) is an equivalence Perfd_{(A,A⁺)} ≃ Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)}. A quasi-inverse sends (S, S⁺) to the untilt (W(S⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ, W(S⁺)/ξ) along a generator ξ of ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺), with ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ a pseudouniformiser (ECD Lemma 3.14 and Theorem 3.17; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). The equivalence carries rational localisations to rational localisations: for f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ B♭ generating the unit ideal, (B⟨f♯/g♯⟩)♭ ≅ B♭⟨f/g⟩ over B♭, and every rational localisation of B arises so. Through Spa (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space) it gives an equivalence between affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(A, A⁺) and over Spa(A♭, A♭⁺), compatible with the tilting homeomorphisms.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) a complete perfectoid Tate pair; no perfectoid base field.
proofSteps: Rings: the tilt is an equivalence between perfectoid A-algebras and perfectoid A♭-algebras with unit and counit (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt; ECD Theorem 3.13, which asserts the general case).

Plus rings: B⁺ ↦ B♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} B⁺ is an inclusion-preserving bijection between rings of integral elements with B♭⁺/ϖ♭ = B⁺/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, ECD Lemma 3.11), natural in B; a morphism B → C carries B⁺ into C⁺ iff its tilt carries B♭⁺ into C♭⁺, since both conditions can be read modulo ϖ♭ ≅ ϖ on the common quotients B♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ B°/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10).

Quasi-inverse: B ≅ W(B♭⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ for the image of the primitive generator ξ of ker θ_A (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction), functorially in (B, B⁺) under (A, A⁺).
Rational localisations: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids (ECD Theorem 3.18; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.3(b)).
Spaces: Spa is an anti-equivalence on complete perfectoid Tate pairs (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and morphisms over Spa(A, A⁺) are morphisms of pairs under (A, A⁺).
