nodes.title: Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭ (ECD Corollary 3.20)
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting). (a) The functor Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ = Perfd/X♭ on slice categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over`), (f : Y → X) ↦ (f♭ : Y♭ → X♭), is an equivalence of categories (a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`). (b) It commutes with restriction to open subspaces of X, and a perfectoid space Y over X is affinoid perfectoid iff Y♭ is; for X = Spa(A, A⁺) it restricts on affinoid perfectoid spaces to the equivalence of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence. (c) Untilts over X: for every perfectoid space T of characteristic p and every morphism g : T → X♭ there are a perfectoid space T♯ with a morphism T♯ → X and an isomorphism ι : (T♯)♭ ≅ T over X♭, and the pair (T♯ → X, ι) is unique up to unique isomorphism; so Hom_Perf(T, X♭) is in natural bijection with isomorphism classes of such pairs, functorially in T. (d) Under the homeomorphisms |Y| ≅ |Y♭| the structure maps correspond. The quasi-inverse depends on X: there is no untilting functor Perf → Perfd without a chosen base (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting, test tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes).
hypotheses: X a perfectoid space (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field).
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: for Y, Y' over X, the map Hom_X(Y, Y') → Hom_{X♭}(Y♭, Y'♭) is a map of sheaves on |Y| = |Y♭| (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24), so it suffices to treat Y affinoid perfectoid mapping into an affinoid perfectoid open V' ⊆ Y' lying over an affinoid perfectoid open U ⊆ X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis); there morphisms are morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs under (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence gives bijectivity.

Essential surjectivity: given g : T → X♭, cover T by affinoid perfectoid T_i with g(T_i) ⊆ U_i♭, U_i ⊆ X affinoid perfectoid; the pair-level equivalence gives affinoid perfectoid untilts T_i♯ over U_i with (T_i♯)♭ ≅ T_i over U_i♭; on overlaps, refined to opens rational in both charts (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)), the restricted untilts are canonically isomorphic by full faithfulness, and these isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition by uniqueness; glue (anchor Layer 5.3) to T♯ → X with (T♯)♭ ≅ T.
(b) and (d) follow from the construction of the glued tilt (open subspaces, affinoid criterion, homeomorphisms); (c) is (a) restated for objects of Perf/X♭.
acceptance: Sch12 Proposition 6.17: for a perfectoid field K, perfectoid spaces over K and over K♭ are equivalent (the case X = Spa(K, K⁺₀), see PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison).

For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl), the perfectoid disc over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) untilts to Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), and Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))) itself (with the identity to X♭) untilts to X.
Unit and counit are isomorphisms compatible with restriction to open subspaces of X.

nodes.title: Characteristic p: the completed tensor product of perfect complete Tate rings is perfect, uniform and perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p, equivalently perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5). Both maps are adic (continuous maps out of a Tate ring are adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so the completed tensor product (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product is defined. Let ϖ ∈ A be a pseudouniformiser, F ⊆ B ⊗_A C the image of B° ⊗_{A°} C° (a ring of definition for R0's topology, because ϖB° ⊆ B⁺ ⊆ B° and likewise for C) and F̂ ⊆ D its ϖ-adic completion. Then: (i) D and F̂ are perfect rings; (ii) D is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence uniform and perfectoid, and the uniformisation D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism; (iii) ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D° for all n ≥ 0, where ϖ^{1/p^n} are the p-power roots in the perfect ring A; in particular ϖD° ⊆ F̂, and F̂ → D° is injective with cokernel killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, i.e. an almost isomorphism for the almost setup of A (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); (iv) the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗_{A°} C° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}.
hypotheses: A, B, C perfect complete Tate rings of characteristic p with morphisms of complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺).
proofSteps: B ⊗_A C is perfect: Frobenius b ⊗ c ↦ b^p ⊗ c^p is bijective with inverse b ⊗ c ↦ b^{1/p} ⊗ c^{1/p}, well defined because the inverse Frobenii of A, B, C are compatible with A → B and A → C (routine).
F is a perfect subring: B° and C° are perfect (x is power-bounded iff x^p is), so Frobenius and its inverse preserve the generators b ⊗ c (b ∈ B°, c ∈ C°); F is open and bounded for R0's topology.
Frobenius and its inverse are continuous for the ϖ-adic topology of F (Φ⁻¹(ϖ^{pk}F) = ϖ^k F), so they extend to F̂ and to D = F̂[1/ϖ]: (i).

(ii) A perfect complete Tate ring is uniform and perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6 proves uniformity by the open mapping argument); a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pair is its own uniformisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (e)).

(iii) For x ∈ D° choose N with ϖ^N x^m ∈ F̂ for all m ≥ 0 (F̂ open, {x^m} bounded); then (ϖ^{N/p^n} x)^{p^n} ∈ F̂ and F̂ is perfect, so ϖ^{N/p^n} x ∈ F̂ for all n; taking n with N/p^n ≤ ε gives ϖ^ε x ∈ F̂ for every ε ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{>0}.

(iv) M := B° ⊗_{A°} C° is perfect by the argument of the first step. If ϖ^k f = 0 in M, applying the inverse Frobenius gives ϖ^{k/p} f^{1/p} = 0, and multiplying by f^{(p-1)/p} gives ϖ^{k/p} f = 0; iterating, ϖ^{k/p^n} f = 0 for all n (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.18).
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K of characteristic p: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩ with F̂ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.
Without perfectness the conclusion fails: 𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_{𝔽_p((t))} 𝔽_p((t))⟨S⟩ is uniform but not perfect.

nodes.title: A uniform Tate ring receiving a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let f : A → B be a continuous ring homomorphism with dense image from a perfectoid Tate ring A to a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring B (B° bounded). Then B is a perfectoid Tate ring and f♭ : A♭ → B♭ has dense image (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3 and Lemma 2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18, class (ii); over ℚ_p Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.6.17(b)). Uniformity of B is a hypothesis: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) (closure of the ideal) is surjective, but the target is not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).
hypotheses: A a perfectoid Tate ring; B a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with B° bounded; f continuous with dense image.
proofSteps: B♭ := lim_{x ↦ x^p} B with the limiting addition is a perfect complete uniform Tate ring of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer f♭(ϖ_A♭), where ϖ_A♭ ∈ A♭ has compatible roots, and θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ is defined and natural (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c), (e); Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1). Only completeness, uniformity and topological nilpotence of p in B are used.

B₀♭ := the closure of f♭(A♭) in B♭ is a closed perfect subring containing f♭(ϖ_A♭), hence a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c); ECD Proposition 3.5, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

B₀ := the untilt of B₀♭ along the image of the primitive ideal ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), with maps A → B₀ → B, the second induced by θ_B, which kills the image of ker θ_A by naturality of θ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (e)); B₀ → B has dense image since W(A♭⁺) → A → B does.

B₀ → B is a strict inclusion, indeed an isometry for the spectral gauges of the images of ϖ_A, because B₀♭ → B♭ is one (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting (b), which needs only that B is uniform; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2).

Metric criterion (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3, after Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2): for the spectral gauge of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, a uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff there is c ∈ (0, 1) with: for every x there is y with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|. B₀ satisfies it; by density and isometry B does, so B is perfectoid; then B₀ → B is a dense strict inclusion of complete rings, hence an isomorphism, and f♭ has dense image.
acceptance: If B is the completed residue field of a point of Spa(A, A⁺) (a uniform nonarchimedean field receiving a dense-image map from the completed colimit of rational localisations), B is perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7, second proof).

The uniformisation of a completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C with B, C perfectoid receives a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base).

nodes.title: Completed tensor products of perfectoid Tate pairs are perfectoid, uniform, and commute with tilting
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1; any characteristic; no perfectoid base field). Both maps are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so the completed tensor product (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C with inl, inr (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product; D⁺ the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺) is defined. Then: (i) D is a perfectoid Tate ring; in particular D is uniform and the uniformisation D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism (the tensor-product norm is the spectral norm, Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13(b)); (ii) (D, D⁺) with inl, inr is a pushout of (B, B⁺) ← (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) in the category of complete perfectoid Tate pairs; (iii) tilting commutes with it: there is a unique isomorphism of Huber pairs (D♭, D♭⁺) ≅ (B♭, B♭⁺) ⊗̂_{(A♭, A♭⁺)} (C♭, C♭⁺) whose composites with inl♭, inr♭ are inl, inr (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13(a)); (iv) for a pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p in A° and compatible p-power roots (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), the ϖ-adic completion F̂ of the image F of B° ⊗_{A°} C° in B ⊗_A C satisfies ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D° for all n, and the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗_{A°} C° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}; so F̂ → D° is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), which over a perfectoid field K is Scholze's statement that A°a ⊗̂_{B°a} C°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra (Sch12 Proposition 6.18). The perfectoid base A is essential: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings.
(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
proofSteps: Adicness: continuous maps out of a Tate ring are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing`), so (D, D⁺) is defined (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product).
Characteristic p: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor.

Candidate untilt: let (R, R⁺), (S, S⁺), (T, T⁺) be the tilts of (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) and (U, U⁺) = S ⊗̂_R T, a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p (previous step) which is a pushout among complete perfectoid Tate pairs (universal property AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property). By PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence there are a perfectoid Tate pair (E, E⁺) under (A, A⁺) with (E♭, E♭⁺) ≅ (U, U⁺) and morphisms (B, B⁺) → (E, E⁺) ← (C, C⁺) untilting S → U ← T; as tilting is an equivalence under (A, A⁺), (E, E⁺) is a pushout among complete perfectoid Tate pairs.
Comparison map: the universal property of (D, D⁺) (E complete Hausdorff, E⁺ closed and integrally closed) gives χ : (D, D⁺) → (E, E⁺) compatible with inl, inr; χ(F̂) ⊆ E°.

Modulo ϖ: the functorial isomorphisms B°/ϖ ≅ S°/ϖ♭, C°/ϖ ≅ T°/ϖ♭ over A°/ϖ ≅ R°/ϖ♭ and E°/ϖ ≅ U°/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality) identify the composite (B° ⊗_{A°} C°)/ϖ → F/ϖ → E°/ϖ with (S° ⊗_{R°} T°)/ϖ♭ → F_U/ϖ♭ → U°/ϖ♭, which is an almost isomorphism by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor (iii)-(iv). The first arrow is surjective, so F/ϖ → E°/ϖ is an almost isomorphism and the kernel of (B° ⊗ C°)/ϖ → F/ϖ is almost zero.

Completion: F̂ and E° are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (F lies in B ⊗_A C, where ϖ is a unit, and the ϖ-adic completion of a ϖ-torsion-free module is ϖ-torsion free); a map of such modules that is an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ is an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ^n for all n (induction with the exact sequences 0 → M/ϖ^n → M/ϖ^{n+1} → M/ϖ → 0) and then an almost isomorphism: apply PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion to the two-term complex F̂ → E° (its Milnor sequence keeps the lim¹ term, which is almost zero, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).

Conclusion: F̂ → E° is injective (torsion free and almost injective) with ϖE° ⊆ F̂, so χ : D = F̂[1/ϖ] → E°[1/ϖ] = E is an isomorphism of topological rings; the plus rings agree because the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ contains D°° (by (iv), as ϖ^ε B° ⊆ B⁺ and ϖ^ε C° ⊆ C⁺) and is integrally closed (Wedhorn Remark 7.15(3)). This gives (i)–(iv); the uniformisation statement is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (e).
acceptance: B ⊗̂_A A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ B⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ for every perfectoid Tate pair (B, B⁺) under (A, A⁺) (perfected Tate algebras, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), compatibly with tilting; in particular A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_A A⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ A⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.

nodes.title: The uniform completed tensor product of perfectoid rings over an arbitrary Tate ring is perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with A a Tate ring (not necessarily perfectoid, uniform or of characteristic p), and let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of Huber pairs with B, C perfectoid Tate rings. Then the uniform completed tensor product B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is a perfectoid Tate ring (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21; Kedlaya–Liu I Corollary 3.6.18 over ℚ_p). If A is perfectoid it equals B ⊗̂_A C (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (i)); otherwise the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C need not be uniform (ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not), and the uniformisation cannot be omitted.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff with A Tate; B, C perfectoid Tate rings; morphisms of Huber pairs from (A, A⁺).
proofSteps: D^u := B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and the image of B ⊗_A C is dense in it (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (a)-(b), R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product).

Let P := B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩, the perfected Tate algebra over B in the (infinite) set C♭° of variables, a perfectoid Tate ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra with Σ = C♭°; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12). The continuous B-algebra map P → D^u with T_s^{1/p^n} ↦ inr((s^{1/p^n})♯) exists by the universal property of P (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra, `lift`), the images being power-bounded and compatible with p-th powers (the sharp map is multiplicative, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).

Its image is dense: it contains inl(B) and inr(x♯) for x ∈ C♭°; every c ∈ C° is a convergent sum Σ_i ((ϖ♭)^i x_i)♯ with x_i ∈ C♭°, obtained by successive approximation from the surjectivity of C♭° → C°/ϖ, x ↦ x♯ mod ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10), for ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯; so inr(C°), hence inr(C) = inr(C°)[1/ϖ], lies in the closure of the image, and so does the image of B ⊗_A C.
By the dense-image criterion (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion) D^u is perfectoid.

In characteristic p a direct argument also works: the Frobenius of D^u has dense image (it contains b ⊗ c = (b^{1/p} ⊗ c^{1/p})^p), satisfies |x^p| = |x|^p for the spectral norm, hence has closed image and is surjective, and is injective as D^u is reduced; so D^u is perfect, hence perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5).

nodes.title: Affinoid perfectoid fibre products: Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) is a fibre product in adic spaces, compatible with open subspaces
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺), Z = Spa(C, C⁺) be affinoid perfectoid spaces and Y → X ← Z morphisms, corresponding (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25) to morphisms of complete perfectoid Tate pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺). Let (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C, a complete perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), hence sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy). Then (a) W = Spa(D, D⁺) with p = Spa(inl) and q = Spa(inr) is a fibre product Y ×_X Z in the anchor's category of adic spaces (a Mathlib `IsPullback` square there), hence in Perfd, and W is affinoid perfectoid; this is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product with its sheafiness hypothesis discharged. (b) For rational subsets U' ⊆ X, U ⊆ Y, V ⊆ Z with U and V mapping into U', the open p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) ⊆ W is a rational subset and equals Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation). (c) For arbitrary open subspaces U ⊆ Y, V ⊆ Z, the open subspace p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) with the restricted projections is a fibre product U ×_X V in adic spaces. (d) The map |W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points) and not injective in general.
hypotheses: Y → X ← Z morphisms of affinoid perfectoid spaces (any characteristic, no base field).
proofSteps: (D, D⁺) is a complete perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and so sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy); (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) are sheafy for the same reason.

(a) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product applies (adicness of the ring maps: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) and gives the universal property against every adic space T; W is affinoid perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space.

(b) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation identifies p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) with a rational subset whose ring is O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V); the rational localisations are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so (a) applies to them.

(c) A pair of morphisms T → U, T → V over X is a pair of morphisms to Y, Z whose images lie in U, V; the induced T → W factors through the open p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces, universal property of open subspaces), uniquely.
(d) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points; non-injectivity: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces, test pullback_galois_points.

nodes.title: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist in adic spaces and are perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → X be morphisms of perfectoid spaces (any characteristic; no perfectoid base field). The fibre product W = Y ×_X Z exists in the anchor's category of adic spaces and is a perfectoid space; with its projections p : W → Y, q : W → Z it is therefore also a fibre product in Perfd, Perfd has all fibre products (Mathlib `HasPullbacks`), and the inclusion Perfd ⥤ AdicSpace preserves them. Construction: W is glued (anchor Layer 5.3) from the affinoid perfectoid spaces W_{U,U',V} = Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property), for affinoid perfectoid opens U' ⊆ X, U ⊆ f⁻¹(U'), V ⊆ g⁻¹(U'), along their common open subspaces, which are fibre products of the intersections (open compatibility (c) there). Pinned conventions: the affinoid formula uses AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product with plus ring the closure of the integral closure of the image of O_Y⁺(U) ⊗ O_Z⁺(V), which is almost, but not in general exactly, the completed tensor product of the plus rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula); the ring is already uniform, so no uniformisation is performed. Affinoid perfectoid spaces and Perf are closed under fibre products; tilting commutes with them (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products); |W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| is surjective but not injective in general. Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Proposition 6.18. Fibre products over a non-perfectoid analytic base are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base, and absolute products in Perf are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/products-in-perf. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.pullback f g` with `HasPullbacks PerfectoidSpace`.
hypotheses: f : Y → X, g : Z → X morphisms of perfectoid spaces.
proofSteps: Affinoid pieces: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property (a) gives W_{U,U',V} = U ×_{U'} V in adic spaces; since U' ⊆ X is open, U ×_{U'} V = U ×_X V (open subspace universal property, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).

Gluing data: for two index triples, the open subspaces p⁻¹(U ∩ Ũ) ∩ q⁻¹(V ∩ Ṽ) of W_{U,U',V} and of W_{Ũ,Ũ',Ṽ} are both fibre products (U ∩ Ũ) ×_X (V ∩ Ṽ) (part (c) there), hence canonically isomorphic, and the cocycle condition follows from uniqueness of the comparison isomorphisms (the pattern of EGA I (3.2.6)); glue with anchor Layer 5.3.

Universal property: given a : T → Y, b : T → Z with f a = g b from an adic space T, cover T by the opens a⁻¹(U) ∩ b⁻¹(V) ∩ (f a)⁻¹(U'); on each the morphism to W_{U,U',V} is unique, the local morphisms agree on overlaps, and they glue (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24).
W is perfectoid (covered by affinoid perfectoid W_{U,U',V}); p and q are adic (every morphism into a perfectoid space is adic); if X, Y, Z have characteristic p so does W (inl is a ring map).
Points: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points on each affinoid piece.
acceptance: Sch12 Proposition 6.18: for perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K, Y ×_X Z exists in adic spaces over K and is perfectoid.

nodes.title: Tilting commutes with fibre products of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: For morphisms Y → X ← Z of perfectoid spaces, the tilts of the projections exhibit (Y ×_X Z)♭ as the fibre product Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ in Perf and in adic spaces: the canonical morphism (Y ×_X Z)♭ → Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ is an isomorphism. On affinoid pieces it is the isomorphism (B ⊗̂_A C)♭ ≅ B♭ ⊗̂_{A♭} C♭ of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iii). More generally the tilting equivalence Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭ preserves every limit that exists in Perfd/X.
hypotheses: Y → X ← Z morphisms of perfectoid spaces.
proofSteps: Y ×_X Z, with its map to X, is the binary product of Y and Z in Perfd/X (Mathlib `Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`: pullbacks give binary products in the slice category).

The tilting functor Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ is an equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence) and equivalences preserve limits (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isEquivalencePreservesLimits`), so it sends this product to the product of Y♭ and Z♭ in Perf/X♭, which is Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces in Perf).

On affinoid pieces, uniqueness of morphisms into a fibre product identifies the resulting isomorphism with the ring-level tilt isomorphism of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iii).

nodes.title: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces over an analytic adic space, in Perfd, via uniform completed tensor products
nodes.statement: Let S be an analytic adic space (anchor Layer 5; every point analytic, e.g. Spa(K, K⁺) for any nonarchimedean field K, or any rigid space) and f : Y → S, g : Z → S morphisms from perfectoid spaces. Then the fibre product Y ×_S Z exists in Perfd: there is a perfectoid space W with morphisms p : W → Y, q : W → Z, f p = g q, such that for every perfectoid space T, Hom(T, W) = Hom(T, Y) ×_{Hom(T, S)} Hom(T, Z). Affinoid-locally, for an open affinoid U' = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S with A a complete Tate ring (the analytic locus is covered by such, anchor Layer 2.3) and affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ f⁻¹(U'), V ⊆ g⁻¹(U'), the piece of W over U, V is Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂ᵘ_A O_Z(V)), the uniform completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product), which is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base). If S is perfectoid, W is the fibre product of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (in all adic spaces). If S is not perfectoid, W is asserted to be a fibre product only in Perfd: the test objects are uniform, the completed tensor product itself need not be uniform (ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not) and its sheafiness is not known. The diagonal Y → Y ×_S Y is defined. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.pullbackOverAnalytic f g`.
hypotheses: S an analytic adic space; f : Y → S, g : Z → S morphisms with Y, Z perfectoid spaces.
proofSteps: Every morphism into the analytic space S is adic and the ring maps O_S(U') → O_Y(U) are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), so R0's (uniform) completed tensor products are defined.

Affinoid universal property in Perfd: for a perfectoid T = Spa(R, R⁺) (R uniform), morphisms T → Spa(D^u) are morphisms of pairs D^u → (R, R⁺) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), which are pairs of morphisms from O_Y(U), O_Z(V) agreeing on A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (b): pushout among complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pairs); for general perfectoid T glue over an affinoid perfectoid cover (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis, Wedhorn Remark 8.24).

Compatibility with rational subsets: the rational localisation of D^u at the preimages of rational U₁ ⊆ U, V₁ ⊆ V is O_Y(U₁) ⊗̂ᵘ_A O_Z(V₁), since both are initial among complete uniform pairs with the same maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation and the universal property of the uniformisation, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c)-(d)).
Glue the pieces as in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (anchor Layer 5.3).
If S is perfectoid, D^u = D (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (i)) and both constructions agree.
acceptance: For K a nonarchimedean field that is not perfectoid (e.g. ℚ_p) and perfectoid spaces Y, Z over Spa(K, K°), Y ×_{Spa K} Z is a perfectoid space; this is the fibre product used for analytic separatedness in PerfectoidSpaces:P8.

nodes.title: Absolute products in Perf
nodes.statement: Let X, Y be perfectoid spaces of characteristic p. The product X × Y exists in Perf (Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5; ECD proof of Proposition 11.4). It is also the fibre product X ×_{Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)} Y in the anchor's category of adic spaces, over the discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p), which is not a perfectoid (nor Tate, nor analytic) space; the structure maps X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) are not adic, so neither PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces nor AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence applies, and Perf has no final object (Berkeley Remark 8.3.6), so the absolute product is not a fibre product in Perf. Affinoid charts: for X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺) affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p with pseudouniformisers ϖ ∈ A, ϖ' ∈ B, and integers m, n ≥ 1, put E = A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B, u_m = (ϖ^m ⊗ 1)(1 ⊗ ϖ')⁻¹ and v_n = (1 ⊗ ϖ'^n)(ϖ ⊗ 1)⁻¹ in E, D_{m,n} = (A° ⊗ B°)[u_m, v_n] ⊆ E; topologise E so that D_{m,n} is open with the (ϖ ⊗ 1)-adic topology (equal to the (1 ⊗ ϖ')-adic one, since ϖ^m = u_m ϖ' and ϖ'^n = v_n ϖ in D_{m,n}); let C_{m,n} be the completion and C⁺_{m,n} the completion of the integral closure in E of the image of (A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[u_m, v_n], an open integrally closed subring. Then (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}) is a complete perfectoid Tate pair (C_{m,n} is a perfect complete Tate ring); a morphism of pairs (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}) → (R, R⁺) to a complete Huber pair with R Tate is the same as morphisms φ : (A, A⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ(ϖ)^m ψ(ϖ')⁻¹ ∈ R⁺ and ψ(ϖ')^n φ(ϖ)⁻¹ ∈ R⁺; for m ≤ m', n ≤ n', Spa(C_{m,n}) is the rational subset {|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1} of Spa(C_{m',n'}); and X × Y = ⋃_{m,n} Spa(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}), glued along these rational open immersions (anchor Layer 5.3). For general X, Y the affinoid products glue. The plus ring must contain u_m and v_n: the integral closure of the image of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺ alone, as written in Berkeley's proof, is not open (see sourceIssues). The absolute product of two perfectoid fields need not be a point: Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) is the perfectoid punctured open unit disc {0 < |s| < 1} over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4), which is not quasi-compact and has infinitely many points. Lean: `HasBinaryProducts PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid spaces of characteristic p.
ϖ ∈ A, ϖ' ∈ B pseudouniformisers of the affinoid charts.
proofSteps: E = A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B is perfect (𝔽_p, A, B perfect); ϖ ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ ϖ' are units of E; D_{m,n} is a subring containing both ϖ^m ⊗ 1 ∈ (1 ⊗ ϖ')D_{m,n} and 1 ⊗ ϖ'^n ∈ (ϖ ⊗ 1)D_{m,n}, so the two adic topologies agree and E is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ ⊗ 1 and ring of definition D_{m,n}.

To extend Frobenius to the completion one must prove continuity of its inverse, not only continuity of Frobenius. Write a = ϖ ⊗ 1, b = 1 ⊗ ϖ′, D = D_{m,n}, u = a^m/b, v = b^n/a. The image D₀ of A° ⊗ B° is perfect. Every element of Φ⁻¹(D) is a sum of D-multiples of u^{i/p}v^{j/p}, 0 ≤ i,j < p. The identities a^m u^{i/p} = u a^{mi/p} b^{1−i/p} and a v^{j/p} = a^{1−j/p} b^{nj/p} show a^{m+1} Φ⁻¹(D) ⊆ D, since the remaining factors belong to D₀. Hence Φ⁻¹(a^{pk}D) ⊆ a^{k−m−1}D for all integers k. Both Φ and Φ⁻¹ are continuous, so extend inversely to C_{m,n}. It is perfect, complete and Tate, hence perfectoid and uniform by PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect.

C⁺_{m,n} is a ring of integral elements: it lies in C°_{m,n} (D_{m,n} is bounded), it is integrally closed, and it is open because (ϖ ⊗ 1)^{m+1} D_{m,n} ⊆ image((A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[u_m, v_n]) (as (ϖ ⊗ 1)^{m+1}(a ⊗ b) = u_m (ϖa ⊗ ϖ'b) with ϖa ∈ A⁺, ϖ'b ∈ B⁺ for a ∈ A°, b ∈ B°) — Wedhorn Remark 7.15.

Universal property of (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}): a ring map E → R from φ, ψ is continuous for the D_{m,n}-topology iff it maps D_{m,n} into a bounded set, which holds when u_m, v_n map into R⁺; it extends to the completion (Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`) and maps C⁺_{m,n} into R⁺ (integral closure, closedness of R⁺).
Rational charts: the universal property identifies Spa(C_{m,n}) → Spa(C_{m',n'}) with the rational localisation at {|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1} (anchor Layer 3.1 universal property).

Every pair (φ, ψ) into a complete Tate pair (R, R⁺) factors through some chart: φ(ϖ)^m ψ(ϖ')⁻¹ → 0 as m → ∞ (φ(ϖ) is topologically nilpotent), so it lies in the open R⁺ for m ≫ 0, and likewise for n. Hence ⋃ Spa(C_{m,n}) represents pairs of morphisms from Tate affinoids; a test adic space T with morphisms to X is analytic, since morphisms send non-analytic points to non-analytic points (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (iii)), so it is covered by Tate affinoids (anchor Layer 2.3), and morphisms glue (Wedhorn Remark 8.24). This gives the product in adic spaces over Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) (an adic space by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy), hence in Perf.
General X, Y: glue the affinoid products over affinoid perfectoid covers, with the open-subspace compatibility (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces) as for fibre products.
acceptance: Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) ≅ the perfectoid punctured open unit disc over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) in the coordinate s, the union of the perfectoid annuli {|t|^m ≤ |s| ≤ |t|^{1/n}} (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4).

For X, Y ∈ Perf over a common perfectoid Z, the canonical morphism X ×_Z Y → X × Y is not an isomorphism in general: for K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), Spa K ×_{Spa K} Spa K = Spa K is a point, while Spa K × Spa K is not.

nodes.title: Scholze's perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K are the perfectoid spaces over Spa(K, K⁺₀)
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition), K° its valuation ring and K⁺₀ ⊆ K° the smallest ring of integral elements of K, the integral closure of ℤ·1 + K°° in K (Wedhorn Remark 7.15(2)); K⁺₀ = K° iff the residue field of K is algebraic over 𝔽_p. (i) Sch12's perfectoid K-algebras (Definition 5.1) and perfectoid affinoid K-algebras (Definition 6.1) are the perfectoid Tate rings, respectively complete perfectoid Tate pairs (R, R⁺), with a continuous K-algebra structure; no condition K° ⊆ R⁺ is imposed. (ii) Sch12's category of perfectoid spaces over K (Definition 6.15: objects of Huber's category of triples whose structure sheaf is a sheaf of complete topological K-algebras, locally affinoid perfectoid; morphisms continuous K-linear) is equivalent to the slice category Perfd/Spa(K, K⁺₀): a morphism X → Spa(K, K⁺₀) is a continuous ring map K → O_X(X) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and every such map sends K⁺₀ into O_X⁺(X), which contains all topologically nilpotent elements and is integrally closed. The full subcategory Perfd/Spa(K, K°) (Bhatt Definition 9.3.9) consists of those X with K° ⊆ O_X⁺(X); it is all of Sch12's category when the residue field of K is algebraic over 𝔽_p (e.g. K = ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))), and a proper full subcategory otherwise. (iii) Sch12's tilt (Definition 6.16) of X over K is the glued tilt X♭ with its structure map to Spa(K♭, K♭⁺₀) (tilting preserves the smallest ring of integral elements, ECD Lemma 3.11), and Sch12 Proposition 6.17 is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence for the base Spa(K, K⁺₀): the functorial bijection Hom(Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), X♭) = Hom(Spa(R, R⁺), X) over K♭, resp. K, holds. (iv) Sch12's fibre products (Proposition 6.18) are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces.
hypotheses: K a perfectoid field.
proofSteps: (i) Sch12 Definition 5.1 (R° open and bounded, Frobenius surjective on R°/ϖ) agrees with ECD Definition 3.1 for Banach K-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras records the comparison); Definition 2.6(ii) asks only R⁺ ⊆ R° open and integrally closed.

(ii) Wedhorn Proposition 8.25 identifies morphisms X → Spa(K, K⁺₀) with continuous ring maps K → O_X(X) carrying K⁺₀ into O_X⁺(X); the latter condition is automatic (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, integral closedness); a morphism of adic spaces over Spa(K, K⁺₀) is exactly a morphism whose ring maps are K-linear. Sch12's category (V) of triples with K-algebra structure is therefore the slice of the anchor's category over Spa(K, K⁺₀), and the perfectoid objects correspond (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space).

Non-surjectivity onto the slice over Spa(K, K°): if the residue field k of K is not algebraic over 𝔽_p, choose a valuation ring V ⊊ k (the residue field of K⁺₀ is the algebraic closure of 𝔽_p in k), and let R⁺ ⊆ K° be its preimage; then (K, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra in Sch12's sense and K° ⊄ R⁺.

(iii) ECD Lemma 3.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting) is an inclusion-preserving bijection, so it maps the smallest ring of integral elements of K to that of K♭; apply PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence with X = Spa(K, K⁺₀); Sch12's Definition 6.16 is the case T = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) of part (c) there.
(iv) Both are fibre products in the same category.
acceptance: For K = ℂ_p: Sch12's perfectoid spaces over ℂ_p are the perfectoid spaces over Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}).

For K the completed perfection of 𝔽_p(x)((t)) and R⁺ the preimage in K° of the valuation ring 𝔽_p[x]^{perf}_{(x)} of the residue field 𝔽_p(x)^{perf}: Spa(K, R⁺) is a perfectoid space over K in Sch12's sense with no morphism to Spa(K, K°).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs: adic completeness, filtered colimits, and independence of the ring of definition of a Tate ring
nodes.statement: Pairs (A, I) (a commutative ring and an ideal) are henselian in Mathlib's sense `HenselianRing A I` (I ⊆ Jacobson radical and simple roots modulo I lift). (a) If A is I-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete I A`), then (A, I) is henselian (Mathlib instance `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing`; Stacks Tag 0ALJ). (b) If (A_j, I_j)_{j ∈ J} is a directed system of henselian pairs (ring maps A_j → A_k carrying I_j into I_k), then (colim A_j, colim I_j) is a henselian pair (colimit in rings, Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`; Stacks Tag 0FWT). In particular, if every A_j is henselian along the ideal generated by the image of a fixed element ϖ ∈ A_{j₀}, so is colim A_j. (c) Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`), ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformiser and A₀, A₀' ⊆ A rings of definition containing ϖ. Then (A₀, ϖA₀) is henselian if and only if (A₀', ϖA₀') is henselian, if and only if (A°, A°°) is henselian, if and only if (A⁺, A°°) is henselian for one (equivalently every) ring of integral elements A⁺ ⊆ A°. A Tate ring with this property is called topologically henselian (`Huber.IsTopologicallyHenselian A`). Every complete Tate ring is topologically henselian, by (a) applied to a ϖ-adically complete ring of definition; and a filtered colimit of Tate rings A_j along continuous maps, with the colimit topology in which colim A_{j,0} is a ring of definition for compatible rings of definition A_{j,0} containing ϖ, is topologically henselian when each A_j is, by (b).
hypotheses: All rings commutative; ϖ a pseudouniformiser (a topologically nilpotent unit) of the Tate ring A; rings of definition are open and bounded subrings.
(c) uses only the abstract ring maps A₀ → A and the topology through the choice of rings of definition; completeness is not assumed in the equivalence.
proofSteps: (a) is Mathlib's instance: an I-adically complete ring is Hausdorff and precomplete, I lies in the Jacobson radical (IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot) and Newton iteration converges (Stacks 0ALJ proof, lifting factorisations modulo Iⁿ).

(b): an element of 1 + I comes from 1 + I_j for some j, where it is a unit; a monic polynomial with a coprime factorisation modulo I comes, with the factorisation and a Bezout identity, from some A_j, where it lifts; map the lift to A (Stacks 0FWT proof). The simple-root formulation of Mathlib's `HenselianRing` is equivalent to the factorisation formulation (Stacks Lemma 15.11.6), so the argument is run in whichever form Mathlib provides.

(c): two rings of definition containing ϖ are commensurable: A₀ ⊆ ϖ^{-N}A₀' and conversely; the ideal ϖA₀ and ϖA₀' generate the same topology and, by the invariance of henselian pairs under replacing the ring by one sharing the ideal as a non-unital ring (Gabber–Ramero Remark 5.1.9(ii), used in Bhatt's proof of Lemma 7.2.3(3)), henselianity transfers along A₀ ∩ A₀' ⊆ A₀, A₀'. A⁺ and A° are filtered colimits of open bounded subrings containing ϖ (Bhatt Lemma 7.2.3(1)); combine with (b).
Completeness of A implies that its rings of definition are ϖ-adically complete (anchor Layer 0: completion of Huber rings), so (a) gives topological henselianity.
acceptance: (ℤ_p, pℤ_p) and (ℤ_p⟦T⟧, (p, T)) are henselian by (a); the henselisation ℤ_(p)^h of ℤ_(p) is henselian but not p-adically complete.
For K a perfectoid field and K_i the finite subextensions of a Galois extension L/K, colim K_i° = L° is henselian along ϖ by (b), although L is not complete.

Non-example: ℤ_(3) (localisation of ℤ at (3)) is not henselian along 3: X² − 7 has the simple root 1 modulo 3 (derivative 2, a unit) but no root in ℤ_(3); accordingly the Tate ring ℚ with the 3-adic topology (ring of definition ℤ_(3)) is not topologically henselian.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a filtered colimit of rings are defined at a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let (R_j)_{j ∈ J} be a directed system of commutative rings with colimit R = colim R_j (Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`), and write FÉt(A) for Mathlib's category `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A` of finite étale A-algebras (`Module.Finite A B` and `Algebra.Etale A B`). Then the base change functors FÉt(R_j) → FÉt(R) (`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`) induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_j FÉt(R_j) ≃ FÉt(R), compatible with tensor products. Concretely: (a) every finite étale R-algebra is isomorphic to S_j ⊗_{R_j} R for some j and some finite étale R_j-algebra S_j; (b) for S_j, T_j ∈ FÉt(R_j) the map colim_{k ≥ j} Hom_{R_k}(S_j ⊗ R_k, T_j ⊗ R_k) → Hom_R(S_j ⊗ R, T_j ⊗ R) is bijective; (c) the rank function of S_j ⊗ R on Spec R, faithful flatness, and the existence of a section of S_j ⊗ R → R descend to some R_k (k ≥ j).
hypotheses: J directed; no noetherian hypothesis.
Finite étale = finite, flat, finitely presented and unramified; equivalently finite projective with perfect trace pairing.
proofSteps: (a): a finite étale R-algebra is finitely presented, hence comes from a finitely presented R_j-algebra S_j (EGA IV 8.8.2); finiteness, flatness and unramifiedness of S_j ⊗ R_k over R_k hold for k ≫ j (EGA IV 8.10.5, 11.2.6, 17.7.8(ii); Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9).

(b): Hom-sets of finitely presented algebras commute with filtered colimits: a map S_j ⊗ R → T_j ⊗ R is determined by the images of finitely many generators satisfying finitely many relations, all defined over some R_k; two maps agreeing over R agree over some R_k.

(c): the rank is read off from the characteristic polynomial of the multiplication on a projective presentation, defined at a finite stage; faithful flatness of a finite étale algebra is surjectivity on Spec, equivalently the rank is everywhere positive, a condition on finitely many idempotents; a section is an algebra map, handled by (b).
acceptance: For R_j = ℚ(ζ_{3^j}) with colimit R = ℚ(μ_{3^∞}): S = R[U]/(U³ − 2) comes from R_0 = ℚ, and its automorphism U ↦ ζ_3U is defined over R_1 = ℚ(ζ_3) but not over R_0 — (b) needs the passage to a larger index.
For a perfectoid field K and its finite subextensions K_i of a Galois L/K, FÉt(colim K_i) = FÉt(L) is 2-colim FÉt(K_i) (used in the Fontaine–Wintenberger node).

nodes.title: Newton approximation: approximate solutions with Jacobian control lift to true solutions over (t, I)-adically complete rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal, F = R[X_1, …, X_N], J ⊆ F a finitely generated ideal and S = F/J. Let H ⊆ F be the Jacobian ideal of the presentation: H := H_R(F, J) = Ann_F Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, J/J²), computed from the naive cotangent complex J/J² → S ⊗_F Ω_{F/R} (Mathlib `Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`), which contains Elkik's ideal H_S = Σ_p Σ_{|α| = p} Δ_α (J_α : J) generated by p × p Jacobian minors times colon ideals (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.6). For a ∈ R^N write p_a = (X_1 − a_1, …, X_N − a_N). (i) (one step; Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.8) If n, h ≥ 0 with n > 2h and t^h ∈ H + p_a and J ⊆ p_a + tⁿIF, then there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b + (t^{n−h}I)²F. (ii) (complete case; Gabber–Ramero Claim 5.4.14) If moreover R is complete for the tI-adic topology, there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b, i.e. f(b) = 0 for every f ∈ J: approximate solutions of a system that is smooth up to t^h lift to exact solutions congruent modulo t^{n−h}I. Elkik's Théorème 1 is the noetherian version with an arbitrary ideal of definition, and Tougeron's lemma (Elkik Lemme 2) the version with the maximal Jacobian minors.
hypotheses: t a non-zero-divisor; I an arbitrary ideal (not necessarily finitely generated); J finitely generated.
H depends only on the presentation (F, J); smoothness of S over R away from V(H·S) (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2(ii)) is not used in (i)–(ii).
proofSteps: (0) (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2) Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, N) only involves the naive cotangent complex J/J² → S ⊗_F Ω_{F/R} (Gabber–Ramero (5.4.3)), so h ∈ H iff multiplication by h on J/J² factors through ∂; hence S_h is smooth over R for h ∈ H (Jacobian criterion, Mathlib `Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_split_injection`), and H annihilates Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, N) for every S-module N.

(i): an approximate solution is an R-algebra map σ: S → R/tⁿI. Lifting σ modulo t^{n−h}I to R/(t^{n−h}I)² is the Newton step: writing f(a + δ) = f(a) + Σ_i ∂_i f(a) δ_i + (terms quadratic in δ) for generators f of J, one needs δ ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N solving the linearised system modulo (t^{n−h}I)²; since t^h ∈ H + p_a, multiplication by t^h on the conormal module factors through the Jacobian map ∂ evaluated at a, and δ is obtained by applying this factorisation to the vector (f(a)) ∈ tⁿI (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.8, phrased there as the vanishing of an obstruction class in Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, t^{n−h}I/(t^{n−h}I)²), killed by t^h because it is killed by p_a and by H).

(ii): iterate (i): starting from a₀ = a, obtain a_{m+1} ≡ a_m modulo ever higher powers of tI with the hypothesis of (i) preserved (the inequality n > 2h improves at each step); the sequence converges tI-adically to b with J ⊆ p_b.

Alternative for complete-intersection presentations (Tougeron, Elkik Lemme 2): write the equations with the Jacobian matrix M(a) and matrices N_i with M(a)N_i = d_i·Id; the system in the correction vectors u_i is étale at u = 0 modulo t^{n−2h}, hence has a true solution by Hensel's lemma in the complete ring.
acceptance: For R = ℤ_p, t = p, I = R, f = X² − 7 ∈ ℤ_p[X] (p odd, 7 a square mod p): a = any square root of 7 modulo p is an approximate solution with h = 0, and (ii) produces the square root of 7 in ℤ_p (Hensel's lemma).
For R = ℤ_p, f = X² with a = 0 modulo p^n: H ∌ unit powers of p near a (the derivative vanishes at 0) and the lemma makes no claim; the double root is not isolated, as it must be.

nodes.title: Elkik's approximation theorem for noetherian henselian pairs (Théorème 2 bis)
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔍) be a henselian pair with A noetherian, Â its 𝔍-adic completion, B a finitely generated A-algebra and B̂ = B ⊗_A Â. Let V ⊆ Spec B be an open subset smooth over Spec A and V̂ its preimage in Spec B̂. Then for every integer n and every Â-section ε̂: Spec Â → Spec B̂ whose restriction to Spec Â ∖ V(𝔍Â) factors through V̂, there is an A-section ε: Spec A → Spec B with ε ≡ ε̂ modulo 𝔍ⁿ whose restriction to Spec A ∖ V(𝔍) factors through V. Equivalently (Elkik Théorème 2): for h ≥ 0 there are n₀, r such that for every presentation B = A[X_1, …, X_N]/J, every n ≥ n₀ and every a⁰ ∈ A^N with J(a⁰) ⊆ 𝔍ⁿ and H_B(a⁰) ⊇ 𝔍^h there is a ∈ A^N, a ≡ a⁰ modulo 𝔍^{n−r}, with J(a) = 0. This is the noetherian input (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.12) of the non-noetherian approximation.
hypotheses: A noetherian; (A, 𝔍) henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing A 𝔍`); B of finite type over A.
The smooth locus V is given; smoothness is Mathlib's `Algebra.Smooth` on affine opens.
proofSteps: (Remark after the statement) It suffices to find, for every n, a section congruent to ε̂ modulo 𝔍ⁿ: if V = Spec B ∖ V(I) and ε̂*(I) ⊇ 𝔍^a Â, any section congruent modulo 𝔍ⁿ, n > a, factors through V over Spec A ∖ V(𝔍).

Tougeron's lemma (Elkik Lemme 2): if the q × q minors Δ of the Jacobian of generators f_1, …, f_q of J satisfy J(a) ⊆ 𝔍ⁿ and Δ(a) ⊇ 𝔍^h with n > 2h, there is a' ≡ a modulo 𝔍^{n−h} with J(a') = 0; the correction system is étale at the origin modulo 𝔍^{n−2h}, and henselianity lifts its approximate zero.

Elkik Lemme 3: replacing Spec B by the vector bundle of the conormal sheaf J/J² of a closed embedding, V becomes smooth of constant relative dimension and is, near every affine open of V, cut out by exactly as many equations as its codimension (a local complete intersection presentation) — this reduces to Tougeron's situation.

Elkik Lemme 4 (𝔍 = (t) principal): choose h ∈ A[X] invertible along ε̂ and inside the lci locus, generators f_1, …, f_{N−d} of J over D(h), and apply Tougeron's lemma to get a section s with s*(f_1, …, f_{N−d}) = 0 congruent to ε̂; by Artin–Rees (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul`) the t-power-torsion part of s*(J) vanishes, so s*(J) = 0.

General 𝔍 = (a_1, …, a_l): induction on l. Over A_1 = the a_1-adic completion apply Théorème 1 (the complete case, P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings in Elkik's noetherian form) and the induction hypothesis for (A/a_1^m, 𝔍/a_1^m) to produce an A_1-section congruent to ε̂; then Lemme 4 for the principal ideal (a_1) approximates it by an A-section.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_(p)^h (the henselisation of ℤ at p, noetherian, henselian along p) and B = A[X]/(X² − 7) (p odd, 7 a nonzero square mod p): the square root of 7 in ℤ_p = Â is approximated by, and in fact equals, an A-point, as the equation is étale.
The corollary (Elkik §II, Corollaire 1 and the theorem following it): a smooth A-algebra B has an A-section lifting any section modulo 𝔍ⁿ.

nodes.title: The henselisation of a pair (A, I)
nodes.statement: For a pair (A, I) (a commutative ring and an ideal) the henselisation is a henselian pair (A^h, I^h) (Mathlib `HenselianRing A^h I^h`) with a map of pairs (A, I) → (A^h, I^h) that is universal among maps from (A, I) to henselian pairs: the functor (A, I) ↦ (A^h, I^h) is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs (Stacks Tag 0A02). It is constructed as the filtered colimit of the étale A-algebras B with A/I ≅ B/IB. Properties: A → A^h is flat, I^h = IA^h, and A/Iⁿ → A^h/IⁿA^h is an isomorphism for every n (Tag 0AGU); henselisation commutes with filtered colimits of pairs (Tag 0A04); if A is noetherian, A^h is noetherian, A and A^h have the same I-adic completion, A → A^h → A^∧ are flat and A^h → A^∧ is faithfully flat (Tag 0AGV).
hypotheses: (A, I) arbitrary; the noetherian statements need A noetherian.
proofSteps: Construction: the category of étale A-algebras B with A/I ≅ B/IB is filtered (fibre products and equalisers of such are again such), and its colimit A^h with I^h = IA^h is henselian: a monic polynomial with a simple root modulo I^h is defined over some B, and adjoining the root gives a further étale B' with the same reduction (Stacks proof of 0A02).

Universal property: for (A, I) → (C, J) with (C, J) henselian, each such B has a unique A-map B → C compatible with the reductions (henselian pairs lift sections of étale algebras, Stacks Tag 09XI; Mathlib `HenselianRing` in its simple-root form, P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions), and these assemble to A^h → C.
Flatness and A/Iⁿ ≅ A^h/IⁿA^h: étale maps are flat and each B satisfies A/Iⁿ ≅ B/IⁿB (étale and an isomorphism modulo I).
Colimits: both sides satisfy the same universal property; P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b) shows the colimit of henselisations is henselian.
Noetherian case: the completions agree by A/Iⁿ ≅ A^h/Iⁿ; A^h is noetherian because its completion is and A^h → A^∧ is faithfully flat (Stacks 0AGV proof).
acceptance: The henselisation of (ℤ, pℤ) is ℤ_(p)^h, the ring of p-adic integers algebraic over ℚ; it is countable, so it differs from ℤ_p.
If (A, I) is henselian, A → A^h is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Approximate solutions over henselian pairs (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.13)
nodes.statement: In the situation of P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings (R a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal, S = R[X_1, …, X_N]/J with J finitely generated, H = H_R(F, J)), assume that the pair (R, tI) is henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing R (t • I)`). If a ∈ R^N and n, h ≥ 0 satisfy n > 2h, t^h ∈ H + p_a and J ⊆ p_a + tⁿIF, then there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b: every approximate solution of a system smooth up to t^h is close to a true solution in R itself, not only in its completion.
hypotheses: t a non-zero-divisor; (R, tI) henselian; R not assumed noetherian or complete.
proofSteps: Complete case: P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings (ii).

General R: choose a finitely generated H' ⊆ H with t^h ∈ H' + p_a; write R as the filtered union of its finitely generated (hence noetherian) subrings R_λ containing t, a, the coefficients of generators of J and H', with I_λ = I ∩ R_λ; after replacing R_λ by their henselisations along tI_λ (P3/henselisation-of-pairs: noetherian, mapping to R by the universal property since (R, tI) is henselian, with the same completion) all pairs (R_λ, tI_λ) are henselian and noetherian and the hypotheses hold over R_λ.

Over the completion R̂_λ, the complete case gives c ≡ a with J_λ ⊆ p_c; the locus U_λ = Spec S_λ ∖ V(H_λ) is smooth over R_λ (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2(ii)) and c factors through it away from V(tI_λ). Elkik's theorem (P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation) gives an R_λ-section congruent to c modulo (tI_λ)^{n−h}; its image in R is the required b.
acceptance: For R = ℤ_(p)^h[p^{1/p^∞}] = colim_n ℤ_(p)^h[p^{1/pⁿ}] (henselian along p by P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b), neither noetherian nor complete), t = p, I = R: the equation X² − 7 (p odd, 7 a nonzero square modulo p) has its simple approximate root modulo p refined to a root in R itself.
The conclusion fails for non-henselian pairs: over ℤ_(p) the equation X² = 7 (p odd, 7 a square mod p, not a square in ℚ) has approximate solutions modulo every p^n but no solution.

nodes.title: Sections of smooth quasi-projective schemes over R[t⁻¹] are dense in those over R^∧[t⁻¹]; smooth maps are open on sections
nodes.statement: Let t ∈ R be a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal with (R, tI) henselian, R^∧ = lim_n R/tⁿI the (t, I)-adic completion and I^∧ the closure of I in R^∧. For a finitely generated R[t⁻¹]-module (or the set of sections X(R[t⁻¹]) of an affine R[t⁻¹]-scheme of finite type embedded in affine space) the (t, I)-adic topology is the linear topology with basis tᵏI·N₀ for a finitely generated R-lattice N₀ (independent of the lattice and of the embedding; Gabber–Ramero 5.4.10–5.4.16), and it glues on quasi-projective schemes (5.4.19). Then: (a) (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.21) for every smooth quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-scheme X, the map X(R[t⁻¹]) → X(R^∧[t⁻¹]) has dense image for the (t, I)- and (t, I^∧)-adic topologies; (b) (Proposition 5.4.30) for a morphism φ: X → Y of quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-schemes, φ_*: X(R[t⁻¹]) → Y(R[t⁻¹]) is continuous, and it is open when φ is smooth.
hypotheses: t a non-zero-divisor, (R, tI) henselian, X, Y quasi-projective over R[t⁻¹], topologies as described.
proofSteps: (a), affine X = Spec S (Claim 5.4.22): choose a finitely presented R-model S₀ = R[X]/J with S₀[t⁻¹] = S; smoothness gives t^h ∈ H_R(R[X], J) + J; approximate a given R^∧-section by an R-point σ₀ agreeing modulo tⁿI; then t^h ∈ H + p and J ⊆ p + tⁿIR[X] for p = ker σ₀, and P3/henselian-approximate-solutions produces a true R-point close to σ₀.

(a), projective space (Claim 5.4.27): a section of P^r over R^∧[t⁻¹] is a rank-one projective quotient, i.e. an idempotent matrix; the scheme of idempotent matrices U_n is smooth over ℤ (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20) and affine, so the affine case applies near it; quasi-projective X (Claim 5.4.29) reduces to open subschemes of projective ones.

(b): continuity by factoring through the graph (closed immersion) and a projection; openness for smooth φ: a section ξ of Y near φ_*(σ) extends over an R-model (Claim 5.4.31), and the fibre X ×_Y ξ is smooth over R[t⁻¹] with an approximate section, which P3/henselian-approximate-solutions makes exact.
acceptance: X = 𝔾_m with R = ℤ_(p)^h, t = p, I = R (so R^∧[1/p] = ℚ_p): the units of ℤ_(p)^h[1/p] are dense in ℚ_p^×.
Openness in (b) fails for non-smooth φ: X = Spec R[t⁻¹][x], Y = Spec R[t⁻¹][y], φ: y = x²; near y = 0 the image of φ_* is not a neighbourhood.

nodes.title: Isomorphism classes of points of a smooth groupoid do not change from R[t⁻¹] to R^∧[t⁻¹]
nodes.statement: Keep the hypotheses of P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs. Let (X₀, X₁, s, t, c, ι) be a groupoid in quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-schemes (objects X₀, morphisms X₁ with source and target s, t: X₁ → X₀, composition c, identity ι), and for an R[t⁻¹]-algebra T let π₀(X₀(T)) denote the set of isomorphism classes of the groupoid of T-points. If X₀ is smooth over R[t⁻¹] and (s, t): X₁ → X₀ ×_{R[t⁻¹]} X₀ is smooth, then the natural map π₀(X₀(R[t⁻¹])) → π₀(X₀(R^∧[t⁻¹])) is bijective (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 5.4.38).
hypotheses: Hypotheses of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.21; X₀ smooth and (s, t) smooth.
proofSteps: Surjective: for σ ∈ X₀(R^∧[t⁻¹]) choose σ₀ ∈ X₀(R[t⁻¹]) close to σ (density, P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs (a)); (σ, σ) = (s, t)(ι(σ)) lies in the image of (s, t)_*, which is open ((b), (s, t) smooth), so (σ, σ₀) is in the image when σ₀ is close enough: σ ≅ σ₀.

Injective: if σ, τ ∈ X₀(R[t⁻¹]) become isomorphic via α ∈ X₁(R^∧[t⁻¹]), approximate α by α₀ ∈ X₁(R[t⁻¹]) (X₁ is smooth, being smooth over the smooth X₀ × X₀); by continuity (s, t)(α₀) = (σ₀, τ₀) is close to (σ, τ); openness of (s, t)_* near (σ, σ) and (τ, τ) makes σ ≅ σ₀ and τ ≅ τ₀ over R[t⁻¹], so σ ≅ τ.
acceptance: The groupoid of idempotent matrices under conjugation (P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion) and of étale algebra structures under GL(P) (P3/etale-algebra-structure-schemes) are the two instances used.
Without smoothness of (s, t) the map can fail to be injective: for the trivial groupoid of a non-smooth X₀ with two points identified only formally, orbits split.

nodes.title: Finitely generated projective modules over R[t⁻¹] and over R^∧[t⁻¹] correspond (Gabber–Ramero Corollary 5.4.42)
nodes.statement: Keep the hypotheses of P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs. Then base change M ↦ M ⊗_R R^∧ induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-modules and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R^∧[t⁻¹]-modules. The groupoid used: U_n = the scheme of idempotent n × n matrices (smooth over ℤ, Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20), F_n = the scheme of quadruples (S, T, φ, ψ) with S, T idempotent and φ, ψ mutually inverse isomorphisms Coker S ⇄ Coker T (smooth over U_n × U_n, Lemma 5.4.41).
hypotheses: Hypotheses of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.21.
proofSteps: U_n is of finite presentation and formally smooth: an idempotent matrix modulo a square-zero ideal lifts (lift M, pass to the commutative algebra R₀[M], lift the idempotent; Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20 via Proposition 2.5.13(i)).
F_n → U_n ×_ℤ U_n is smooth: given (S, T) and an isomorphism of cokernels modulo a nilpotent ideal, lift it by projectivity and Nakayama (Lemma 5.4.41).

(U_n, F_n, s, t) with the evident identity and composition is a groupoid in affine schemes of finite type over ℤ satisfying the hypotheses of P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs; its π₀ over a ring T is the set of isomorphism classes of projective T-modules generated by n elements (every such module is the cokernel of an idempotent), so the orbit comparison is the claim.
acceptance: Degenerate case: if R is already (t, I)-adically complete, R^∧ = R and the bijection is the identity.

The bijection is compatible with direct sums and tensor products of projective modules, since base change is; it is the input that makes the underlying module of a finite étale R^∧[t⁻¹]-algebra descend.

nodes.title: The scheme of étale algebra structures on a projective module is smooth, and GL acts on it étale-ly
nodes.statement: Let R, t be as in P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs and P a finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-module; for an R[t⁻¹]-scheme S write P_S = O_S ⊗ P. (a) The functor S ↦ {commutative unital O_S-algebra structures (µ, 1) on P_S} is represented by an affine R[t⁻¹]-scheme X_P of finite presentation (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.45). (b) The subfunctor of étale algebra structures is represented by an affine open U_P ⊆ X_P — the non-vanishing locus of the discriminant of the trace form — and U_P is smooth over R[t⁻¹] (Lemma 5.4.46). (c) S ↦ Aut_{O_S}(P_S) is represented by a group scheme Aut_P of finite presentation, locally GL_n (Lemma 5.4.50). (d) The morphism Aut_P ×_{R[t⁻¹]} U_P → U_P ×_{R[t⁻¹]} U_P, (g, µ) ↦ (µ^g, µ), with µ^g the transported structure, is étale (Lemma 5.4.53); in particular (U_P, Aut_P × U_P) is a groupoid satisfying the hypotheses of P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs, and its π₀ over T is the set of isomorphism classes of finite étale T-algebras whose underlying module is isomorphic to P_T.
hypotheses: P finitely generated projective over R[t⁻¹]; étale = finite étale here, the module being finite projective.
proofSteps: (a): Zariski-locally P is free with basis e_1, …, e_n; a multiplication is given by structure constants a_{ijk} and a unit by b_l subject to finitely many polynomial identities (associativity, commutativity, unit); the functor is an fppf sheaf, so the local representing schemes glue.

(b): a finite projective algebra is étale iff the discriminant of its trace form is a unit (Mathlib `Algebra.traceForm`, `traceForm_nondegenerate` for fields; Gabber–Ramero Theorem 4.1.14), an open condition; formal smoothness: an étale algebra over a nilpotent thickening's base lifts, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, and its underlying module is forced to be P (étale algebras deform uniquely — Stacks Tag 039R, 'une équivalence remarquable de catégories'; Gabber–Ramero Proposition 3.2.30).
(d): of finite presentation; formally étale because an isomorphism of étale algebras over a nilpotent thickening Z₀ ⊆ Z extends uniquely to Z (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.2.18(iii); Stacks 039R).

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras do not change under henselian completion: FÉt(R[t⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(R^∧[t⁻¹]), and FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â) for a topologically henselian Tate ring
nodes.statement: (a) (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.54; book numbering 5.4.53) Let R be a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal with (R, tI) henselian, and R^∧ the (t, I)-adic completion. Then base change B ↦ B ⊗_{R[t⁻¹]} R^∧[t⁻¹] is an equivalence of categories FÉt(R[t⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(R^∧[t⁻¹]) (Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`), compatible with tensor products; it preserves and reflects ranks, faithful flatness and splitness. (b) (Tate-ring form; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8) Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`) which is topologically henselian (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c): a ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ, ϖ a pseudouniformiser, is henselian along ϖA₀), and Â its completion (Tau Ceti completion of Huber rings), with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion Â₀. Then B ↦ B ⊗_A Â is an equivalence FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â). This is (a) with R = A₀, t = ϖ, I = A₀, since A = A₀[ϖ⁻¹] and Â = Â₀[ϖ⁻¹]. (c) (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.4) For a perfectoid field K and a flat K°-algebra A henselian along (ϖ), A[ϖ⁻¹]_fét ≃ Â[ϖ⁻¹]_fét, Â the ϖ-adic completion — the special case R = A, t = ϖ, I = A of (a). No perfectoid, base-field or noetherian hypothesis enters (a) or (b).
hypotheses: t a non-zero-divisor (automatic for t = ϖ a unit of A inside a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A).

Finite étale algebras are those of Mathlib's `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`; the topology on B ⊗_A Â is not part of the statement (it is the natural module topology, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra).
proofSteps: Essential surjectivity in (a): the underlying module P^∧ of a finite étale R^∧[t⁻¹]-algebra is finite projective, so P^∧ ≅ P ⊗ R^∧[t⁻¹] for a finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-module P (P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion).

The étale algebra structures on P form the smooth groupoid of P3/etale-algebra-structure-schemes; by P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs isomorphism classes of finite étale structures on P and on P ⊗ R^∧[t⁻¹] correspond, so (P^∧, µ^∧) comes from R[t⁻¹].

Full faithfulness: for finite étale Y₁, Y₂ over X = Spec R[t⁻¹], the functor Z ↦ Hom_Z(Z ×_X Y₁, Z ×_X Y₂) is represented by a finite étale X-scheme H (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 8.2.23); viewed as a trivial groupoid its (s, t) is the diagonal, an open immersion, so P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs gives H(R[t⁻¹]) = H(R^∧[t⁻¹]).

(b) is (a) for (A₀, ϖ): A₀ is ϖ-torsion free (ϖ is a unit of A ⊇ A₀), A₀[ϖ⁻¹] = A, and the ϖ-adic completion of A₀ inverted at ϖ is Â (anchor Layer 0 completion of Huber rings); independence of the ring of definition is P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c).
(c) is the instance R = A flat over K° (so ϖ is a non-zero-divisor), I = R.
acceptance: Every complete Tate ring is topologically henselian, so (b) is vacuous there; the content is for non-complete ones: for a perfectoid field K and an algebraic extension L/K, FÉt(L) ≃ FÉt(L̂) (L° = colim of the valuation rings of finite subextensions is henselian along ϖ).
For A = colim_U O_X(U) over the rational neighbourhoods U of a point x (P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), (b) identifies FÉt(A) with FÉt of the completion.

Non-example: A = ℚ with the 3-adic topology (ring of definition ℤ_(3), not henselian) and Â = ℚ_3: B = ℚ(√7) is finite étale over ℚ with Hom_ℚ(B, ℚ) = ∅, while B ⊗ ℚ_3 ≅ ℚ_3 × ℚ_3 has two ℚ_3-points, so base change FÉt(ℚ) → FÉt(ℚ_3) is not full.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a completed filtered colimit of complete Tate rings come from a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let (A_i)_{i ∈ I} be a filtered system of complete Tate rings along continuous ring maps, with compatible rings of definition A_{i,0} and a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i₀,0} mapping to pseudouniformisers (for instance A_{i,0} = A_i° when all A_i are uniform, or A_{i,0} = A_i⁺ for Huber pairs (A_i, A_i⁺)). Give A_∞ = colim A_i the Tate topology with ring of definition colim A_{i,0} and ϖ-adic topology on it, and let A = Â_∞ be its completion. Then the base change functors 2-colim_i FÉt(A_i) → FÉt(A_∞) → FÉt(A) are equivalences of categories compatible with tensor products. In particular (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5(i), generalised): if (R_i) is a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings and R is the completion of colim R_i with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i° (a perfectoid Tate ring, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings), then R_fét ≃ 2-colim_i (R_i)_fét; and the same holds for the rational localisations of affinoid perfectoid spaces along cofiltered limits (the form used by ECD Proposition 6.4(i)).
hypotheses: The A_i complete; the rings of definition compatible and containing the image of one pseudouniformiser.
No perfectoid hypothesis for the first statement.
proofSteps: 2-colim_i FÉt(A_i) ≃ FÉt(A_∞): P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings.

colim A_{i,0} is henselian along ϖ: each A_{i,0} is ϖ-adically complete, hence henselian (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (a)), and filtered colimits of henselian pairs are henselian ((b)).
FÉt(A_∞) ≃ FÉt(A): P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b), A_∞ being topologically henselian with completion A.

Perfectoid case: with A_{i,0} = R_i° (the R_i are uniform), A = R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings, a perfectoid Tate ring by (b) there; the equivalence is the first statement for this system.
acceptance: For perfectoid K and the perfectoid closed disc R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ written as the completed colimit of K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ (not perfectoid), every finite étale R-algebra is defined over some K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩.

Uniqueness is part of the equivalence: two finite-level models of the same finite étale A-algebra become isomorphic at a further finite stage, with a unique isomorphism compatible with the given one over A.

nodes.title: Relative Frobenius of a weakly étale map is an isomorphism; étale algebras over perfect rings are perfect
nodes.statement: (a) Let A → B be a weakly étale map of 𝔽_p-algebras (A → B flat and the multiplication B ⊗_A B → B flat; every étale map is weakly étale). Then the square formed by A → B and the absolute Frobenius endomorphisms (Mathlib `frobenius A p`, `frobenius B p`) is a pushout: the relative Frobenius F_{B/A}: B ⊗_{A, Frob} A → B, b ⊗ a ↦ b^p a, is an isomorphism. In particular, if A is perfect (Mathlib `PerfectRing A p`), then so is B, and B ⊗_{A, Frob^{-n}} A ≅ B for all n. (b) (almost version, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.13(ii)) The same holds for a weakly étale morphism A → B of almost algebras over a basic setup (V, 𝔪) of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup): the Frobenius square of almost V-algebras is cocartesian. Consequently, for a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformiser ϖ, ϖ^p | p, a finite étale (R°a/ϖ)-algebra B is relatively perfect over R°a/ϖ: Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B (the input of Scholze 2012 Proposition 5.22).
hypotheses: Characteristic p; weakly étale: flat with flat diagonal.
In (b), almost algebras and weak étaleness are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P0 (Gabber–Ramero §3.1).
proofSteps: Weakly étale maps are stable under base change and composition, and every map between weakly étale A-algebras is weakly étale (Bhatt, proof of Lemma 4.3.8; Stacks Tag 092A).
F_{B/A} is a map of weakly étale A-algebras, hence weakly étale; a diagram chase shows it factors a power of Frobenius on source and target.

A weakly étale map α: R → S that factors a power of Frobenius on R and on S is an isomorphism: it is faithfully flat (if M ⊗_R S = 0, then Frob^n kills M ⊗ R) and a flat epimorphism-up-to-Frobenius; the multiplication S ⊗_R S → S is weakly étale and invertible up to Frobenius, hence an isomorphism (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.13(i), Bhatt Lemma 4.3.8). Apply to F_{B/A}.
Perfectness: if Frob_A is bijective, B ⊗_{A,Frob} A ≅ B and the pushout of the bijection Frob_A is the bijection Frob_B.
(b): the same argument in the category of almost algebras (Gabber–Ramero 3.5.10–3.5.13), using PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness for weak étaleness.
acceptance: For A = 𝔽_p(t^{1/p^∞}) and the Artin–Schreier extension B = A[u]/(u^p − u − t) (étale): B is a perfect field and the relative Frobenius B ⊗_{A,Frob} A → B is an isomorphism of A-algebras of dimension p.
Non-example: A = 𝔽_p is perfect and B = 𝔽_p[ε]/(ε²) is finite flat but not étale; B is not perfect (ε^p = 0), so flatness alone does not suffice.

nodes.title: In characteristic p, finite étale algebras are insensitive to completed perfection
nodes.statement: Let S be a complete Tate ring of characteristic p with a ring of definition S₀ ∋ ϖ, and let R = (S^{perf})^ be the completed perfection: the completion of S^{perf} = colim(S → S → ⋯) (transition maps Frobenius x ↦ x^p) for the Tate topology with ring of definition colim S₀^{1/pⁿ}; R is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) when uniform. Then base change is an equivalence FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(R). In particular (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5(ii)) for a p-finite perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺), the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid (S, S⁺) of topologically finite type over a characteristic-p perfectoid field, R_fét ≃ S_fét; the base field is not needed.
hypotheses: Characteristic p; S complete Tate.
The absolute Frobenius S → S is a ring map, and S^{1/pⁿ} denotes S viewed as an S-algebra through Frobenius n times.
proofSteps: Each transition map S → S^{1/p} (Frobenius) induces an equivalence FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(S^{1/p}): it is integral, universally injective and surjective on spectra (a universal homeomorphism), so topological invariance of the étale site applies (Stacks Tag 04DZ); concretely B ↦ B ⊗_{S, Frob} S has quasi-inverse given by Frobenius twist, the relative Frobenius of an étale algebra being an isomorphism (P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect).
FÉt(S^{perf}) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(S^{1/pⁿ}) ≃ FÉt(S) by P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings, and FÉt(S^{perf}) ≃ FÉt(R) by P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit.
acceptance: S = K⟨T⟩ for a perfectoid field K of characteristic p: finite étale K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras are exactly the completed perfections of finite étale K⟨T⟩-algebras, e.g. the Artin–Schreier cover u^p − u = T.
The inseparable extension S → S[T^{1/p}]... is not étale and is not in the image: the equivalence concerns étale algebras only.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over the completed residue field spread out to a rational neighbourhood
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`, A complete, `Huber.IsTateRing`), X = Spa(A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`) and x ∈ X with completed residue field k(x)^ (a complete nonarchimedean field; the completion of k(x) = Frac(A/supp x) for the valuation topology of x). For rational subsets U ∋ x (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`) let O(U) be the rational localisation (anchor Layer 3). Then base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(O(U)) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^), compatible with tensor products. Concretely: every finite étale k(x)^-algebra is L ⊗ k(x)^ for some U ∋ x and L ∈ FÉt(O(U)); and for L, L' ∈ FÉt(O(U)), every k(x)^-algebra map L ⊗ k(x)^ → L' ⊗ k(x)^ comes from an O(V)-algebra map over some rational V with x ∈ V ⊆ U, two maps agreeing over k(x)^ agree over some such V. No sheafiness of (A, A⁺) is required.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate; rational subsets containing x form a filtered (downward directed) family, and O(U) → O(V) for V ⊆ U are the restriction maps.
proofSteps: Let A_x = colim_{U ∋ x} O(U) with ring of definition A_{x,0} = colim O⁺(U) ∋ ϖ; A_{x,0} is henselian along ϖ (each O⁺(U) is ϖ-adically complete; P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (a), (b)), and FÉt(A_x) = 2-colim FÉt(O(U)) (P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings).

The kernel N of A_{x,0} → k(x)⁺ (the valuation ring of x, completed) is ϖ-divisible: if f ∈ O⁺(U) has |f(x)| = 0, then V = {|f| ≤ |ϖ|} ∩ U is a rational neighbourhood of x on which f ∈ ϖO⁺(V); so N = ϖN, ϖ is invertible on N, and the ϖ-adic completion of A_{x,0} is the ϖ-adic completion of A_{x,0}/N, which is the completion of the valuation ring k(x)⁺, the image being dense (Berkeley, argument after Theorem 7.4.8).
Hence the completion of the Tate ring A_x is k(x)^, and FÉt(A_x) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^) by P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b).
acceptance: For X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and x the Gauss point, the quadratic extension k(x)^(√T) of k(x)^ spreads out to the finite étale O(U)-algebra O(U)[S]/(S² − T) on U = {|T| = 1}, and to no neighbourhood of the point T = 0 (T is not a unit there).
Rank-one and higher-rank points have the same completed residue field as their maximal generalisation, and the statement holds at every point.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a uniform complete Tate ring are uniform, and their power-bounded elements are the integral closure
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete uniform Tate ring (A° bounded; Tau Ceti `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`), A⁺ ⊆ A° a ring of integral elements, and B ∈ FÉt(A) with its natural topology and plus ring B⁺ = integral closure of A⁺ in B (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra). Then: (a) B is uniform: if b_1, …, b_n ∈ B⁺ generate B as an A-module, then B° ⊆ {b ∈ B : Tr_{B/A}(b b_i) ∈ A° for all i}, a bounded set because the trace pairing is perfect; (b) B° is the integral closure of A° in B; (c) Tr_{B/A}(B°) ⊆ A°. The pair (B, B⁺) is a complete uniform Tate Huber pair.
hypotheses: A complete, uniform, Tate; B finite étale over A as a ring.
proofSteps: Generators in B⁺: B is finite over A and every element of B becomes integral over A⁺ after multiplication by a power of ϖ, so generators can be chosen in B⁺.

Trace bound: for b ∈ B° the element b b_i is power bounded; its characteristic polynomial over A has coefficients of spectral norm ≤ 1 at every point x of Spa(A, A°) (they are elementary symmetric functions of the eigenvalues of multiplication in the finite étale k(x)^-algebra B ⊗ k(x)^, each of absolute value ≤ 1), hence in A° by uniformity (A° = {a : |a(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, anchor Layer 2); so Tr(b b_i) ∈ A°. This proves (c) and the inclusion in (a).

The set {b : Tr(b b_i) ∈ A° ∀i} is bounded: the perfect trace pairing identifies B with Hom_A(B, A) topologically (open mapping for finite projective modules), and the image lies in a bounded set (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.10.1; Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16).

(b): elements integral over A° are power bounded since B° is an integrally closed subring containing A°; conversely the characteristic polynomial of b ∈ B° has coefficients in A° by the trace-bound step, so b is integral over A° (Cayley–Hamilton).
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p and B = ℚ_p(√p): B° = ℤ_p[√p] is the integral closure of ℤ_p, bounded, and Tr(B°) = 2ℤ_p ⊆ ℤ_p.
Non-example: B = A[ε]/(ε²) is finite projective but not étale, and not uniform: λε is power bounded for every λ ∈ A, so B° is unbounded; its trace pairing is degenerate.
