nodes.title: Almost purity in characteristic p: finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (equivalently a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect; no base field), ϖ ∈ R a pseudouniformiser (it has all p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} in R°), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, and S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology and plus ring S⁺ = integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S is perfect, complete and uniform, hence a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, and (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair; (ii) S° is the integral closure of R° in S and S°/S⁺ is almost zero, so S°a = S⁺a; (iii) S°a is an almost finite étale R°a-algebra (almost finitely presented projective and unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S lies in (S°a ⊗_{R°a} S°a)_*); (iv) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° whose composite is multiplication by ε; (v) if S is faithfully flat over R, then Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° and R°a → S°a is almost faithfully flat and almost split. The statement specialises to Scholze 2012 Proposition 5.23 for R a perfectoid K-algebra, K a perfectoid field of characteristic p, and to the finite separable extensions of a perfectoid field of characteristic p.
hypotheses: R perfect, complete, Tate, characteristic p; no perfectoid base field.

Almost mathematics for the basic setup (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), equivalently the ideal (ϖ^{1/p^∞}); almost finite étale in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras (Gabber–Ramero §3.1).
Not claimed: S° finite, flat or étale over R°; S free over R.
proofSteps: (i): S is perfect by P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect; complete Tate with its natural topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) and uniform (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform; alternatively PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform, S being perfect and complete); perfect complete uniform Tate rings of characteristic p are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect); (S, S⁺) is a Huber pair by A1.
(ii): S° = integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b)); S°° ⊆ S⁺ since S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).

(iii) unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S satisfies ϖ^N e ∈ im(S° ⊗_{R°} S°) for some N; as Frobenius is bijective on S° ⊗_{R°} S° (both perfect), ϖ^{N/p^m} e ∈ im(S° ⊗ S°) for every m, so e is an almost element (Scholze 2012 proof of 5.23; Bhatt Proposition 4.3.4).

(iv): write ϖ^N e = Σ_{i=1}^n x_i ⊗ y_i with x_i, y_i ∈ S°; then ϖ^{N/p^m} e = Σ x_i^{1/p^m} ⊗ y_i^{1/p^m} with the same n. For a finite étale algebra and e = Σ a_i ⊗ b_i one has Σ_i Tr_{S/R}(f a_i) b_i = f (Bhatt Construction 4.3.3: Tr of the diagonal factor is 1), so s ↦ (Tr(s x_i^{1/p^m}))_i, (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i y_i^{1/p^m} are maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° (Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c)) composing to ϖ^{N/p^m}: uniform almost finite projectivity. Almost finitely presented projective with an almost idempotent is almost finite étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).

(v): Tr(S) = R for faithfully flat S, so ϖ^c = Tr(f) with f ∈ S°; compatibility of the trace with Frobenius gives ϖ^{c/p^n} = Tr(f^{1/p^n}) with f^{1/p^n} ∈ S°, whence R°° ⊆ Tr(S°°) up to almost zero and R°a → S°a is almost split (Bhatt Remark 4.3.5).
acceptance: Reviewer-authored test (no source example): for K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ and the Artin–Schreier extension S = K[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1}), S is a perfectoid field and S°a is finite étale and uniformly almost finite projective (n = p) over K°a; S° is not finite free over K° at any finite level, and this is not claimed.
The bound n on the number of generators is independent of ε (uniformity); for S of constant rank d one can take n = d², and n = d after localising where S is free.

A non-field instance: R = 𝔽_p[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] (the characteristic-p analogue of ECD Example 3.4(iv)) and S = R[u]/(u^p − u − T^{-1}): the theorem applies without any perfectoid base field.

nodes.title: Characteristic p: inverting ϖ is an equivalence between almost finite étale R°a-algebras and finite étale R-algebras
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser ϖ. Let (R°a)_afet be the category of almost finite étale R°a-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). Then the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* the ring of almost elements, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints), with its natural topology, is an equivalence of categories, compatible with tensor products; a quasi-inverse is S ↦ S°a. Moreover every A ∈ (R°a)_afet is uniformly almost finite projective, A_* is perfect, ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete, and A_* is the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; almost faithful flatness of A corresponds to faithful flatness of A_*[ϖ⁻¹].
hypotheses: R perfect complete Tate of characteristic p; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).
This is Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.28 for V = R°, ε = ϖ (V perfect, m = ∪ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}V).
proofSteps: Well defined: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective over R (almost finite projective modules become finite projective after inverting ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and unramified (the almost idempotent becomes an idempotent), hence finite étale.
Essential surjectivity: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] with S°a ∈ (R°a)_afet by P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p.

Full faithfulness (Bhatt Lemma 4.3.7): A ≅ T^a for T the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]. A is perfect (the almost version of P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect, almost finite étale maps being weakly étale), so A_* is perfect; ϖ is a non-zero-divisor on A_* (almost flatness). For f ∈ T, the R-span of f^ℕ lies in ϖ^{-c}A_*, so ϖ^{c/pⁿ} f ∈ A_* for all n by perfectness, i.e. f ∈ A_*; conversely almost finite generation gives ϖ g^ℕ ⊆ ϖ^{-c}T, whence g ∈ T_*. As T is functorial in the R-algebra A_*[ϖ⁻¹], the functor is fully faithful.
Uniformity and completeness: P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv) for S = A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; A_* = S° is ϖ-adically complete.
acceptance: R = K a perfectoid field of characteristic p: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) ≃ finite products of finite separable extensions L, via L ↦ L°a.
Degenerate: A = R°a ↦ R, A = 0 ↦ 0, A = (R°a)ⁿ ↦ Rⁿ.

Non-example of the integral statement: the functor from finite étale R°-algebras (honest, not almost) to FÉt(R) is not essentially surjective — the Artin–Schreier cover of 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ has no finite étale model over the valuation ring.

nodes.title: The untilting functor on finite étale algebras, T ↦ T♯, via almost finite étale integral structures
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) and choose a pseudouniformiser ϖ♭ ∈ R♭ with ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯ satisfying ϖ^p | p in R° (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), so that R♭°/ϖ♭ = R°/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Define the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) as the composite FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), T ↦ T°a ↦ T°a/ϖ♭ ↦ A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] =: T♯, where the first equivalence is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence, the middle equivalence is the unique flat deformation of almost finite étale algebras along the ϖ-adically complete flat R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), and the last functor inverts ϖ (natural module topology on T♯). Properties: T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring, finite étale over R, with a canonical isomorphism (T♯)♭ ≅ T of R♭-algebras (so (−)♯ is inverse to tilting on its image; compatible with the untilting of perfectoid algebras of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt); (T♯)°a = A is almost finite étale over R°a; the functor is independent of ϖ♭ up to canonical isomorphism, preserves tensor products, finite products, ranks (rank of T♯ at x ∈ Spa R equals the rank of T at x♭) and faithful flatness; and it commutes with base change along every map of perfectoid Tate rings R → R' (for example a rational localisation or the completed residue field at a point): (T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'. Equivalently (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 3.6.20, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.10) T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ for a generator ξ of ker(θ: W(R♭⁺) → R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction), which shows finite étaleness without almost mathematics.
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.
ϖ♭ with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p; different choices give canonically isomorphic functors.
proofSteps: Middle identification: the categories of almost finite étale algebras over R♭°a/ϖ♭ and R°a/ϖ coincide because the rings coincide (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings) and R♭°a = R♭⁺a, R°a = R⁺a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).

Lifting: R°a is flat over the basic setup and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary), so reduction modulo ϖ is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 5.3.27), and the lift A is flat and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete).

Perfectoidness and tilt: A/ϖ = T°a/ϖ♭ is a perfectoid (R°a/ϖ)-algebra (relative Frobenius isomorphism, P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect (b)); A is its unique flat deformation, hence a perfectoid R°a-algebra, and A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is a perfectoid R-algebra whose tilt has the same reduction modulo ϖ♭, i.e. is T (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).
Finite étale: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective and unramified after inverting ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

Base change: each step commutes with base change along R°a → R'°a (flat deformations are unique, reduction modulo ϖ and inverting ϖ commute with tensor products); the tilt of R → R' is R♭ → R'♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality).
Ranks: the rank of an almost finite projective module is read off modulo ϖ and after inverting ϖ, and Spa R ≅ Spa R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets).
acceptance: The untilt of R♭ is R, of R♭ × R♭ is R × R, of 0 is 0.
For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p, and p odd: the untilt of K♭(t^{1/2}) is K(p^{1/2}) (Bhatt Example 3.2.9).

nodes.title: The untilting functor FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) is fully faithful, inverse to tilting on its image, with image the S having almost finite étale integral structure
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field). The untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is fully faithful and, on its essential image, inverse to tilting: for S = T♯, S is perfectoid and S♭ ≅ T. Its essential image consists exactly of the finite étale R-algebras S such that S (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a; for such S, S°a is uniformly almost finite projective over R°a. The functor preserves degrees (rank functions), tensor products and faithful flatness. For R = K a perfectoid field this is the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; for R of characteristic p (R♭ = R) it is the identity.
hypotheses: No claim of essential surjectivity here; that is P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence (ECD 6.1(ii)).
Neither étaleness of S° over R° nor freeness of S over R is asserted or needed.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: each functor in the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor except the last is an equivalence; the last, (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹], is fully faithful because A_* is recovered functorially as the total integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* is the power-bounded subring of the perfectoid, uniform A_*[ϖ⁻¹], PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; almost finite generation gives the reverse inclusion; Bhatt, proof of Theorem 6.2.10, functor (d)).

Image: T♯ has the stated properties (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor). Conversely, if S ∈ FÉt(R) is perfectoid with S°a almost finite étale, then S°a/ϖ is almost finite étale over R°a/ϖ = R♭°a/ϖ♭; let T := the characteristic-p finite étale algebra with T°a/ϖ♭ ≅ S°a/ϖ (P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence and PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras on the tilt side); uniqueness of flat lifts gives S°a ≅ (T♯)°a and S ≅ T♯.

Uniformity: uniform almost finite projectivity lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi, for the root setup of ϖ^{1/p^∞}) from the characteristic-p case (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)).
Degrees, tensor products, faithful flatness: P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.
acceptance: For R = K a perfectoid field this gives a fully faithful, degree-preserving functor FÉt(K♭) → FÉt(K), the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; when K♭ is algebraically closed its image is all of FÉt(K) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and T = R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − t) (ℓ ≠ p prime, t♯ = T): T♯ ≅ R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), a Kummer cover, in the image with S°a almost finite étale.

nodes.title: If the tilt of a perfectoid field is algebraically closed, so is the field
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) with tilt K♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field). If K♭ is algebraically closed (Mathlib `IsAlgClosed K♭`), then K is algebraically closed.
hypotheses: K perfectoid field of any characteristic (in characteristic p, K♭ = K and the statement is trivial).
proofSteps: Let P ∈ K°[X] be monic irreducible of degree d ≥ 1. The Newton polygon of P is a line (P irreducible over the complete field K, unique extension of the absolute value: Mathlib `spectralNorm`), and as |K^×| = |K♭^×| is divisible (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) one may rescale so that |a₀| = 1.

Choose Q ∈ K♭°[X] monic with the same image in K°/ϖ[X] = K♭°/ϖ♭[X] (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field) and a root y ∈ K♭° of Q (K♭ algebraically closed). Then P(y♯) ≡ 0 modulo ϖ (sharp map, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).

P(X + y♯) is irreducible with constant term P(y♯); rescale P₁(X) = c^{-d}P(cX + y♯) with |c|^d = |P(y♯)| ≤ |ϖ|, integral again by the straight Newton polygon; iterate to get a Cauchy sequence x_n with |P(x_n)| ≤ |ϖ|ⁿ converging to a root of P (Scholze 2012 Proposition 3.8; Kedlaya's argument in Bhatt Proposition 3.2.10).
acceptance: The completed algebraic closure ℂ_p of ℚ_p is algebraically closed, with tilt ℂ_p♭ algebraically closed; this lemma recovers the first from the second.
The converse also holds (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)).

nodes.title: Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid, and tilting is a degree-preserving equivalence of finite extensions
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field (characteristic 0 or p) with tilt K♭. (i) Every finite extension L/K, with its natural topology (the unique extension of the absolute value, Mathlib `spectralNorm`), is a perfectoid field. (ii) The untilting functor (−)♯ of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is an equivalence FÉt(K♭) ≃ FÉt(K) with quasi-inverse L ↦ L♭; it restricts to an equivalence between finite field extensions of K♭ and of K, preserving degrees, automorphism groups and Galois extensions. (iii) K is algebraically closed if and only if K♭ is. (iv) For every finite extension L/K, L°a is almost finite étale over K°a (Tate, Gabber–Ramero §6.6 for deeply ramified fields), uniformly almost finite projective.
hypotheses: K perfectoid field; finite extensions carry their natural topology; finite étale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`).
An alternative, ramification-theoretic proof (Gabber–Ramero Propositions 6.6.2 and 6.6.6: L°a/K°a étale for deeply ramified K; 6.3.6: finite projectivity) is not the route planned here.
proofSteps: Characteristic p: (i) and (iv) are P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p for R = K; (ii) is the identity; (iii) trivial.
(ii) full faithfulness and degrees: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for R = K.

Essential surjectivity: let M be the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭ (perfect and complete, hence a perfectoid field); its untilt M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) is a perfectoid field over K (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field: R is a perfectoid field iff R♭ is) and algebraically closed (P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field).

The union N ⊆ M♯ of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭ is a subfield algebraic over K and dense in M♯ (M is the completed colimit of the perfectoid fields L, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ over K, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (c), and the colimit of the L♯ is dense in it, (a)); by Krasner's lemma (Mathlib `IsKrasner.of_completeSpace`, applied over finite subextensions of N/K, which are complete) N is separably closed; as K has characteristic 0 in this step, every finite extension F/K is separable and embeds in some L♯ with L/K♭ finite Galois.

L♯/K is Galois with Gal(L♯/K) ≅ Gal(L/K♭) (untilting preserves degrees and automorphisms); F = (L♯)^H for a subgroup H, and F♭ := L^H satisfies (F♭)♯ ⊆ (L♯)^H = F with equal degrees, so F is an untilt. General finite étale K-algebras are finite products of such F.
(i): F ≅ (F♭)♯ is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) and a field; its topology is the natural one (finite-dimensional K-vector space).

(iii): if K♭ is algebraically closed, apply P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field; if K is, every finite extension of K♭ untilts to a finite extension of K of the same degree, hence is trivial, so K♭ (perfect) is algebraically closed.
(iv): L is in the essential image of (−)♯, so L°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful).
acceptance: Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ and 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ have equivalent categories of finite extensions (P3/fontaine-wintenberger).

For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd), L is perfectoid, L♭ is a quadratic extension of K♭, and L°a/K°a is almost finite étale although L°/K° is ramified (the different of K(p^{1/2p^n})/K_n has valuation 1/(2pⁿ) → 0, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).
Non-example: ℚ_p is not perfectoid and its finite extensions are not either (discretely valued, ECD Remark 3.3); the theorem needs K perfectoid.

nodes.title: The completed cyclotomic extension of a finite extension of ℚ_p is perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p inside a fixed algebraic closure, and C its completion. The closure L of K(μ_{p^∞}) in C is a perfectoid field: L = K·ℚ_p^cycl is the compositum of K with the completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), a finite extension of ℚ_p^cycl of degree at most [K : ℚ_p], and K(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in it. Its tilt is the finite extension of (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ corresponding to L under the tilting equivalence of finite extensions.
hypotheses: K a finite extension of ℚ_p; no ramification hypothesis.
The perfectoid condition is checked once, for ℚ_p^cycl (P1), and transported along the finite extension L/ℚ_p^cycl by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.
proofSteps: K·ℚ_p^cycl is a finite extension of the complete field ℚ_p^cycl (generated by a primitive element of K over ℚ_p), hence complete for the unique extension of the absolute value; so it is closed in C.
K(μ_{p^∞}) = K·ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in K·ℚ_p^cycl: ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in ℚ_p^cycl and K·ℚ_p^cycl = Σ K·ℚ_p^cycl over a K-basis, so L = K·ℚ_p^cycl.

ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); a finite extension of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field and tilting matches finite extensions (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (i), (ii)).
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p this is ℚ_p^cycl itself.

For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}), L = ℚ_p^cycl(p^{1/p}) is a perfectoid field of degree p over ℚ_p^cycl (a Kummer extension: p^{1/p} ∉ ℚ_p^cycl because ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p is abelian and ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) is not Galois over ℚ_p), while K itself is not perfectoid.

nodes.title: The completed tensor product of plus rings need not be integrally closed
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with algebraically closed residue field, for instance the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) with ℚ̆_p the completion of the maximal unramified extension of ℚ_p, let ℓ be a prime with ℓ ∤ p(p − 1), and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), a cyclic Galois extension of degree ℓ which is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields) with trivial residue extension. With A = K, B = C = L and plus rings the rings of integers, D = L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ and D⁺ = (L°)^ℓ, while L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ is injective and not surjective. So the map from the ϖ-adic completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ to D⁺ in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) is an almost isomorphism that is not an isomorphism, and the completed tensor product of plus rings is not integrally closed in D, hence not a ring of integral elements.
hypotheses: K perfectoid with algebraically closed residue field; ℓ a prime not dividing p(p − 1).
The perfectoidness of L is the finite-extension theorem of this layer; the rest is the formula of P2.
proofSteps: (iv) K contains μ_ℓ (Hensel's lemma over the algebraically closed residue field) and p^{1/ℓ} ∉ K (1/ℓ is not in the value group (p − 1)⁻¹ℤ[1/p]), so L/K is cyclic of degree ℓ and L ⊗_K L ≅ L^ℓ, a ⊗ b ↦ (a g(b))_g. As the value group of K is dense, 𝔪_K L° = 𝔪_L, so L°/𝔪_K L° is the residue field of L, which equals that of K. If L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ (injective, the source being K°-flat) were surjective, K° → L° would be a Galois extension of rings with group Gal(L/K), hence L° would be finite projective, thus free, of rank ℓ over the local ring K°, contradicting dim L°/𝔪_K L° = 1.
The formula of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) identifies D⁺ with (L°)^ℓ up to the almost isomorphism, which is therefore not an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Fontaine–Wintenberger: the absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and of its tilt are isomorphic
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K♭. Fix an algebraic closure K̄ of K with completion C, so that C♭ is an algebraically closed perfectoid field containing K♭ (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)), and let K♭^sep be the separable closure of K♭ in C♭. Then L ↦ L♭ (for finite Galois L/K inside K̄, with L♭ ⊆ C♭ by functoriality of tilting) defines an isomorphism of profinite groups Gal(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K♭^sep/K♭) (Mathlib `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` up to the choice of closures), compatible with the Galois correspondences (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`): finite subextensions of K̄/K correspond to finite subextensions of K♭^sep/K♭ with the same degrees. Application (Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1): the absolute Galois groups of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and of 𝔽_p((t)) are canonically isomorphic; this uses in addition that an algebraic extension F of a complete field and its completion F̂ have the same absolute Galois group (FÉt(F) ≃ FÉt(F̂), F° being henselian: P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b)), and that 𝔽_p((t)) → 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) is purely inseparable (Frobenius twists do not change finite étale algebras, P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection).
hypotheses: K perfectoid field; closures fixed as described; continuity is part of the claim (isomorphism of profinite groups).
proofSteps: For finite Galois L/K ⊆ K̄, L is perfectoid and L♭/K♭ is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ Gal(L♭/K♭) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii): equivalence preserving degrees and automorphisms).
The embeddings: L ⊆ C induces L♭ ⊆ C♭, landing in K♭^sep (L♭ is separable over K♭); every finite separable extension of K♭ inside C♭ arises (essential surjectivity), and inclusions correspond.

Gal(K̄/K) = lim_L Gal(L/K) over finite Galois subextensions (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.algEquivToLimit`), likewise for K♭; the isomorphisms of the finite quotients are compatible with restriction (functoriality), so their limit is an isomorphism of profinite groups.

Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_K for K its completion, and G_{𝔽_p((t))} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{K♭} (completion and purely inseparable extension), then apply the main statement with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p.
acceptance: Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}.
For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})), G_K ≅ G_{K♭} with K♭ ≅ 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t = ε − 1 for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ K♭°: the Fontaine–Wintenberger field-of-norms isomorphism.
Consequence: for C algebraically closed perfectoid, Spa(C, C⁺) and Spa(C♭, C♭⁺) both have trivial finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).

nodes.title: Tilting is an equivalence between finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring and over its tilt (ECD 6.1(ii))
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭. Then the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse the tilting functor S ↦ S♭ (S being perfectoid). It is compatible with tensor products, with base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings (in particular rational localisations and completed residue fields), and preserves ranks and faithful flatness. For every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R° with tilt R♭⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), it induces an equivalence between finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) and (R♭, R♭⁺) → (S♭, S♭⁺) (plus rings the integral closures; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), i.e. between finite étale affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(R, R⁺) and over Spa(R♭, R♭⁺).
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.

The gluing uses rational coverings of Spa(R, R⁺) and the effective descent of finite étale algebras along them (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent), which needs no sheafiness; the sheaf property of O is not used.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful.

Local essential surjectivity: fix S ∈ FÉt(R), X = Spa(R, R⁺), x ∈ X. The completed residue field k(x)^ is a perfectoid field with tilt k(x♭)^ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). By P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii), S ⊗_R k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ for some T_x ∈ FÉt(k(x♭)^). By P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X♭ there are a rational U♭ ∋ x♭ and T_U ∈ FÉt(O_{X♭}(U♭)) with T_U ⊗ k(x♭)^ ≅ T_x; U♭ is the tilt of a rational U ∋ x with O_X(U) perfectoid of tilt O_{X♭}(U♭) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

Then (T_U)♯ ∈ FÉt(O_X(U)) satisfies (T_U)♯ ⊗ k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ ≅ S ⊗ k(x)^ (base change compatibility of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor); by the full faithfulness half of P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X, after shrinking U, (T_U)♯ ≅ S ⊗_R O_X(U).

Quasi-compactness of X (anchor Layer 2) gives a finite rational covering X = ∪ U_i with T_i ∈ FÉt(O(U_i♭)) and φ_i: T_i♯ ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i). On the rational U_ij = U_i ∩ U_j, φ_j⁻¹ ∘ φ_i descends uniquely to T_i ⊗ O(U_ij♭) ≅ T_j ⊗ O(U_ij♭) (full faithfulness over the perfectoid O(U_ij), whose tilt is O(U_ij♭)); the cocycle condition holds by faithfulness over U_ijk.

Glue: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent on X♭ gives T ∈ FÉt(R♭) with T ⊗ O(U_i♭) ≅ T_i compatibly; then T♯ ⊗ O(U_i) ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i) compatibly on overlaps, and the full faithfulness of descent on X gives T♯ ≅ S.

Quasi-inverse: T♯ is perfectoid with (T♯)♭ ≅ T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor), so S ↦ S♭ is quasi-inverse. Plus rings: the integral closure of R⁺ in S tilts to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭, both being the elements of absolute value ≤ 1 at the points over Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).
acceptance: For R = K a perfectoid field this is P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii).

For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩): the finite étale R-algebras are the untilts of finite étale algebras over the characteristic-p ring; e.g. the Kummer cover R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), ℓ ≠ p, is the untilt of R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − T♭).
The non-field example of ECD Example 3.4(iv), R = ℤ_p^cycl⟦T^{1/p^∞}⟧⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T], is covered: no base field is used.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid (ECD 6.1(i))
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) and S a finite étale R-algebra (Mathlib `Module.Finite R S`, `Algebra.Etale R S`) with its natural topology as a finite R-module. Then S is a perfectoid Tate ring; S ≅ (S♭)♯ with S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); for every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R°, with S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S (the finite étale pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S` of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair whose tilt (S♭, S♭⁺) has S♭⁺ the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭. Consequently Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is a finite étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces. This serves AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.5(1), Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 2.15(a)).
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale as a ring; the topology on S is the natural module topology (complete, since S is finite projective).
proofSteps: By P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S ≅ T♯ for T := S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor).
The natural topology on S agrees with the topology of T♯ (both are the natural finite R-module topology; any R-linear isomorphism of finite projective modules is a homeomorphism).
Plus rings: as in the last step of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S⁺ corresponds to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭ under PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.

(S, S⁺) is sheafy (perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so Spa(S, S⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space finite étale over Spa(R, R⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism).
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p^cycl and S = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): S is a perfectoid field (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R[u]/(u² − (1 + pT)) (p odd; étale since 1 + pT is a unit and 2 is invertible): S is perfectoid.

Non-example (why étale matters): S = R[u]/(u²) is finite but not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid; S = R[u]/(u² − p) over R = ℚ_p^cycl is finite étale and perfectoid, but the analogous extension ℚ_p(√p) of the non-perfectoid ℚ_p is not perfectoid.

nodes.title: Almost purity, categorical form: (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) by inverting ϖ, compatibly with tilting
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p, and R⁺ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then: (a) the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (natural topology), is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse S ↦ S°a = S⁺a, compatible with tensor products and base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings; (b) the six categories FÉt(R) ≃ (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet ≃ (R♭°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R♭) of Scholze's diagram are equivalent by the functors of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor, and the composite is the tilting equivalence of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence; (c) (R⁺a)_afet = (R°a)_afet, since R⁺a = R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup; ECD Definition 3.23). In Bhatt's notation: inverting p (resp. t) gives R°a_afet ≃ R_fet (resp. S°a_afet ≃ S_fet) and tilting gives R°a_afet ≃ S°a_afet for S = R♭.
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).
proofSteps: Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is T♯ for some T (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), so S°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the essential image consists of S with almost finite étale S°a).

A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is fully faithful (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful, proof) and essentially surjective: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] since (S°a)_* = S° for perfectoid S (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; S perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).

(b): each functor of the chain is an equivalence: P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence on the tilt side, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras for the two reductions modulo ϖ, (a) on the untilt side.
(c): S⁺ ⊆ S° with S°/S⁺ almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii) applied to the perfectoid S).
acceptance: R = K a perfectoid field: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) via L ↦ L°a (Berkeley Theorem 7.3.2 and the diagram following it).
Characteristic p: this is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence (Gabber–Ramero 3.5.28).
Non-example: the analogous functor on honest (non-almost) finite étale R°-algebras is not essentially surjective: over K = ℚ_p^cycl, K(p^{1/2})° is not étale over K°.

nodes.title: The integral closure is almost finite étale: S° over R° for S finite étale over a perfectoid Tate ring R (ECD 6.1(iii))
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, ϖ a pseudouniformiser, S ∈ FÉt(R) and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S° is the integral closure of R° in S, S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S°, and S°a = S⁺a is an almost finite étale R°a = R⁺a-algebra: almost finitely presented, almost projective, and unramified (the diagonal idempotent of S ⊗_R S is an almost element of S° ⊗_{R°} S°); (ii) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° composing to multiplication by ε; (iii) Tr_{S/R}(S°) ⊆ R° and the trace pairing induces an almost isomorphism S°a → alHom_{R°a}(S°a, R°a); (iv) if S is faithfully flat over R, S°a is almost faithfully flat over R°a, Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° (up to almost zero), and R°a → S°a is almost split. Not claimed, and false in general: S° finite, flat or étale over R°, or S free over R.
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
proofSteps: (i): by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence, S ≅ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] with A almost finite étale and A = S°a; S° is the integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b), S being uniform); S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S° as S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).

(ii): uniformity holds in characteristic p (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)) and lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi) through the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.

(iii): an almost finite projective algebra is almost finite étale iff its trace pairing is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 4.1.14); Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c).

(iv): faithful flatness of S is positivity of ranks, preserved by tilting; in characteristic p, R°a → S°a is almost split with trace surjective onto R°° (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (v)); reduce modulo ϖ and lift: almost splitting modulo ϖ of an almost projective map lifts, and trace surjectivity is checked modulo ϖ by Nakayama for the ϖ-adically complete R°.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): L°a is almost finite étale over K°a though L°/K° is ramified; the trace of L° contains every element of positive valuation (Tate's computation, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).

Kedlaya–Liu's formulation: o_B is uniformly almost finite projective and almost étale over o_A for B ∈ FÉt(A), A perfectoid (Theorem 5.5.9); Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.24: Tr: B°° → A°° surjective for B faithfully finite étale.

nodes.title: The almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Theorem 6.1)
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1; characteristic 0, p, or neither; no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭, and FÉt(R) the category of finite étale R-algebras with their natural topologies. (i) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid). (ii) Tilting S ↦ S♭ is an equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭), with quasi-inverse the untilting functor (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence). (iii) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S° is almost finite étale over R° (equivalently S⁺a over R⁺a for any ring of integral elements and S⁺ its integral closure), and uniformly almost finite projective (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale); categorically, A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence). The three conclusions are distinct statements: (iii) is about the integral structure up to almost zero and is neither étaleness of S° over R° nor finite freeness of S over R. Consequences recorded elsewhere: every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale); for R = K a perfectoid field, (i)–(iii) are P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.

nodes.title: Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy; perfectoid spaces are locally strongly sheafy
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. For every n ≥ 0 the Tate algebra R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ (Tau Ceti `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R`) is stably uniform, hence sheafy for every ring of integral elements; that is, R is strongly sheafy in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (`Huber.IsStronglySheafy R`). Consequently every perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) is a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy`), and every rational localisation and every finite étale algebra of a perfectoid Tate ring is strongly sheafy. This makes available, for perfectoid spaces, A1's local-to-global description of finite étale maps, fibre products of étale maps inside adic spaces, and the étale and finite étale sites with their structure sheaves.
hypotheses: R perfectoid Tate (ECD Definition 3.1); p is topologically nilpotent in R because ϖ^p | p, so R is a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra.
proofSteps: The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), hence stably uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy).

R⟨T⟩ → R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ splits as a map of topological R⟨T⟩-modules: R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the completed direct sum of the free rank-one modules R⟨T⟩·T^b over b ∈ (ℤ[1/p] ∩ [0, 1))ⁿ, and the projection onto b = 0 is continuous and R⟨T⟩-linear.

A complete Tate ring admitting a topologically split map to a stably uniform complete Tate ring is stably uniform, hence sheafy by Buzzard–Verberkmoes (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy; anchor Layer 4).

nodes.title: Finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(i))
nodes.statement: Let X, Y be perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: the full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces locally of the form Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid). A morphism f: Y → X is finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f`) if it is finite étale as a morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism: X has a cover by open affinoids V = Spa(A, A⁺) with f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺) over V, B ∈ FÉt(A) with its natural topology and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺). No second notion is introduced: `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` is A1's `AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` of the underlying morphism. ECD's defining condition — for every open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X the preimage f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid with R → S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S — is equivalent (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale), as are Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (a cover of X by such affinoids) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1). X_fét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces finite étale over X (all X-morphisms); for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, global sections give X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. Conventions: the plus ring is the integral closure, never S° when R⁺ ≠ R°; f need not be surjective; the degree x ↦ dim_{k(x)}(O_Y ⊗ k(x)) is locally constant.
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid; for Y an arbitrary adic space with Y → X finite étale, Y is automatically perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).
proofSteps: Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f := AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` on the underlying morphism (perfectoid spaces are analytic, their charts being Tate).
The affinoid model Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(R), R perfectoid, is an affinoid perfectoid space: S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and sheafy.
acceptance: The fold map X ⊔ X → X and ∅ → X are finite étale; an open immersion that is not closed is not.
For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) and ℓ ≠ p, the Kummer cover T ↦ T^ℓ (Spa of R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) is finite étale of degree ℓ.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(ii))
nodes.statement: A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f`) if it is étale in A1's local sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`): every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood V ⊆ Y such that f|_V factors as V ↪ W → U ↪ X with V → W an open immersion, W → U finite étale (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces) and U ⊆ X open. W is then automatically perfectoid. This is ECD Definition 6.2(ii) (whose printed condition 'y ∈ Y' is read as y ∈ V), Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(iii) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(2). Equivalent local form: U may be taken a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid open of X, W = Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(O(U)), and V a rational subset of W; so étale morphisms are locally composites 'rational embedding, finite étale, rational embedding' of affinoid perfectoid spaces. X_ét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces étale over X (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). Étale morphisms need not be separated or quasi-compact.
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid; an adic space étale over a perfectoid X is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).
proofSteps: Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f := AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f` on the underlying morphism.

W perfectoid: W → U finite étale with U perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid, locally on U); rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

nodes.title: Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces; tilting invariance and base change
nodes.statement: (Scholze 2012 Definition 7.2, over an arbitrary perfectoid base) A morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) of perfectoid Huber pairs is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale (S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology, S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale f`) if X has a cover by open affinoid perfectoid V with f⁻¹(V) affinoid perfectoid and (O_X(V), O⁺_X(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O⁺_Y(f⁻¹V)) strongly finite étale; strongly étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale f`) if locally on Y it factors as an open immersion, a strongly finite étale map and an open immersion. Properties: (a) f is strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭ is (the almost finite étale condition is transported by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b)); (b) base change along arbitrary maps Z → X of perfectoid spaces preserves both classes, with affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C (already complete, being finite projective over C), D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺ in D, and |Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| surjective (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(i)–(ii), with the printed |X ×_Z Y| read as the fibre product of the base change); (c) composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.8); (d) in characteristic p every (finite) étale map is strongly (finite) étale, and by almost purity this holds in general (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale), so the strong classes coincide with P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces and P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces.
hypotheses: Perfectoid spaces without base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) on each chart (R°a = R⁺a).
proofSteps: Definition: the affinoid condition is stable under restriction to rational subsets (base change of almost finite étale algebras, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras, and rational localisation of the perfectoid pair, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction), so the global notion is well defined.

(b), affinoid case: A ⊗_B C is finite projective over C, hence complete; it is finite étale over C and D°a = A°a ⊗ C°a is almost finite étale (base change); the universal property among perfectoid spaces follows from that of Spa of a finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv)); surjectivity on points from Huber's argument (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).

(a): the tilting slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence) matches affinoid perfectoid covers; strongly finite étale affinoid maps correspond under P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b).
acceptance: The strong notion is a priori stronger: it requires S°a almost finite étale; in characteristic 0 the equality with finite étale is a theorem (almost purity), not part of the definition.

nodes.title: Preimages of affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with strongly finite étale ring map
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be a finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), or more generally a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces with X perfectoid, and let V = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X be an open affinoid perfectoid subspace (arbitrary perfectoid Tate R, no base field). Then f⁻¹(V) is affinoid perfectoid: f⁻¹(V) = Spa(S, S⁺) with S = O_Y(f⁻¹V) ∈ FÉt(R) perfectoid and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S, and (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) is strongly finite étale (S°a almost finite étale over R°a). Global sections give an equivalence V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op, and strongly finite étale covers of V correspond to finite étale R-algebras (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.6 and Theorem 7.9(i)–(ii), Bhatt Proposition 10.0.6 and Corollary 10.0.7, in general). In particular every finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces satisfies ECD Definition 6.2(i). Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.7 (in characteristic p, étale maps are locally base changes of étale maps of noetherian affinoid adic spaces) is not needed for this.
hypotheses: X perfectoid; f finite étale in A1's sense; V affinoid perfectoid open.
proofSteps: R is strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), so AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (a), (c) gives f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S`) with S ∈ FÉt(R), and V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. (The descent of finite étale algebras along the rational cover of V on which f is known to be affinoid is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent; Scholze's noetherian approximation, via P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit and p-finite affinoids, is replaced by it.)

S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), so the map of pairs is strongly finite étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change).
acceptance: A finite étale cover of the perfectoid closed disc glued from covers of two rational pieces with compatible gluing is Spa of a single finite étale algebra over R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, with plus ring the integral closure of R⁺.
Openness of strongly étale maps follows (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); it is not assumed.

nodes.title: Every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale)
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then f is finite étale iff it is strongly finite étale, and étale iff it is strongly étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change). In characteristic p this is P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p; in general it is a consequence of almost purity (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale). Hence the tilting invariance and base-change properties of the strong classes hold for all (finite) étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid spaces over no fixed base.
proofSteps: Strongly ⇒ plain: by definition.
Finite étale ⇒ strongly finite étale: over each affinoid perfectoid V ⊆ X, P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids.
Étale ⇒ strongly étale: the finite étale factor W → U of the local description is strongly finite étale by the previous step.

nodes.title: Comparison of perfectoid finite étale and étale morphisms with AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and with finite étale algebras
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space. (a) (Perfectoidness) If g: Y → X is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of analytic adic spaces in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), then Y is a perfectoid space. (b) (Morphism classes) For morphisms of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: finite étale in A1's sense (= P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); ECD Definition 6.2(i) (for every open affinoid perfectoid U the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with integral-closure plus ring); Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (for one open affinoid perfectoid cover); Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1); strongly finite étale. Likewise étale in A1's sense ⇔ ECD 6.2(ii) ⇔ Scholze 2012 7.1(iii) ⇔ Berkeley 7.5.1(2) ⇔ strongly étale. (c) (Algebraic comparison) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, the functors X_fét → FÉt(R)^op (global sections), FÉt(R) → {finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)} (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`, plus ring forced to be the integral closure) and the latter → Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` (forget topology and plus ring) are equivalences; every finite étale R-algebra is perfectoid for its natural topology. (d) (Sites) The category of perfectoid spaces étale (resp. finite étale) over X is the small étale (resp. finite étale) site of the underlying adic space in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site), with the same coverings; A1's structure sheaves O, O⁺ on it (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), its Galois category of finite étale objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category) and its basis of affinoid objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison) apply. (e) (Base change from adic spaces; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv) and Proposition 7.10) If Y' → X' is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (e.g. locally noetherian ones) and Z → X' is a morphism from a perfectoid space, then Y' ×_{X'} Z exists, is perfectoid, and is finite étale (resp. étale) over Z; for affinoids its ring is D = A ⊗_B C with D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺.
hypotheses: X perfectoid, hence locally strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy); A1's notions are defined for all analytic adic spaces.
proofSteps: (a): locally on X, Y is Spa(S, S⁺) with S finite étale over a perfectoid R (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global over the strongly sheafy affinoid perfectoid charts), perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid; for étale maps, Y is locally an open subspace of such a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).

(b): A1 ⇔ Scholze 7.1(ii) by definition; A1 ⇒ ECD 6.2(i) by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids; ECD 6.2(i) ⇒ A1 trivially; ⇔ strongly by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale; Berkeley 7.5.1(1) quantifies over opens of the target and is equivalent by the same lemma. The étale case follows from the finite étale case and the definitions.

(c): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv) (morphisms of the pairs are the algebra maps); the forgetful functor to CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R is an equivalence because the topology and the plus ring are determined.
(d): objects étale over X in A1's sense are perfectoid by (a); the morphism classes agree by (b); coverings are jointly surjective families in both.

(e): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change for the fibre product with locally strongly sheafy Z; perfectoidness by (a) applied over Z; it is the fibre product in perfectoid spaces over the analytic base X' of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base (the uniform completion is unnecessary, the algebra being finite projective over the perfectoid factor).

nodes.title: Étale and finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces: composition, base change, cancellation, openness, tilting
nodes.statement: For morphisms of perfectoid spaces (Berkeley Proposition 7.5.2; ECD after Definition 6.2; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.8, Proposition 7.10): (1) composites of (finite) étale morphisms are (finite) étale; (2) for f: Y → X (finite) étale and any g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces, the fibre product Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is (finite) étale over X', agrees with A1's fibre product of adic spaces, has the affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C, D⁺ = integral closure of C⁺ (no completion needed), and |Y ×_X X'| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| is surjective; (3) if g and g ∘ f are (finite) étale, so is f; (4) f is (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭: Y♭ → X♭ is; (5) étale morphisms are open; quasi-compact étale morphisms have quasi-compact open image; the diagonal of an étale morphism is an open immersion, and of a finite étale morphism an open and closed immersion.
hypotheses: All spaces perfectoid; fibre products in perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2.
proofSteps: (1), (3), (5): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal, applied to the underlying adic spaces (locally strongly sheafy by P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), with P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale identifying the classes.

(2): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change gives the fibre product of adic spaces with its affinoid formula; it is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)) and therefore satisfies the universal property among perfectoid spaces, so it is the perfectoid fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property); surjectivity on points from A1.

(4): by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale, f is (finite) étale iff strongly (finite) étale, and the strong classes are tilting invariant (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (a)) — on affinoids by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence with plus rings, and the tilting slice equivalence PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence matches open covers.
acceptance: For X' = Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) → X at a point x, the fibre of a finite étale Y → X is Spa of the finite étale k(x)^-algebra O_Y(f⁻¹V) ⊗ k(x)^.
For the Kummer cover f of the perfectoid torus over ℚ_p^cycl, f♭ is the Kummer cover u ↦ u^ℓ of the tilted torus over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^.

nodes.title: The étale site X_ét and the finite étale site X_fét of a perfectoid space
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space. Its étale site X_ét (`PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale X`) is the small étale site of the underlying locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site; P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy): objects the adic spaces étale over X — all perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)), i.e. the perfectoid spaces étale over X of ECD — with all X-morphisms (étale by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (3)), and the topology generated by jointly surjective families (on all points, including higher-rank ones). The finite étale site X_fét is the full subcategory of finite étale objects with the induced jointly-surjective topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). Structure: (i) X_ét has finite limits (fibre products of perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and a basis X_ét^aff of affinoid perfectoid objects étale over X, closed under rational subsets, finite étale maps and fibre products (Kedlaya–Liu 8.3.1: perfectoid spaces are stably adic), which is a dense subsite (Mathlib `Functor.IsDenseSubsite`); (ii) a morphism g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces induces a morphism of sites X'_ét → X_ét by base change, functorially; a morphism X → Y to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (e.g. locally noetherian) induces a morphism of sites X_ét → Y_ét (Scholze 2012 after Definition 7.11); (iii) O_{X_ét}: U ↦ O_U(U) and O⁺_{X_ét}: U ↦ O⁺_U(U) are sheaves of rings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), as are O⁺/ϖ and O^{+a}; (iv) for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op; (v) for X connected and a geometric point, X_fét is a Galois category with fundamental group π₁(X) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category), and for X = Spa(K, K⁺), K a perfectoid field, π₁ = Gal(K^sep/K).
hypotheses: X perfectoid; sites are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 with the coverings of ECD (jointly surjective).
proofSteps: Take A1's site of the underlying adic space; perfectoidness of all objects and the equality of the morphism classes is P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale.
Site axioms, morphisms of sites: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (i)–(iv) with the fibre products identified by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (2).

Basis: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison; affinoid objects are affinoid perfectoid by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids.
Sheaves: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf; O⁺/ϖ and the almost sheaves by sheafification (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology).
acceptance: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every covering of X in X_ét has a member with a section near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).
For X = Spa(K, O_K), K perfectoid field, X_fét ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets.

nodes.title: Étale descent for finite étale morphisms and finite projective modules on perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with étale site X_ét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). (a) (Locality) A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is finite étale if, for some covering {X_i → X} in X_ét, every base change Y ×_X X_i → X_i is finite étale; étaleness of f is local on Y and on X for open coverings. (b) (Stack) The prestack U ↦ U_fét (finite étale perfectoid spaces over U, with isomorphisms) on X_ét is a stack for the étale topology (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`): finite étale spaces with descent data along an étale covering descend uniquely. (c) (Vector bundles; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22(b), (d)) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, M ↦ M ⊗_R O_{X_ét} is an equivalence between finitely generated projective R-modules and finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules, and M ⊗ O is a sheaf on X_ét with M ⊗ O(Y) = M ⊗_R O(Y) on affinoid perfectoid Y ∈ X_ét. Descent along v-covers is not part of this node (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks).
hypotheses: X perfectoid; coverings jointly surjective families of étale maps.
proofSteps: Reduction: every covering in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object can be refined by composites of rational coverings and single surjective finite étale maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction, after Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.20 and de Jong–van der Put); it suffices to prove the claims for these two kinds of coverings.

Rational coverings: effective descent of finite étale algebras (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent) and of finite projective modules (Kiehl gluing on sheafy Tate affinoids, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing; perfectoid pairs are sheafy).

Surjective finite étale Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺): R → S is faithfully flat; faithfully flat descent of modules (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`, `ModuleCat.reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.4) descends the module and its multiplication; finiteness, projectivity and étaleness descend (Mathlib `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, `Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.5). The descended algebra is finite étale over R, hence perfectoid with the integral-closure plus ring (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (c)); finite projective modules descend along the sheafy finite étale surjection by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent.
(a) follows from (b) applied to the base-changed family with its canonical descent datum, together with full faithfulness (the equaliser property of O, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf).
acceptance: For a finite Galois étale cover Y → X with group G and a G-equivariant finite étale Y' → Y, Y' descends to a finite étale X' → X with Y' = X' ×_X Y (Galois descent).
For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every finite locally free O_{X_ét}-module is free (c).

nodes.title: Tilting identifies the étale sites: X_ét ≃ X♭_ét, compatibly with affinoids, fibre products, coverings and O⁺/ϖ
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting). The tilting functor Y ↦ Y♭ of the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence: perfectoid spaces over X ≃ perfectoid spaces over X♭) restricts to equivalences of categories X_ét ≃ X♭_ét and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). These equivalences preserve and reflect affinoid perfectoid objects (with Spa(S, S⁺)♭ = Spa(S♭, S♭⁺)), fibre products, and covering families (|Y| ≅ |Y♭| compatibly with the maps to |X| ≅ |X♭|); hence they are equivalences of sites and induce equivalences of topoi Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X♭_ét) (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`). They are functorial in X: compatible with the morphisms of sites induced by maps X' → X and their tilts. For a pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ of X (locally), they identify the sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ and O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and the almost sheaves O⁺a/ϖ and O⁺a_{X♭}/ϖ♭, on the identified sites. For affinoid X = Spa(R, R⁺) the restriction to X_fét is the tilting equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭) of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.
hypotheses: X perfectoid over no fixed base; ϖ chosen on affinoid perfectoid opens as in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.
proofSteps: Objects: Y → X is étale iff Y♭ → X♭ is (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (4)); essential surjectivity from the slice equivalence (every perfectoid space over X♭ is Y♭ for a perfectoid Y over X).

Affinoid perfectoid objects: Spa(S, S⁺) ↦ Spa(S♭, S♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting); finite étale objects over affinoids correspond by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.

Coverings: |Y| ≅ |Y♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, glued), compatibly with the projections, so joint surjectivity is preserved; fibre products are preserved by the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products).
Topoi: an equivalence of sites preserving and reflecting coverings induces an equivalence of sheaf categories (Mathlib `Equivalence.sheafCongr`).

O⁺/ϖ: on affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(S, S⁺), S⁺/ϖ = S♭⁺/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, ECD Lemma 3.11), compatibly with rational restriction and finite étale base change; sheafify.
acceptance: The site isomorphism is compatible with the homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭| (open subspaces correspond to open subspaces).
For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl), X_ét ≃ X♭_ét recovers Fontaine–Wintenberger (P3/fontaine-wintenberger) on the finite étale part.
Non-example: tilting is not a morphism of ringed sites (O_X and O_{X♭} are not identified; only O⁺/ϖ is).

nodes.title: Almost acyclicity of O⁺ and acyclicity of O on the étale site of an affinoid perfectoid space
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space (R perfectoid Tate, no base field) with étale site X_ét, and write H^i(X_ét, −) for sheaf cohomology of abelian sheaves on X_ét (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). Then: (a) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is almost zero (killed by R°°) for i > 0; (b) H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0; (c) for every finite covering {U_j → U} in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object U by affinoid perfectoid objects, the augmented Čech complex of O⁺ is almost exact and that of O is exact; (d) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)^a = (R⁺/ϖ)^a and H^i(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ) is almost zero for i > 0; (e) for every finitely generated projective R-module M, H^i(X_ét, M ⊗_R O) = 0 for i > 0. The same holds on the analytic site (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity) and for every affinoid perfectoid object of X_ét.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; almost zero = killed by every pseudouniformiser (ECD Definition 3.21).
proofSteps: Reduction to Čech complexes: the affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis of X_ét stable under fibre products (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space); by the Čech-to-derived comparison on an acyclic basis (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison; its almost version PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology) and the covering reduction of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.21), it suffices to show (c) for rational coverings and for single surjective finite étale maps Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺).

Rational coverings: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity for O⁺, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy (c) for O.

Surjective finite étale R → S: S is faithfully flat and finite étale; the n-fold fibre products are Spa of S^{⊗_R n} with plus rings whose almost versions are (S⁺a)^{⊗ n} over R⁺a (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence: the equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) respects tensor products). The Čech complex of O⁺ is the Amitsur complex of R⁺a → S⁺a, which is almost faithfully flat (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale (iv)), hence almost exact (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact, within PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent); the complex of O is the Amitsur complex of the faithfully flat R → S, exact (Mathlib `CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat` in degree 0; faithfully flat descent).
H⁰ exactly: O⁺ is a sheaf with O⁺(X) = R⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), not merely almost.
(b) from (a) by inverting ϖ on the Čech complexes of finite coverings (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion), or directly from the exactness in (c).
(d): O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free; the long exact sequence of 0 → O⁺ → O⁺ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (multiplication by ϖ) and (a). (e): M ⊗ O is a direct summand of Oⁿ.
acceptance: For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and O⁺(Y)^G = R⁺ (the Čech complex of the cover is the complex of inhomogeneous cochains).

In characteristic p, H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i ≥ 1 gives, with the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → 𝔽_p → O → O → 0, H^i(X_ét, 𝔽_p) = 0 for i ≥ 2 (used by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion).

For X = Spa(K, O_K), K a perfectoid field, H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is the Galois cohomology H^i(Gal(K̄/K), O_{K̄}) of the discrete module O_{K̄}; it is almost zero for i > 0 because each finite Galois L/K has L°a almost finite étale and almost faithfully flat over K°a (Tate's computation, recovered from almost purity).

nodes.title: ECD Theorem 6.3: the tilting equivalence of étale sites and the almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét
nodes.statement: (ECD Theorem 6.3, over an arbitrary perfectoid base.) Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭. (i) Tilting induces an equivalence of sites X_ét ≃ X♭_ét (and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét), functorial in X, preserving affinoid perfectoid objects, fibre products and coverings, identifying O⁺/ϖ with O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and inducing an equivalence of étale topoi (P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence). (ii) If X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and the R⁺-modules H^i(X_ét, O⁺) are almost zero for i > 0; moreover H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0, and the sheaf U ↦ O_U(U) on X_ét is a sheaf (P3/etale-almost-acyclicity). Here X_ét is the étale site of P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space (= A1's site of the underlying adic space).
hypotheses: X perfectoid; no base field; cohomology is sheaf cohomology on X_ét.
proofSteps: (i): P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence.
(ii): P3/etale-almost-acyclicity (a), (b); the sheaf property is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf via P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space.
The declaration bundles the two halves as ECD Theorem 6.3 and its consumers cite them.
acceptance: For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O_Y⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and (O_Y⁺(Y))^G = O_X⁺(X) (a special case of the Čech statement).

nodes.title: Affinoid perfectoid fields and (K, K⁺)-valued points of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: An affinoid perfectoid field is a pair (K, K⁺) of a perfectoid field K (a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field, ECD Definition 3.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) and an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K; equivalently K⁺ is a valuation subring with K°° ⊂ K⁺ ⊂ K° = O_K, so (K, K⁺) is a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) and Spa(K, K⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space. It is algebraically closed if K is. A morphism (K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺) is a morphism of Huber pairs (a continuous field homomorphism carrying K⁺ into L⁺), also called an extension of affinoid perfectoid fields. The points of Spa(K, K⁺) are the valuation subrings V with K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°; they form a chain under inclusion, K⁺ is the unique closed point, K° is the unique rank-one point, every point is a specialization of K° and a generalization of K⁺, and the quasicompact open subsets are the Spa(K, K'⁺) for valuation subrings K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K°. For a perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) the set of (K, K⁺)-valued points is X(K, K⁺) := Hom_Perfd(Spa(K, K⁺), X); it is covariant in X, contravariant in (K, K⁺), and carries the closed-point map X(K, K⁺) → |X|. For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X(K, K⁺) is the set of morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺), and the closed-point map sends φ to spaComap φ of the closed point.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; perfectoid fields are those of ECD Definition 3.6, of either characteristic, with no base field.
K⁺ is a valuation subring. Open integrally closed subrings that are not valuation subrings (they occur in ECD Lemma 9.9) do not give affinoid perfectoid fields.
proofSteps: Open and bounded subrings of K lie between K°° and K°: an open integrally closed subring contains every topologically nilpotent element (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`) and a bounded one consists of power-bounded elements; conversely K°° is open and K° bounded because K is a nonarchimedean field.

Points of Spa(K, K⁺): a continuous valuation v with v ≤ 1 on K⁺ has valuation ring V ⊇ K⁺; if x ∈ V had |x|_K > 1 then x⁻¹ would be topologically nilpotent, so v(x⁻¹) < 1 by continuity, contradicting v(x) ≤ 1; hence V ⊆ K°. Overrings of the valuation ring K⁺ are its localizations at primes, hence a chain. Quasicompact opens are the rational subsets {|f| ≤ 1}, f ∈ K, which are the Spa(K, K⁺[f]) (anchor Layer 2 rational subsets).

The description of X(K, K⁺) for affinoid X is the universal property of affinoid adic spaces (morphisms W → Spa(R, R⁺) are the morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_W(W), O_W⁺(W)); requested from the anchor, Layer 5) applied to W = Spa(K, K⁺), with O(W) = K and O⁺(W) = K⁺.
acceptance: Spa(K, K°) is a single point, and for X affinoid perfectoid X(K, K°) is the set of continuous ring maps R → K with R⁺ → K°.
If K⁺ has rank two, Spa(K, K⁺) has exactly two points: the open rank-one point K° and the closed point K⁺.

nodes.title: Morphisms of perfectoid spaces are generalizing and spectral
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (more generally of analytic adic spaces). Then the continuous map |f| : |Y| → |X| is generalizing (Mathlib `GeneralizingMap`: for y ∈ Y and a generalization x' of f(y) there is a generalization y' of y with f(y') = x'), and it is spectral on spectral opens (for open affinoids V ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, V → U is a spectral map, Mathlib `IsSpectralMap`). Consequently the image of every morphism, and of every quasicompact open under a morphism, is stable under generalization, and the image of a quasicompact open is pro-constructible in any spectral open containing it.
hypotheses: X and Y are perfectoid spaces, so every point is analytic (every point of Spa of a Tate ring is analytic, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isAnalyticPoint_of_isTateRing`).
proofSteps: Generalizations of an analytic point: for y ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) with B Tate, the generalizations of y form a chain in bijection with the valuation subrings V of the completed residue field with K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° (vertical generalization; horizontal generalizations do not occur at analytic points). This description is requested from the anchor, Layer 2.

Lifting: with x = f(y), the field map K(x) → K(y) satisfies K(y)⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and K(y)° ∩ K(x) = K(x)°. A generalization x' of x is a valuation ring V' with K(x)⁺ ⊆ V' ⊆ K(x)°; it is the localization of K(x)⁺ at a prime 𝔭. The extension K(x)⁺ ⊆ K(y)⁺ of valuation rings is local, so Spec K(y)⁺ → Spec K(x)⁺ is a surjective order-preserving map of chains; let 𝔮 be the largest prime over 𝔭. It contains 𝔪(K(y)°), which lies over 𝔪(K(x)°) ⊆ 𝔭, so V := K(y)⁺_𝔮 satisfies K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° and V ∩ K(x) = V'. The point y' given by V is the required lift.

Spectrality: the preimage of a rational subset under a morphism of affinoid adic spaces is rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`), and quasicompact opens of an affinoid are finite unions of rational subsets; for spectral (qcqs) opens cover by finitely many affinoids.

Images: a generalizing map has generalization-stable image; the image of a pro-constructible subset under a spectral map of spectral spaces is pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets).
acceptance: The inclusion of a rational subset U ⊆ X is generalizing: U is open, hence stable under generalization.
For the map Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, K⁺) induced by an extension of perfectoid fields, the image is the rank-one point, which is stable under generalization but not closed when K⁺ ≠ K°.

nodes.title: Quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: A perfectoid space X is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated) if |X| is quasicompact (resp. a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`). A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is quasicompact if f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every quasicompact open U ⊆ |X|, equivalently for every open affinoid U ⊆ X; it is quasiseparated if the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal` in the category of perfectoid spaces, whose fibre products are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is quasicompact; qcqs means both. Equivalently, f is quasiseparated if and only if for every open affinoid U ⊆ X and all open affinoids V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) the intersection V ∩ W is quasicompact; if X is affinoid (or quasiseparated), f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is quasiseparated. By ECD Proposition 8.3 these agree with the topos-theoretic notions of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos for the sheaves represented by perfectoid spaces.
hypotheses: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), and open affinoids of a fibre product V ×_U W are the affinoid perfectoid spaces given by the P2 affinoid formula.
proofSteps: Quasicompactness is local on the target and testable on affinoids because affinoids form a basis of quasicompact opens stable under finite intersection inside an affinoid (rational subsets, anchor Layer 2).

Diagonal criterion: the open subsets V ×_U W (V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) affinoid, U ⊆ X affinoid) cover Y ×_X Y and are affinoid; Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_U W) = V ∩ W; so Δ_f is quasicompact if and only if all V ∩ W are quasicompact.
If X is quasiseparated the same criterion shows that f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is.
acceptance: Every morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is qcqs.
The inclusion of the open unit disc (the union of the rational subsets {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|}) into the perfectoid closed unit disc is quasiseparated but not quasicompact.
