nodes.title: Injections of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for every perfectoid space Z the map f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective (ECD Definition 5.1). It suffices to test affinoid perfectoid Z, because two morphisms Z → Y that agree on an open affinoid cover of Z agree. In the category Perfd of perfectoid spaces this says exactly that f is a monomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`), and, fibre products existing in Perfd (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), it is equivalent to the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y being an isomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`). Injections are not determined by |f| being injective: the characterisations on points, residue fields and underlying spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria.
hypotheses: Perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (ECD Definition 3.19): adic spaces of the anchor, locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring; Perfd is a full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces.
proofSteps: Reduction to affinoid Z: morphisms of adic spaces are determined locally on the source (anchor Layer 5 gluing).
Mono ⇔ Δ_f iso is Mathlib `pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff` applied in Perfd, which has pullbacks by P2.
acceptance: Rational open immersions U ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺) are injections (universal property of rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`).
Diagonals are injections, being split monomorphisms (Mathlib instance `IsSplitMono (pullback.diagonal f)`).

nodes.title: Almost integral perfectoid criterion: a ϖ-complete ring with almost bijective Frobenius gives a perfectoid Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let A⁺ be a ring and ϖ ∈ A⁺ a non-zero-divisor such that (i) ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} ∈ A⁺ and ϖ^p divides p in A⁺; (ii) A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete and separated; (iii) the Frobenius Φ : A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ, x ↦ x^p, is an almost isomorphism for the basic setup (A⁺, 𝔪) with 𝔪 = ⋃ₙ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup): its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Let A := A⁺[1/ϖ], topologized so that A⁺ is open with the ϖ-adic topology. Then A is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 with pseudouniformizer ϖ; its power-bounded subring is A° = A⁺_* := {x ∈ A : ϖ^{1/pⁿ}x ∈ A⁺ for all n}; A⁺ ⊆ A° and A°/A⁺ is almost zero; the integral closure of A⁺ in A is a ring of integral elements; and Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is an isomorphism. This is the Tate-ring form of Sch12 Lemma 5.6 (stated there over a perfectoid field K for perfectoid K°ᵃ-algebras).
hypotheses: No base field: A⁺ is an arbitrary ring; in characteristic p the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous.
Almost mathematics is taken for the idempotent ideal 𝔪 = ⋃ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (flat because ϖ is a non-zero-divisor).
proofSteps: A⁺_* = (A⁺ᵃ)_* is the module of almost elements; for the ϖ-torsion-free A⁺ it is {x ∈ A : εx ∈ A⁺ for all ε ∈ 𝔪}, ϖ-torsion free, ϖ-adically complete, and almost equal to A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion; Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii),(iv)).
Φ : A⁺_*/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺_*/ϖ is injective: if x ∈ A⁺_* and x^p ∈ ϖA⁺_*, almost injectivity gives ε^{1/p}x ∈ ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* for all ε ∈ 𝔪, so x ∈ (ϖ^{1/p}A⁺)_* = ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).
If x ∈ A and x^p ∈ A⁺_* then x ∈ A⁺_* (Sch12 Lemma 5.7): with y = ϖ^{k/p}x ∈ A⁺_*, injectivity of Φ lowers k by one while k ≥ 1, using that A⁺_* has no ϖ-torsion.

A° = A⁺_*: elements of A⁺_* are power-bounded; if x is power-bounded then εx is topologically nilpotent for ε ∈ 𝔪, so (εx)^{p^N} ∈ A⁺_* for large N, hence εx ∈ A⁺_* by the previous step, for all ε; hence x ∈ A⁺_*. In particular A° ⊆ ϖ⁻¹A⁺ is bounded, so A is uniform, complete and Tate with pseudouniformizer ϖ.

Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is surjective: it is almost surjective, so for x ∈ A° there is y ∈ A° with ϖ^{1/p}x ≡ y^p mod ϖA°; z := y/ϖ^{1/p²} has z^p ∈ A° and x ≡ z^p mod ϖ^{(p−1)/p}A°, hence z ∈ A° by the root lemma, and the residual error lies in 𝔪A°, which gives surjectivity modulo ϖ (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).

ϖ^p divides p in A°, and Φ is an isomorphism A°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A°/ϖ; replacing ϖ by ϖ^{1/p} is harmless, so A satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). The integral closure of A⁺ is open (it contains A⁺) and contained in A° (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`).
acceptance: For a perfectoid field C with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting p-power roots and A⁺ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective, and A = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid with A° = A⁺.
Non-example: for A⁺ = O_C⟨T⟩ Frobenius modulo ϖ^{1/p} is not almost surjective (no element ϖ^εT is a p-th power modulo ϖ), and C⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid.
The ϖ-adic completion of a filtered colimit of rings of integral elements of perfectoid pairs satisfies the hypotheses (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets).

nodes.title: Integral perfectoid criterion: integral perfectoid rings give perfectoid Tate rings (compatible-root annuli)
nodes.statement: Let R₀ be a ring and π ∈ R₀ a non-zero-divisor with π^p | p such that R₀ is π-adically complete, and suppose that R₀ is an integral perfectoid ring (BMS1 Definition 3.5, PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings) — for instance because Frobenius R₀/π → R₀/π^p is an isomorphism (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)). Then R := R₀[1/π], with the π-adic topology on R₀, is a complete Tate ring that is perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1), R₀ ⊆ R°, πR° ⊆ R₀, and after replacing π by a unit multiple admitting compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9) the cokernel R°/R₀ is killed by every π^{1/pⁿ}. The criterion is about the pair (R₀, π): it is never inferred from the name of an integral model. Application (compatible-root period annuli): for a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{>0}, the ϖ-adic completion A⁺ of R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) satisfies the hypotheses (it is free over R° on the monomials T^α, S^β modulo the relations, and Frobenius is bijective from A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} to A⁺/ϖ on that basis; for a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊊ R° in place of R° it is almost bijective and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion applies), so the annulus ring A⁺[1/ϖ] = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^a/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; the same holds after base change of an annulus along a compatible-root extension, which is how perfectoidness of the chart cover of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 is checked. Without the roots of T the Frobenius criterion fails and R⟨T, ϖ^a/T⟩ is not perfectoid.
hypotheses: π is a non-zero-divisor; without this the localization loses information and the conclusion fails.

Integral perfectoid is the BMS1 notion (π-adically complete for some π with π^p | p, Frobenius surjective on R₀/p, ker θ principal), owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; its comparison with rings of integral elements of perfectoid Tate rings (BMS1 Lemma 3.20) is PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison.
proofSteps: BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i),(ii) (inside PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison): an integral perfectoid R₀ has Φ : R₀/π → R₀/π^p an isomorphism, and conversely a π-torsion-free π-complete R₀ with that isomorphism is integral perfectoid.
Replace π by uπ, u ∈ R₀^×, with compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9, 'moreover' part).

Apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion with A⁺ = R₀ and ϖ = π: Frobenius is bijective, a fortiori almost bijective; this gives R perfectoid, R° = (R₀)_* and R°/R₀ almost zero; since π·(R₀)_* ⊆ R₀ one gets πR° ⊆ R₀ (BMS1 Lemma 3.21, whose proof is 'as in Sch12 Lemma 5.6').

Annuli: R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ}) is a free R°-module on the monomials T^α (α ≥ 0) and S^β (β > 0) in ℤ[1/p], hence ϖ-torsion free; Frobenius sends c·T^α to c^p·T^{pα}, and R°/ϖ^{1/p} → R°/ϖ is bijective (ECD Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2 for the pseudouniformizer ϖ^{1/p}), so Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective.
acceptance: Perfectoid annulus: for C a perfectoid field and a = 1, R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{1/pⁿ}) gives the perfectoid ring of the annulus |ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1, which is the rational localization C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
BMS1 Example 3.6: ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is integral perfectoid, and ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/p] is perfectoid (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).

Non-example: R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) has compatible roots of T, but Φ : R₀/ϖ^{1/p} → R₀/ϖ kills the nonzero class of T^{1/p}; R₀[1/ϖ] = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) is not reduced, hence not perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).

nodes.title: The perfectoid space attached to a filtered intersection of rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space, ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformizer with ϖ^p | p admitting compatible p-power roots (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), and 𝒰 a nonempty family of rational subsets of X that is filtered (for U, V ∈ 𝒰 some W ∈ 𝒰 lies in U ∩ V); put T := ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U ⊆ |X|. Let S⁺_𝒰 be the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U) and S_𝒰 := S⁺_𝒰[1/ϖ], topologized by the ϖ-adic topology on S⁺_𝒰, and let ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 := Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) → X be induced by the compatible maps O_X(U) → S_𝒰. Then: (a) S_𝒰 is a perfectoid Tate ring, S⁺_𝒰 is a ring of integral elements, S⁺_𝒰 ⊆ S_𝒰° with almost zero cokernel, S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ = colim_U O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ, and each O_X(U) → S_𝒰 has dense image; (b) |ι_𝒰| is a homeomorphism of |Z_𝒰| onto T with its subspace topology, and T is pro-constructible and stable under generalization; (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_𝒰 if and only if |g|(|W|) ⊆ T, and then uniquely; in particular ι_𝒰 is an injection and Z_𝒰 is the limit of the U ∈ 𝒰 in the category of perfectoid spaces; (d) Z_𝒰 depends, up to unique isomorphism over X, only on the subset T. The residue-field points of ECD Example 5.2 and the universal Zariski closed subspaces of Scholze's torsion paper Lemma II.2.2 are the cases 𝒰 = {rational neighbourhoods of x} and 𝒰 = {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; the family 𝒰 consists of rational subsets and is filtered; no base field.
Completions are ϖ-adic; they do not depend on the choice of ϖ among pseudouniformizers of R.
proofSteps: Valuative description of the colimit: s ∈ O_X(U₀) (U₀ ∈ 𝒰) has image in colim O⁺ iff |s| ≤ 1 on T. Indeed {x ∈ U₀ : |s(x)| ≤ 1} is a rational subset, O⁺_X(U) = {f : |f| ≤ 1 on U} (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one` on O(U)), and by compactness of the constructible topology (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets) T ⊆ V for a quasicompact open V forces some U ∈ 𝒰 to lie in V.

Frobenius: each (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is a perfectoid pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so Φ : O⁺(U)/ϖ^{1/p} → O⁺(U)/ϖ is an almost isomorphism (bijective on O(U)°, and O(U)°/O⁺(U) is almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii), PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). Filtered colimits and ϖ-adic completion preserve almost isomorphisms modulo ϖ, ϖ-torsion freeness and ϖ^p | p; apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion to A⁺ = S⁺_𝒰.

Points: a point z of Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) restricts to each O(U) with |O⁺(U)| ≤ 1, hence (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`) to a point of every U, so to a point of T; conversely a point x ∈ T defines compatible continuous valuations on the O(U), bounded by 1 on colim O⁺(U), which extend continuously to the completion. The resulting continuous bijection |Z_𝒰| → T is spectral and generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), T is spectral as a pro-constructible subset (anchor Layer 1.3), so it is a homeomorphism (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient).

Ring of integral elements: S⁺_𝒰 is open; if s ∈ S_𝒰 is integral over S⁺_𝒰 then |s| ≤ 1 on Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰); approximating s modulo ϖS⁺_𝒰 by s₀ in the image of some O(U) gives |s₀| ≤ 1 on T, so s₀, and then s, lies in S⁺_𝒰 by the valuative description.

Universal property: for W = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid with |g| ⊆ T, g factors uniquely through every U ∈ 𝒰 (rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), the compatible maps O⁺(U) → A⁺ extend uniquely to S⁺_𝒰 because A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete; general W by gluing (anchor Layer 5). Uniqueness makes ι_𝒰 an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Hom(W, Z_𝒰) = lim Hom(W, U).
Independence: the universal property depends only on T.
acceptance: 𝒰 = {U}: Z_𝒰 = U.
𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of a point x: Z_𝒰 = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (ECD Example 5.2).
If T = ∅ then S_𝒰 = 0 and Z_𝒰 is empty.

nodes.title: The completed residue field point i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid space X and a point x ∈ X, the completed residue field K(x) with its open and bounded valuation subring K(x)⁺ is an affinoid perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), and there is a canonical morphism i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X sending the closed point to x: on an affinoid perfectoid neighbourhood U = Spa(R, R⁺) of x it is given by (R, R⁺) → (K(x), K(x)⁺), independently of U. Moreover (ECD Example 5.2): (a) i_x is isomorphic over U to the pro-rational subspace ι_𝒰 for 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x in U (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets), so K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V) and K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ; (b) i_x is an injection and |i_x| is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of x; (c) every (K, K⁺)-valued point φ of X whose closed point maps to x factors uniquely as φ = i_x ∘ φ' with φ' : Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) given by a morphism of affinoid perfectoid fields; (d) for f : Y → X and y ∈ Y with f(y) = x, f ∘ i_y = i_x ∘ Spa(K(x) → K(y)).
hypotheses: X is a perfectoid space; x is any point (not necessarily of rank one).
proofSteps: Independence of U: two affinoid neighbourhoods contain a common rational neighbourhood, and restriction maps are compatible with the maps to K(x) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields).

(a),(b): the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods of x is the set of generalizations of x (in a spectral space the generalizations of x are the intersection of its quasicompact open neighbourhoods); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets, whose ring S⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim O⁺(V), which is K(x)⁺ (ECD Example 5.2).

(c): φ maps |Spa(K, K⁺)| into the generalizations of x (the closed point goes to x, every point of Spa(K, K⁺) generalizes the closed point, and continuous maps preserve specialization), so it factors uniquely through i_x by the universal property of (a); the factorization is a morphism (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) because both are affinoid.
(d) follows from the construction of completed residue fields and uniqueness in (c).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x its closed point, i_x is the identity.
For the Gauss point η of the perfectoid closed unit disc over a perfectoid field C, K(η) is the completion of C(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm and K(η)⁺ = K(η)°.

nodes.title: A qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated perfectoid space with a unique closed point x. Then i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X is an isomorphism; in particular X is affinoid, O_X(X) = K(x) and O⁺_X(X) = K(x)⁺.
hypotheses: X qcqs (|X| is then a spectral space, being quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally spectral).
proofSteps: In the spectral space |X| every point specializes to a closed point, which is x; so every open neighbourhood of x is all of X.
An affinoid open neighbourhood U of x therefore equals X, so X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid, and every rational neighbourhood of x is X.
By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (a), K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺(V) = R⁺, hence K(x)⁺ = R⁺, K(x) = R and i_x is the identity.

nodes.title: Points of fibre products of perfectoid spaces surject onto compatible pairs
nodes.statement: Let Y₁ → X ← Y₂ be morphisms of perfectoid spaces and W = Y₁ ×_X Y₂ their fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then |W| → |Y₁| ×_{|X|} |Y₂| is surjective, and it is spectral on spectral opens. Consequently, for points y₁ ∈ Y₁, y₂ ∈ Y₂ with the same image x ∈ X there are an affinoid perfectoid field (L, L⁺) and (L, L⁺)-valued points ỹ_i ∈ Y_i(L, L⁺) whose closed points map to y_i and whose images in X(L, L⁺) agree: take w ∈ W over (y₁, y₂), (L, L⁺) = (K(w), K(w)⁺) and ỹ_i = pr_i ∘ i_w.
hypotheses: Fibre products are those of Perfd (the uniform completion of the completed tensor product on affinoids).
proofSteps: Reduce to affinoid X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺) containing y_i (open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products).

W = Spa(D, D⁺) with D the uniform completion of B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ (P2 affinoid formula); uniformization does not change the adic spectrum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d)), and the adic spectrum of a completion is that of the uncompleted pair.

Amalgamation: there is a valuation v on B₁ ⊗_A B₂ restricting to y₁ and y₂ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation); restricting v to the convex subgroup generated by the value groups of y₁, y₂ gives a continuous valuation bounded by 1 on the image of B₁⁺ ⊗ B₂⁺, hence on its integral closure, as in the proof of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points.
Spectrality: preimages of rational subsets are rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`).
The (L, L⁺)-points: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection applied to w.

nodes.title: Every affinoid perfectoid field embeds into an algebraically closed one, and (K, K⁺)-points are detected there
nodes.statement: Let (K, K⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid field. (a) Let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of K and C⁺ ⊆ C° the preimage of a valuation subring of the residue field of C° dominating the image of K⁺. Then C is an algebraically closed perfectoid field, (C, C⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid field, K → C is a morphism (K, K⁺) → (C, C⁺), and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺. (b) The induced map π : Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) sends the closed point to the closed point. (c) For every perfectoid space Y the restriction map Y(K, K⁺) → Y(C, C⁺), φ ↦ φ ∘ π, is injective. In particular a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is injective on (K, K⁺)-points for all affinoid perfectoid fields as soon as it is injective on (C, C⁺)-points for all algebraically closed ones.
hypotheses: No assumption on the characteristic of K.
proofSteps: C is perfectoid: its value group is divisible, it is not discretely valued, and Frobenius is surjective on C°/p because every element of the ring of integers of the algebraic closure has a p-th root (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition).

C is algebraically closed: in characteristic 0 by Mathlib `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange` applied to the dense algebraic closure; in characteristic p this is the classical continuity-of-roots argument (Krasner), not covered by that Mathlib lemma (recorded gap).

C⁺: K⁺ is the preimage of a valuation ring k⁺ of the residue field k = K°/K°°; the residue field k_C of C° is an algebraic closure of k; a valuation subring k_C⁺ of k_C dominating the local ring of the integral closure of k⁺ exists (Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`), and k_C⁺ ∩ k = k⁺ because valuation rings are maximal for domination; put C⁺ = preimage of k_C⁺. It contains C°°, so it is open and bounded.
(b): the closed point of Spa(C, C⁺) is C⁺ and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺.

(c): if φ ∘ π = ψ ∘ π then φ and ψ send the closed point to the same y (by (b)), so both factor through i_y (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)) by morphisms (K(y), K(y)⁺) → (K, K⁺) whose composites with the injective map K → C agree; hence φ = ψ.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed) and K⁺ = K°, C = ℂ_p and C⁺ = O_{ℂ_p}.
If K⁺ has rank two, C⁺ has rank two and π is a bijection on closed points and on rank-one points.

nodes.title: Completed tensor products over a nonarchimedean field preserve kernels and strictness
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value (an analytic field) and V, W, X Banach K-modules, with ⊗̂_K the completed projective tensor product. (a) V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective. (b) For a bounded K-linear f : V → W with f_X := f ⊗̂ id_X : V ⊗̂_K X → W ⊗̂_K X, the natural map ker(f) ⊗̂_K X → ker(f_X) is a bijection. (c) If f is strict then so is f_X. Consequently, for an isometric embedding K → L of analytic fields and every Banach K-module V, the map V → L ⊗̂_K V is injective; in particular L ⊗̂_K V = 0 implies V = 0.
hypotheses: K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; Banach modules are complete normed K-vector spaces.
proofSteps: Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 2.2.9: all three parts reduce to Banach modules containing dense subspaces of countable dimension; there (a) follows from Schauder bases of V and W, and (b), (c) from a Schauder basis of X ([Ked10, Lemma 1.3.11], unread; the reduction to countable type is recorded as a gap).
Consequence: apply (b) to the inclusion K → L (injective and strict) tensored with V: the kernel of V = K ⊗̂_K V → L ⊗̂_K V is 0 ⊗̂_K V = 0.
acceptance: For V finite-dimensional over K, V ⊗̂_K X = V ⊗_K X and (b) is the exactness of V ⊗_K − over a field.
For a closed subspace V' ⊆ V, V' ⊗̂_K X → V ⊗̂_K X is injective with closed image.

nodes.title: A map of perfectoid fields that is injective on geometric points is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let K → L be a continuous homomorphism of perfectoid fields (it is injective and, after normalisation, isometric). Suppose that for every algebraically closed perfectoid field C, any two continuous homomorphisms L → C that agree on K are equal; equivalently Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is injective on (C, O_C)-valued points. Then K → L is an isomorphism. The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is required for all perfectoid fields C instead of algebraically closed ones.
hypotheses: Both fields perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.6), of the same characteristic.
proofSteps: D := L ⊗̂_K L is a perfectoid Tate ring, already uniform before any uniformization (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; KL15 Proposition 3.6.11 for ℚ_p-algebras; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).

For a ∈ L the element a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a maps to 0 in K(z) for every rank-one point z of Spa(D, D°): K(z) is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), it embeds into an algebraically closed perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), and the two composites L → C agree on K.

Hence its spectral seminorm, the maximum over the Gel'fand spectrum, i.e. over the rank-one points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm), vanishes, and it is 0 because D is uniform. So the multiplication D → L, whose kernel is topologically generated by these elements, is an isomorphism, and inl : L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism.

With V := L/K (a K-Banach space, K being closed in L), the strict exact sequence 0 → K → L → V → 0 stays strict exact after L ⊗̂_K − (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel (b), (c)); as L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism, V ⊗̂_K L = 0, hence V = 0 and K = L.
acceptance: For a nontrivial finite separable extension L/K, the hypothesis fails: two distinct K-embeddings L → C exist.
For K → K the hypothesis holds trivially and the conclusion is the identity.

nodes.title: (K, K⁺)-points of a map that is injective on points with isomorphic rank-one residue fields
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is injective and, for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x, the map of completed residue fields K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism. Then for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective, and its image consists of the φ whose closed point maps into f(|Y|).
hypotheses: X, Y perfectoid spaces; the hypothesis is condition (iii) of ECD Proposition 5.3.
proofSteps: Every φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) factors uniquely through i_x, x = image of the closed point (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)); replace X by X' := Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by Y' := Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

The hypothesis passes to Y' → X': Y' → Y is a base change of the injection i_x; along a chain of generalizations the completed residue fields coincide, and by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective each point of |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| has exactly one preimage, because the fibre product of two affinoid fields with the same field over a third is Spa of that field with the larger of the two valuation rings.

Now |Y'| ⊆ |X'| is stable under generalization (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing) inside the chain |X'|; every quasicompact open V ⊆ Y' has a unique closed point v, so V = Spa(K(v), K(v)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point) with K(v) = K(x); thus Y' is an increasing union of open subspaces Spa(K(x), K'⁺) ⊆ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points).

For each such open, Spa(K(x), K'⁺)(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)(K, K⁺) is injective with image the morphisms (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) carrying K'⁺ into K⁺, i.e. those whose closed point lands in Spa(K(x), K'⁺). Taking the union gives the claim for Y' → X', hence for Y → X.
acceptance: For f = i_x, (K, K⁺)-points of Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) are the (K, K⁺)-points of X whose closed point is a generalization of x.

sources.match: The core of the argument.

nodes.title: The stalk of O⁺/ϖ at x is K(x)⁺/ϖ
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space (more generally an analytic adic space), U ⊆ X open, ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(U) a pseudouniformizer and x ∈ U. The natural map O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺ has dense image, its kernel I satisfies I = ϖI, and the induced map O⁺_{X,x}/ϖ → K(x)⁺/ϖ is an isomorphism. Consequently the stalk at x of the sheaf O⁺_X/ϖ is K(x)⁺/ϖ.
hypotheses: O⁺_X(V) = {f ∈ O_X(V) : |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ V} (anchor Layer 3.3).
proofSteps: Dense image: the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x} is dense in K(x), and O⁺_{X,x} maps onto a dense subring of K(x)⁺ (completed residue field construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). Since ϖK(x)⁺ is open, O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺/ϖ is surjective.
Kernel: if f ∈ O⁺_X(V) has f(x) = 0 then V' := {y ∈ V : |f(y)| ≤ |ϖ(y)|} is a rational neighbourhood of x on which f/ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(V') with (f/ϖ)(x) = 0; so I = ϖI.
Injectivity modulo ϖ: if g ∈ O⁺_{X,x} maps into ϖK(x)⁺, lift the quotient to h ∈ O⁺_{X,x}; then g − ϖh ∈ I = ϖI.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x the closed point, O⁺_{X,x} = K⁺ and the lemma is trivial.

nodes.title: A homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue pairs is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is a homeomorphism and, for every y ∈ Y with x = f(y), the map (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K(y), K(y)⁺) is an isomorphism of affinoid perfectoid fields. Then f is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: No quasicompactness is assumed: over an open affinoid U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to U, hence qcqs.
proofSteps: Work over a rational subset U ⊆ X with pseudouniformizer ϖ; put V = f⁻¹(U). By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer the map of sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖ) on |U| is an isomorphism on stalks (f is a homeomorphism), hence an isomorphism; by dévissage along 0 → O⁺/ϖ^{n−1} → O⁺/ϖⁿ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free) so is O⁺_X/ϖⁿ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ).

Taking sections: O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity), and O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) is injective; comparing through the isomorphism H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) ≅ H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) shows that O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ is an almost isomorphism.

Both O⁺_X(U) and O⁺_Y(V) are ϖ-adically complete (V is covered by finitely many affinoids); passing to the limit (the lim and lim¹ of almost zero systems are almost zero) and inverting ϖ gives O_X(U) ≅ O_Y(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

The valuations at y and f(y) agree by hypothesis, O⁺ = {|·| ≤ 1} on both sides, so f is an isomorphism of structure sheaves compatible with the stalk valuations over the homeomorphism |f|, i.e. an isomorphism in the anchor's category of adic spaces (anchor Layers 3.4 and 5).
acceptance: The identity of any perfectoid space.
Non-example: Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite extension L ≠ K is a homeomorphism of one-point spaces but K → L is not an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps: bijectivity on points and on (C, C⁺)-points
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated morphism of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps). The following are equivalent: (i) f is an isomorphism; (ii) |f| : |Y| → |X| is bijective and for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x the map K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism; (iii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is a bijection; (iv) for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺) the map Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺) is a bijection. (ECD Lemma 5.4.)
hypotheses: f quasicompact and quasiseparated; this is used in (ii)+(iii) ⇒ (i) to make |f| a spectral map of spectral spaces over an affinoid.
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii), (iii), (iv) are clear; (iii) ⇒ (iv) is trivial.

(ii) ⇒ (iii): a (K, K⁺)-point of X with closed point x factors through i_x (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); replace X by Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by the base change. Then Y has a unique closed point y, so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point); K(x) = K(y) by (ii), and bijectivity of |f| forces K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.

(iii) ⇒ (ii): it suffices that Y ×_X Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) is an isomorphism; (iii) gives a unique section; i_y for its image y still satisfies (iii), so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺), and K(x) → K(y) → K(x) composing to the identity forces K(y) = K(x) and K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.

(iv) ⇒ (ii): |f| is surjective (extend (K(x), K(x)⁺) to an algebraically closed (C, C⁺) with C⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and lift, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field); |f| is injective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective gives two (L, L⁺)-points with equal image, extended to (C, C⁺)); for rank-one y ↦ x, Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (C, O_C)-points because f and i_y are, so K(x) = K(y) by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity. (ECD argues instead by Galois equivariance; see sourceIssues.)

(ii) + (iii) ⇒ (i): reduce to X affinoid, so Y is qcqs; |f| is a bijective, generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), spectral map of spectral spaces, hence a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient) and a homeomorphism; the residue pairs agree by the proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii), so f is an isomorphism by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs.
acceptance: ECD Lemma 7.19: a qcqs map to a strictly totally disconnected space that is a bijective injection is an isomorphism.

Quasicompactness is needed: for an infinite profinite set S and X = S × Spa(C, O_C) = Spa(C⁰(S, C), C⁰(S, O_C)), the map Y = ⊔_{s∈S} Spa(C, O_C) → X is bijective on underlying sets and on all (K, K⁺)-points (Spa(K, K⁺) is connected) but is not an isomorphism; it is not quasicompact.
A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is qcqs and bijective on points but fails (ii) and (iv).

nodes.title: Characterisations of injections of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces); (ii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺), Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective; (ii') the same for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺); (iii) |f| is injective and K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x; (iv) |f| is injective and, for every perfectoid space Z, Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) ×_{C⁰(|Z|, |X|)} C⁰(|Z|, |Y|) is a bijection, i.e. f is final among morphisms g : Z → X for which |g| factors through a continuous map |Z| → |Y|. In particular injections Y → X are determined, up to unique isomorphism over X, by the continuous injection |Y| → |X|; |Y| need not carry the subspace topology of |X|. (ECD Proposition 5.3; (ii') is Berkeley Lectures Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3).)
hypotheses: No quasicompactness hypothesis.
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (ii') are clear; (ii') ⇒ (ii) is PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field (c); (iv) ⇒ (i) is clear.
(ii) ⇒ (iii), injectivity of |f|: if y₁ ≠ y₂ map to x, base change along i_x and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective give (L, L⁺)-points ỹ₁ ≠ ỹ₂ with the same image.

(ii) ⇒ (iii), residue fields: for rank-one y ↦ x, g : Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (K, K⁺)-points because f and the injection i_y are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); conclude by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity.

(iii) ⇒ (iv): by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps, f_* is injective on (K, K⁺)-points with image the points whose closed point lies in f(|Y|). Given g : Z → X with |g| factoring continuously through |Y|, work locally on Z so that X, Y, Z are affinoid; the qcqs map Y ×_X Z → Z is then bijective on all (K, K⁺)-points, hence an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion), and its inverse gives the unique factorization; uniqueness glues.
Determination by |Y| → |X| is (iv).
acceptance: Rational open immersions and the residue-field points i_x satisfy (iii).
Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite separable extension L ≠ K fails (ii') and (iii) although |f| is injective.
ECD Lemma 9.9 applies (ii) together with the valuative criterion to recognise an injection.

nodes.title: Base change of injections, and the underlying space of a pulled-back injection
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be an injection of perfectoid spaces and X' → X any morphism, with base change f' : Y' = X' ×_X Y → X'. Then f' is an injection, and the natural map |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is a homeomorphism (the target with the fibre product topology). Moreover composites of injections are injections, and if g ∘ f is an injection then so is f. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (i).)
hypotheses: f an injection; X' → X arbitrary.
proofSteps: f' is an injection: monomorphisms are stable under pullback (in any category with pullbacks).

|Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is injective because |f| and |f'| are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii)); it is surjective and spectral (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective) and generalizing, both sides being generalization-stable subsets of |X'| (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing).
On spectral opens a bijective generalizing spectral map of spectral spaces is a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient), hence a homeomorphism.
Composition and cancellation are formal from the definition.
acceptance: For f a rational open immersion U ⊆ X, Y' is the preimage of U in X' with its open subspace structure.

nodes.title: Injections are exactly the universally injective maps
nodes.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if and only if it is universally injective: for every morphism X' → X the base change f' : X' ×_X Y → X' is injective on underlying spaces. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (ii).)
hypotheses: None beyond the existence of fibre products.
proofSteps: ⇒: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii).

⇐: given g : Z → X, pull back along g to reduce to Z = X; it suffices that f has at most one section. A section h is an injection (split monomorphism), and |X| → |Y| → |X| is the identity with both maps injective, so |h| is a homeomorphism with inverse |f|.
By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv) applied to h, every morphism into Y factors uniquely through h; so h is an isomorphism, f is its inverse, and the section is unique.
acceptance: A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is injective on points but not universally injective: its self-fibre product has two points over one.

nodes.title: Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces) and |f| : |Y| → |X| is a locally closed immersion, i.e. a topological embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`) with locally closed image (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed`). It is an open immersion (resp. closed immersion) if moreover |f| is an open (resp. closed) embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`) (ECD Definition 5.6). The definition is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent structure: an injection is determined by its image as a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)), so an immersion is determined up to unique isomorphism over X by the locally closed subset f(|Y|). These notions live in the namespace `PerfectoidSpace` and are compared with the anchor's open and closed immersions in PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/anchor-closed-immersion-comparison; closed immersions are strictly more general than Zariski closed immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed).
hypotheses: Topology of |Y| is its own spectral-space topology; the embedding condition says it is the subspace topology.
proofSteps: The definition is a conjunction of an injection with a topological condition; nothing to construct.
Uniqueness given the image: two immersions with the same image are injections with homeomorphic images, hence uniquely isomorphic over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).
acceptance: The inclusion of a rational subset, and of any open subset with its open subspace structure, is an open immersion.
Diagonals are immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

nodes.title: Immersions are stable under base change and composition; closed immersions are quasicompact
nodes.statement: Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces are stable under composition and under base change along arbitrary morphisms; for an immersion f : Y → X and X' → X, the image of the base change is the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|. Closed immersions are quasicompact; an immersion is a closed immersion if and only if its image is closed.
hypotheses: Morphisms of perfectoid spaces; fibre products as in P2.
proofSteps: Base change: by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition the base change f' is an injection and |Y'| ≅ |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|; since |Y| → |X| is an embedding, the fibre product topology is the subspace topology of the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|, which is locally closed (open, closed) when f(|Y|) is.

Composition: composites of injections are injections, and composites of embeddings with locally closed (open, closed) images have locally closed (open, closed) images (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed.image` for embeddings with locally closed range).
Quasicompactness: for a quasicompact open U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to the closed subset f(|Y|) ∩ U of U.

nodes.title: Open immersions of perfectoid spaces agree with the anchor's open immersions
nodes.statement: For a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: (a) f is an open immersion in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion; (b) f is an open immersion of adic spaces in the sense of the anchor (Layer 5.1): an isomorphism onto the open adic subspace X|_U, U = f(|Y|). Every open subset U ⊆ |X| underlies the perfectoid open subspace X|_U (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are open affinoid perfectoid subspaces, and the open immersions into X correspond bijectively to the open subsets of |X|.
hypotheses: Perfectoid spaces are adic spaces of the anchor (P2), so both notions apply to the same morphisms.
proofSteps: (b) ⇒ (a): X|_U → X is a monomorphism, because a morphism Z → X factors through X|_U if and only if |Z| lands in U, and then uniquely (anchor Layer 5.1 universal property of open subspaces); |X|_U| → |X| is an open embedding.
(a) ⇒ (b): X|_U → X is an injection with the same image and topology as f, so Y ≅ X|_U over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).
acceptance: For X = Spa(R, R⁺) and U = X(T/s) rational, (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is the rational localization and U → X is an open immersion in both senses.

nodes.title: Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions into affinoid perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. For an ideal I ⊆ R put V(I) := {x ∈ |X| : |g(x)| = 0 for all g ∈ I}; a subset Z ⊆ |X| is Zariski closed if Z = V(I) for some ideal I (Scholze torsion paper Definition II.2.1). A morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces is a Zariski closed immersion (defined by I) if f is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion) and f(|Z|) = V(I) (ECD Definition 5.7 (i)). Conventions: V(I) depends only on the closure of I and on its radical; V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F with U_F := {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F} rational, because I is an ideal and |ϖ(x)|ⁿ → 0 cofinally at every continuous valuation; V(I) is closed, pro-constructible and stable under generalization; V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J) and V(IJ) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J). Every Zariski closed subset is the image of exactly one Zariski closed immersion up to unique isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal). A Zariski closed immersion defined by I is not Spa(R/I, ·): the perfectoid structure on V(I) kills all compatible p-power roots.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; the global notion over non-affinoid X (locally Zariski closed) is PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding.
proofSteps: V(I) = ⋂ U_F: '⊆' is clear; if |g(x)| ≠ 0 for some g ∈ I then |ϖ^{−n}g(x)| > 1 for n large, as |ϖ(x)|ⁿ is eventually below every element of the value group of the continuous valuation x (anchor Layer 1.5), and ϖ^{−n}g ∈ I.

Closedness: V(I) = ⋂_{g∈I} {|g| = 0} and each {|g| = 0} is the complement of ⋃_n {|ϖⁿ| ≤ |g|}, a union of rational subsets; pro-constructibility and generalization-stability follow from the intersection formula.
The formula V(I) = image of the anchor's quotient pair: Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom` identifies {v : I ⊆ supp v} with V(I).
acceptance: For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V((T)) is the single point T = 0, and V((T − 1)) is the profinite set of classical points (T^{1/pⁿ}) = (ζ_{pⁿ}^a)_n, a ∈ ℤ_p, when C contains all p-power roots of unity.

nodes.title: Strongly Zariski closed immersions: surjective perfectoid quotients
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. A morphism f : Z → X is strongly Zariski closed if Z = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, f is induced by a morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with R → S surjective, and S⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺ in S (ECD Definition 5.7 (ii)). Equivalently (by the open mapping theorem, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), with I := ker(R → S) closed, (S, S⁺) is isomorphic to the anchor's quotient pair Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I` and R/I is perfectoid. The plus-ring clause is part of the definition: it is what makes a strongly Zariski closed map a closed immersion. Scholze's earlier Definition II.2.6 (R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective) omits it and is strictly weaker (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion).
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; S perfectoid is part of the data (a quotient R/I of a perfectoid R is perfectoid iff it is uniform, Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4(a)).
proofSteps: Equivalence with the quotient pair: R → S is a continuous surjection of complete Tate rings, hence open (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`), so R/I ≅ S topologically, I closed; the plus rings agree by definition of Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` (integral closure of the image of R⁺).
acceptance: The diagonal Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(S, S⁺) ×_{Spa(R, R⁺)} Spa(S, S⁺) of any map of affinoid perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

nodes.title: A surjection of perfectoid Tate rings is almost surjective on integral elements
nodes.statement: Let ψ : R → S be a surjective continuous homomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings and R⁺ ⊆ R°, S⁺ ⊆ S° rings of integral elements with ψ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺. Then R° → S° and R⁺ → S⁺ are almost surjective: for every pseudouniformizer ϖ of R admitting compatible p-power roots, S°/ψ(R°) and S⁺/ψ(R⁺) are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Equivalently, the quotient seminorm on S induced by the spectral norm of R equals the spectral norm of S. In particular, for a strongly Zariski closed Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺), R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.8).
hypotheses: R, S perfectoid Tate rings of any characteristic, not necessarily over a field or over ℚ_p.
proofSteps: Promote R and S to uniform Banach rings with their spectral norms; ψ is submetric, and by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`) the quotient norm is at most c times the spectral norm of S for some c > 1.

Improvement c ↦ c^{1/p}: given b ∈ S, lift b^p to a₀ with |a₀| ≤ c|b|^p, approximate a₀ by a sharp element ♯(x) with x ∈ R♭ and α(a₀ − ♯(x)) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a₀), |b|^p} for every α in the Gel'fand spectrum of R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (d); Kedlaya AWS (2.8.5.1), whose factor p⁻¹ is α(p) for the normalisation |p| = p⁻¹), and take a = ♯(x^{1/p}) (♯ is multiplicative, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map); the p-th power map estimate in a nonarchimedean field gives |b − ψ(a)| ≤ p^{−1/p}|b| at every point of the Gel'fand spectrum, the case β(p) = 0 being trivial (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.5, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(c)).
Iterating, the quotient norm is ≤ c^{1/pⁿ}·(spectral norm) for all n, so it equals the spectral norm; hence ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°) + ϖS° for all n, and completeness gives ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°).
For plus rings: ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S⁺ ⊆ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R°) ⊆ ψ(R°°) ⊆ ψ(R⁺).
acceptance: R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S = C (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0): R° → S° = O_C is surjective.
Characteristic p: a strict surjection of perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebras is almost optimal (KL15 Remark 3.1.6(a)).

nodes.title: Surjectivity and closed ideals with perfectoid quotient under tilting
nodes.statement: Let f : A → B be a continuous homomorphism of Tate rings with A perfectoid. (a) If B is uniform and f is surjective then B is perfectoid. (b) If B is perfectoid then f is surjective if and only if its tilt f♭ : A♭ → B♭ is surjective. (c) I ↦ I♭ := ker(A♭ → (A/I)♭) is a bijection between closed ideals I ⊆ A with A/I uniform (equivalently perfectoid) and closed perfect ideals of A♭; the inverse sends J to the closure of the ideal generated by {♯(x) : x ∈ J}. (d) A closed ideal I ⊆ A has A/I perfectoid if and only if I is the closure of the ideal generated by ♯(x^{1/pⁿ}) for x in some subset of A♭ and all n ≥ 0. (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4, Corollaries 2.4.5–2.4.6.)
hypotheses: Tate rings; A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1.
proofSteps: (a): a uniform ring with a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3(a) via Lemma 2.8.4).

(b) ⇐: θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺ is surjective, so the composite W(A♭) → W(B♭) → B is surjective when f♭ is (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel). ⇒: from PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings, lift ♯(b) with norm ≤ p^{1/2}|b| and correct by sharp approximations (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c), with (e) bounding ♯(b) − ♯(f♭(a)) − ♯(b − f♭(a))); iterating lifts every b ∈ B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.6, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(d)).

(c): by (b), closed ideals with perfectoid quotient correspond to surjections of perfectoid rings, hence to surjections of their tilts, i.e. to closed ideals of A♭ with perfect uniform quotient; a quotient of a perfect uniform ring by a closed perfect ideal is perfect and uniform (x̃^{1/p} lifts x^{1/p}), and conversely the kernel of a map to a perfect ring is perfect.
(d) follows from (c) with the subset {♯(x) : x ∈ I♭}.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I the closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0), A/I = K and I♭ is the closure of (T♭^{1/pⁿ}).

nodes.title: The universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and I ⊆ R an ideal. Let 𝒰_I := {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}, U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}, and let ι_I : Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) → X be the pro-rational subspace of 𝒰_I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets): S_I⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_F O⁺_X(U_F) and S_I = S_I⁺[1/ϖ]. Then: (a) Z_I is affinoid perfectoid and R → S_I has dense image; (b) |ι_I| is a homeomorphism onto V(I); (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_I if and only if g^*(h) = 0 in O_W(W) for all h ∈ I, if and only if |g| lands in V(I), and then uniquely; (d) ι_I is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion); (e) I^perf := ker(R → S_I) is a closed ideal containing I, equal to {h ∈ R : |h| = 0 on V(I)}, and Z_{I^perf} = Z_I; (f) Z_I depends only on V(I). In characteristic-free generality this is Scholze's Lemma II.2.2 with Remark II.2.3 (stated over a perfectoid field) and Bhatt's Proposition 9.4.1 (1)–(3). Surjectivity of R → S_I is ECD Theorem 5.8 and is imported (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed); it is not used in this construction.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid with a pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots; I arbitrary (not necessarily closed or finitely generated).
proofSteps: V(I) = ⋂ U_F (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion), and 𝒰_I is filtered (U_F ∩ U_G = U_{F∪G}); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets for (a), (b) and the topological universal property.

(c): if |g| lands in V(I), each g^*(h), h ∈ I, vanishes at every point of W; on an affinoid perfectoid open of W (uniform) its spectral seminorm, a maximum over points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm), is 0, so g^*(h) = 0. Conversely g^*(h) = 0 forces |h| = 0 on the image.
(d): ι_I is an injection with |ι_I| a homeomorphism onto the closed subset V(I), hence a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion), with image V(I).
(e), (f): h ∈ ker(R → S_I) iff |h| = 0 on |Z_I| = V(I) (S_I uniform); both Z_I and Z_{I^perf} are pro-rational subspaces with intersection V(I) = V(I^perf).
acceptance: For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I = (T): S_I = C, and I^perf is the closure of the ideal generated by all T^{1/pⁿ}.
For I = 0: Z_I = X; for I = R: Z_I = ∅.

nodes.title: A surjective perfectoid quotient is a Zariski closed immersion (the direction proved here)
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be affinoid perfectoid, ψ : R → S a surjective continuous homomorphism onto a perfectoid Tate ring, I := ker ψ and S⁺ the integral closure of ψ(R⁺). Then: (a) I is closed and (S, S⁺) ≅ Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`; (b) Z := Spa(S, S⁺) → X is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I, and |Z| → V(I) is a homeomorphism; (c) Z ≅ Z_I over X, so S = S_I and I = I^perf. Thus every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed. The converse is ECD Theorem 5.8, imported in PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed.
hypotheses: S perfectoid; ψ surjective.
proofSteps: (a): ψ is open by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), so S ≅ R/I topologically; I is closed as the kernel of a continuous map to a Hausdorff ring; S⁺ matches Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` by definition.

(b): maps W → Z from affinoid perfectoid W are morphisms (S, S⁺) → (O_W(W), O⁺_W(W)); as ψ is surjective they are determined by the composite with ψ, so Z → X is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces). |Z| → |X| is a closed embedding with image {v : I ⊆ supp v} = V(I) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`).
(c): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal.

nodes.title: Criteria for strong Zariski closedness in terms of almost surjectivity on plus rings
nodes.statement: Let f : Z = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces, ϖ a pseudouniformizer of R with compatible p-power roots, and let T⁺ denote the integral closure of the image of R⁺ in S. The following are equivalent: (a) f is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion); (b) R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective and S⁺ = T⁺; (c) R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ is almost surjective and S⁺ = T⁺. Scholze's Definition II.2.6 (R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective, with no condition on S⁺) is strictly weaker: Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ ⊊ R° satisfies it, but is not a closed immersion.
hypotheses: Z, X affinoid perfectoid.
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings.
(b) ⇒ (c) is clear.

(c) ⇒ (b): successive approximation, using that R⁺ and S⁺ are ϖ-adically complete and the exponents ε/2, ε/4, … sum to less than ε: ϖ^{ε/2}s = r₀ + ϖs₁, ϖ^{ε/4}s₁ = r₁ + ϖs₂, … converges to a lift of ϖ^ε s.
(b) ⇒ (a): ϖ^εS⁺ ⊆ image(R⁺) gives S = S⁺[1/ϖ] = image(R), so R → S is surjective, and S⁺ = T⁺ holds by hypothesis.

Non-example: R → R is surjective and R°/R⁺ is almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), while the image of Spa(R, R°) in Spa(R, R⁺) is the set {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ R°}, which is not closed when R⁺ ≠ R° (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).
acceptance: The diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces satisfies (a)–(c).

nodes.title: Base change of Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions
nodes.statement: Let Z → X be a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces, X' = Spa(R', R'⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) any morphism, and Z' = Z ×_X X' = Spa(S', S'⁺). (i) If Z → X is Zariski closed defined by I ⊆ R, then Z' → X' is Zariski closed defined by IR'; more precisely Z_I ×_X X' ≅ Z_{IR'} over X'. (ii) If Z → X is strongly Zariski closed, so is Z' → X', and with I⁺ := ker(R⁺ → S⁺), I'⁺ := ker(R'⁺ → S'⁺) the maps I⁺/ϖⁿ ⊗_{R⁺/ϖⁿ} R'⁺/ϖⁿ → I'⁺/ϖⁿ are almost surjective for all n ≥ 0. (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.9.)
hypotheses: Affinoid perfectoid spaces; fibre products as in P2.
proofSteps: (i): a morphism W → X' factors through Z_I ×_X X' iff W → X kills I iff W → X' kills IR' (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed (c)); both are Zariski closed by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal.

(ii): S'⁺/ϖ is almost isomorphic to S⁺/ϖ ⊗_{R⁺/ϖ} R'⁺/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii), reduced modulo ϖ), so R'⁺/ϖ → S'⁺/ϖ is almost surjective, R' → S' is surjective and S'⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R'⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion (c) ⇒ (a), after identifying S'⁺ with that integral closure through PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed and (i)).

Ideals: 0 → I⁺/ϖ → R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ → 0 is almost exact (S⁺ is ϖ-torsion free and R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings); tensoring with R'⁺/ϖ over R⁺/ϖ is right exact, which gives the almost surjectivity for n = 1, and dévissage gives all n.
acceptance: Restriction of a Zariski closed immersion to a rational subset U ⊆ X is Zariski closed in U, defined by I·O_X(U) (the case used in PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding).

nodes.title: Comparison with the anchor's closed immersions
nodes.statement: (a) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, a morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed if and only if it is isomorphic over X to the anchor's closed immersion Spa(Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) J) → Spa(R, R⁺) (anchor Layer 2.4 and Layer 5.1; Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient`) for a closed ideal J ⊆ R with R/J perfectoid; then J = ker(R → S). (b) For arbitrary X, a morphism of perfectoid spaces is a closed immersion in the anchor's sense (affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy) if and only if it is, locally on X, strongly Zariski closed; such a morphism is a closed immersion in the sense of ECD Definition 5.6 whose restrictions over open affinoids are Zariski closed. (c) The anchor's closed immersion defined by a closed ideal J of a perfectoid R need not have perfectoid source: for R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and J = (T), R/J is not reduced, whereas the Zariski closed subspace V(T) is Spa(C, O_C). (d) That every Zariski closed immersion into an affinoid is of the form (a) is ECD Theorem 5.8 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed).
hypotheses: Perfectoid spaces are adic spaces of the anchor (P2); the anchor's closed immersions are those of its Layer 5.1.
proofSteps: (a): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion (equivalence with the quotient pair) and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed.

(b): both notions are affinoid-local on X (anchor Layer 5.1 independence of the affinoid cover; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition for ECD closed immersions); combine with (a) on each affinoid.
(c): Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed for V(T).
acceptance: The diagonal of a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is an anchor closed immersion with perfectoid source.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and Zariski closed immersions are different notions
nodes.statement: (a) Every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed, and every Zariski closed immersion is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion). (b) The image of an immersion is stable under generalization, so a closed subset of |X| that is not (the closed point of Spa(K, K⁺) for K⁺ of rank two) is not the image of any immersion: the Zariski statements do not extend to arbitrary closed subsets. (c) A closed immersion need not be Zariski closed: for X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with C a perfectoid field and ϖ ∈ C a pseudouniformizer with compatible roots, the subset T := ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|} (the closed annulus {|T| = 1} together with the rank-two point y with |T(y)| = 1⁻) is the complement of the open unit disc, hence closed, and ι : Z_𝒰 → X for 𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}} (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets) is a closed immersion with image T; but T is not Zariski closed, since every g ∈ C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ vanishing on T vanishes at the Gauss point, hence is 0 (the Gauss norm is the spectral norm), while T ≠ X. (d) Equivalently, a closed immersion Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces does not force R → S to be surjective (Berkeley Lectures, remark after Definition 17.4.2).
hypotheses: Perfectoid spaces over no fixed base; C any perfectoid field in (c).
proofSteps: (b): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing; the closed point K⁺ has the generalization K°.

(c): T is an intersection of rational subsets, so ι is an injection with |ι| a homeomorphism onto T (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets); the complement of T is ⋃_n {|T| < |ϖ^{1/pⁿ}|}, a union of rational subsets, so T is closed and ι is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion).
(c), not Zariski closed: if T = V(I) then every g ∈ I vanishes at the Gauss point η ∈ T, whose value is the spectral (Gauss) norm of g, so I = 0 and V(I) = X ∋ 0 ∉ T.
(d): here S = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and R → S is not surjective (T⁻¹ is not in the image), matching Berkeley's remark.
acceptance: The closed point of Spa(K, K⁺) (rank two) is closed but not the image of an immersion; the closure of the annulus is the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski closed.

nodes.title: The diagonal of a morphism of perfectoid spaces is an immersion
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion). More precisely: (a) Δ_f is a split monomorphism, hence an injection; (b) for open affinoids V ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, the restriction V → V ×_U V is strongly Zariski closed: the multiplication map from the affinoid ring of V ×_U V onto O_Y(V) is surjective and O⁺_Y(V) is the integral closure of the image of the plus ring; (c) the open subsets V ×_U V cover an open W ⊆ |Y ×_X Y| containing Δ_f(|Y|), and Δ_f(|Y|) is closed in W, with |Δ_f| a homeomorphism onto its image. (ECD Proposition 5.9.)
hypotheses: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces (P2); on affinoids V ×_U V = Spa of the completed tensor product of O(V) with itself over O(U), which is already perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1).
proofSteps: (a): Mathlib instance `IsSplitMono (pullback.diagonal f)` and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces.

(b): the multiplication m satisfies m ∘ inl = id, so it is surjective and O⁺_Y(V) = m(inl(O⁺_Y(V))) is contained in the integral closure of m(plus ring), which is contained in O⁺_Y(V); hence V → V ×_U V is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion), so a Zariski closed, in particular closed, immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed).

(c): Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_U V) = V and Δ_f(|Y|) ∩ |V ×_U V| = Δ_f(|V|), which is closed in |V ×_U V| by (b); hence Δ_f(|Y|) is closed in W = ⋃ |V ×_U V| and locally closed in |Y ×_X Y|; pr₁ ∘ Δ_f = id shows that |Δ_f| is an embedding.
acceptance: For Y = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) over X = Spa(C, O_C), Δ_f is the Zariski closed immersion defined by (T^{1/pⁿ} ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) in C⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩; the single equation T − S cuts out the larger set where T^{1/pⁿ} and S^{1/pⁿ} differ by p-power roots of unity.
ECD Remark 7.9: Δ_f is therefore affinoid pro-étale locally.

nodes.title: Separated morphisms of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is separated if its diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion) (ECD Definition 5.10); it is quasiseparated if Δ_f is quasicompact (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps). In Mathlib's vocabulary, IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion on Perfd, the pattern of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`. Since Δ_f is always an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map), f is separated if and only if Δ_f(|Y|) is closed. The category Perfd has no final object, so separatedness is a relative notion.
hypotheses: Fibre products as in P2.
proofSteps: The definition applies the closed-immersion notion to Δ_f; the reformulation uses that immersions with closed image are closed immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).

nodes.title: Valuative criterion for separatedness of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) f is separated; (ii) |Δ_f| : |Y| → |Y ×_X Y| is a closed immersion of topological spaces; (iii) f is quasiseparated and for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) and every commutative square formed by a : Spa(K, O_K) → Y and b : Spa(K, K⁺) → X with f ∘ a = b ∘ j (j : Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺) the inclusion of the rank-one point) there is at most one c : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y with c ∘ j = a and f ∘ c = b. (ECD Proposition 5.11.)
hypotheses: No quasicompactness of f; quasiseparatedness appears in (iii).
proofSteps: (i) ⇔ (ii): Δ_f is an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map), so it is a closed immersion iff |Δ_f| is.

(ii) ⇒ (iii): closed immersions are quasicompact (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition), so f is quasiseparated. Two lifts give z : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y ×_X Y whose restriction to Spa(K, O_K) lands in Δ_f(|Y|); the rank-one point is dense in Spa(K, K⁺), so z lands in the closed set Δ_f(|Y|), and since Δ_f is an immersion z factors through it (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)); the two lifts agree.

(iii) ⇒ (ii): Δ_f is a quasicompact immersion, so locally its image is pro-constructible (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), and its closure is the set of specializations (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible). A specialization w' of w = Δ_f(y) is the closed point of i_{w'} : Spa(K(w'), K(w')⁺) → Y ×_X Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection), whose rank-one point is the rank-one generalization of w, which lies in the generalization-stable set Δ_f(|Y|); so i_{w'} ∘ j factors through Δ_f, and uniqueness in (iii) applied to pr₁ ∘ i_{w'}, pr₂ ∘ i_{w'} shows that i_{w'} factors through Δ_f. Hence the image is closed under specialization, hence closed.
acceptance: The glued disc of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map (test not_isSeparated_gluedDisc) violates (iii) at (K, K⁺) = (K(y), K(y)⁺): the rank-one point lies in the overlap and has two extensions.
ECD Lemma 9.9: a separated étale map over Spa(K, K⁺) that is an isomorphism on rank-one points is an injection.
Berkeley Proposition 17.4.4 and ECD Proposition 10.9 extend the criterion to v-sheaves and v-stacks (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3).

nodes.title: Maps from Spa(R, R⁺) into a separated space are determined on Spa(R, R°)
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated morphism of perfectoid spaces and (R, R⁺) a perfectoid Tate ring with a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R°. If a, b : Spa(R, R⁺) → Y satisfy f ∘ a = f ∘ b and a ∘ j = b ∘ j for the inclusion j : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺), then a = b. This is the perfectoid-space case of ECD Proposition 10.10, proved without reduction to totally disconnected spaces.
hypotheses: f separated; (R, R⁺) any perfectoid pair (no base field).
proofSteps: Let E := Spa(R, R⁺) ×_{(a,b), Y ×_X Y, Δ_f} Y → Spa(R, R⁺), the equalizer of a and b; it is a closed immersion, being a base change of Δ_f (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).

Its image contains Spa(R, R°), which contains every rank-one point of Spa(R, R⁺): continuous rank-one valuations are ≤ 1 on power-bounded elements (Tau Ceti `Valuation.IsContinuous.le_one_of_isPowerBounded`).

Every point of Spa(R, R⁺) specializes its rank-one generalization, so the closed image is everything; E → Spa(R, R⁺) is then an injection that is a homeomorphism, hence an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)), and a = b.

nodes.title: Tilting of injections, immersions, separatedness and strongly Zariski closed immersions
nodes.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ and f : Y → X a morphism with tilt f♭ : Y♭ → X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting; |Y| = |Y♭|, |X| = |X♭|). (a) f is an injection, an immersion, an open or closed immersion, quasiseparated or separated if and only if f♭ is. (b) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) and Z = Spa(S, S⁺) affinoid: f : Z → X is strongly Zariski closed if and only if f♭ is (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.7). (c) Formulas for a strongly Zariski closed f with I := ker(R → S): I♭ := ker(R♭ → S♭) is a closed perfect ideal and I is the closure of the ideal generated by ♯(I♭); S♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} S⁺ and S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ compatibly with R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ; S⁺ = {s ∈ S : |s(z)| ≤ 1 for z ∈ |Z|}; and |Z| = V(I) = V(I♭) inside |X| = |X♭|.
hypotheses: The tilt of a perfectoid space over X is taken through the slice equivalence Perfd/X ≅ Perfd/X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence).
proofSteps: (a): tilting preserves fibre products (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products), so (Δ_f)♭ = Δ_{f♭}; injections are the maps with Δ an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces); the topological conditions only involve |f| = |f♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets); separatedness and quasiseparatedness are conditions on Δ.

(b): R → S surjective iff R♭ → S♭ surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (b)); almost surjectivity of R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjectivity modulo ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion), and R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ is R♭⁺/ϖ♭ → S♭⁺/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.11); the plus-ring clause is preserved because R⁺ ↦ R♭⁺ is an inclusion-preserving bijection of rings of integral elements compatible with maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).

(c): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (c); P1/tilt-integral-subrings; Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`; and |g(x♭)| = |g♯(x)| under the tilting homeomorphism, so V(I♭) = V(♯(I♭)) = V(I).
acceptance: For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = C (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0), the tilt is C♭⟨T♭^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C♭ with I♭ the closure of (T♭^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0).
Diagonals: (Δ_f)♭ = Δ_{f♭}, so f is separated iff f♭ is.

nodes.title: A compatible pseudouniformiser with p-power roots on a tail of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate pairs
nodes.statement: Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Claim: for every object i₀ of I there is ϖ ∈ R_{i₀}⁺ such that (a) ϖ is a pseudouniformiser of R_{i₀} (a topologically nilpotent unit, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`), ϖ^p divides p in R_{i₀}⁺, and ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R_{i₀}⁺ (ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}; (b) for every morphism a: j → i₀ of I, φ_a(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of R_j, φ_a(ϖ)^p divides p in R_j⁺, and the φ_a(ϖ^{1/p^n}) are compatible p-power roots of φ_a(ϖ) in R_j⁺. Such a pair (i₀, ϖ) is called a compatible pseudouniformiser of the system ('any compatible choice of pseudouniformizers for large i' in ECD 6.4). The comma category I/i₀ (objects j with a morphism to i₀; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over i₀`) is initial in I, so every limit over I may be computed on the tail I/i₀. For two parallel morphisms a, b: j ⇉ i₀ the elements φ_a(ϖ), φ_b(ϖ) of R_j need not agree; they have the same image in colim_i R_i⁺, which is the only place where compatibility is used.
hypotheses: I small and cofiltered (in particular nonempty); every R_i a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1) with a ring of integral elements R_i⁺.
Transition maps are continuous ring maps carrying R_i⁺ into R_j⁺; no injectivity, flatness or density is assumed.
proofSteps: By PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots applied to (R_{i₀}, R_{i₀}⁺) there is a pseudouniformiser ϖ₀ ∈ R_{i₀}° with ϖ₀^p | p in R_{i₀}° and compatible p-power roots ϖ₀^{1/p^n}; these roots are topologically nilpotent, hence lie in R_{i₀}⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).

Put ϖ := (ϖ₀^{1/p})^{p-1}. Writing p = ϖ₀^p u with u ∈ R_{i₀}°, one has p = ϖ^p · (ϖ₀ u) and ϖ₀u is topologically nilpotent, hence in R_{i₀}⁺; so ϖ^p | p in R_{i₀}⁺, and (ϖ₀^{1/p^{n+1}})^{p-1} is a compatible system of p-power roots of ϖ in R_{i₀}⁺. ϖ is a unit and topologically nilpotent, so a pseudouniformiser.

A continuous ring map sends units to units and topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent elements, and φ_a(R_{i₀}⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺; applying φ_a to p = ϖ^p·c and to the root relations gives (b).

Initiality of I/i₀ → I is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget` for cofiltered I; hence limits (and, dually, the colimits of rings over I^op used in P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs) are unchanged by passing to the tail.
acceptance: For K = C_p and R_{i₀} = C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with R_{i₀}⁺ = O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ϖ = p^{1/p} (with roots p^{1/p^{n+1}}) satisfies ϖ^p = p | p; its image under the continuous map T^{1/p^m} ↦ p^{1/p^{m+1}}T^{1/p^m} is again such a pseudouniformiser.
In characteristic p (for instance R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞})) completed) the condition ϖ^p | p = 0 is empty and ϖ = t with roots t^{1/p^n} works, in accordance with ECD Proposition 3.5.

nodes.title: The ϖ-adic completion of a ring integrally closed in its localisation away from a nonzerodivisor
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and ϖ ∈ A a nonzerodivisor such that A is integrally closed in A[1/ϖ] (Mathlib `IsIntegrallyClosedIn A (Localization.Away ϖ)`). Let Â := lim_n A/ϖ^nA be its ϖ-adic completion (Mathlib `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A`). Then: (a) Â is ϖ-adically complete and separated, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on Â, and A/ϖ^nA → Â/ϖ^nÂ is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 1; (b) the kernel of A → Â is J := ⋂_n ϖ^nA, which satisfies J = ϖJ, and A/J is again ϖ-torsion free and integrally closed in (A/J)[1/ϖ]; (c) Â is integrally closed in Â[1/ϖ]; (d) if A is p-root closed in A[1/ϖ] (g ∈ A[1/ϖ] and g^p ∈ A imply g ∈ A), so is Â in Â[1/ϖ]; (e) for the topology on Â[1/ϖ] in which Â is open with its ϖ-adic topology, the image of A[1/ϖ] is dense. No noetherian or separatedness hypothesis on A is made.
hypotheses: ϖ a nonzerodivisor of A; A integrally closed in A[1/ϖ].
A need not be ϖ-adically separated: filtered colimits of separated rings need not be separated, which is the case of interest.
proofSteps: (a) Stacks Tag 05GG for the finitely generated ideal ϖA gives completeness of Â and Â/ϖ^nÂ = A/ϖ^nA (Mathlib `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete` for completeness). Torsion-freeness: if ϖ·(x_n)_n = 0 in lim A/ϖ^n then ϖx_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^{n+1}A, so x_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^nA because ϖ is a nonzerodivisor, hence x_n = 0 for all n.

(b) If x ∈ J then x = ϖy_n with y_n ∈ ϖ^{n-1}A, and y_n = y_m by torsion-freeness, so J = ϖJ; A/J is ϖ-torsion free and integrally closed in its localisation because J is uniquely ϖ-divisible, J = J[1/ϖ] (Bhatt, Lemma 5.1.2, first paragraph). Replace A by A/J; now A ⊆ Â and A = Â ∩ A[1/ϖ] inside Â[1/ϖ].

(c) Let g = ϖ^{-c}h (h ∈ Â, c ≥ 0) satisfy g^d + s_{d-1}g^{d-1} + … + s_0 = 0 with s_k ∈ Â, so h^d + Σ_k s_k h^k ϖ^{c(d-k)} = 0. Choose N ≥ c(d+1) and a, a_k ∈ A with a ≡ h and a_k ≡ s_k mod ϖ^NÂ (possible by (a)). Then e' := a^d + Σ_k a_k a^k ϖ^{c(d-k)} ∈ A has image in ϖ^NÂ; as A/ϖ^NA → Â/ϖ^NÂ is injective, e' = ϖ^N e with e ∈ A. Hence z := a/ϖ^c ∈ A[1/ϖ] satisfies z^d + Σ_k a_k z^k - ϖ^{N-cd}e = 0, a monic equation over A, so z ∈ A. Therefore g = z + ϖ^{-c}(h - a) ∈ A + ϖ^{N-c}Â ⊆ Â.
(d) The same approximation with the equation T^p - g^p (Bhatt, Lemma 5.1.1(1)).
(e) A → Â has dense image since Â/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n; inverting ϖ preserves density.
acceptance: A = Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] (the union of the Z_p[p^{1/p^n}]) with ϖ = p: Â is the valuation ring of the completion of Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), integrally closed in its fraction field.
The hypothesis in (c) is needed: A = Z_p[pζ_p] ⊆ Q_p(ζ_p) is p-adically complete and ζ_p ∈ A[1/p] is integral over A but not in A.
