nodes.title: The completed direct limit (R, R⁺) of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate pairs
nodes.statement: Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Fix a compatible pseudouniformiser (i₀, ϖ) (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer). Put A := colim_{i ∈ I^op} R_i⁺, the filtered colimit of rings (Mathlib `CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimit`), and write ϖ for its image in A. Define R⁺ := Â = lim_n A/ϖ^nA, the ϖ-adic completion of A, and R := R⁺[1/ϖ], topologised so that R⁺ is an open subring with its ϖ-adic topology (so (R⁺, ϖR⁺) is a pair of definition and R is a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ). For i in the tail I/i₀ the canonical map ι_i: R_i = R_i⁺[1/ϖ] → R is continuous with ι_i(R_i⁺) ⊆ R⁺ and ι_j ∘ φ_a = ι_i; (R, R⁺) with the ι_i is the completed direct limit of the system. Conventions: the completion is the ϖ-adic completion of the uncompleted colimit of the plus rings, never a completion of colim R_i for some other topology; A need not be ϖ-adically separated, so the ι_i need not be injective; R⁺ is integrally closed in R and (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid); the construction is independent of (i₀, ϖ) and of the tail (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice). Universal property: for every complete Tate pair (S, S⁺) with S⁺ bounded in S (for instance S uniform) and every compatible family of morphisms of pairs ψ_i: (R_i, R_i⁺) → (S, S⁺), i ∈ I/i₀, there is a unique morphism of pairs ψ: (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with ψ ∘ ι_i = ψ_i.
hypotheses: The standing setting of this layer; a compatible pseudouniformiser (i₀, ϖ).
The universal property is stated for targets whose plus ring is bounded (hence ϖ-adically complete); it is not claimed for arbitrary complete Huber pairs.
proofSteps: A exists as a filtered colimit in CommRingCat (mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A since it is a unit in every R_i ⊇ R_i⁺ and multiplication by ϖ is injective at every stage of the filtered colimit.
A[1/ϖ] = colim R_i (localisation commutes with filtered colimits) and A is integrally closed in it: an integral equation lives at a finite stage, where R_i⁺ is integrally closed in R_i.

R⁺ := Â is ϖ-adically complete, ϖ-torsion free, with R⁺/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (a)); R := R⁺[1/ϖ] with basis of neighbourhoods {ϖ^nR⁺} is a complete Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing with pair of definition (R⁺, ϖR⁺), tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition).

Each R_i⁺ is bounded and open in the uniform ring R_i (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so its subspace topology is the ϖ-adic one (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero); hence R_i⁺ → A → Â is continuous, and so is its extension ι_i to R_i = R_i⁺[1/ϖ]; the ι_i are compatible by construction of the colimit.

Universal property: the ψ_i induce A → S⁺ (colimit property), which is continuous for the ϖ-adic topology because S⁺ is bounded and open, hence carries the ϖ-adic topology; S⁺ is closed in the complete S, so ϖ-adically complete, and the map extends uniquely to Â → S⁺; invert ϖ (a unit in S). Uniqueness follows from density of A in Â (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (e)).
acceptance: Profinite sets: K a perfectoid field, S = lim_n S_n with S_n = {0,1}^n, R_n = K^{S_n}, R_n⁺ = O_K^{S_n}; then A is the ring of locally constant functions S → O_K, R⁺ = C^0(S, O_K) and R = C^0(S, K).
ECD Example 5.2: for x in an affinoid perfectoid X₀, the rational neighbourhoods U ∋ x give R⁺ = K(x)⁺, with K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{U ∋ x} O⁺(U)/ϖ.

nodes.title: The completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs is a perfectoid Tate pair
nodes.statement: In the situation of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: (a) R⁺ is open and bounded in R and integrally closed in R, so R⁺ is a ring of integral elements and ϖR° ⊆ R⁺ ⊆ R°; (b) R is uniform; (c) ϖ^p divides p in R⁺, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R⁺, and Frobenius R⁺/ϖR⁺ → R⁺/ϖ^pR⁺, x ↦ x^p, is an isomorphism, so R⁺ is an integral perfectoid ring (BMS1 Definition 3.5); (d) R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings for the filtered system i ↦ R_i over (I/i₀)^op with the pseudouniformiser ϖ, hence a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 whose tilt R♭ is the completed direct limit of the R_i♭; so (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair and the ι_i are morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs; (e) if all R_i have characteristic p then R is a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p; if the system lives over a perfectoid Tate ring B (compatible maps B → R_i) then R is a perfectoid B-algebra. No perfectoid base field is assumed. Perfectoidness of the ring and its tilt are the P1 theorem; this node adds the plus ring R⁺ = completion of colim R_i⁺.
hypotheses: The standing setting; (i₀, ϖ) a compatible pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p in R_{i₀}⁺ (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer).
The R_i are perfectoid; a completed colimit of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid, but that situation is a tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7) and is not covered here.
proofSteps: (d): on the tail, i ↦ R_i is a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings over (I/i₀)^op with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer). Since ϖR_i° ⊆ R_i°° ⊆ R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), A = colim R_i⁺ ⊆ colim R_i° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A, so the ϖ-adic completions of the two colimits give the same complete Tate ring: R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings, a perfectoid Tate ring by (b) there, with tilt the completed direct limit of the R_i♭ by (c) there. In particular R is uniform: (b).

By P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness applied to A (ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A, being a unit in every R_i ⊇ R_i⁺; A is integrally closed in A[1/ϖ] = colim R_i because an integral equation lives at a finite stage, where R_i⁺ is integrally closed): R⁺/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R⁺, and R⁺ is integrally closed in R.

(a): R⁺ is bounded (a ring of definition), hence R⁺ ⊆ R°. For x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so some power lies in the open R⁺, and ϖx ∈ R⁺ by integral closedness (the argument of ECD Example 3.22(ii); tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).

(c): for i in the tail, Frobenius R_i⁺/ϖ → R_i⁺/ϖ^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); filtered colimits are exact, so Frobenius A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is bijective, hence so is R⁺/ϖ → R⁺/ϖ^p (previous step), and ϖ^p | p passes from A to R⁺ along the canonical completion map, which need not be injective. With ϖ-adic completeness and ϖ a nonzerodivisor, R⁺ is integral perfectoid by BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison), as BMS1 Lemma 3.20 also gives from (d).
(d), pairs: R⁺ is a ring of integral elements of the perfectoid Tate ring R by (a), so (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) and ι_i(R_i⁺) ⊆ R⁺ by construction.
(e): in characteristic p use ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect); B-algebra structures pass to colimits and completions.
acceptance: Profinite sets: C^0(S, K) is a perfectoid Tate ring for every profinite S and perfectoid field K, with C^0(S, K)° = C^0(S, O_K).
Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 4.6: the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebras is perfectoid affinoid; this node proves it without a base field.

Non-example of the hypothesis: the tower Q_p(p^{1/p^n}) consists of discretely valued, non-perfectoid fields (ECD Remark 3.3); its completed colimit is perfectoid but is not an instance of this theorem.

nodes.title: The completed direct limit does not depend on the compatible pseudouniformiser or on the tail
nodes.statement: In the situation of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: (a) if (i₀, ϖ) and (i₀', ϖ') are two compatible pseudouniformisers, the ϖ-adic and ϖ'-adic topologies on A = colim R_i⁺ coincide, and the identity of A induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs (R_ϖ, R_ϖ⁺) ≅ (R_ϖ', R_ϖ'⁺) compatible with all ι_i; (b) for an initial functor u: I' → I (for instance the inclusion of a tail I/i₁, or of a cofinal subposet) the completed direct limit of the restricted system is canonically isomorphic to that of the original one, compatibly with the ι; (c) these isomorphisms compose (for three choices, the composite of two comparison isomorphisms is the third) and commute with the universal property `lift`; (d) consequently Spa(R, R⁺) with its projections to the X_i is well defined up to unique isomorphism.
hypotheses: The standing setting; I cofiltered.
proofSteps: (a) Choose k ∈ I with morphisms to i₀ and i₀'. In R_k both images are pseudouniformisers and ϖR_k⁺, ϖ'R_k⁺ are open neighbourhoods of 0; since ϖ' is topologically nilpotent, ϖ'^N ∈ ϖR_k⁺ for some N, and symmetrically ϖ^N ∈ ϖ'R_k⁺. Hence ϖ'^{Nn}A ⊆ ϖ^nA and ϖ^{Nn}A ⊆ ϖ'^nA for all n, the two filtrations are cofinal, the two completions of A coincide, and ϖ' becomes a unit in R_ϖ (it divides ϖ^N, a unit).

(b) Restriction along an initial functor does not change the colimit of rings (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.colimitIso` for the opposite functor; `CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget` for tails), and the pseudouniformiser is unchanged.
(c) Uniqueness in the universal property of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs.
(d) Apply Spa and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (the perfectoid property does not depend on ϖ).
acceptance: In the profinite example, ϖ, ϖ^{1/p} and uϖ (u ∈ O_K^×) give the same C^0(S, O_K); restricting to S_n with n ≥ 5 gives the same pair.
If I has a terminal object t, every object maps to t, the tail I/t is all of I, and (b) for this tail is the identity.

nodes.title: Uniformity of perfectoid spaces: global integral sections are ϖ-adically complete
nodes.statement: Let Y be a perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) and ϖ ∈ O_Y(Y) a unit whose restriction to every affinoid perfectoid open U ⊆ Y is a pseudouniformiser of O_Y(U) (for instance the pullback of a pseudouniformiser along a morphism Y → Spa(R_{i₀}, R_{i₀}⁺)). Then O_Y⁺(Y) is ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete and separated, and the restriction maps O_Y⁺(Y) → O_Y⁺(U) to affinoid perfectoid opens are continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, the ϖ-adic topology of O_Y⁺(U) being its subspace topology in O_Y(U). Consequently, for every ring A containing ϖ, every ring map A → O_Y⁺(Y) extends uniquely to the ϖ-adic completion Â, and the induced maps Â[1/ϖ] → O_Y(U) are continuous.
hypotheses: Y perfectoid; ϖ a pseudouniformiser on every affinoid perfectoid open of Y.
proofSteps: Affinoid case: for U = Spa(S, S⁺) affinoid perfectoid, O_Y⁺(U) = S⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity, H^0(U, O⁺) = S⁺; anchor Layer 2.3, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)); S⁺ is bounded and open in the complete uniform ring S, hence ϖ-adically complete, separated and ϖ-torsion free with the ϖ-adic topology equal to the subspace topology.

Cover Y by affinoid perfectoid opens U_k and each U_k ∩ U_l by affinoid perfectoid opens W_{klm} (P2/perfectoid-space). O⁺_Y is a sheaf (the subsheaf of functions of absolute value ≤ 1, anchor Layer 3.3), so O⁺_Y(Y) is the kernel of ∏_k O⁺(U_k) ⇉ ∏ O⁺(W_{klm}).

Products of ϖ-adically complete ϖ-torsion-free modules are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (ϖ^n∏M_k = ∏ϖ^nM_k); the kernel K of a map M → N of such modules satisfies K ∩ ϖ^nM = ϖ^nK because N is ϖ-torsion free, and K is closed, so K is ϖ-adically complete.
Extension: A → O⁺_Y(Y) is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, hence extends uniquely to Â (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`); continuity into O_Y(U) follows from step 1.
acceptance: For Y = S × Spa(K, O_K) with S profinite, O⁺(Y) = C^0(S, O_K) is ϖ-adically complete although it is a limit over the finite covers of S.

The statement fails for non-uniform adic spaces: for a complete Tate ring S whose S⁺ is unbounded the ϖ-adic topology of S⁺ is strictly finer than its subspace topology, which is why the limit of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces is taken in perfectoid spaces.

nodes.title: Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Let (R, R⁺) be the completed direct limit for a compatible pseudouniformiser (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs), a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid), and put X := Spa(R, R⁺), an affinoid perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), with projections p_i: X → X_i induced by ι_i (i in the tail; for general i through any j → i, i₀). Then (X, (p_i)) is a limit of the diagram (X_i) in the category of perfectoid spaces: for every perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i) is bijective. In particular X is the limit in the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces, O_X(X) = R and O⁺_X(X) = R⁺, and X is independent of the choices up to unique isomorphism (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice). Companion statements: |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism, ECD 6.4(o)); rational subsets and their rings are computed at finite stages (P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets); for ω₁-cofiltered I no completion is needed (P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit); cardinal bounds (P5/limit-cardinal-bounds). The limit is claimed in perfectoid spaces only; for a non-uniform adic space Y a compatible family Y → X_i need not induce a map continuous for the ϖ-adic topology of colim R_i⁺.
hypotheses: The standing setting; the X_i are affinoid perfectoid (the construction is not applied to non-perfectoid X_i: such towers are tilde-limits, PerfectoidSpaces:P7).

Morphisms into affinoid perfectoid spaces are described by the adjunction of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids (Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1(ii)) for sheafy pairs; perfectoid pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy).
proofSteps: X is an affinoid perfectoid space: (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid), sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy, so Spa(R, R⁺) is an affinoid adic space (anchor Layer 5) and perfectoid (P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), with (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) = (R, R⁺) (P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iv)).
For a perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, Spa(S, S⁺)) = Hom_CAff((S, S⁺), (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y))) naturally in Y for sheafy (S, S⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids).

A compatible family f_i: Y → X_i gives compatible morphisms (R_i, R_i⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)), hence A = colim R_i⁺ → O_Y⁺(Y); ϖ maps to a pseudouniformiser on every affinoid perfectoid open, so the map extends uniquely to R⁺ = Â → O_Y⁺(Y) (P5/integral-sections-are-varpi-complete) and then to R = R⁺[1/ϖ] → O_Y(Y), continuously into each O_Y(U).

Uniqueness: two maps (R, R⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)) agreeing on the dense images of the R_i agree (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs, API denseRange_ι, and Hausdorffness of O_Y(U)). Hence Hom(Y, X) = lim Hom(Y, X_i).
Independence of choices: P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice.
acceptance: Berkeley Example 8.2.2: for a perfectoid field K and a profinite set S = lim S_n, lim_n (S_n × Spa(K, O_K)) = Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K)); this is the S × Spa(K, O_K) of DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds.

ECD Example 5.2: for x in an affinoid perfectoid X₀, lim_{U ∋ x rational} U = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) in perfectoid spaces; more generally, for a filtered family 𝒰 of rational subsets of an affinoid perfectoid X₀ (transition maps the restrictions), the construction specialises to PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection.

The tower Spa(Q_p(p^{1/p^n}), Z_p[p^{1/p^n}]) is not a diagram of perfectoid spaces (ECD Remark 3.3); identifying Spa of the completion of Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) with its limit is a tilde-limit statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P7, not an instance of this node.

nodes.title: The adic spectrum of a completed direct limit of Tate pairs is the inverse limit of the adic spectra
nodes.statement: Let I be small cofiltered and (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i ∈ I} an Iᵒᵖ-indexed diagram of Tate Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`, `Huber.IsTateRing`; complete or not) with continuous morphisms of pairs, together with i₀, a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i₀}⁺ and rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i⁺ (i ∈ I/i₀) containing the image of ϖ with φ_a(A_{i,0}) ⊆ A_{j,0} (for uniform A_i take A_{i,0} = A_i⁺). Let L := colim A_i, L⁺ := colim A_i⁺ and L_0 := colim A_{i,0}, with the topology on L in which L_0 is an open subring with its ϖ-adic topology, and let (L̂, L̂⁺) be the completion. Then: (a) (L, L⁺) is a Tate Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (L, L⁺) are morphisms of pairs; (b) the map Spa(L, L⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) given by the Tau Ceti maps `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap` is a homeomorphism onto the inverse limit in topological spaces; (c) every rational subset of Spa(L, L⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset R(T_i/s_i) of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺), with T_i a finite set generating the unit ideal of A_i; (d) composing with the homeomorphism Spa(L̂, L̂⁺) ≅ Spa(L, L⁺) (Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 = Huber 1993 Proposition 3.9; requested from anchor Layer 2), (b) and (c) hold for the completed direct limit; the limit is a spectral space and the projections are spectral. For perfectoid pairs with A_{i,0} = A_i⁺ the completion is the (R, R⁺) of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs.
hypotheses: The rings of definition must be chosen compatibly; the ϖ-adic topology on L_0 is the colimit topology used by Kedlaya–Liu (infimum seminorm) and by Sch12 Lemma 6.13(ii).

The completion step is imported: Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets (Wedhorn 7.48, Huber 1993, 3.9), which the anchor's Layer 2 references but does not list as a target (requests.json).
proofSteps: Points of Spv: a valuative relation on L restricts along each A_i → L (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap), compatibly; conversely a compatible family of valuative relations on the A_i defines one on L, because any two elements of L come from a common stage (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.3). So Spv(L) → lim Spv(A_i) is bijective.

Membership in Spa: for a Tate pair with ring of definition B ∋ ϖ, a valuation v lies in Spa iff v ≤ 1 on the plus ring and v(ϖ) is cofinal in the value group (Wedhorn Remark 7.11(1) with I = ϖB, an ideal of definition of B because the ϖ^nB form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero); since A = A⁺[1/ϖ], cofinality holds iff for every a with v(a) ≠ 0 there is n with v(ϖ^n) < v(a). Each condition involves finitely many elements, so v ∈ Spa(L, L⁺) iff every restriction lies in Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff).

Topology: rational subsets R(T/s) with T ⊆ L finite generating L form a basis of Spa(L, L⁺). Choose i where T, s and a relation Σ t b_t = 1 are defined; then R(T/s) is the preimage of R(T_i/s_i) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset). Preimages of opens of Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are open (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap). Hence the bijection is a homeomorphism and (c) holds.

(d) Transfer along Spa(L̂, L̂⁺) ≅ Spa(L, L⁺) (anchor Layer 2 request), which matches rational subsets. Spectrality: each Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is spectral (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition) and the transition maps are spectral (preimages of rational subsets are rational), so the limit is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).
acceptance: Profinite sets: |Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K))| = S × |Spa(K, O_K)| = lim_n S_n × |Spa(K, O_K)|.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (a) is the case of Kedlaya–Liu affinoid systems; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond uses the case of a finite étale tower over a Tate pair with compatible rings of definition.

nodes.title: The underlying space of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the inverse limit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (o))
nodes.statement: Let X = lim_i X_i be the limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). Then the map |X| → lim_i |X_i| induced by the projections is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces: lim_i |X_i| (inverse limit in topological spaces) is spectral, the projections |X| → |X_i| and the transition maps are spectral, and the map is a homeomorphism. Moreover every rational subset U ⊆ X equals p_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and some rational subset U_i ⊆ X_i.
hypotheses: The standing setting; X the limit of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces.
proofSteps: Apply P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs to the perfectoid pairs with rings of definition A_{i,0} = R_i⁺ (bounded because R_i is uniform, P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); its completion is (R, R⁺) (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs), so Spa(R, R⁺) → lim Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) is a homeomorphism and rational subsets descend.

Spectrality of the limit and of the projections: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces, with each |X_i| spectral and transition maps spectral (preimages of rational subsets are rational).
acceptance: Profinite sets: |S × Spa(K, O_K)| = S × |Spa(K, O_K)|, with S carrying its profinite topology.
ECD Example 5.2: |Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| = ⋂_{U ∋ x} U with the subspace topology, U ranging over rational neighbourhoods of x in X₀.

nodes.title: Quasicompact opens, constructible sets and clopen sets in cofiltered limits of spectral spaces come from a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ S_i a diagram of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps f_a: S_j → S_i (Mathlib `SpectralSpace`, `IsSpectralMap`), and S = lim_i S_i with projections p_i. Then: (a) every quasicompact open U ⊆ S equals p_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and some quasicompact open U_i ⊆ S_i; more generally every constructible subset of S is the preimage of a constructible subset of some S_i; (b) if U_i, U_i' ⊆ S_i are quasicompact opens with p_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ p_i^{-1}(U_i') (resp. =), there is a: j → i with f_a^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ f_a^{-1}(U_i') (resp. =); in particular, if p_i^{-1}(U_i) = S then f_a^{-1}(U_i) = S_j for some a, and if p_i^{-1}(U_i) = ∅ then f_a^{-1}(U_i) = ∅ for some a; (c) finite unions and intersections of such identities hold at a common finite stage; (d) if U_i ⊆ S_i is a quasicompact open and p_i^{-1}(U_i) is open and closed in S, then f_a^{-1}(U_i) is open and closed in S_j for some a: j → i.
hypotheses: I cofiltered; all S_i spectral and all transition maps spectral.
proofSteps: S is spectral and the p_i are spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); the sets p_i^{-1}(V), V ⊆ S_i quasicompact open, form a basis of S closed under finite intersections (cofilteredness), so a quasicompact open is a finite union of them, all defined at a common stage: (a) for opens. Constructible sets: Stacks Tag 0A2Y.

(b): D := U_i ∖ U_i' is constructible, hence closed in the constructible topology and compact Hausdorff there (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite; tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible.isCompact); the preimages D_j (j over I/i) form a cofiltered diagram of compact Hausdorff spaces, spectral maps being continuous for the constructible topologies, with limit p_i^{-1}(D) = ∅. A cofiltered limit of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces is nonempty (mathlib:TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system), so some D_j is empty.
(c) Finitely many applications of (b) at a common stage (cofilteredness).

(d) S ∖ p_i^{-1}(U_i) is closed in the spectral space S, hence quasicompact, and open, so by (a) it is p_j^{-1}(W_j); apply (b) to U_j ∪ W_j = S_j and U_j ∩ W_j = ∅ at a further stage (the argument of ECD's proof of 6.4(iii)).
acceptance: S = lim_n {0,1}^n (Cantor set): its clopen subsets are exactly the preimages of subsets of some {0,1}^n; the open subset S ∖ {s} is not quasicompact and is not the preimage of an open subset of any finite stage, so quasicompactness is needed in (a).
Sch12 Lemma 6.13(iv): a quasicompact open U_i containing the image of S contains the image of S_j for some j — the case p_i^{-1}(U_i) = S of (b).

nodes.title: Base changes of a qcqs perfectoid space along a cofiltered limit form a limit, with spectral underlying spaces
nodes.statement: In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let g_i: Y_i → X_i be a morphism of perfectoid spaces with Y_i quasicompact and quasiseparated (for instance a qcqs étale Y_i), and put Y_j := Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j (a: j → i) and Y := Y_i ×_{X_i} X, fibre products of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then Y = lim_{j ∈ I/i} Y_j in perfectoid spaces, |Y| → lim_j |Y_j| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces, and for every affinoid perfectoid open V_i ⊆ Y_i the V_j := V_i ×_{X_i} X_j are affinoid perfectoid with V := V_i ×_{X_i} X = lim V_j (so O(V) is the completed direct limit of the O(V_j)).
hypotheses: The standing setting; Y_i qcqs; fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist and fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
proofSteps: Limits commute with fibre products: for perfectoid T, Hom(T, Y_i ×_{X_i} X) = Hom(T, Y_i) ×_{Hom(T, X_i)} lim_j Hom(T, X_j) = lim_j Hom(T, Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property).

Cover Y_i by finitely many affinoid perfectoid opens V_i^1, …, V_i^m; the V_j^k are affinoid perfectoid and V^k = lim_j V_j^k (step 1 with Y_i replaced by V_i^k), so |V^k| = lim |V_j^k| (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism).

The |V^k| form an open cover of |Y|, and a point (y_j) of lim |Y_j| lies in lim_j |V_j^k| for any k with y_i ∈ V_i^k, since V_j^k is the preimage of V_i^k; so the homeomorphisms glue to |Y| ≅ lim |Y_j|. Y_j is qcqs, so |Y_j| is spectral (quasiseparated: Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`), and the limit is spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).
acceptance: For Y_i = Y_i' ×_{X_i} Y_i'' with Y_i', Y_i'' qcqs étale (the Z_i of ECD's proof of 6.4(ii)), |Z| = lim |Z_j|.
Profinite sets: for a finite étale Y_0 → Spa(K, O_K) = X_0, Y = S × Y_0 and |Y| = S × |Y_0|.

nodes.title: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let X = lim X_i be as in P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, or more generally Y = lim_j Y_j for a qcqs Y_i → X_i and its base changes (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes). Then: (a) every quasicompact open U ⊆ |Y| is p_j^{-1}(U_j) for some j and some quasicompact open U_j ⊆ |Y_j|, and the open perfectoid subspace U is U_j ×_{Y_j} Y; (b) two quasicompact opens of |Y_j| with the same preimage in Y have the same preimage in some Y_k; if a quasicompact open contains the image of Y, it contains the image of Y_k for some k; (c) a quasicompact open of |Y_j| whose preimage in Y is open and closed has open and closed preimage in Y_k for some k; (d) every finite cover of Y by quasicompact opens is the pullback of a finite cover of some Y_j by quasicompact opens; (e) for Y = X: every rational subset of X is p_i^{-1}(U_i) for a rational subset U_i ⊆ X_i, i.e. for T ⊆ R finite generating R and s ∈ R there are i, T_i ⊆ R_i finite generating R_i and s_i ∈ R_i with R(T/s) = R(ι_i(T_i)/ι_i(s_i)).
hypotheses: The standing setting; for (a)-(d) any qcqs Y_i → X_i.
proofSteps: |Y| = lim |Y_j| as spectral spaces (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism for Y = X; P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes in general).

(a)-(d) are P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces applied to this limit; the open subspace structure: the base change of an open immersion is the open subspace on the preimage (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces, fibre products P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
(e) is P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs (c) for the perfectoid system.
acceptance: ECD, proof of 6.4(ii): the image of f_i: Y_i → Y_i' is a quasicompact open over which Y' → Y_i' factors, hence Y_j' → Y_i' factors over it for large j.
Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.7: any rational covering of the completed direct limit is defined at a finite stage.

nodes.title: Restriction of a cofiltered limit to a rational subset of a finite stage
nodes.statement: In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let U_i ⊆ X_i be a quasicompact open subset, U_j := X(a)^{-1}(U_i) for a: j → i, and U := p_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ X. Then U = lim_{j ∈ I/i} U_j in perfectoid spaces. If U_i is rational, then each U_j is a rational subset of X_j, hence affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), U is a rational subset of X, and (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the completed direct limit of the (O_{X_j}(U_j), O⁺_{X_j}(U_j)): the canonical map from the ϖ-adic completion of colim_j O⁺_{X_j}(U_j) to O⁺_X(U) is an isomorphism (Sch12 Lemma 6.13(iii), Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.6.5(a)).
hypotheses: The standing setting; U_i quasicompact open (rational for the ring statement).
proofSteps: Base change of an open immersion is the open subspace on the preimage: U_j = U_i ×_{X_i} X_j and U = U_i ×_{X_i} X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).

For a perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, U) is the set of f: Y → X with f(|Y|) ⊆ U; by P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces and P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism this is the set of compatible families f_j: Y → X_j with f_j(|Y|) ⊆ U_j, i.e. lim Hom(Y, U_j). So U = lim U_j.

Rational case: U_j and U are rational (preimages of rational subsets are rational, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset), affinoid perfectoid; P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces applied to (U_j) gives lim U_j = Spa of the completed direct limit, and uniqueness of limits identifies it with (O(U), O⁺(U)) (restriction maps: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction).
acceptance: Profinite sets: for a clopen C_n ⊆ S_n, the restriction of S × Spa(K, O_K) to C × Spa(K, O_K) (C the preimage of C_n) is Spa(C^0(C, K), C^0(C, O_K)).
For X₀ affinoid perfectoid and x ∈ U_0 rational, restricting the system of rational neighbourhoods of x to those inside U_0 does not change the limit Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺).

nodes.title: ω₁-cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces need no completion
nodes.statement: In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces assume that I is ω₁-cofiltered: every functor J → I from a category J with countably many morphisms extends to a cone J^◁ → I (equivalently Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered Iᵒᵖ ℵ₁`, ℵ₁ regular by `Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`). Then A = colim_i R_i⁺ is ϖ-adically separated and complete, so the canonical maps colim_i R_i⁺ → R⁺ and colim_i R_i → R are ring isomorphisms (bijective). Equivalently, for an ℵ₁-filtered diagram of perfectoid Tate pairs the uncompleted colimit (colim R_i, colim R_i⁺), with colim R_i⁺ carrying its ϖ-adic topology, is a perfectoid Tate pair and O(lim X_i) = colim O(X_i). For countable index categories such as I = ℕᵒᵖ both properties fail in general: colim R_i⁺ → R⁺ need be neither surjective nor injective.
hypotheses: The standing setting; I ω₁-cofiltered in ECD's sense (a countable diagram in I has a cone).
proofSteps: Separated: if x ∈ ⋂_n ϖ^nA, choose for each n a stage i_n and y_n ∈ R_{i_n}⁺ witnessing x = ϖ^n y_n in the colimit, together with the morphisms relating these stages to a stage of x; these form a countable diagram in I, which has a cone j. In R_j⁺ the image x_j satisfies x_j ∈ ϖ^nR_j⁺ for all n, so x_j = 0 as R_j⁺ is ϖ-adically separated; hence x = 0 in A.

Complete: a Cauchy sequence (x_n) in A with x_{n+1} - x_n ∈ ϖ^nA involves countably many elements and relations, all realised in a single R_j⁺ by ω₁-cofilteredness; R_j⁺ is ϖ-adically complete, so the sequence has a limit in R_j⁺ whose image is a limit in A.
Hence A → Â = R⁺ is bijective (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (a)); inverting ϖ, colim R_i = A[1/ϖ] → R⁺[1/ϖ] = R is bijective (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs).
acceptance: ECD Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.6: O and O⁺ commute with ω₁-filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid pairs, which is this theorem applied to X ↦ O(X).

Non-examples for I = ℕᵒᵖ: for the profinite system (S_n = {0,1}^n) colim R_n⁺ = LC(S, O_K) ≠ C^0(S, O_K) = R⁺ (not surjective); for R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m} the element T is in ⋂ ϖ^n colim R_n⁺, so colim R_n⁺ → R⁺ = O_K is not injective.

nodes.title: Every countable subset of a perfectoid Tate ring lies in a closed, topologically countably generated perfectoid subring
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair and ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p in R⁺ and compatible p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer for the constant system). For every countable subset C ⊆ R there is a closed subring R' ⊆ R such that: C ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}} ∪ {ϖ^{1/p^n}} ⊆ R'; R' has a countable dense subset (equivalently R' is the closure of a countably generated subring: R' is topologically countably generated); R' with the subspace topology is a perfectoid Tate ring with R'° = R' ∩ R°; R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺ is a ring of integral elements of R', and the inclusion (R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺) is a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs. Moreover |R'| ≤ 2^{ℵ₀}.
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1); C countable.
proofSteps: Choose countable subrings D_0 ⊆ D_1 ⊆ … of R: D_0 is generated by C, ϖ^{±1}, the ϖ^{1/p^n} and p/ϖ^p; D_{k+1} is generated by D_k and, for each d ∈ D_k ∩ R°, elements y_d, z_d ∈ R° with d = y_d^p + ϖ^p z_d, which exist because Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective for every pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer). Put D := ⋃_k D_k (countable) and R' := closure of D.

R' is a closed subring of the complete R, hence complete; ϖ is a unit of R' (ϖ^{-1} ∈ D) and topologically nilpotent; R' ∩ R⁺ is open in R' and bounded, a ring of definition, so R' is a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing). A subset of R' is bounded in R' iff it is bounded in R (for a subset of R', both conditions are equivalent to containment in ϖ^{-n}(R' ∩ R⁺) for some n), so R'° = R' ∩ R° is bounded: R' is uniform.

Frobenius: for x ∈ R'° choose d ∈ D with x - d ∈ ϖ^pR⁺ ∩ R' (density; an open neighbourhood of 0 in R'). Then d ∈ D ∩ R°, so y_d, z_d ∈ D ∩ R° ⊆ R'°, and x - y_d^p = (x - d) + ϖ^p z_d ∈ ϖ^p R'°. Also ϖ^p | p in R'° since p/ϖ^p ∈ D ∩ R°. Hence R' is perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1).
R'⁺ = R' ∩ R⁺ is open in R', integrally closed in R' (R⁺ is integrally closed in R) and contained in R'° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).

Cardinality: R' is complete metrisable with a countable dense subset, so every element is the limit of a sequence in D and |R'| ≤ ℵ₀^{ℵ₀} = 2^{ℵ₀} (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound, the case λ = ℵ₀).
acceptance: For R = C^0(S, K) with S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁} and K = C_p, and C a countable set of functions depending only on the coordinates in a countable J ⊆ ℵ₁, one may take R' = C^0({0,1}^J, C_p) pulled back to S.
If R already has a countable dense subset (for example C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), one may take R' = R.

nodes.title: Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and ϖ as in P5/countable-perfectoid-hull. Let 𝒮(R) be the set of closed subrings R' ⊆ R containing ϖ^{±1} that are perfectoid Tate rings for the subspace topology and admit a countable dense subset, ordered by inclusion, and put R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺. Then: (a) 𝒮(R) is ω₁-directed (every countable subset of 𝒮(R) has an upper bound in 𝒮(R)) and ⋃_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} R' = R; (b) colim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} (R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺) is an isomorphism of Huber pairs, without completion; (c) X = lim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} Spa(R', R'⁺) in perfectoid spaces and |X| = lim |Spa(R', R'⁺)|: X is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces with topologically countably generated rings of functions; (d) every R' ∈ 𝒮(R) has cardinality ≤ 2^{ℵ₀}; hence, for every uncountable strong limit cardinal κ (in particular every cutoff cardinal of ECD Lemma 4.1), X is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces whose rings have cardinality < κ. This ω₁-presentation is the form in which ECD's cutoff-independence argument (Proposition 8.2) can be carried out for singular cutoff cardinals (see sourceIssues).
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; no countability assumption on R.
proofSteps: (a) Given countably many R'_k ∈ 𝒮(R) with countable dense subsets C_k, apply P5/countable-perfectoid-hull to ⋃_k C_k to get R'' ∈ 𝒮(R) containing every C_k, hence every R'_k (R'' is closed). Every x ∈ R lies in the hull of {x}.

(b) The union of an ω₁-directed family of subrings is the colimit, and it equals R and R⁺ by (a); no completion is needed (P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit), and the topologies agree because R'⁺ carries the subspace, i.e. ϖ-adic, topology.

(c) P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces and P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism for the ω₁-cofiltered diagram 𝒮(R)^op, whose completed direct limit is (R, R⁺) by (b) (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice for the choice of ϖ).
(d) P5/countable-perfectoid-hull; 2^{ℵ₀} < κ for κ an uncountable strong limit (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal).
acceptance: X = Spa(C^0(S, C_p), C^0(S, O_{C_p})) with S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁}: the subrings C^0({0,1}^J, C_p), J ⊆ ℵ₁ countable, are cofinal in 𝒮(R), since a continuous function on S depends on countably many coordinates.
Degenerate case: if R has a countable dense subset, R is the largest element of 𝒮(R) and the presentation is trivial.

Non-example: if R has no countable dense subset, X is not the limit of an ℕᵒᵖ-indexed tower of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (the union of the countable dense subsets of the images would be a countable dense subset of R), so an uncountable ω₁-cofiltered index category is necessary.

nodes.title: Cardinal bounds for cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let κ be a cutoff cardinal (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal, ECD Lemma 4.1), λ < κ a cardinal, I a cofiltered category with fewer than λ morphisms, and X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (i ∈ I) a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces such that |R_i| < κ' for all i, for some strong limit cardinal κ' < κ (this holds when all X_i are κ'-small in the sense of ECD Definition 4.2). Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim X_i. Then |colim R_i⁺| < κ, |R⁺| < κ, |R| < κ, |X| < κ, and |O_X(U)| < κ for every open affinoid U ⊆ X. These are the two conditions of ECD Definition 4.2, so X is κ-small; PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space defines κ-smallness by exactly these conditions.
hypotheses: κ as in ECD Lemma 4.1; I λ-small with λ < κ; each |R_i| < κ' with κ' < κ a strong limit cardinal.
proofSteps: By clause (iii) of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (the κ_μ being cofinal in κ) choose a strong limit cardinal κ'' with κ' ≤ κ'' < κ and cofinality of κ'' larger than λ.
|colim R_i⁺| ≤ Σ_{i} |R_i| is a sum of fewer than λ < cf(κ'') cardinals each < κ'', hence < κ''.

R⁺ is first countable (ϖ-adic) with a dense subring (the image of colim R_i⁺) of cardinality μ < κ'' < κ, so |R⁺| ≤ μ^{ℵ₀} ≤ 2^μ < κ (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound; κ strong limit); |R| ≤ |R⁺|·ℵ₀ since R = ⋃_n ϖ^{-n}R⁺.
|X| ≤ |Set(R × R)| = 2^{|R|} < κ: a point of Spa(R, R⁺) is a valuative relation on R, i.e. a subset of R × R (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum; mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set).

For U ⊆ X open affinoid, U is a finite union of rational subsets U_k of X (quasicompactness), O(U) ↪ ∏_k O(U_k) (sheaf property, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), and O(U_k) has a dense subring of the form R[1/s_k] of cardinality |R| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so |O(U_k)| < κ by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound.

nodes.title: The 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories
nodes.statement: Let J be a small filtered category and F a pseudofunctor from J (as a locally discrete bicategory) to categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`): categories C_j, functors F_a: C_i → C_j for a: i → j, and coherent natural isomorphisms F_{ba} ≅ F_b ∘ F_a and F_{id} ≅ id. The filtered 2-colimit 2-colim_j C_j is the category whose objects are pairs (i, x) with x an object of C_i, whose morphisms are Hom((i, x), (j, y)) := colim_{(k, a: i → k, b: j → k)} Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y) (a filtered colimit of sets over the category of cospans under i and j), with composition and identities induced from the C_k (Berkeley Remark 7.4.7). It carries functors ι_i: C_i → 2-colim C_j and isomorphisms ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i, and is the pseudo-colimit of F: pseudo-cocones (G_i: C_i → D, G_j ∘ F_a ≅ G_i coherently) correspond, up to unique isomorphism, to functors G: 2-colim C_j → D. For a pseudo-cocone the induced G is faithful iff morphisms in some C_k with equal images in D become equal in some further C_{k'}; full iff every morphism G_i x → G_j y of D comes from a morphism in some C_k; essentially surjective iff every object of D is isomorphic to some G_i x. In this layer J = Iᵒᵖ, C_i = a category of objects over X_i and F_a = base change; 'the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim (X_i)_? → X_?' means that the induced G is an equivalence.
hypotheses: J small and filtered; F a pseudofunctor (base change is only defined up to canonical isomorphism).
proofSteps: Composition: representatives f ∈ Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y), g ∈ Hom_{C_l}(F_c y, F_d z) are pushed to a common k' under k, l compatible on j (filteredness) and composed there, using the coherence isomorphisms of F; independence of representatives and associativity are checked at a further common stage.

The ι_i and ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i are the identity on representatives; a pseudo-cocone defines G(i, x) := G_i x and G on representatives via the cocone isomorphisms; uniqueness up to unique isomorphism is formal.
The three criteria unwind the definition of Hom in 2-colim C_j and Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence` (fully faithful and essentially surjective).
acceptance: Berkeley Remark 7.4.7: for the filtered system of categories of finite étale algebras over complete Tate rings A_i, Hom in the 2-colimit is the colimit of Hom over common targets, and the comparison functor to finite étale algebras over the completed colimit is an equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit read through isEquivalence_desc_iff).
For the constant pseudofunctor at a category C over a filtered J the 2-colimit is equivalent to C.

nodes.title: Finite étale objects over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces come from a finite stage (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i))
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim_i X_i be a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). Then the base change functors (X_i)_fét → X_fét induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories). Ring form: base change S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R (no completion; the tensor product is finite projective over R) induces an equivalence 2-colim_i FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R), compatible with tensor products and ranks, and the plus rings of the corresponding perfectoid spaces are the integral closures of R_i⁺, R⁺. Explicitly: (lifting) every finite étale R-algebra is S_i ⊗_{R_i} R for some i and some finite étale R_i-algebra S_i; (uniqueness) for finite étale R_i-algebras S_i, S_i', every R-algebra map S_i ⊗ R → S_i' ⊗ R is the base change of an R_j-algebra map for some j → i, and two R_j-algebra maps with the same base change to R agree over some R_k. The theorem concerns finite étale algebras; finitely presented algebras over R do not in general come from a finite stage.
hypotheses: The standing setting; (i₀, ϖ) a compatible pseudouniformiser.

The algebraic input — finite étale algebras over a completed direct limit of complete Tate rings, through the henselian approximation theorem (Elkik; Gabber–Ramero arXiv Proposition 5.4.54 = book 5.4.53; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8) — is owned by PerfectoidSpaces:P3 (P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit, P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation) and imported; this node adds the identification of the completion with the limit's ring and the passage to spaces.
proofSteps: Ring form: apply PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit to the filtered system (R_i) with the compatible rings of definition A_{i,0} = R_i⁺ (bounded, as R_i is uniform) and the compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ. Its proof is: 2-colim FÉt(R_i) ≅ FÉt(L) for L := colim R_i (P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings), L is topologically henselian with ring of definition L_0 = colim R_i⁺ (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b), (c)), and FÉt(L) ≅ FÉt(L̂) (P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b); Gabber–Ramero 5.4.54 with t = ϖ, I = L_0; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8).

The completion L̂ of L for the ϖ-adic topology on L_0 is the ring R of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs (L̂_0 = R⁺ and L̂ = R⁺[1/ϖ]), and the composite 2-colim FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R) is S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R because (S_i ⊗_{R_i} L) ⊗_L R = S_i ⊗_{R_i} R.

Geometric form: for an affinoid perfectoid Z = Spa(T, T⁺), W ↦ O(W) is an anti-equivalence Z_fét ≅ FÉt(T)^op with inverse S ↦ Spa(S, integral closure of T⁺ in S) (ECD after Definition 6.2; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (c), P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces, P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids, P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), and base change of spaces corresponds to S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R (P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
acceptance: Profinite sets: finite étale C^0(S, K)-algebras are, locally on S, constant: each is (S_n-indexed family of finite étale K-algebras) ⊗ C^0(S, K) for some n.

A finite étale cover of a limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the pullback of one at a finite stage, unique up to unique isomorphism after enlarging the stage (ECD proof of Lemma 7.16: a splitting over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood).
Non-example: C^0(S, K)/(f) with f(s) = Σ_k s_k ϖ^k is finitely presented but not flat, so not a base change from any finite stage; the theorem is special to finite étale algebras.

nodes.title: Faithfulness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph argument)
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs and f_i, g_i: Y_i → Y_i' morphisms over X_i. If their base changes f, g: Y → Y' over X are equal, then f_j = g_j for some a: j → i (f_j, g_j the base changes to X_j). Equivalently, the functor 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs is faithful.
hypotheses: The standing setting; Y_i, Y_i' qcqs étale over X_i.
proofSteps: The graph Γ_{f_i}: Y_i → Z_i := Y_i ×_{X_i} Y_i' is a section of the projection Z_i → Y_i, which is étale (base change of Y_i' → X_i, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); sections of étale maps are open immersions (a section is the base change of the diagonal, an open immersion for étale maps: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5); AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (b) via P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale). Γ_{f_i} is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), so it is determined by the quasicompact open image Γ_{f_i}(|Y_i|) ⊆ |Z_i| (ECD Proposition 5.3(iv), PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria). Likewise for g_i.
Z_i is qcqs, and Z = Z_i ×_{X_i} X = lim_j Z_j with |Z| = lim |Z_j| spectral (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes).

The two images agree after pullback to |Z| (f = g); by P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (b) they agree after pullback to |Z_j| for some j. The base changes Γ_{f_j}, Γ_{g_j} are the graphs of f_j, g_j and have these pulled-back images, so f_j = g_j.
acceptance: Two X_0-endomorphisms of a finite étale Y_0 → X_0 that agree over the limit agree at a finite stage.
Faithfulness fails for non-quasicompact Y_i: the argument needs the images of the graphs to be quasicompact.

nodes.title: Surjectivity and isomorphism of qcqs étale maps are detected at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let h_i: Y_i → Y_i' be a morphism in (X_i)_ét,qcqs with base changes h_j over X_j and h over X. (a) If |h| is surjective, then |h_j| is surjective for some a: j → i; in particular, if a qcqs étale Y_i → X_i has surjective base change to X, then Y_j → X_j is surjective for some j. (b) If h is an isomorphism, then h_j is an isomorphism for some j.
hypotheses: The standing setting; h_i a morphism of qcqs étale X_i-spaces (automatically étale by cancellation, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (3)).
proofSteps: (a) h_i is étale with quasicompact source, so W_i := h_i(|Y_i|) is a quasicompact open subset of |Y_i'| (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5)). The image of h_j is the preimage of W_i in |Y_j'|, because |Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_j'| → |Y_i| ×_{|Y_i'|} |Y_j'| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective; Y_j = Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_j'); likewise over X. If h is surjective, the preimage of W_i in |Y'| is |Y'| = lim |Y_j'| (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes), so by P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (b) the preimage of W_i in |Y_j'| is all of |Y_j'| for some j.

(b) Apply (a) to h_i and to the diagonal Δ_{h_i}: Y_i → Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_i, a morphism of qcqs étale X_i-spaces and an open immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5)), whose base change Δ_h is an isomorphism. For large j, Δ_{h_j} is a surjective open immersion, hence an isomorphism, so h_j is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and h_j is surjective by (a).

A surjective étale injection is an isomorphism: |h_j| is a continuous open bijection, hence a homeomorphism; by ECD Proposition 5.3(iv) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria) h_j is final among maps whose underlying map factors continuously through |Y_j|, so id_{Y_j'} factors through h_j, and h_j is an isomorphism.

proofSteps: Local structure: every point of Y has an open neighbourhood V with V ⊆ W → U ⊆ X, where U is a rational subset of X, W → U is finite étale (so W is affinoid perfectoid) and V is a rational subset of W (ECD Definition 6.2(ii); standard affinoid form AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism via PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids). As Y is quasicompact, finitely many such V^1, …, V^m cover Y.

Each piece descends: U = p_i^{-1}(U_i) for a rational U_i ⊆ X_i (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (e)); U = lim_j U_j (P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets); W → U descends to a finite étale W_j → U_j (P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation applied to the system (U_j)); W = lim W_j (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes), so the rational V ⊆ W descends to a rational V_j ⊆ W_j (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (e)). Thus V^k ≅ V^k_j ×_{X_j} X with V^k_j qcqs étale over X_j.

Gluing: Y is quasiseparated, so V^k ∩ V^l is a quasicompact open of V^k = lim_j V^k_j and descends to a quasicompact open V^{kl}_j ⊆ V^k_j (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (a)); the identifications V^{kl} ≅ V^{lk} descend to isomorphisms over some X_j (P5/finite-stage-fullness and P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection (b)), and the finitely many cocycle conditions hold at a further stage (P5/finite-stage-faithfulness). Glue (anchor Layer 5 gluing, P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces) to Y_j, qcqs and étale over X_j, with Y_j ×_{X_j} X ≅ Y.
acceptance: A rational subset of a finite étale cover of a rational subset of X descends; a finite union of such opens glued along quasicompact overlaps descends.

Non-example: for X = S × Spa(K, O_K) (S profinite without isolated points), the open subspace Y = X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K)) is étale and quasiseparated but not quasicompact, and it is not the base change of an open subspace of any finite stage.

nodes.title: κ-small perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Fix a cardinal κ with ℵ₀ < κ that is a strong limit (2^λ < κ for every cardinal λ < κ); every cutoff cardinal of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (ECD Lemma 4.1) is one. A perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: an adic space locally isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) for a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field) is κ-small if (i) its underlying set |X| has cardinality #|X| < κ, and (ii) for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X (so A = O_X(U)) the ring A has cardinality #A < κ. The full subcategory of κ-small perfectoid spaces is written Perfd_κ, and for a κ-small X the category of κ-small perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X is X_proét,κ (ECD Definition 8.1). Conventions: cardinalities are those of underlying sets; the plus rings carry no condition (A⁺ ⊆ A); clause (ii) quantifies over all open affinoid subspaces, and there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ of them, so no separate count of charts is imposed; the predicate is invariant under isomorphism and monotone in κ. The bound in (ii) is not uniform over the charts: the stronger notion with a single bound λ < κ is PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space, and for quasicompact X the two agree.
hypotheses: κ is an uncountable strong limit cardinal; ECD notes that this is all §4 needs. Mathlib's `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts ℵ₀ as a strong limit, so ℵ₀ < κ is a separate hypothesis.

The cofinality clauses (ii) and (iii) of the cutoff lemma are not part of the definition; they are used only in the limit statements (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits) and in D1's countable iteration.
Clause (ii) is not implied by clause (i) (a one-point space with a large field), and clause (i) is not implied by clause (ii) (a disjoint union of κ points): both are needed.
proofSteps: Define `IsKappaSmall κ X` as the conjunction of #|X| < κ and #O_X(U) < κ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X, using the open affinoid subspaces of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space.
Record invariance under isomorphisms of perfectoid spaces (an isomorphism induces a bijection of points and of open affinoid subspaces with isomorphic rings) and monotonicity in κ.
Record the affinoid characterisation #A < κ and the cover criterion, which are the theorems PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion.

Essential smallness of Perfd_κ: a κ-small X is determined up to isomorphism by the topological space |X| (a set of cardinality < κ) and the restriction of (O_X, O_X⁺) with its valuations to the basis of open affinoid subspaces, whose rings have cardinality < κ; transporting all of these along injections into κ shows that the isomorphism classes of κ-small perfectoid spaces form a set, so Perfd_κ is essentially small (mathlib `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`).
acceptance: For every uncountable strong limit κ, Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) and the perfectoid disc Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) are κ-small: their rings have cardinality 2^ℵ₀ < κ.
The empty perfectoid space is κ-small.

nodes.title: Cardinality of complete Tate rings with a dense subring, and of their rational localisations, finite étale algebras and completed tensor products
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`, with its topology complete and separated). (a) If D ⊆ A is a dense subset with #D ≤ λ for an infinite cardinal λ, then #A ≤ λ^ℵ₀ ≤ 2^λ. (b) Consequently, with λ_A := #A + ℵ₀: (b1) for a rational subset U = R(T/s) of Spa(A, A⁺), the rational localisation A⟨T/s⟩ (Tau Ceti `completionLocObj`) has cardinality ≤ λ_A^ℵ₀, as the image of A[1/s] is dense; (b2) a finite étale A-algebra B with its canonical topology has #B ≤ λ_A, being a quotient of some Aⁿ; (b3) for morphisms of complete Tate pairs A → B and A → C, the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) and its uniformisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) have cardinality ≤ (#B·#C·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀, as the image of B ⊗_A C is dense. (c) If κ is an uncountable strong limit and λ < κ, each of these bounds is < κ. This is the Tate-ring instance of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound (the conditional form of ECD Remark 4.3): the first countability it needs holds because the sets ϖⁿA₀ form a countable basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`).
hypotheses: A Hausdorff: without it the limit of a sequence is not unique and the bound fails.
Completeness is not needed for (a) (only Hausdorff and first countable); it is part of the setting of (b).
proofSteps: (a): by first countability every a ∈ A is the limit of a sequence in D; as A is Hausdorff the limit map from the set of convergent sequences in D to A is well defined and surjective, so #A ≤ #D^ℵ₀ ≤ λ^ℵ₀ (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound), and λ^ℵ₀ ≤ (2^λ)^ℵ₀ = 2^{λ·ℵ₀} = 2^λ (mathlib `Cardinal.power_mul`, `Cardinal.power_le_power_right`).
(b1): A⟨T/s⟩ is the completion of A[1/s] for the localisation topology, and #A[1/s] ≤ #A·ℵ₀.
(b2): B is generated as an A-module by finitely many elements, so it is a quotient of Aⁿ.
(b3): the image of B ⊗_A C, a quotient of the free abelian group on B × C, is dense in the completion; uniformisation is a separated completion of a quotient, so the same bound applies.
(c): 2^λ < κ for λ < κ.
acceptance: A = C_p with the dense countable subfield of algebraic numbers: #C_p ≤ ℵ₀^ℵ₀ = 2^ℵ₀.
A = C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with dense subring Q̄_p[T^{1/p^∞}]: # ≤ 2^ℵ₀.

Without the Hausdorff hypothesis the bound fails: in K[T] with the Gauss-norm topology the ideal (T − c) with |c| > 1 is dense, and K[T]/(T − c) ≅ K with the quotient topology has the dense subset {0}.

nodes.title: Uniformly κ-small perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. A perfectoid space X is uniformly κ-small if there is a cardinal λ < κ such that #|X| ≤ λ and #O_X(U) ≤ λ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X; equivalently, X is κ'-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space) for some cardinal κ' < κ (take κ' = λ⁺, which is < κ because κ is a limit cardinal). Properties: (a) uniformly κ-small implies κ-small; (b) a quasicompact κ-small perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small, so the two notions have the same affinoid and the same qcqs objects; (c) if κ is regular (a strongly inaccessible cardinal) the two notions agree; (d) they differ for every κ of cofinality ω₁, in particular for the cutoff cardinals κ(µ) with cf µ = ω₁ constructed in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1: ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°), with perfectoid fields K_α whose cardinalities are < κ and cofinal in κ, is κ-small and not uniformly κ-small. The uniformly κ-small spaces satisfy the cover criterion and the stability under fibre products that ECD Proposition 4.4 states for κ-small spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure).
hypotheses: κ uncountable strong limit; the class is intended for the cutoff cardinals of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal, which are in general singular.
ECD's own set-theoretic statements (Proposition 6.4, Lemma 11.22) are formulated with such a uniform bound κ' < κ; this node names that hypothesis.
proofSteps: Define `IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X` as ∃ λ < κ, #|X| ≤ λ ∧ ∀ U open affinoid, #O_X(U) ≤ λ, and prove the equivalence with ∃ κ' < κ, IsKappaSmall κ' X using λ⁺ < κ.

(a) is immediate. (b): cover a quasicompact κ-small X by finitely many open affinoids V_1, …, V_n; an open affinoid U ⊆ X is covered by finitely many rational subsets W_k of the V_j contained in U, #O(W_k) ≤ (#O(V_j)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality), and O(U) embeds into ∏_k O(W_k) because O_X is a sheaf (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity); so λ := max(#|X|, max_j (#O(V_j)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀) < κ works.
(c): there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ open affinoid subspaces, and for regular κ a supremum of fewer than κ cardinals below κ is below κ (mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord` with cf κ = κ).

(d): the space has ℵ₁ points; each open affinoid subspace is a finite union of components, whose ring is a finite product of fields K_α of cardinality < κ, so the space is κ-small; any common bound λ would be ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ. Perfectoid fields K_α with λ_α ≤ #K_α ≤ λ_α^ℵ₀ exist for every cardinal λ_α (completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), and κ(ω₁) of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1 has cofinality ω₁.
acceptance: Every κ-small affinoid perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small with λ the cardinality of its ring raised to ℵ₀.
The example of (d) separates the notions for κ = κ(ω₁).

nodes.title: The adic spectrum of A has at most 2^{#A·#A} points
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring and A⁺ ⊆ A a subring. Then #Spa(A, A⁺) ≤ 2^{#A·#A}: a point of Spv A is determined by its valuative relation {(a, b) ∈ A × A : |a(x)| ≤ |b(x)|} (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.ext'`), so Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ Spv A injects into the power set of A × A. For A infinite this is 2^{#A}. Consequently, if κ is an uncountable strong limit and #A < κ then #Spa(A, A⁺) < κ, and a perfectoid space covered by a family of open affinoids Spa(A_j, A_j⁺), j ∈ J, has at most #J · sup_j 2^{#A_j·#A_j} points.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on A⁺ or on the topology is needed: the bound is for Spv A.
proofSteps: The map Spv A → Set (A × A), x ↦ {(a, b) : x.vle a b}, is injective by `ValuationSpectrum.ext'`; restrict it to spa A⁺ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`).
#Set (A × A) = 2^{#A·#A} (mathlib `Cardinal.mk_set`, `Cardinal.mk_prod`), and #A·#A = #A for A infinite (mathlib `Cardinal.mul_eq_self`).
For a cover, the union bound #⋃_j |U_j| ≤ #J · sup_j #|U_j| (mathlib `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`).
acceptance: Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) has one point, well below the bound 2^{2^ℵ₀}.
A bound in terms of #A alone is needed and attained in order of magnitude: the classical points of Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) alone number #K°.

nodes.title: Cover criterion for κ-smallness (ECD Proposition 4.4, corrected for singular κ)
nodes.statement: Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal and X a perfectoid space. (a) If X is κ-small, then X is covered by fewer than κ open affinoid subspaces Spa(A, A⁺) with #A < κ (namely by all of them: there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ). (b) If X has a cover {U_j = Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)}_{j∈J} by open affinoid subspaces with #A_j < κ for all j, then every open affinoid subspace U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X has #A < κ; so such an X is κ-small as soon as #|X| < κ. (c) If moreover #J < κ and sup_j #A_j < κ — automatic when J is finite, or when #J < cf κ — then #|X| < κ, and X is κ-small, indeed uniformly κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space). (d) In particular an affinoid perfectoid space Spa(A, A⁺) is κ-small iff #A < κ, and a quasicompact perfectoid space is κ-small iff it has a finite cover by open affinoid subspaces whose rings have cardinality < κ. (e) The converse of (a) as printed in ECD Proposition 4.4 — a cover by fewer than κ open affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ, without a uniform bound, implies κ-small — holds for regular κ and fails whenever cf κ ≤ #J: for κ of cofinality ω₁ (such as the cutoff cardinal κ(ω₁) of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and perfectoid fields K_α, α < ω₁, with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs Spa(K_α⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K_α°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is covered by ω₁ < κ open affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ and has at least κ points.
hypotheses: κ uncountable strong limit. Part (c) needs the uniform bound; part (e) records exactly where the printed statement needs it.
proofSteps: (a): the open subsets of |X| number at most 2^{#|X|} < κ, open affinoid subspaces cover X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space), and each has ring of cardinality < κ by definition.

(b): U is quasicompact (Tau Ceti `spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`); each U ∩ U_j is a union of rational subsets of U_j, so finitely many rational subsets W_k ⊆ U ∩ U_{j_k} cover U. #O(W_k) ≤ (#A_{j_k}·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality (b1)), and A = O_X(U) embeds into ∏_k O(W_k) since O_X is a sheaf (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity).

(c): #|U_j| ≤ 2^{#A_j·#A_j} ≤ 2^λ with λ := sup_j #A_j + ℵ₀ < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality), hence #|X| ≤ #J · 2^λ < κ; if #J < cf κ then sup_j #A_j < κ by mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`.
(d): take J a singleton, respectively finite, and use (b), (c).

(e): for regular κ, cf κ = κ > #J and (c) applies. For the counterexample, the points x_a : T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ a^{1/pⁿ} (a ∈ K_α°) of the disc over K_α (characteristic p, perfect) are pairwise distinct, so #|X| ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ, while each disc ring has cardinality ≤ #K_α^ℵ₀ < κ; the fields K_α are completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples).
acceptance: Affinoid instance (ECD's use in §7–§8): Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is κ-small for every cutoff cardinal κ, its ring having cardinality 2^ℵ₀.
A countable disjoint union of copies of Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is κ-small for every cutoff κ by (c) (#J = ℵ₀ < cf κ).
The counterexample of (e) for κ = κ(ω₁).

nodes.title: Closure properties of κ-small perfectoid spaces: open subspaces, disjoint unions, fibre products
nodes.statement: Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. (a) An open subspace of a κ-small (resp. uniformly κ-small) perfectoid space is κ-small (resp. uniformly κ-small). (b) A disjoint union ⊔_{j∈J} X_j is uniformly κ-small if #J < κ and all X_j are κ'-small for one κ' < κ; finite disjoint unions of κ-small spaces are κ-small. (c) (ECD Proposition 4.4, 'in particular') For morphisms X → Z ← Y of perfectoid spaces with X and Y uniformly κ-small (Z arbitrary), the fibre product X ×_Z Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is uniformly κ-small: if #|X|, #|Y| ≤ λ and all open affinoid rings of X and Y have cardinality ≤ λ (λ ≥ ℵ₀), then X ×_Z Y is covered by at most 2^λ open affinoids U ×_W V with rings of cardinality ≤ λ^ℵ₀ and has at most 2^{2^λ} points. In particular fibre products of κ-small quasicompact (for instance affinoid) perfectoid spaces are κ-small, and the κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces are stable under fibre products. (d) For κ of cofinality ω₁ the unrestricted statement fails: for a perfectoid field L of characteristic p and perfectoid fields K_α ⊇ L (α < ω₁) that are completed perfections of L(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm, with λ_α < κ cofinal in κ, X := ⊔_α Spa(K_α, K_α°) is κ-small but X ×_{Spa(L, L°)} X is not, since Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) has at least λ_α points.
hypotheses: κ uncountable strong limit; Z need not be κ-small in (c).
The fibre product is that of perfectoid spaces over a general perfectoid Tate base (P2), with affinoid charts given by the uniform completed tensor product.
proofSteps: (a): points and open affinoid subspaces of an open V ⊆ X are points and open affinoid subspaces of X.
(b): apply PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (c) to the cover by the charts of the X_j.

(c): the triples (U, V, W) of open affinoids with U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y, W ⊆ Z and U, V mapping into W give an open cover of X ×_Z Y by the U ×_W V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces); choosing one W per pair (U, V) uses at most 2^λ·2^λ charts. The ring of U ×_W V is the uniform completed tensor product of O(U) and O(V) over O(W), of cardinality ≤ (λ·λ·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = λ^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality (b3)); then PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (c) and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality give the bounds. Quasicompact κ-small spaces are uniformly κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space (b)).

(d): X is κ-small (ℵ₁ points; each open affinoid is a finite union of components). For β < λ_α choose a perfectoid field C ⊇ L and elements c_γ ∈ C (γ < λ_α) of absolute value 1 with residues algebraically independent over the residue field of L; x_γ ↦ c_γ and x_γ ↦ d_γ (d_γ = c_γ for γ ≠ β, d_β = c_β + t) are isometric L-embeddings K_α → C, and together they give a point p_β of Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) with |x_β ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_β|(p_β) = |t| and |x_γ ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_γ|(p_β) = 0 for γ ≠ β; so the p_β are pairwise distinct and #|X ×_{Spa L} X| ≥ sup_α λ_α = κ.
acceptance: For X = Y = Z = Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, …), X ×_Z Y = X is κ-small.
Spa(C_p) ×_{Spa(K)} Spa(C_p) for K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧ has infinitely many points and ring of cardinality 2^ℵ₀, hence is κ-small for every cutoff κ.
The counterexample (d) shows that ECD's 'stable under finite products' needs the uniform or quasicompact hypothesis for singular κ.

nodes.title: Tilting preserves κ-smallness
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring A with tilt A♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), #A♭ ≤ (#A)^ℵ₀ and #A ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀·ℵ₀. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit κ and a perfectoid space X with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting), X is κ-small iff X♭ is κ-small, and X is uniformly κ-small iff X♭ is; tilting restricts to an equivalence between κ-small perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid space S and κ-small perfectoid spaces over S♭.
hypotheses: No base field; any characteristic.
proofSteps: #A♭ ≤ (#A)^ℵ₀: as a multiplicative monoid A♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} A ⊆ A^ℕ (ECD Definition 3.9, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).

#A ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀·ℵ₀: A°/ϖ ≅ A♭°/ϖ♭ for a compatible pseudouniformiser (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); each ϖᵏA°/ϖ^{k+1}A° is a quotient of A°/ϖ, so #A°/ϖⁿ ≤ (#A°/ϖ)ⁿ; A° is ϖ-adically complete, so A° = lim A°/ϖⁿ has cardinality ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀; and A = ⋃_n ϖ^{-n}A°.

Spaces: |X| ≅ |X♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), and U ↦ U♭ is a bijection between open affinoid perfectoid subspaces with O(U♭) = O(U)♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting); since κ is a strong limit, λ^ℵ₀ < κ for λ < κ.
acceptance: C_p and its tilt, the completed algebraic closure of F_p((t)), both have cardinality 2^ℵ₀.
The tilt of a κ-small affinoid perfectoid space is κ-small: the diamond Spd of DiamondsAndVStacks:D6 keeps κ-small objects κ-small.

nodes.title: Cofiltered limits of uniformly bounded κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces are κ-small (set-theoretic clause of ECD Proposition 6.4)
nodes.statement: Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). (a) If #Mor(I) ≤ λ and #R_i ≤ λ for all i, with λ infinite, then #R ≤ λ^ℵ₀; so for an uncountable strong limit κ > λ, X is κ-small (and uniformly κ-small). (b) (ECD) If κ is a cutoff cardinal (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal), I is λ-small for some λ < κ and all X_i are κ′-small for one strong limit κ′ < κ, then X is κ-small; if κ′ = κ_λ is a strong limit of cofinality > λ (clause (iii) of the cutoff lemma), then X is even κ_λ-small, so the bound does not grow with the diagram. (c) The uniform bound cannot be dropped: for κ of cofinality ω₁ and a tower of perfectoid fields K_0 ⊆ K_1 ⊆ … ⊆ K_α ⊆ … (α < ω₁) with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, the X_α = Spa(K_α, K_α°) are κ-small, I = ω₁ has fewer than κ elements, and the limit (the completed union) is not κ-small.
hypotheses: The ring-level bound #R ≤ (#Mor(I)·sup_i #R_i)^ℵ₀ is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds; this node states it for P6's κ-small notion.
proofSteps: (a): colim R_i⁺ has cardinality ≤ #Mor(I)·λ ≤ λ, and R⁺ is its ϖ-adic completion (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), in which it is dense, so #R⁺ ≤ λ^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality); R = R⁺[1/ϖ]; then PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
(b): with λ' := max(λ, κ′) < κ apply (a). For κ′ = κ_λ of cofinality > λ, sup_i #R_i < κ_λ (mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`), and #R ≤ (sup)^ℵ₀ < κ_λ as κ_λ is a strong limit.
(c): the completed union has cardinality ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ.
acceptance: ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): X_∞ = lim_J X_J over the finite subsets J of fewer than κ affinoid étale covers is κ-small, with a bound depending only on #O(X).
The tower of (c) shows the necessity of 'one κ′ for all i'.

nodes.title: Size of the affinoid étale site: rings bounded by #O(X)^ℵ₀, fewer than κ isomorphism classes
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and μ(X) := (#R + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀. (a) Every affinoid perfectoid space Y étale over X (Y ∈ X_ét^aff, étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces) has #O_Y(Y) ≤ μ(X) and #|Y| ≤ 2^{μ(X)}. (b) X_ét^aff is essentially small: it has at most 2^{μ(X)} isomorphism classes of objects, and #Hom_X(Y, Y') ≤ 2^{μ(X)} for all objects. (c) If κ is an uncountable strong limit and X is κ-small, then every object of X_ét^aff is κ-small, X_ét^aff has fewer than κ isomorphism classes of objects, and all its Hom-sets have fewer than κ elements; in particular the isomorphism classes of affinoid étale surjections onto X form a set of cardinality < κ (the count in ECD's proof of Lemma 7.18).
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; no size hypothesis in (a), (b).
proofSteps: Local structure (ECD Definition 6.2(ii)): every y ∈ Y has a neighbourhood V ⊆ Y that is a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid W finite étale over a rational subset U ⊆ X (shrink the open sets of the definition; W is affinoid by ECD Definition 6.2(i), PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids); Y is quasicompact, so finitely many such V_1, …, V_n cover Y.

Cardinalities (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality): #O(U) ≤ (#R·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = μ; #O(W) ≤ #O(U)·ℵ₀; #O(V_k) ≤ (#O(W)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = μ; O(Y) embeds into ∏_k O(V_k) (O_Y is a sheaf, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), so #O(Y) ≤ μⁿ = μ; #|Y| ≤ 2^μ by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality.

Counting: an object is determined up to isomorphism by a Tate ring structure on a set of cardinality ≤ μ (ring operations, a ring of definition and a pseudouniformiser), a plus subring, and a continuous ring map R → O(Y): at most (2^μ)^4·μ^{#R} = 2^μ classes; Hom_X(Y, Y') injects into the ring maps O(Y') → O(Y), at most μ^μ = 2^μ.
(c): #R < κ gives μ ≤ 2^{#R+ℵ₀} < κ and 2^μ < κ; κ-smallness of Y by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
acceptance: X = Spa(C, O_C) with C algebraically closed: X_ét^aff is equivalent to finite sets (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point), with countably many isomorphism classes.

X = Spa(K, O_K) for a perfectoid field K: the objects are finite disjoint unions of Spa(L, O_L) with L/K finite separable (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), each of cardinality #K.
