nodes.title: Every affinoid perfectoid space is the cofiltered limit of its κ-small perfectoid quotients (κ-bounded form of ECD Proposition 6.5)
nodes.statement: Let (S, S⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1) with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p divides p in S°, and let A ⊆ S be a subset. Then there is a closed subring S' ⊆ S containing A ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}} with #S' ≤ (#A + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ such that, with the subspace topology, S' is a perfectoid Tate ring, S'° = S' ∩ S°, and (S', S' ∩ S⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit κ and a morphism Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces with #R < κ, the set P_κ(Y/X) of closed subrings S' ⊆ S of cardinality < κ that contain the image of R and for which (S', S' ∩ S⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair, ordered by inclusion, satisfies: (a) it is directed, and every subfamily of cardinality ≤ λ whose members have cardinality ≤ λ, for a λ < κ, has an upper bound of cardinality ≤ λ^ℵ₀; in particular it is ω₁-directed; (b) ⋃ S' = S and ⋃ (S' ∩ S⁺) = S⁺; (c) Y = lim_{S' ∈ P_κ(Y/X)} Spa(S', S' ∩ S⁺) in perfectoid spaces over X, a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces over X whose colimit of plus rings is already complete. For countable A this recovers the final statement of ECD Proposition 6.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition). P_κ(Y/X) is not κ-directed when κ is singular, so the directedness in (a) is the uniformly bounded one.
hypotheses: (S, S⁺) perfectoid; no base field. The upper bound in (a) needs the uniform bound λ on the members.
proofSteps: Construction: A_0 := the subring generated by A ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}}; A_{n+1} := the subring generated by A_n and, for each x ∈ A_n ∩ S°, one chosen y_x ∈ S° with y_x^p − x ∈ ϖ^p S° (it exists because Φ : S°/ϖ → S°/ϖ^p is surjective, ECD Definition 3.1, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); A' := ⋃_n A_n, so #A' ≤ #A + ℵ₀; S' := the closure of A' (mathlib `Subring.topologicalClosure`), of cardinality ≤ (#A + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality).

S' is a complete Tate ring with ring of definition S' ∩ S_0 and pseudouniformiser ϖ, and ϖⁿ(S' ∩ S_0) = S' ∩ ϖⁿS_0 as ϖ^{-1} ∈ S'; bounded subsets of S' are those bounded in S, so S'° = S' ∩ S° (Tau Ceti `powerBoundedSubring`), which is bounded: S' is uniform; p/ϖ^p ∈ S' ∩ S° = S'°.

Frobenius on S'°/ϖ is injective: if y ∈ S'° and y^p ∈ ϖ^p S'° then (y/ϖ)^p ∈ S°, so y/ϖ ∈ S° (S° is integrally closed, Tau Ceti `isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`) and y/ϖ ∈ S'. Surjective onto S'°/ϖ^p: for x ∈ S'° choose x_n ∈ A' with x − x_n ∈ ϖ^p S°; then x_n ∈ A' ∩ S°, y := y_{x_n} ∈ A' ∩ S°, and y^p − x ∈ ϖ^p S° ∩ S' = ϖ^p S'°. S' ∩ S⁺ is open, integrally closed and contained in S'°.

(a): apply the construction to the union of the family (cardinality ≤ λ·λ). (b): each s ∈ S lies in the S' generated by {s} and the image of R. (c): by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces the limit is Spa of the ϖ-adic completion of ⋃ (S' ∩ S⁺) = S⁺, which is already complete; each Spa(S', S' ∩ S⁺) is κ-small by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
Singular κ: a family of cf κ members with cardinalities cofinal in κ has no upper bound in P_κ(Y/X).
acceptance: For S = K⟨T_β^{1/p^∞} : β < µ⟩ (perfectoid polydisc in µ ≥ κ variables over a perfectoid field K with #K < κ), the subrings K⟨T_β^{1/p^∞} : β ∈ F⟩ for countable F lie in P_κ, and Y is their limit.
ECD's use in the proof of Proposition 8.2: a κ′-small affinoid over X is a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoids over X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence).

nodes.title: ECD Proposition 6.4(iv) in the form used by the pro-étale calculus: affinoid étale objects and surjectivity descend to a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces over a small index category, with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺, R = R⁺[1/ϖ]). For a perfectoid space T write T_ét^aff for the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over T (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces). (a) (ECD Proposition 6.4(iv), which is AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv) The base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét^aff → X_ét^aff. (b) (Descent of surjectivity) If Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff and Y_i ×_{X_i} X → X is surjective, there is j_0 → i such that Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j → X_j is surjective for every j → j_0. (c) (Relation to the quasicompact separated stage of P5) If Y ∈ X_ét^aff and Z_i → X_i is a qcqs étale model of Y (Z_i ×_{X_i} X ≅ Y; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects, ECD 6.4(ii)), then Z_i ×_{X_i} X_j is affinoid perfectoid and isomorphic over X_j to the model given by (a) for all j beyond some j_0. Affinoidness at a finite stage is the content of (a) and is not a consequence of ECD 6.4(ii)–(iii) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations (c)). (d) (Relative form) If B is an affinoid perfectoid space and the X_i → B are compatible étale maps (for instance a pro-étale presentation of X over B), then every Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff and every Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j lies in B_ét^aff, so the finite-stage models of (a) are affinoid étale over B. (e) The equivalences of ECD 6.4 (i)–(iv) are compatible with the inclusions X_fét ⊆ X_ét^aff ⊆ X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs (AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4). No step uses v-descent, a diamond atlas or the comparison of analytic adic spaces with diamonds.
hypotheses: X_i affinoid perfectoid of any characteristic, over no base field; I small and cofiltered.
The equivalence (a) is imported from AdicEtaleGeometry:A3; this node adds the consequences (b)–(d) that the proofs of ECD Lemma 7.11(i), Lemma 7.18 and Proposition 8.5 use.
proofSteps: (a): cite AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv (full faithfulness from ECD 6.4(ii); essential surjectivity in characteristic p through Huber's standard étale presentation, transported by tilting).

(b): the image V_i of |Y_i| in |X_i| is a quasicompact open (étale maps are open, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open; Y_i is quasicompact). Since |Y_i ×_{X_i} T| → |Y_i| ×_{|X_i|} |T| is surjective for étale Y_i → X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), the image of |Y| in |X| is the preimage of V_i, which is |X| by hypothesis. The preimages C_j of the closed set |X_i| ∖ V_i in |X_j| (j → i) form a cofiltered system of spectral spaces along spectral maps whose limit is its preimage in |X| = lim |X_j| (P5, ECD 6.4(o)), which is empty; so some C_{j_0} is empty (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces), and then C_j = ∅ for j → j_0, which by the same surjectivity means Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j → X_j is surjective.
(c): AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations (c).

(d): composites of étale maps are étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open) and fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
(e): AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4.
acceptance: ECD Lemma 7.18: an affinoid étale cover of X_∞ = lim_J X_J comes from some X_J by (a) and stays a cover there by (b); it splits over X_{J'} for J' ⊋ J containing it.

nodes.title: Affinoid pro-étale morphisms and pro-étale presentations
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space). f is affinoid pro-étale if Y = Spa(S, S⁺) and X = Spa(R, R⁺) are affinoid perfectoid and there are a small cofiltered category I, a functor i ↦ (Y_i → X) from I to X_ét^aff (affinoid perfectoid spaces Y_i = Spa(S_i, S_i⁺) with an étale structure map to X in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2, and X-morphisms as transition maps) and an X-isomorphism Y ≅ lim_i Y_i, the limit being taken in perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: S⁺ ≅ the ϖ-adic completion of colim S_i⁺ for a pseudouniformiser ϖ of R, and S = S⁺[1/ϖ]). The data (I, (Y_i), the isomorphism) is a pro-étale presentation of f. Conventions: the transition maps are X-morphisms between étale X-spaces and hence étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); they are not required to be surjective or finite étale, which distinguishes these presentations from those of Scholze 2013 used in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism; I is small but of arbitrary size; being affinoid pro-étale is the existence of a presentation. X_proét^aff denotes the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces over X on the affinoid pro-étale X-spaces. Basic facts recorded with the definition: every étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid pro-étale (constant presentation); |Y| = lim |Y_i| (ECD 6.4(o)); the image of |Y| in |X| is the intersection of the quasicompact open images of the |Y_i|, hence pro-constructible and stable under generalisation.
hypotheses: X and Y affinoid perfectoid is part of the definition; perfectoidness of the limit is supplied by P5.
ECD writes Y = lim Y_i; in a formalisation the presentation is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces over X together with the étaleness of its legs' index objects.
proofSteps: Define `ProEtalePresentation f` as a structure with fields: a small cofiltered category I, a functor I ⥤ X_ét^aff, and an isomorphism over X from Y to the limit of its composite with the forgetful functor to perfectoid spaces; define `IsAffinoidProEtale f` as its nonemptiness.
Constant presentation: for Y ∈ X_ét^aff take I = ∗.

Underlying space: |Y| ≅ lim |Y_i| by P5 (ECD 6.4(o)); the image of |Y| → |X| equals ⋂_i im(|Y_i| → |X|): for x in the intersection the fibres of |Y_i| over x are nonempty spectral spaces with spectral transition maps, so their limit, the fibre of |Y|, is nonempty (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); each image is a quasicompact open (étale maps are open, P3).
acceptance: Rational subsets, finite étale maps of affinoids and their composites are affinoid pro-étale.
Zariski closed immersions are affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale).

nodes.title: Pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale if for every y ∈ Y there are an open neighbourhood V ⊆ Y of y and an open subset U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U such that V and U are affinoid perfectoid and f|_V : V → U is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map). Conventions: V and U can be chosen rational inside any given neighbourhoods of y and f(y) (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); X_proét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X with all X-morphisms, which are automatically pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits); for κ-small X, X_proét,κ is its full subcategory of κ-small objects. Pro-étale morphisms need not be open, need not be locally of finite type, and being pro-étale is local on the source and, for open covers, on the target, but not local on the target for the pro-étale topology. This is not Mathlib's pro-étale site of a scheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`, defined by weakly étale maps) nor Scholze 2013's X_proét of a locally noetherian adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected).
hypotheses: f an arbitrary morphism of perfectoid spaces, over no base field.
The definition asks for affinoid V and U; ECD's 'open subset U' is taken affinoid, as the restriction f|_V must be affinoid pro-étale.
proofSteps: Define `IsProEtale f` by the stated local condition with V and U open affinoid perfectoid subspaces.
Record: affinoid pro-étale maps are pro-étale; étale maps are pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); pro-étaleness is local on the source and for open covers of the target.

nodes.title: The product X × S of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set, and its relative form X ×_{S₀} S
nodes.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, φ : |X| → S₀ a continuous map to a profinite set and S → S₀ a continuous map of profinite sets. Write S → S₀ as a cofiltered limit of maps of finite discrete sets S_k → S₀,k (k ∈ K) compatible with S → S₀ (mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, `DiscreteQuotient`). Each φ_k : |X| → S₀,k is locally constant, so X = ⊔_{t∈S₀,k} X_{k,t} with X_{k,t} := φ_k⁻¹(t) open and closed, hence a rational subset cut out by an idempotent of O(X) (O_X is a sheaf, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity); X ×_{S₀,k} S_k := ⊔_{s∈S_k} X_{k,image(s)} is affinoid perfectoid and affinoid étale over X. Define X ×_{S₀} S := lim_k X ×_{S₀,k} S_k (limit in perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), and X × S := X ×_∗ S = lim_k X × S_k (ECD, after Definition 7.8). Properties: (a) universal property: for every perfectoid space T over X, X-morphisms T → X ×_{S₀} S correspond to continuous maps |T| → S over S₀; in particular the construction is independent of the presentation and functorial in S → S₀; (b) X ×_{S₀} S → X is affinoid pro-étale with the above pro-étale presentation; (c) |X ×_{S₀} S| = |X| ×_{S₀} S; (d) O⁺(X × S) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X)) and O(X × S) = C⁰(S, O(X)), continuous maps for the ϖ-adic topology on O⁺(X) (for X = Spa(K, O_K) this is ECD's Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K))); (e) for a morphism T → X, T ×_X (X ×_{S₀} S) = T ×_{S₀} S; (f) (X × S)♭ = X♭ × S; (g) for S locally profinite, X × S is glued from the X × S_c over the compact open subsets S_c ⊆ S and is pro-étale, not affinoid unless S is compact, over X.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; S, S₀ profinite (locally profinite in (g)).
X × S is not the disjoint union of #S copies of X when S is infinite.
proofSteps: Presentation: by `Profinite.asLimit`, S₀ = lim of its finite discrete quotients and S = lim of those finite discrete quotients of S compatible with them; K is cofiltered.
Clopen decomposition: an open and closed U ⊆ |X| gives O(X) = O(U) × O(X ∖ U) by the sheaf property, hence an idempotent e with U = {|e| ≥ 1}, a rational subset.

(a): X-morphisms T → X × S_k are decompositions of T into open and closed pieces indexed by S_k, i.e. locally constant maps |T| → S_k; passing to the limit gives continuous maps |T| → S (maps to a profinite set are compatible systems of maps to its finite quotients); the relative case adds compatibility with φ.
(b): each X ×_{S₀,k} S_k is a finite disjoint union of rational subsets of X, hence in X_ét^aff.
(c): P5 (ECD 6.4(o)) and the computation for finite S_k.
(d): colim_k Map(S_k, O⁺(X)) is the ring of locally constant maps S → O⁺(X), and its ϖ-adic completion is lim_n C⁰(S, O⁺(X)/ϖⁿ) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X)) (mathlib `LocallyConstant`, `ContinuousMap`).

(e): limits commute with fibre products (P2 fibre products, P5 limits). (f): tilting commutes with cofiltered limits and finite disjoint unions (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting).

nodes.title: Maps from a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces to a qcqs étale space factor through a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, (Y_i)_{i∈I} a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces over X (compatible structure maps; no étaleness assumed) with limit Y = lim_i Y_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), and T → X an étale morphism from a quasicompact quasiseparated perfectoid space (for instance T ∈ X_ét^aff). Then the canonical map colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, T) → Hom_X(Y, T) is bijective: every X-morphism Y → T factors through some Y_i, and two X-morphisms Y_i → T that agree on Y agree on Y_j for some j → i.
hypotheses: T quasicompact quasiseparated and étale over X; the Y_i need not be étale over X.
proofSteps: Hom_X(Y, T) = Hom_Y(Y, Y ×_X T), sections of the base change, which is qcqs étale over Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

For a fixed i, Y ×_X T = (Y_i ×_X T) ×_{Y_i} Y and Y = Y_i ×_{Y_i} Y are base changes of objects of (Y_i)_ét,qcqs; full faithfulness in ECD Proposition 6.4(ii) for the system (Y_j)_{j→i} (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects) gives Hom_Y(Y, Y ×_X T) = colim_j Hom_{Y_j}(Y_j, Y_j ×_X T).
Hom_{Y_j}(Y_j, Y_j ×_X T) = Hom_X(Y_j, T), compatibly in j.

(Alternative route, Berkeley Lemma 8.2.4: T is locally a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps; for rational embeddings use the constructible-topology argument on |Y| = lim |Y_i|, for finite étale maps ECD 6.4(i).)

nodes.title: The canonical presentation: Y is affinoid pro-étale over X iff Y is the limit of all affinoid étale X-spaces under it
nodes.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space and g : Y → X a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space. Let E_Y be the category of pairs (T, t) with T ∈ X_ét^aff and t : Y → T an X-morphism, with morphisms (T, t) → (T', t') the X-morphisms u : T → T' with u ∘ t = t' — the category of elements of Hom_X(Y, −) on X_ét^aff. Then: (a) E_Y is essentially small and cofiltered; (b) there is a canonical X-morphism c_Y : Y → lim_{E_Y} T (limit over a small skeleton, in perfectoid spaces); (c) g is affinoid pro-étale iff c_Y is an isomorphism; (d) for any pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i, the functor I → E_Y, i ↦ (Y_i, pr_i), is initial.
hypotheses: Y and X affinoid perfectoid.
proofSteps: (a): X_ét^aff is essentially small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound) and has finite limits: X is final; T_1 ×_{T_0} T_2 is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and étale over X (T_1 → T_0 is étale as a map of étale X-spaces; base change and composition, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); the equalizer of u, v : T_1 ⇉ T_2 is T_1 ×_{T_2 ×_X T_2} T_2 along (u, v) and the diagonal, étale over T_1 because the diagonal is a map of étale X-spaces. Hom_X(Y, −) preserves finite limits, so its category of elements is cofiltered (mathlib `IsCofiltered.of_hasFiniteLimits` applied to E_Y, which inherits the finite limits).
(b): the (T, t) form a cone over the forgetful functor E_Y → perfectoid spaces over X.

(d): by mathlib `Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`: every (T, t) receives a morphism from some (Y_i, pr_i) since t factors through some Y_i, and two such factorizations agree after some j → i — both by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage.

(c): if g is affinoid pro-étale, (d) and mathlib `Functor.Initial.limitIso` identify lim_{E_Y} T with lim_I Y_i = Y, compatibly with c_Y; conversely, if c_Y is an isomorphism, a small skeleton of E_Y is a pro-étale presentation.
acceptance: For Y ∈ X_ét^aff, (Y, id) is initial in E_Y and c_Y is the identity.

nodes.title: Affinoid pro-étale spaces over X are the pro-objects of the affinoid étale site (ECD Proposition 7.10)
nodes.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, X_ét^aff the category of étale maps Y → X from affinoid perfectoid spaces (essentially small and finitely complete, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation) and X_proét^aff the category of affinoid pro-étale maps Y → X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map). Let Pro(X_ét^aff) be the pro-category (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces; the opposite of Mathlib's Ind of the opposite category), with objects formal limits "lim" Y_i over small cofiltered categories and Hom("lim" Y_i, "lim" Z_j) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j). Then the realisation functor ρ_X : Pro(X_ét^aff) → X_proét^aff, "lim" Y_i ↦ lim Y_i (limit in perfectoid spaces), is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse Y ↦ "lim"_{(T,t)∈E_Y} T. Equivalently, for affinoid pro-étale Y = lim Y_i and Z = lim Z_j over X, Hom_X(Y, Z) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j).
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; Pro is taken with small cofiltered index categories after replacing X_ét^aff by a small skeleton.
proofSteps: ρ_X on morphisms: a compatible family of classes in colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j) induces maps lim Y_i → Z_j and hence lim Y_i → lim Z_j; functoriality is formal.
Essential surjectivity: every affinoid pro-étale Y has a pro-étale presentation, by definition.

Full faithfulness: Hom_X(Y, lim_j Z_j) = lim_j Hom_X(Y, Z_j) by the universal property of the limit, and Hom_X(lim_i Y_i, Z_j) = colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j) by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage.
Quasi-inverse: PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation (c).
acceptance: X = Spa(C, O_C), C algebraically closed: X_ét^aff ≃ FinSet, and the theorem becomes Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite ≃ X_proét^aff, S ↦ X × S (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point).

nodes.title: κ-small affinoid pro-étale spaces are the pro-objects with fewer than κ indices (ECD Proposition 7.10, κ-part)
nodes.statement: Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal and X a κ-small affinoid perfectoid space. (a) An affinoid pro-étale Y → X is κ-small iff it admits a pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i with #Mor(I) < κ; all Y_i ∈ X_ét^aff are then κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound). (b) Let Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) be the full subcategory of Pro(X_ét^aff) of pro-objects isomorphic to one indexed by a cofiltered category with fewer than κ morphisms. The realisation ρ_X of PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence restricts to an equivalence Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) ≃ X_proét,κ^aff with the full subcategory of κ-small affinoid pro-étale X-spaces. (c) Every affinoid pro-étale Y → X is the limit, along a directed poset, of κ-small affinoid pro-étale Y_J → X: for a presentation indexed by I, J runs over the cofiltered subcategories (not required to be full) of I with fewer than κ morphisms and Y_J := lim_{i∈J} Y_i (the pro-étale form of the first step of ECD's proof of Proposition 8.2; for arbitrary affinoid Y see PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs).
hypotheses: κ uncountable strong limit; X κ-small affinoid. ECD states (b) without proof.
proofSteps: (a) ⇒: by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation Y = lim over a small skeleton of E_Y. Objects of X_ét^aff have fewer than κ isomorphism classes and rings of cardinality ≤ μ(X) < κ; #Hom_X(Y, T) ≤ #O(Y)^{#O(T)} < κ as κ is a strong limit and #O(Y) < κ; so the skeleton has fewer than κ objects and morphisms (sums of fewer than κ cardinals uniformly bounded below κ).
(a) ⇐: #colim_i O⁺(Y_i) ≤ #Mor(I)·μ(X) < κ, so #O(Y) < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits (a)), and Y is κ-small by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
(b): from (a), since both sides are full subcategories and ρ_X is an equivalence.

(c): start with at most λ objects and morphisms of I, where λ is infinite. Include their sources and targets, identities and finite composites; choose cones for finite diagrams, including equalizers for parallel pairs, and repeat countably many times. The resulting subcategory is cofiltered with at most λ morphisms. It must not be required to be full: the ambient hom-sets can be arbitrarily large. The poset of all cofiltered subcategories with fewer than κ morphisms is directed by applying this construction to the union of any two. Its union contains every object and morphism of I, so compatible cones give lim_J Y_J = lim_I Y_i = Y; each Y_J is κ-small by (a). This poset is directed; κ-directedness is not asserted.
acceptance: X = Spa(C, O_C): X × S is κ-small iff S is the limit of fewer than κ finite sets, and then #C⁰(S, C) < κ.
ECD Proposition 8.2: a κ'-small affinoid pro-étale Y → X is a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoid pro-étale Y_J → X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence).

The small-subcategory construction cannot demand fullness: the one-object category of an arbitrarily large commutative monoid with an absorbing zero is cofiltered, but its only nonempty full subcategory contains all endomorphisms. A non-full subcategory generated by the identity and zero is small and cofiltered.

nodes.title: Affinoid pro-étale spaces over a geometric point are products with profinite sets
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed perfectoid field and X = Spa(C, O_C). (a) The functor F ↦ X × F = ⊔_F X from finite sets to X_ét^aff is an equivalence. (b) The functor S ↦ X × S from profinite sets to X_proét^aff (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set) is an equivalence: every affinoid pro-étale Y → X is X-isomorphic to X × S for a profinite set S, and S ≅ |Y|. (c) The hypothesis C⁺ = O_C is needed: for an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊊ O_C the rational open immersion Spa(C, O_C) ↪ Spa(C, C⁺) is affinoid étale and not of the form Spa(C, C⁺) × S.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed, with the valuation subring O_C.
proofSteps: (a): |X| is one point. An étale Y → X is locally an open subspace of a finite étale W → U with U ⊆ X open, so U = X; finite étale C-algebras are products of copies of C (C algebraically closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields); open subsets of X × F are unions of copies of X; Y quasicompact gives Y ≅ X × F with F = |Y| finite. X-morphisms X × F → X × F' are continuous C-algebra maps C^{F'} → C^F, i.e. maps F → F'.

(b): by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence and (a), X_proét^aff ≃ Pro(FinSet); Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces restricted to Hausdorff objects: a profinite set is the limit of its finite discrete quotients, mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, and continuous maps to a finite set factor through one); the composite is S ↦ X × S by construction.
(c): for a ∈ O_C ∖ C⁺ the rational subset {|a| ≤ 1} of Spa(C, C⁺) is its generic point Spa(C, O_C); a space X × S → X is surjective or empty.

nodes.title: Zariski closed immersions are affinoid pro-étale: the rational-intersection presentation (ECD Remark 7.9)
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and I ⊆ R an ideal. For a finite subset F ⊆ I let U_F := {x ∈ X : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all f ∈ F} = X(F/1), a rational subset (F ∪ {1} generates the unit ideal). (a) V(I) := {x ∈ X : |f(x)| = 0 for all f ∈ I} equals ⋂_F U_F. (b) The cofiltered limit Z_I := lim_F U_F over the finite subsets of I ordered by inclusion (a limit in perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces) is affinoid perfectoid, and Z_I → X is a Zariski closed immersion in the sense of ECD Definition 5.7(i) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion) with |Z_I| = V(I) as a subspace of |X|. (c) Every Zariski closed immersion Z → X of perfectoid spaces with vanishing locus V(I) is X-isomorphic to Z_I. In particular (ECD Remark 7.9) every Zariski closed immersion Z ↪ X into an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid pro-étale, with pro-étale presentation (U_F)_F by rational open immersions. The proof uses neither ECD Theorem 5.8 nor PerfectoidQuotients:Q4: strong Zariski closedness is not needed.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; I any ideal of R = O_X(X) (its closure defines the same locus).
The ideal property of I is used: ϖ^{-n}f ∈ I for f ∈ I, which turns 'bounded by 1' into 'zero'.
proofSteps: (a): ⋂_F U_F ⊇ V(I) is clear. Conversely, if x ∈ ⋂_F U_F and f ∈ I, then ϖ^{-n}f ∈ I (ϖ a unit of R, Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`), so |f(x)| ≤ |ϖ(x)|ⁿ for all n; as x is continuous and ϖ topologically nilpotent, the |ϖ(x)|ⁿ become smaller than every element of the value group of x, so f(x) = 0. The membership condition of U_F is Tau Ceti `mem_rationalSubset_iff` with denominator 1.

(b): Z_I exists and is affinoid perfectoid by P5. Each U_F → X is an open immersion, hence an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Hom(T, Z_I) = lim_F Hom(T, U_F) ⊆ Hom(T, X), so Z_I → X is an injection. |Z_I| = lim_F |U_F| = ⋂_F U_F = V(I) with the subspace topology (P5, ECD 6.4(o), and the inclusions U_F ⊆ X are embeddings). V(I) is closed, so Z_I → X is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion, ECD Definition 5.6), cut out by I, i.e. Zariski closed.

(c): Z → X and Z_I → X are injections that are homeomorphisms onto the same subspace V(I). By ECD Proposition 5.3(iv) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria) an injection is final among maps whose underlying continuous map factors continuously through its image, so each factors uniquely through the other and they are X-isomorphic.
The U_F → X are rational open immersions, hence objects of X_ét^aff, and (U_F)_F is a pro-étale presentation (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map).

nodes.title: Zariski closed equals strongly Zariski closed (ECD Theorem 5.8, imported from PerfectoidQuotients Q4)
nodes.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid space X = Spa(R, R⁺) and a morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces, f is a Zariski closed immersion if and only if f is strongly Zariski closed. The direction strongly Zariski closed ⇒ Zariski closed, i.e. the case of an already given surjective perfectoid quotient R → S, is proved in P4 (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed). The direction Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed is ECD Theorem 5.8 and is imported from PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed (Bhatt–Scholze, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, via surjectivity of perfectoidization); it is not proved here. Consequences: for every ideal I ⊆ R the map R → S_I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed) is surjective with kernel I^perf = {h : |h| = 0 on V(I)}, S_I⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺, and R⁺ → S_I⁺ is almost surjective. For R = ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and I = (T − 1) this gives R ↠ C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p), contradicting Scholze's Remark II.2.4 and Bhatt's Warning 9.4.2. No node of the layers P0–P7 uses the stronger direction (the diagonal and Zariski closed pro-étale statements of this layer need only the elementary one); PerfectoidSpaces:P8 and AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 use it. The comparison is recorded after P4 because PerfectoidQuotients Q4 is built on P4.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; the imported theorem is used by PerfectoidSpaces:P8 and AdicEtaleGeometry:A3.
proofSteps: ⇐: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed.

⇒: PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed (ECD Theorem 5.8); with PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal the Zariski closed immersion is Z_I, and Q4's closed perfectoid quotient R' = S_perfd[1/ϖ] is S_I.
Almost surjectivity on plus rings then follows from PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings (ECD notes that BS22 Theorem 7.4 also gives it).

Alternative routes recorded for the owner of ECD 5.8: Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.12 (Bhatt) proves surjectivity of a perfectoid ring onto the uniform completion of A/I through André's flatness lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma); in characteristic p the statement is Scholze's elementary Lemma II.2.5.

nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i, and g : X' → X a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space. Then Y' := X' ×_X Y is affinoid perfectoid and f' : Y' → X' is affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation Y' = lim_i X' ×_X Y_i; moreover |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is surjective.
hypotheses: X, X', Y affinoid perfectoid.
proofSteps: X' ×_X Y_i is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and étale over X' (base change, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), so it lies in X'_ét^aff; the transition maps are X'-morphisms.
Fibre products commute with cofiltered limits in perfectoid spaces (both are limits and exist here: P2, P5), so lim_i (X' ×_X Y_i) = X' ×_X lim_i Y_i = Y'.

Surjectivity on points: each |X' ×_X Y_i| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y_i| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change); over a point (x', y) the fibres form a cofiltered system of nonempty spectral spaces, with nonempty limit (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

nodes.title: Cofiltered limits of affinoid pro-étale X-spaces are affinoid pro-étale (the geometric form of Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C))
nodes.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space and (Y_k)_{k∈K} a small cofiltered diagram in X_proét^aff (affinoid pro-étale X-spaces and X-morphisms). Then its limit Y = lim_k Y_k in perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces) is affinoid pro-étale over X and is the limit of the diagram in X_proét^aff. Under the equivalence ρ_X of PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence, Y corresponds to the limit in Pro(X_ét^aff) of the corresponding pro-objects: ρ_X preserves cofiltered limits.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid; K small cofiltered.
proofSteps: By PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation it suffices that c_Y : Y → lim_{E_Y} T is an isomorphism. Fix a pseudouniformiser ϖ of O(X). By P5, O⁺(lim_{E_Y} T)/ϖ = colim_{E_Y} O⁺(T)/ϖ and O⁺(Y)/ϖ = colim_k O⁺(Y_k)/ϖ = colim_k colim_{E_{Y_k}} O⁺(T)/ϖ.

The comparison colim_{E_Y} O⁺(T)/ϖ → O⁺(Y)/ϖ is surjective, since every object (T, Y_k → T) of E_{Y_k} gives an object of E_Y; and injective: if a ∈ O⁺(T)/ϖ dies in O⁺(Y)/ϖ, factor t : Y → T through some Y_k and then through some object T' of E_{Y_k} (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage, twice); a dies in O⁺(T'')/ϖ for some T'' further along E_{Y_{k'}}, which gives a morphism (T'', ·) → (T, t) of E_Y killing a.
Both O⁺-rings are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free, so c_Y is an isomorphism on O⁺ and O, hence of affinoid perfectoid spaces over X (P5).
Pro side: the natural functor Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C) and the cofiltered limits of Pro(C) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces) correspond to this limit under ρ_X.

nodes.title: Étale maps are pro-étale, and affinoid pro-étale maps restrict to affinoid opens
nodes.statement: (a) Every étale morphism of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale, and every étale morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid pro-étale. (b) If f : Y → X is affinoid pro-étale, U ⊆ X is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace and V ⊆ f⁻¹(U) is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace, then f|_V : V → U is affinoid pro-étale. (c) Consequently f : Y → X is pro-étale iff every y ∈ Y has rational neighbourhoods V ∋ y and U ∋ f(y), inside any given neighbourhoods, with f(V) ⊆ U and f|_V affinoid pro-étale; pro-étaleness is local on the source, local on the target for open covers, and stable under restriction to open subspaces of the source and over open subspaces of the target.
hypotheses: No hypotheses beyond those stated.
proofSteps: (a): by ECD Definition 6.2(ii), near y an étale map is V ↪ W → U with V open in W and W finite étale over an open U ⊆ X; shrink U to a rational subset U' ∋ f(y), replace W by W ×_U U', which is affinoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), and V by a rational subset of W ×_U U' containing y; the result is affinoid étale over U', hence affinoid pro-étale.

(b): f⁻¹(U) = U ×_X Y → U is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change); V ↪ f⁻¹(U) is an open immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces, hence affinoid étale; compose (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
(c): combine (b) with PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map and the fact that rational subsets form a basis of each affinoid perfectoid space.
acceptance: A rational subset of a rational subset is affinoid pro-étale over X.

nodes.title: X_proét^aff has all small limits, computed in perfectoid spaces (ECD Lemma 7.11(iv))
nodes.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid space X, the category X_proét^aff has all small limits, and they are computed in perfectoid spaces over X: the final object is id_X; fibre products Y ×_Z Y' of objects of X_proét^aff are the fibre products of perfectoid spaces; cofiltered limits are the limits of P5; every small limit is a cofiltered limit of finite limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces, and the inclusion X_proét^aff → (perfectoid spaces over X) preserves all small limits. Under ρ_X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence) this is the statement that Pro(C) has all small limits for C = X_ét^aff finitely complete.
hypotheses: X affinoid perfectoid.
proofSteps: Final object: id_X.

Fibre products: Y ×_Z Y' is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces); Y → Z is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation), so its base change Y ×_Z Y' → Y' is (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change), and so is the composite with Y' → X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).

nodes.title: Stability of pro-étale morphisms: composition, base change, cancellation and limits (ECD Lemma 7.11)
nodes.statement: (i) Composites of pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale. (ii) If f : Y → X is pro-étale and g : X' → X is any morphism of perfectoid spaces, then f' : X' ×_X Y → X' is pro-étale. (iii) If Y → X and Y' → X are pro-étale, every X-morphism Y → Y' is pro-étale. (iv) For affinoid X, X_proét^aff has all small limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits). The affinoid versions of (i)–(iii) are PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition, P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change and P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation. Consequences: X_proét (perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X, with all X-morphisms) contains X_ét, is closed under fibre products, which are computed in perfectoid spaces, and for Y ∈ X_proét, Y_proét ≃ X_proét/Y. These are the stability assertions the big and small pro-étale sites of DiamondsAndVStacks:D2 rest on; pro-étaleness is not claimed to be local on the target for the pro-étale topology.
hypotheses: Arbitrary perfectoid spaces in (i)–(iii); X affinoid in (iv).
proofSteps: (ii): for y' ∈ X' ×_X Y over x' ∈ X' and y ∈ Y, choose affinoid V ∋ y and U ⊇ f(V) with V → U affinoid pro-étale and an affinoid U' ⊆ g⁻¹(U) containing x'; U' ×_U V is an open subspace of X' ×_X Y containing y', and U' ×_U V → U' is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change).

(i): for z ∈ Z choose V_Y ∋ g(z), U ⊆ X with V_Y → U affinoid pro-étale, and V_Z ∋ z, W ⊆ Y with V_Z → W affinoid pro-étale; shrink to a rational W' ⊆ W ∩ V_Y containing g(z) and V_Z' ⊆ V_Z ∩ g⁻¹(W') (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); then V_Z' → W' → V_Y → U is a composite of affinoid pro-étale maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).

(iii): for y ∈ Y choose a rational U ⊆ X containing the image of y over which both Y and Y' are affinoid pro-étale near y and g(y), shrink to rational V ∋ y and V' ∋ g(y) with g(V) ⊆ V' affinoid pro-étale over U (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking), and apply PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation to V → V' over U.
(iv): PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits.

Consequences: fibre products Y ×_Z Y' in X_proét are pro-étale over Y' by (iii) and (ii) and over X by (i); étale maps are pro-étale by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking (a); the slice statement is (i) and (iii).

nodes.title: Diagonals and graphs of morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. (a) The diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is pro-étale; if X = Spa(R, R⁺) and Y = Spa(S, S⁺) are affinoid, Δ_f is a Zariski closed immersion, cut out by the kernel of the multiplication map S ⊗̂_R S → S, and affinoid pro-étale. (b) For morphisms Y → X and Y' → X and an X-morphism g : Y → Y', the graph Γ_g : Y → Y ×_X Y' is pro-étale, affinoid pro-étale when X, Y, Y' are affinoid.
hypotheses: f arbitrary; no separatedness or finiteness hypothesis.
proofSteps: (a), affinoid case: S ⊗̂_R S → S is surjective, so Δ_f is strongly Zariski closed (ECD Proposition 5.9, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion), hence Zariski closed with ideal the kernel (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed), hence affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale).

(a), general case: for y ∈ Y choose an affinoid W ⊆ X containing f(y) and an affinoid V ⊆ f⁻¹(W) containing y; V ×_W V is an open affinoid subspace of Y ×_X Y (P2) with Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_W V) = V and Δ_f|_V = Δ_{V/W}, which is affinoid pro-étale; so Δ_f is pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map).

(b): Γ_g is the base change of Δ_{Y'/X} along g ×_X id : Y ×_X Y' → Y' ×_X Y', so it is pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits (ii)); in the affinoid case use PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change.

nodes.title: Perfectoid tilde-limits X ~ lim X_i of analytic adic spaces
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ X_i a functor from I to analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5: every point analytic) whose transition morphisms f_a: X_j → X_i (a: j → i) are quasicompact and quasiseparated, X a perfectoid space in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (ECD Definition 3.19: locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, of characteristic 0 or p, no base field), and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i)_i a compatible family (f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i). The pair (X, φ) is a perfectoid tilde-limit of (X_i), written X ~ lim_i X_i, if it is a tilde-limit for Huber's carrier ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity in the generality of Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1, i.e. (a) the continuous map |X| → lim_i |X_i| into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`) is a homeomorphism, and (b) every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X such that the union, over i ∈ I and over open subsets V ⊆ X_i with φ_i(U) ⊆ V, of the images of the restriction maps O_{X_i}(V) → A is dense in A. Conventions pinned: (i) the index category is cofiltered and only the transition maps, not the X_i, are required to be quasicompact and quasiseparated; (ii) no perfectoid base field is fixed: the X_i may be of characteristic 0 or p, and X may lie over a different base than the X_i (Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: the X_i over Q_p, X perfectoid; Scholze's universal cover of an affinoid over Q_p with limit over C_p); (iii) the two conditions (a) and (b) are independent and both are required (tests below); (iv) a tilde-limit is not a categorical limit in adic spaces: X ~ X_0 may hold with X ≇ X_0 (Scholze–Weinstein after Proposition 2.4.4). Equivalent forms of (b), used throughout the stage: (b′) there is an open cover of X by affinoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) for which colim_{(i, V)} O_{X_i}(V) → A has dense image, V running over open affinoids of X_i through which U → X_i factors (Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1); (b″) the same with U affinoid perfectoid and V a quasicompact open at one level (the good affinoid perfectoids of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid; Scholze's survey Definition 2.20). The equivalences (b) ⇔ (b′) ⇔ (b″) given (a) are PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis.
hypotheses: I small and cofiltered; transition maps of (X_i) quasicompact and quasiseparated; each X_i an analytic adic space (sheafy, anchor Layer 5).
X a perfectoid space (sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy) and φ a compatible family of morphisms of adic spaces.
Only the density clause is formulated with sections; the weaker residue-field variant of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit.
proofSteps: Definition: the predicate is the conjunction of (a) and (b); (a) uses the limit of underlying topological spaces, (b) the sheaf O_X and the presheaves O_{X_i} on open subsets.

The predicate is H0's Huber tilde-limit for the underlying adic spaces, read with Scholze–Weinstein's hypotheses on the system (transition maps qcqs rather than all X_i qcqs); the compatibility test below records the agreement when all spaces are qcqs.

The equivalent forms (b′), (b″) are proved in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis; the relation with the residue-field variant is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit.

nodes.title: Residue-field tilde-limits X ~′ lim X_i over locally noetherian adic spaces (Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14)
nodes.statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category, (X_i) an I-indexed system of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space: covered by Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X a perfectoid space and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i) a compatible family. Then X ~′ lim X_i (Scholze's notation X ~ lim X_i of Definition 7.14, written ~′ in Scholze–Weinstein after Theorem 2.4.7) means: (a) |X| → lim_i |X_i| is a homeomorphism, and (c) for every x ∈ X with images x_i = φ_i(x), the map of completed residue fields colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^ has dense image, where k(y)^ is the completion of the residue field of O_{Y,y} for the valuation of y (equivalently, colim_i k(x_i) → k(x) has dense image for the valuation topologies). Conventions: no perfectoid base field is fixed (Scholze 2012 works over a perfectoid field K; the definition and the results of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison use only that X is perfectoid and the X_i are qcqs locally noetherian); by Remark 7.15, (a) forces |X| to be spectral, in particular X quasicompact and quasiseparated.
hypotheses: Every X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; transition maps are then automatically qcqs.

The density condition is pointwise on residue fields; the sectionwise condition of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit implies it (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit).
proofSteps: Definition by the two conditions (a), (c).

Remark 7.15: the X_i are spectral with spectral transition maps (qcqs adic spaces and qcqs morphisms), so lim |X_i| is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces; Stacks Lemma 5.24.5), and (a) transports this to |X|.

nodes.title: Good affinoid perfectoid subsets of a tilde-limit
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be as in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, X a perfectoid space with a compatible cone φ. A good affinoid perfectoid of (X, φ) is a triple (W, i_0, V) where W = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X is an affinoid perfectoid open subset (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), i_0 ∈ I and V ⊆ X_{i_0} is a quasicompact open subset such that (i) W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V), and (ii) writing V_a := f_a^{-1}(V) ⊆ X_j for a: j → i_0 (the slice category I/i_0, cofiltered), the ring map colim_{a ∈ (I/i_0)^op} O_{X_j}(V_a) → R has dense image. When moreover the V_a are affinoid, V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺), the pair (R, R⁺) is determined by the system (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-uniform-completion). This is the form of Scholze's survey (the paragraph before Proposition 2.22: dense image and homeomorphism with the limit of the finite-level affinoids), of Scholze's torsion paper Theorem III.1.2(iii) and Definition III.3.5(i) (V the preimage of an affinoid V_m at finite level, lim H⁰(V_m, O) → H⁰(V, O) with dense image), and of Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8 (standard affinoids pulled back from level K(p^N)). Under X ~ lim X_i the homeomorphism |W| ≅ lim_a |V_a| is automatic, since W is the preimage of V.
hypotheses: W affinoid perfectoid and exactly the preimage of the quasicompact open V ⊆ X_{i_0}; the colimit is over the cofiltered slice I/i_0.
The density is for the topology of R; no topology is placed on the colimit.
proofSteps: Definition (a structure carrying W, i_0, V and the two properties).
The homeomorphism |W| ≅ lim |V_a| under X ~ lim X_i: preimages commute with limits of topological spaces, and V is open.
acceptance: For a perfectoid Tate ring R with compatible p-power roots of ϖ, the whole perfectoid disc Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is good at level 0 with V = X_0, and so is its rational subset {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} with V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ X_0.
Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: V_i = π_HT^{-1}(V_i) (i = 1, 2) are good at level K(p^N) with V = S_i.

nodes.title: Frobenius-controlled integral towers
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. A Frobenius-controlled integral tower (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) consists of: (1) a sequence of rings A_0⁺ → A_1⁺ → A_2⁺ → ⋯ with transition maps t_m: A_m⁺ → A_{m+1}⁺; (2) an element ϖ ∈ A_0⁺ (its images again written ϖ), the compatible pseudouniformiser, such that every A_m⁺ is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A_m⁺`) and p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺; then every A_m⁺/ϖ^p is an F_p-algebra and absolute Frobenius induces a ring homomorphism Φ_m: A_m⁺/ϖ → A_m⁺/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p (well defined because (x + ϖy)^p ≡ x^p mod pϖA_m⁺ + ϖ^pA_m⁺ = ϖ^pA_m⁺); (3) the eventual Frobenius lifting condition modulo ϖ^p: an index m_0 and, for every m ≥ m_0, a ring isomorphism w_m: A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p such that (i) t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1} as maps A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p (t_m reduced modulo ϖ^p), and (ii) the w_m are compatible with the transition maps: w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m as maps A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p (t reduced modulo ϖ on the left and modulo ϖ^p on the right). The generic fibres are the complete Tate rings A_m := A_m⁺[1/ϖ] with ring of definition A_m⁺ (ϖ-adic topology) and the Huber pairs (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) with A_m⁺⁺ the integral closure of A_m⁺ in A_m; X_m := Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺). The finite levels A_m are not assumed perfectoid (in the sources they are strongly noetherian). Source form: if all A_m⁺ are flat algebras over an integral perfectoid ring O with ϖ ∈ O (O = Z_p^cycl or O_K for a perfectoid field K) and t_m modulo ϖ^p is identified, O-linearly, with the relative Frobenius of A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p over O/ϖ^p, then w_m is the composite of the canonical isomorphism A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p ≅ (A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p)^{(p)} ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p with A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ,Φ_O} O/ϖ^p (Φ_O: O/ϖ ≅ O/ϖ^p is bijective because O is perfectoid); in Scholze's torsion paper ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p} and ϖ^p = p^{1−ε}.
hypotheses: ϖ ∈ A_0⁺ with p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺ (the condition ϖ^p | p of ECD Definition 3.1, placed on the integral model); A_m⁺ ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete.
The w_m are data (isomorphisms), compatible with the transition maps, and exist only from m_0 on: this is the eventual Frobenius lifting condition modulo the p-th power of the pseudouniformiser.
Characteristic p is allowed (p = 0 ∈ A_m⁺, e.g. relative Frobenius towers over a perfect base).
proofSteps: Definition. Well-definedness of Φ_m uses only p ∈ ϖ^pA_m⁺ and the binomial theorem.

The constructor from relative Frobenius over an integral perfectoid base O uses that Frobenius O/ϖ → O/ϖ^p is bijective (BMS Lemma 3.10 for O; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison) and base change of the Frobenius twist along it.
acceptance: The Siegel anticanonical tower X(p^{-m}ε) of Scholze's torsion paper (ε < 1/2): over an affine Spf R_{m_0} ⊂ X(p^{-m_0}ε) the preimages Spf R_m form a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p} (Corollary III.2.19).
The compatible-root disc R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ over a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) whose ϖ has compatible p-power roots, with w_m(r T^{a/p^{m+1}}) = Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}.

nodes.title: Completion and inversion of a Frobenius-controlled tower
nodes.statement: For a Frobenius-controlled integral tower (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower) define: A_∞⁺ := the ϖ-adic completion of the direct limit colim_m A_m⁺ (Mathlib `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ})` of `Ring.DirectLimit`); A_∞ := A_∞⁺[1/ϖ], topologised so that A_∞⁺ is an open ring of definition with the ϖ-adic topology (a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ); A_∞⁺⁺ := the integral closure of A_∞⁺ in A_∞ (a ring of integral elements). Completion/inversion formula: (i) A_∞⁺/ϖ^k A_∞⁺ = colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^k A_m⁺ for every k ≥ 1; (ii) A_∞⁺ is ϖ-torsion-free, so A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞; (iii) (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is the completed direct limit of the Huber pairs (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) in the sense of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 (compatible rings of definition A_m⁺ with ideals of definition ϖA_m⁺, so ϖA_{m'}⁺ = (ϖA_m⁺)A_{m'}⁺); (iv) the construction depends only on the tail of the tower (shift invariance) and is functorial for morphisms of towers. No uniform completion is taken: by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound the ϖ-adic topology on A_∞⁺ is already the spectral topology of A_∞.
hypotheses: A Frobenius-controlled integral tower; ϖ-torsion-freeness of the A_m⁺ is what makes the direct limit and its completion ϖ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: (i): for the finitely generated ideal (ϖ), the ϖ-adic completion M^ of a module satisfies M^/ϖ^k = M/ϖ^k (Mathlib `AdicCompletion`; Stacks 05GG as cited there), and quotients commute with direct limits.
(ii): a direct limit of ϖ-torsion-free rings is ϖ-torsion-free, and ϖ-torsion-freeness passes to the ϖ-adic completion by (i) (multiplication by ϖ on the inverse system of the M/ϖ^k).

(iii): the conditions of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 hold with A_{m,0} = A_m⁺ and I_m = ϖA_m⁺; the plus rings: the integral closure of colim A_m⁺⁺ in colim A_m is the integral closure of colim A_m⁺, and completion followed by integral closure gives A_∞⁺⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit).
(iv): a cofinal subsequence has the same direct limit; morphisms of towers induce maps of direct limits and of completions.
acceptance: Compatible-root disc: for the tower R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩, A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_∞ = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
Siegel tower: R_∞ = the p-adic completion of colim_m R_m (Scholze's torsion paper, proof of Corollary III.2.19).

nodes.title: Preperfectoid adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be an analytic adic space in the generality of Scholze–Weinstein §2.1 (an analytic Yoneda-adic space, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation; the sheafy adic spaces of anchor Layer 5 form a full subcategory). For an open affinoid U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A⁺, the strong completion (Â, Â⁺) of (A, A⁺) is the completion of (A, A⁺) for the topology on A that gives A⁺ the ϖ-adic topology (Â⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of A⁺, Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]; independent of ϖ). X is preperfectoid if X has a cover by open affinoids U_α = Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) whose strong completions (Â_α, Â_α⁺) are perfectoid Tate pairs (ECD Definition 3.1). Over a perfectoid field K this is Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.3.4 (they complete for the p-adic topology on A⁺); Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.3.9 defines X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) to be preperfectoid when every base change to a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 is, and Proposition 2.3.10 compares the two when X lies over a perfectoid K. The natural topology of A and the ϖ-adic topology of A⁺ can differ, and then A itself need not be perfectoid: the nonreduced point Spa(K[X]/X², O_K + KX) is preperfectoid with strong completion (K, O_K).
hypotheses: X analytic; the strong completion is taken for the ϖ-adic topology on the plus ring, not the natural topology of A.
Stability: locally closed subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid (Scholze–Weinstein Propositions 2.3.7 and 2.3.11).
proofSteps: Definition. Independence of ϖ: two pseudouniformisers of A lying in A⁺ each divide a power of the other in A⁺ (both are topologically nilpotent units with inverses bounded by powers of the other), so they define the same adic topology on A⁺.

Stability under locally closed subspaces: open subspaces by definition; for closed subspaces Scholze–Weinstein's proof of Proposition 2.3.7 writes Y = Spa(A/I, B⁺) as the intersection of rational neighbourhoods U_i = {|f_1|, …, |f_k| ≤ |ϖ|^n} and shows the strong completion of O_Y is the completed colimit of the perfectoid O_X(U_i), hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower).
acceptance: Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.3.13: the generic fibre of Spf Z_p⟦X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟧ over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is preperfectoid.
Every perfectoid space is preperfectoid (its affinoid perfectoids are their own strong completions).

nodes.title: The strong completion X̂ of a preperfectoid space and X̂ ~ X
nodes.statement: Let X be a preperfectoid analytic adic space (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/preperfectoid-space). There is a perfectoid space X̂ with a morphism X̂ → X (of Yoneda-adic spaces) such that: (i) |X̂| → |X| is a homeomorphism; (ii) for every open affinoid U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X whose strong completion (Â, Â⁺) is perfectoid, the corresponding open subspace of X̂ is Spa(Â, Â⁺); (iii) X̂ is universal for morphisms from perfectoid spaces to X: every morphism Y → X with Y perfectoid factors uniquely through X̂; (iv) when X is an adic space in the sense of anchor Layer 5 (sheafy affinoid coordinate rings), X̂ ~ X, i.e. (X̂, X̂ → X) is a perfectoid tilde-limit of the one-object system X in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.4, stated there for adic spaces in their §2.1 generality). X̂ is unique up to unique isomorphism by (iii).
hypotheses: X preperfectoid; the construction is over no base field (Scholze–Weinstein state it over Spa(K, O_K)).
proofSteps: Affinoid case: for U = Spa(A, A⁺) with (Â, Â⁺) perfectoid, Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism: continuous valuations of (A, A⁺) bounded by 1 on A⁺ are continuous for the ϖ-adic topology on A⁺ (their restriction to A⁺ satisfies |ϖ^n| → 0), and extend uniquely to the completion; rational subsets correspond (anchor Layer 2).

Gluing: for a rational subset U′ ⊆ U, the strong completion of O_X(U′) is the rational localisation of (Â, Â⁺), perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids; so the Spa(Â, Â⁺) glue along the open cover to a perfectoid space (anchor Layer 5 gluing).

(iii): a map from an affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(B, B⁺) to U corresponds to a continuous (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺); since B⁺ is ϖ-adically complete and the map A⁺ → B⁺ is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, it extends uniquely to (Â, Â⁺); glue over covers.
(iv): (a) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit is (i); (b) holds on each Spa(Â, Â⁺) since A is dense in Â.
acceptance: For a perfectoid field K: the strong completion of Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) is Spa(K, O_K), and Spa(K, O_K) ~ Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) although the two spaces differ.
For X perfectoid, X̂ = X.

Hom(−, X̂) = Hom(−, X) on perfectoid spaces

nodes.title: Cofinality witnesses for families of compact open subgroups
nodes.statement: Let G be a Hausdorff topological group in which the compact open subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of 1 (a locally profinite group: a profinite group, or G(Q_p) for a linear algebraic group G over Q_p). Write CO(G) for the set of compact open subgroups, a cofiltered category under inclusion (K′ → K when K′ ⊆ K; K ∩ K′ is compact open). A level family is a cofiltered category J with a functor j ↦ K_j to CO(G). A cofinality witness for (K_j) is a function U ↦ j(U) from the open subgroups U of G (equivalently from open neighbourhoods of 1) to J with K_{j(U)} ⊆ U. By Mathlib's criterion `CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` (morphisms in CO(G) are unique, so the second condition is automatic), a witness makes j ↦ K_j an initial functor J → CO(G); hence, for every tower (X_K)_{K ∈ CO(G)} of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps (a Shimura tower at p) and every perfectoid X with compatible maps, X ~ lim_{K ∈ CO(G)} X_K iff X ~ lim_{j ∈ J} X_{K_j} (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change). A level family without a witness only computes the tilde-limit of the subtower it indexes: no infinite-level statement for the full tower follows from it.
hypotheses: G locally profinite (Hausdorff, compact open subgroups a neighbourhood basis of 1).
The witness is data; its existence for decreasing sequences inside a compact open subgroup is characterised in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/compact-open-subgroup-cofinality.
proofSteps: Definition. Initiality: for K ∈ CO(G) take j = j(K); any two maps K_j → K agree (thin category), so Mathlib's criterion applies.
acceptance: The principal congruence subgroups K(p^n) = ker(GSp_{2g}(Z_p) → GSp_{2g}(Z/p^n)) have a witness in GSp_{2g}(Q_p), so the Siegel tower of Scholze's torsion paper Theorem III.1.2 may be indexed by n (Theorem III.1.2(iii)).
The family Γ_0(p^n) ⊂ GL_2(Z_p) has no witness: its limit computes the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞)-level of Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(1), not the full infinite level.

uses.how: prove cofinality of the chosen principal/congruence systems before forming the inverse limit
the tower over all K_p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(Q_p) and the subtower of the Γ(p^m) have the same perfectoid tilde-limit
restricting to a cofinal subsystem gives a good tower with the same limit
a non-cofinal family of levels gives no torsor under the full group

nodes.title: Good affinoid perfectoids cover a tilde-limit and are stable under rational subsets (Scholze's survey Proposition 2.22)
nodes.statement: Let (X_i) be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps and X a perfectoid space with a compatible cone such that |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism. (i) If X ~ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), then X is covered by good affinoid perfectoids (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid) with V affinoid at their level. (ii) If (W, i_0, V) is good and U ⊆ W is a rational subset, then U is good at some level j → i_0 with a quasicompact open V′ ⊆ V_a; if V is affinoid, V′ can be taken a rational subset of V_a. (iii) Hence the good affinoid perfectoids form a basis of the topology of X. (iv) Conversely, if X is covered by good affinoid perfectoids, then X ~ lim X_i. Consequently the conditions (b), (b′), (b″) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit are equivalent given (a).
hypotheses: |X| → lim |X_i| a homeomorphism throughout.
proofSteps: (i) Given x, choose an affinoid U ∋ x as in (b); choose a rational neighbourhood U′ = U(f/g) ⊆ U of x that is affinoid perfectoid (rational subsets of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids) and maps into an affinoid open of some X_i; by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem` the parameters f, g can be replaced by nearby elements of the dense image of the finite-level sections without changing U′.

|U′| is quasicompact open in |X| ≅ lim |X_i|; restricting to the preimages of an affinoid open of X_i (spectral, with spectral transition maps since the transition maps are qcqs), Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 gives a quasicompact open V at a finite level with U′ = φ^{-1}(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces); shrinking by (ii) makes V affinoid.

Density on U′: O_X(U′) is the completion of O_X(U)[1/g] with ring of definition generated by O_X(U)_0[f/g] (anchor Layer 3 structure presheaf); since f, g come from a finite level, the images of the O_{X_j}(V_a) contain a dense subring (survey: 'the density statement is preserved').
(ii) same argument inside W; (iii) rational subsets of the members of a cover form a basis; (iv) the good affinoids give (b″), which implies (b).
acceptance: In the compatible-root disc tower every rational subset of the perfectoid disc is the preimage of a rational subset at a finite level and is good.

nodes.title: A perfectoid tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian spaces is a residue-field tilde-limit
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit) with every X_i quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally noetherian. Then X ~′ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit): for every x ∈ X with images x_i, colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^ has dense image.
hypotheses: X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic, so that ~′ is defined.
proofSteps: Condition (a) is common to both notions.

Fix x ∈ X and a good affinoid perfectoid W ∋ x (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis). The rational neighbourhoods of x in W are good (same node) and cofinal among neighbourhoods of x; the residue field k(x) is the colimit of the O_X(U) over them modulo the support of x, and O_X(U) → k(x)^ is continuous.

For each good U with level V_a, the image of colim_a O(V_a) is dense in O_X(U), hence its image in k(x)^ is dense in the image of O_X(U); the image of O(V_a) → k(x)^ factors through k(x_j) (x_j ∈ V_a). Taking the union over U, colim_j k(x_j) has dense image in k(x), hence colim_j k(x_j)^ in k(x)^.
acceptance: For the compatible-root disc tower over a perfectoid field, the Gauss point x has k(x_n)^ = completion of K(T^{1/p^n}) for the Gauss norm, whose union is dense in k(x)^.

nodes.title: Completed direct limits of Huber pairs give tilde-limits (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2)
nodes.statement: Let (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} be a filtered direct system of complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with continuous transition maps, and assume there are rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i mapped into one another and finitely generated ideals of definition I_i ⊆ A_{i,0} with I_j = I_i A_{j,0} for j ≥ i. Let A := colim_i A_i with the topology making A_0 := colim_i A_{i,0} an open subring with the I-adic topology, I := colim_i I_i; let A⁺ := the integral closure in A of the image of colim_i A_i⁺, and (Â, Â⁺) the completion. Then (i) (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (A, A⁺) are continuous; (ii) a valuation on A is a continuous valuation with |A⁺| ≤ 1 iff its restrictions to all A_i are, so the restriction map Spa(Â, Â⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a bijection, and it is a homeomorphism; (iii) every rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺); (iv) colim_i A_i → Â has dense image. Consequently, if the X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are adic spaces (A_i sheafy) and Â is perfectoid, then Spa(Â, Â⁺) ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit). In the Tate case with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i_0,0}, the hypotheses hold with I_i = ϖA_{i,0}.
hypotheses: Filtered system of complete Huber pairs with compatible rings of definition and ideals of definition satisfying I_j = I_i A_{j,0}.

Perfectoidness of Â is a hypothesis of the final clause; it is supplied by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers, by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower, or by the application.
proofSteps: (i) A_0 is open with f.g. ideal of definition I (images of generators of I_{i_0}); each A_i⁺ contains the topologically nilpotent A_{i,0}-ideal I_i (anchor Layer 0: open integrally closed subrings contain the topologically nilpotent elements, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`), so A⁺ ⊇ I is open; power-boundedness of the image of A_i⁺ follows from continuity.

(ii) A valuation v on A restricts to valuations v_i; v is continuous iff v(I^n) → 0 in the sense of continuity for the I-adic ring of definition, which is detected on the generators of I_{i_0}, hence on any single A_i; |A⁺| ≤ 1 iff |A_i⁺| ≤ 1 for all i (integral closure does not change the condition: Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`). Completion does not change Spa (anchor Layer 2).

(iii) and the topology: a rational subset R(T/s) of Spa(A, A⁺) with T, s ⊂ A involves finitely many elements, which come from some A_i, and its preimage statement is Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`; rational subsets form bases on both sides, so the continuous bijection is open.
(iv) A is dense in its completion.

In the Tate case (compatible pseudouniformiser), (i)-(iii) are PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs; this node adds the general Huber-ring form of Scholze–Weinstein and the tilde-limit conclusion.
Final clause: (a) of the tilde-limit is (ii), (b) is (iv) applied to the single affinoid Spa(Â, Â⁺).
acceptance: The compatible-root disc: (R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) with A_{n,0} = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, I_n = ϖA_{n,0}; the completion is R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
Scholze–Weinstein §3: T(G)^{ad} ~ lim G[p^n]^{ad} from this proposition (proof of Proposition 3.3.2 there).

nodes.title: A good affinoid perfectoid is the uniform completion of the finite-level coordinate rings; finite étale algebras descend
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit and (W, i_0, V) a good affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid), W = Spa(R, R⁺), such that every V_a (a: j → i_0) is affinoid, V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺) (for instance when the transition maps are affinoid). Let (C, C⁺) be the completed direct limit of the (A_a, A_a⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit, Tate case with a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i_0} that is also one of R). Then: (i) the canonical map (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) identifies (R, R⁺) with the uniformization of (C, C⁺) (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization), R⁺ being the integral closure of the closure of the image of C⁺; in particular R is determined by the system (V_a); (ii) base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_a FÉt(A_a) → FÉt(R), and similarly for every rational localisation of W pulled back from a finite level.
hypotheses: All V_a affinoid; ϖ a common pseudouniformiser.
R perfectoid, hence uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).
proofSteps: Spectral seminorms: for c ∈ colim A_a, sup over rank-one points of Spa(R, R⁺) of |c| equals the sup over rank-one points of Spa(C, C⁺), because Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ lim |V_a| ≅ Spa(C, C⁺) compatibly with evaluation (tilde-limit condition (a) and PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (ii)).

R is uniform, so its topology is defined by its spectral norm; the image of colim A_a is dense (goodness); hence C → R extends to an isometric isomorphism from the separated completion of C for the spectral seminorm, i.e. C^u ≅ R (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13). Plus rings: both are the elements of absolute value ≤ 1 on the common spectrum (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`).

(ii): FÉt(colim A_a) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(A_a) since finite étale algebras and their morphisms are finitely presented; FÉt(colim A_a) ≃ FÉt(C) because colim A_{a,0} is henselian along ϖ as a filtered colimit of ϖ-adically complete rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions) and Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8 (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation); FÉt(C) ≃ FÉt(C^u) = FÉt(R) by Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(a).
acceptance: For the compatible-root disc tower, C = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ already uniform, and every finite étale R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra is defined over some R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩.
ECD Lemma 15.3/Proposition 15.4: for the universal finite étale tower A → A_i of a Tate Z_p-algebra, the uniform completion of colim A_i is perfectoid and is the ring of the tilde-limit.

nodes.title: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a tilde-limit come from finite level
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit. (i) Every quasicompact open U ⊆ X is φ_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and a quasicompact open U_i ⊆ X_i; if U_i, U′_i ⊆ X_i are quasicompact open with φ_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ φ_i^{-1}(U′_i), then f_a^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ f_a^{-1}(U′_i) for some a: j → i, and likewise for equalities, finite unions and finite intersections; (ii) a finite cover of a quasicompact open U ⊆ X by quasicompact opens is the preimage of a finite cover at some finite level; (iii) if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and U = W ∩ {|f_k| ≤ |g| ≠ 0} is a rational subset of W, there are j → i_0 and f′_k, g′ ∈ O(V_a) with U = φ_j^{-1}(U_a(f′/g′)) for the rational subset U_a(f′/g′) of V_a when V_a is affinoid; in general U = φ_j^{-1} of the quasicompact open {|f′_k| ≤ |g′| ≠ 0} ⊆ V_a.
hypotheses: X ~ lim X_i; in (iii) the finite-level V_a affinoid for the rational form.
proofSteps: (i), (ii): reduce to the spectral case over an affinoid open at a finite level and apply Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 (parts (1)-(4)) to lim |V_a| ≅ φ^{-1}(V).

(iii): perturb f_k, g inside the neighbourhood of Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem` to elements of the dense image of colim O(V_a) (the ideal generated by the f_k is open since W is Tate and the f_k generate the unit ideal); the preimage of a rational subset is rational (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`).
acceptance: Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson, proof of Theorem 2.17: the rational subset X_{∞,w} of V_1 is the preimage of an affinoid S ⊆ X_{K(p^N)} 'since rational subsets come from finite level'.
Hansen–Johansson Lemma 5.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/finite-level-affinoid-basis): every rational subset of the limit is the preimage of a rational subset at a finite level.

nodes.title: A perfectoid tilde-limit represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on perfectoid spaces and is unique (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.5)
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with quasicompact quasiseparated transition maps and X ~ lim X_i a perfectoid tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit). Then for every perfectoid space Y (of any characteristic, over no fixed base field), and more generally every analytic adic space Y covered by affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B uniform, the map Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i), g ↦ (φ_i ∘ g)_i, is bijective. Consequently: (i) X represents the functor Y ↦ lim_i Hom(Y, X_i) on perfectoid spaces; (ii) if (X′, φ′) is another perfectoid tilde-limit of the same system, there is a unique isomorphism X ≅ X′ compatible with the cones; (iii) a morphism of systems (X_i) → (X′_i) (over a common index category) induces a unique morphism between perfectoid tilde-limits commuting with the cones; (iv) over a base S (all X_i over S compatibly), the same holds for S-morphisms.
hypotheses: Only uniformity of the coordinate rings of Y is used, not perfectoidness; no perfectoid base field (Scholze–Weinstein state it for perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebras).
proofSteps: Both sides are sheaves on Y for the analytic topology (adic spaces are sheaves; lim of sheaves), so one may assume Y = Spa(B, B⁺) affinoid with B uniform, and, using the continuous map |Y| → lim |X_i| ≅ |X| and the basis of good affinoids (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis), that the compatible maps ψ_i factor through V_a for a good (W, i_0, V), W = Spa(R, R⁺).
Injectivity: two maps g, g′: Y → W with φ_i g = φ_i g′ agree on |Y| (|W| ≅ lim |V_a|) and their ring maps R → B agree on the dense image of colim_a O(V_a), hence everywhere by continuity.

Valuation comparison: for y ∈ Y let x ∈ W be the point with φ_j(x) = ψ_j(y) for all j (bijectivity of |W| → lim |V_a|). For c ∈ colim_a O(V_a), |ψ^*c(y)| ≤ |ψ^*c′(y)| iff |c(x)| ≤ |c′(x)| (both valuations restrict to the same point of each V_a).

Factorisation: if c maps to 0 in R then |c(x)| = 0 for all x, so ψ^*c vanishes at every point of Spa(B, B⁺); B uniform implies ψ^*c = 0 (its spectral seminorm is a norm). So colim O(V_a) → B factors through the image C′ ⊆ R.

Continuity: choose a pseudouniformiser ϖ′ of R in C′ (units near a pseudouniformiser are pseudouniformisers). If c ∈ C′ ∩ ϖ′^n R⁺ then |c(x)| ≤ |ϖ′(x)|^n on W, hence |ψ^*c| ≤ |ψ^*ϖ′|^n on Spa(B, B⁺), so ψ^*c ∈ (ψ^*ϖ′)^n B⁺ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`); ψ^*ϖ′ is a topologically nilpotent unit of B (it is nonvanishing and of absolute value < 1 at every point; anchor Layers 1-2). Hence C′ → B is uniformly continuous and extends to R → B, R⁺ → B⁺ (C′ ∩ R⁺ is dense in R⁺ because R⁺ is open).

The resulting map of Huber pairs gives g: Y → W with φ_j g = ψ_j (maps into an affinoid adic space are maps of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 5). Glue over covers; (ii)-(iv) are formal consequences of representability.
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper Corollary III.2.19 and Theorem III.1.2(i): uniqueness of the perfectoid anticanonical tower and of X*_{Γ(p^∞)} up to unique isomorphism.
Two perfectoid tilde-limits of the compatible-root disc tower (for instance R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and its presentation through T ↦ T^p transition maps) are uniquely isomorphic.
