nodes.title: Tilde-limits and inverse limits of represented functors and of diamonds
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces over Spa(Z_p, Z_p) with qcqs transition maps. (i) If X ~ lim X_i is a perfectoid tilde-limit, then h_X ≅ lim_i h_{X_i} as presheaves on the category of perfectoid spaces (h_Y = Hom(−, Y)), and the induced map of v-sheaves X^◇ → lim_i X_i^◇ on Perf (diamonds of DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor; the limit is a diamond by DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons) is an isomorphism, compatible with |X^◇| = |X| ≅ lim |X_i| = lim |X_i^◇|. (ii) If the X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are affinoid with completed direct limit (A, A⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit) and uniformization (A^u, A^{u+}), then lim_i Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spd(A^u, A^{u+}) and |lim_i X_i^◇| ≅ |Spa(A^u, A^{u+})|; if moreover A^u is perfectoid, then X := Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ~ lim X_i and X^◇ ≅ lim X_i^◇. (iii) If lim_i X_i^◇ ≅ X^◇ for a perfectoid space X with compatible maps to the X_i (the hypothesis of Hansen–Johansson Lemma 5.11 and Definition 5.12), then |X| → lim_i |X_i| is a homeomorphism and (when the X_i are qcqs, or locally over a qcqs open at a finite level) every quasicompact open and every rational subset of X is the preimage of one at a finite level; the density condition (b) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit is then equivalent, on an affinoid W = φ^{-1}(Spa(A_a, A_a⁺)), to perfectoidness of the uniformization of colim A_a (then W = Spa of it by (ii) and full faithfulness of untilts).
hypotheses: X_i analytic over Spa(Z_p, Z_p) so that X_i^◇ is defined (ECD Definition 15.5).
Representability of lim X_i^◇ alone gives the topological clause and finite-level descriptions; the density clause is stated separately in (iii).
proofSteps: (i): the presheaf statement is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness. For S ∈ Perf, a point of lim X_i^◇(S) is a compatible family of untilts (S^♯_i, ι_i) with maps S^♯_i → X_i; marked untilts have no automorphisms and are compatible with the transition maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair), so it is one untilt S^♯ with compatible maps S^♯ → X_i, i.e. by representability a map S^♯ → X. Topological compatibility: |Y^◇| = |Y| for analytic Y (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor) and |lim Y_i| ≅ lim |Y_i| for locally spatial diamonds with qcqs transition maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons).

(ii): compatible maps of pairs (A_i, A_i⁺) → (O(S^♯), O⁺(S^♯)) are a map from colim, which extends uniquely to the completion (O(S^♯) is complete) and then to the uniformization (O(S^♯) is uniform; uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of uniform rings, Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization). If A^u is perfectoid, Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ~ lim X_i by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (Spa is unchanged by uniformization) and Spd(A^u, A^{u+}) = Spa(A^u, A^{u+})^◇ (ECD Lemma 15.2).

(iii): topology as in (i); finite-level descriptions by Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 as in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/rational-subsets-from-finite-level; for the density clause, W^◇ ≅ lim Spd(A_a, A_a⁺) ≅ Spd((colim A_a)^u) by (ii), and a perfectoid pair is determined by its diamond with untilt (tilting slice equivalence, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence), so W ≅ Spa of the uniformization exactly when the latter is perfectoid, in which case colim A_a is dense in O(W).
acceptance: ECD Proposition 15.4: for the universal finite étale G_i-torsor tower A → A_i of a Tate Z_p-algebra, Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim Spd(A_i, A_i⁺), and Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) ~ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) by (ii).

Hansen–Johansson Lemma 5.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/finite-level-affinoid-basis): for locally noetherian X_i with finite transition maps and lim X_i^◇ perfectoid, rational subsets of the limit are pulled back from finite levels, by (iii).

nodes.title: Tilde-limits are invariant under initial changes of index category
nodes.statement: Let u: J → I be an initial functor between small cofiltered categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`; for directed sets, a coinitial subset). For a system (X_i)_{i∈I} of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, a perfectoid space X and a compatible cone (φ_i), X ~ lim_{i∈I} X_i iff X ~ lim_{j∈J} X_{u(j)} for the restricted cone (φ_{u(j)}). In particular: (a) for every i_0 ∈ I the forgetful functor I/i_0 → I is initial, so a tilde-limit depends only on the tail of the system; (b) for I = ℕ (as an inverse system) any infinite subsequence may be used; (c) for level families of compact open subgroups with a cofinality witness (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness), the full tower and the witnessed subtower have the same perfectoid tilde-limits.
hypotheses: u initial; both categories small and cofiltered.
proofSteps: Topology: for u initial, the canonical map lim_I |X_i| → lim_J |X_{u(j)}| is an isomorphism in TopCat (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`), compatible with the maps from |X|.

Density: for each i there is j with a morphism u(j) → i (initiality), and the images of O_{X_i}(V) in O_X(U) are contained in the images of O_{X_{u(j)}}(f^{-1}V); conversely J-terms are I-terms, so the unions in condition (b) agree.
(a) uses Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` for the slice; (c) is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness.

nodes.title: Restriction of a tilde-limit to compatible open and rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I, U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0} an open subset (in particular a rational subset of an affinoid open), U_a := f_a^{-1}(U_{i_0}) ⊆ X_j for a: j → i_0, and U := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(U_{i_0}), an open perfectoid subspace of X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then U ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} U_a (the slice category I/i_0, which is initial in I by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change). Moreover, if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and U_{i_0} = V(f/g) is a rational subset of V, then W ∩ U = Spa(R⟨f/g⟩, R⟨f/g⟩⁺) is the rational localisation of (R, R⁺) = (O(W), O⁺(W)) at the pulled-back parameters (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), it is good at level i_0 with the rational subset V(f/g), and colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a(f/g)) → R⟨f/g⟩ has dense image.
hypotheses: U_{i_0} open at one finite level; the transition maps restricted to the U_a stay qcqs.
proofSteps: Topology: preimages of an open subset commute with limits of topological spaces, so the homeomorphism |X| ≅ lim |X_i| restricts to |U| ≅ lim_a |U_a|.

Density: U is covered by the rational subsets of good affinoids W of X that lie in U and are pulled back from finite levels (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis); these are good for the system (U_a), which gives (b″) and hence (b).

The rational form: the structure presheaf on rational subsets (anchor Layer 3) and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids identify O(W ∩ U); the finite-level sections O(V_a)[f/g] have dense image.

nodes.title: A decreasing family of open subgroups of a profinite group is cofinal iff its intersection is trivial
nodes.statement: Let K be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group; Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp`) and (K_n)_{n≥0} a decreasing sequence of closed subgroups (more generally a family of closed subgroups directed downwards). Then every open neighbourhood of 1 in K (equivalently every open subgroup) contains some K_n if and only if ⋂_n K_n = {1}. Consequences: (i) for a closed subgroup H ⊆ GL_N(Z_p), the principal congruence subgroups H ∩ (1 + p^n M_N(Z_p)), n ≥ 1, are cofinal among the open subgroups of H and give a cofinality witness (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness) in any locally profinite G containing H as a compact open subgroup; (ii) Γ_0(p^n) and Γ_1(p^n) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL_2(Z_p): c ≡ 0, d ≡ 1 mod p^n} are not cofinal in GL_2(Z_p), since both contain the unipotent upper triangular subgroup; (iii) a family (K′_n) with K′_n ⊆ K_n and (K_n) cofinal is cofinal.
hypotheses: K profinite (compactness is essential: in a non-compact group a decreasing family of open subgroups with trivial intersection need not be cofinal).
proofSteps: ⇐: for U open with 1 ∈ U, the sets K_n \ U are closed in the compact space K, directed downwards, with empty intersection (⋂ K_n = {1} ⊆ U); by the finite intersection property one of them is empty, i.e. K_n ⊆ U.

⇒: open subgroups of a profinite group intersect to {1}: every open neighbourhood of 1 contains an open normal subgroup (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`) and K is Hausdorff; equivalently apply Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.closedSubgroup_eq_sInf_open` to the trivial subgroup.
(i): ⋂_n (1 + p^n M_N(Z_p)) = {1}; (ii): the matrix (1 1; 0 1) lies in every Γ_0(p^n) and Γ_1(p^n) but not in 1 + pM_2(Z_p); (iii) immediate.
acceptance: The Siegel levels Γ(p^m) ⊂ GSp_{2g}(Z_p) of Scholze's torsion paper form a cofinal family; the anticanonical levels Γ_0(p^m) do not, and their tilde-limit is the Γ_0(p^∞)-level of Corollary III.2.19.

nodes.title: Locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, i_0 ∈ I, and (V^α)_{α} an open cover of X_{i_0}, with preimages V^α_a := f_a^{-1}(V^α) ⊆ X_j (a: j → i_0). (i) Locality: a perfectoid space X with a compatible cone satisfies X ~ lim X_i iff for every α the open subspace U^α := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V^α) satisfies U^α ~ lim_a V^α_a. (ii) Gluing: if for every α the system (V^α_a)_a has a perfectoid tilde-limit U^α, then there is a perfectoid space X with a compatible cone and X ~ lim X_i; X is glued from the U^α along the open subspaces U^{αβ} ⊆ U^α that are the restrictions of U^α to V^α ∩ V^β (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), identified by the unique isomorphisms of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness (which also give the cocycle condition). (iii) Torsion-paper form: suppose that for all large m the X_m are the generic fibres of a tower and that |lim_m X_m| is covered by subsets W that are preimages of affinoid opens V_m = Spa(R_m, R_m⁺) ⊆ X_m for all sufficiently large m (compatible with the transition maps) such that, with R_∞⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_m R_m⁺ and R_∞ = R_∞⁺[1/ϖ], (R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺) is perfectoid (R_∞⁺⁺ the integral closure of R_∞⁺); then there is a unique perfectoid space X_∞ with |X_∞| = lim |X_m| and X_∞ ~ lim X_m, whose restriction to each W is Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺).
hypotheses: Transition maps qcqs; the cover is by opens of one finite level.
In (iii), 'for all large m' allows the affinoid description to start at a level depending on W.
proofSteps: (i): lim |V^α_a| is the preimage of V^α in lim |X_j|, an open subset, and these cover; a continuous bijection that restricts to homeomorphisms over an open cover is a homeomorphism; condition (b) is local by definition.

(ii): the U^α restricted to V^α ∩ V^β are tilde-limits of the same system (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), hence uniquely isomorphic compatibly with cones (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness); uniqueness gives the cocycle condition on triple overlaps; glue adic spaces along opens (anchor Layer 5) — perfectoidness is local (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space); the cones glue by uniqueness, and (i) gives X ~ lim X_i.

(iii): for each W, Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m V_m by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (Tate case, rings of definition R_m⁺); apply (ii) to the cover of the finite level by the V_m (and their finite unions, using that the W are open in |lim X_m|).
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper, §III.3: |X*_{Γ(p^∞)}| has a natural structure of perfectoid space obtained by gluing the Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺) over affinoid perfectoid subsets (Definition III.3.5), and X*_{Γ(p^∞)} ~ lim X*_{K_p}.
Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: X_∞ is glued from the two affinoid perfectoids V_1, V_2 pulled back from level K(p^N).

nodes.title: Finite étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I and g: Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0} a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism). Put Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j for a: j → i_0 (finite étale over X_j; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X. Then Y exists in adic spaces, is a perfectoid space, Y → X is finite étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), and Y ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} Y_a. Affinoid formula: if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and g^{-1}(V) = Spa(B, B⁺) with B ∈ FÉt(A) and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), then the preimage of W in Y is Spa(B ⊗_A R, (B ⊗_A R)⁺) with (B ⊗_A R)⁺ the integral closure of R⁺, and colim_a (B ⊗_A O(V_a)) → B ⊗_A R has dense image; it is good at level i_0 with V′ = g^{-1}(V).
hypotheses: g finite étale at one finite level; X perfectoid.
proofSteps: Existence and perfectoidness: the fibre product along a map from a perfectoid space exists and is perfectoid and finite étale over X (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii)-(iv) and Proposition 7.10, in PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change; ECD Theorem 6.1(i) for B ⊗_A R).
Density: B is finite projective over A, so B ⊗_A − commutes with direct limits and carries a dense-image map colim_a O(V_a) → R to a dense-image map (locally B is a direct summand of A^n).

Topology: over a good W with all V_a affinoid, |Spa(B ⊗_A R)| = |Spa((B ⊗_A C)^u)| = |Spa(B ⊗_A C)| = lim_a |Spa(B ⊗_A O(V_a))| by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-uniform-completion (R = C^u), Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(b) and Definition 2.8.13 (uniformization commutes with finite étale base change and does not change Spa) and PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit applied to the finite étale pairs; in general cover by such W (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis) and use that the question is local over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (i)).
Hence (a) and (b″) hold for Y.
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper, §III.2.4: D_m → X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a finite étale pulls back to the perfectoid space D_{mΓ_0(p^∞)} over the anticanonical tower.
Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11(2): pulling back the finite étale X_{Γ_1*(p^n)} → X_{Γ_0*(p^n)} gives a tower of finite étale perfectoid spaces over X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a.

Kummer test: over a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0 and p ≠ 2, the perfectoid torus X = Spa(K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩); pulling back the finite étale S ↦ S² = T cover gives Y = Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^n}⟩).

nodes.title: Étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3, étale case)
nodes.statement: Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I and g: Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0} an étale morphism of analytic adic spaces in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism (locally an open immersion into a space finite étale over an open subset). Put Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j and Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X. Then Y exists, is a perfectoid space étale over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Y ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} Y_a. This is the case of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3 (base change along an arbitrary Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0}, proved there by reference to Huber's Remark 2.4.3) in which the base change of a perfectoid space is again perfectoid, and the sectionwise version of Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16.
hypotheses: g étale; for non-étale g the fibre product Y need not be perfectoid and is not considered here (Zariski-closed base changes are PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers).
proofSteps: Existence and étaleness: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii), Proposition 7.10).

Locality: by the local description of étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, equivalent form: rational subset of a finite étale cover of a rational subset of an affinoid open), Y_{i_0} is covered by opens Z ⊆ Y_{i_0} of the form Z ⊆ Z′ → V ⊆ X_{i_0} with V open, Z′ → V finite étale and Z ⊆ Z′ open.

For each such piece: restrict to V (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), base change along Z′ → V (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change), restrict to Z (rational restriction again); so the preimage of Z in Y is ~ lim of the preimages of Z in the Y_a.
Glue: the preimages of the Z cover Y, so Y ~ lim Y_a by the locality clause of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing.
acceptance: Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11: 'perfectoid tilde-limits commute with fibre products', used for the finite étale torsors between the Γ_0-, Γ_1- and Γ-level towers.
An open immersion U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0} recovers PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction.

nodes.title: Frobenius on the completed tower is bijective modulo ϖ, and the uniformity bound ϖA_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺
nodes.statement: Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with completion (A_∞⁺, A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion). Then: (i) Φ: A_∞⁺/ϖ → A_∞⁺/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p, is a bijection (in fact colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p is, and these are the quotients of A_∞⁺); (ii) A_∞⁺ is a ϖ-torsion-free, ϖ-adically complete ring with p ∈ ϖ^pA_∞⁺ and bijective Frobenius modulo ϖ, hence an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Definition 3.5 (Lemma 3.10(ii)); (iii) uniformity bound: A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞° and ϖ·A_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺; more precisely, after replacing ϖ by a unit multiple admitting a compatible system of p-power roots (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.9), the cokernel of A_∞⁺ → A_∞° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, i.e. A_∞⁺ → A_∞° is an almost isomorphism for the ideal (ϖ^{1/p^∞}) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); consequently A_∞° is bounded, A_∞ is uniform, and the ϖ-adic topology on A_∞⁺ is the topology of the spectral norm of A_∞; (iv) A_∞⁺⁺ satisfies A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞⁺⁺ ⊆ A_∞° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_∞⁺.
hypotheses: A Frobenius-controlled integral tower; only the terms m ≥ m_0 matter.
proofSteps: (i) Surjectivity: for y ∈ A_m⁺/ϖ^p with m ≥ m_0 put x = w_m^{-1}(y) ∈ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ; then t_m(y) = t_m(w_m(x)) = Φ_{m+1}(x), so y becomes a p-th power in the colimit. Injectivity: if x ∈ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ has Φ_{m+1}(x) = t_m(w_m(x)) = 0 in A_k⁺/ϖ^p for some k > m, then by the compatibility w_k(t(x)) = t(w_m(x)) = 0 in A_k⁺/ϖ^p (x transported to A_{k+1}⁺/ϖ), and w_k is injective, so x vanishes in A_{k+1}⁺/ϖ. The quotients of A_∞⁺ are those of the colimit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (i)).

(ii) Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.10(ii) applied with π = ϖ, a non-zero-divisor by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (ii); the definition of integral perfectoid rings is PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings.

(iii) Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.21 (R_0 = A_∞⁺, π = ϖ): R_0[1/π] with the π-adic topology on R_0 is a complete Tate ring, perfectoid in Fontaine's sense, with πR° ⊆ R_0 and R_0 ⊆ R° with cokernel killed by all fractional powers of π; imported through PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison. Directly: A_∞⁺ is p-root closed in A_∞ by injectivity in (i) (x ∈ A_∞, x^p ∈ A_∞⁺ ⇒ x ∈ A_∞⁺, by induction on the ϖ-adic valuation of a denominator), and for x ∈ A_∞° with x^{p^n} ∈ ϖ^{-c}A_∞⁺ for all n, (ϖ^{c/p^n}x)^{p^n} ∈ A_∞⁺ gives ϖ^{c/p^n}x ∈ A_∞⁺ for all n, hence ϖx ∈ A_∞⁺.
(iv) A_∞° is integrally closed in A_∞ and contains A_∞⁺, so it contains A_∞⁺⁺.
acceptance: For the compatible-root disc tower, A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_∞° = R°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩; the bound ϖR°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ holds because ϖR° ⊆ R°° ⊆ R⁺.
Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: absolute Frobenius induces R_∞/p^{(1−ε)/p} ≅ R_∞/p^{1−ε}, so R_∞ is a perfectoid Z_p^cycl,a-algebra.

nodes.title: The perfectoid Frobenius criterion: Frobenius-controlled towers have perfectoid tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower) with generic fibres (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) and completion (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion). Then: (i) A_∞ is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (complete, uniform, with the pseudouniformiser ϖ satisfying ϖ^p | p in A_∞° and Φ: A_∞°/ϖ ≅ A_∞°/ϖ^p), of characteristic 0 or p according to A_0⁺, and (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair; (ii) the restriction map identifies |Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)| with lim_m |Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)|, and, when the A_m are sheafy (for instance strongly noetherian, as for affinoids of rigid spaces), X_∞ := Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m X_m in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, X_∞ is unique up to unique isomorphism, and it represents lim_m Hom(−, X_m) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) global form: let (𝔛_m) be a tower of flat ϖ-adic formal schemes (over a ϖ-adically complete base) with generic fibres X_m analytic adic spaces, and suppose 𝔛_{m_0} has an affine open cover by Spf A_{m_0}⁺ whose preimages Spf A_m⁺ (m ≥ m_0) form Frobenius-controlled towers compatibly with restriction; then the generic fibres have a perfectoid tilde-limit X_∞ ~ lim X_m, glued from the Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing), which is the generic fibre of the formal scheme lim 𝔛_m (limit in formal schemes, affine-locally Spf A_∞⁺). This theorem concerns towers whose finite levels are not perfectoid; the case of perfectoid finite levels is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower.
hypotheses: Frobenius-controlled integral tower (the eventual Frobenius lifting modulo ϖ^p is the only input beyond flatness and completeness).
For (ii)-(iii), the generic fibres are adic spaces (sheafy coordinate rings) so that the tilde-limit is defined.
proofSteps: (i): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound gives that A_∞⁺ is integral perfectoid, A_∞ uniform with A_∞° almost equal to A_∞⁺, and A_∞ perfectoid in Fontaine's sense (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.21), which is ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A_∞⁺⁺ is open (contains A_∞⁺), integrally closed and contained in A_∞°.

(ii): the tower of pairs satisfies the hypotheses of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{m,0} = A_m⁺ and I_m = ϖA_m⁺, whose completed direct limit is (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (iii)); perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so X_∞ is a perfectoid space and the final clause of that lemma gives X_∞ ~ lim X_m; uniqueness and representability are PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness.

(iii): on each affine piece apply (ii); the pieces are compatible with restriction (rational localisation commutes with the construction on both sides, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction) and glue by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii)-(iii). The formal-scheme limit is affine-locally Spf of the ϖ-adic completion of colim A_m⁺, whose generic fibre is Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺).
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: for 0 ≤ ε < 1/2 there are unique perfectoid spaces X_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_m X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a (and similarly X*, A) over Q_p^cycl, the transition maps of the integral models X(p^{-m}ε) agreeing with relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε}.
Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(1): X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_n X_{Γ_0*(p^n)}(ε)_a for Hilbert modular varieties, via Lemma 5.12 (relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ}).

Compatible-root disc and torus: the towers R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ and R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩ over a perfectoid Tate pair give Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩) and Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩) (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Example 4.4 for the torus over a perfectoid field).

The Hilbert-modular instance: relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ} an isomorphism on the limit, whence perfectoid generic fibre and the tilde-limit.
The tilde-limit and its uniqueness from the completed limit.
The completed limit is a perfectoid integral algebra (Scholze 2012 Definition 5.1(ii)); this node reaches the same conclusion over no base field via BMS Lemmas 3.10 and 3.21.
The torus tower over a perfectoid field, with affinoid perfectoid limit.

nodes.title: The tilt of the limit of a Frobenius-controlled tower
nodes.statement: Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower and (S_•⁺, t, m_0, w′) a Frobenius-controlled integral tower of characteristic p (p = 0 in S_0⁺), together with ring isomorphisms α_m: A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ S_m⁺/t^p for m ≥ m_0 compatible with the transition maps (and with the w, w′). Then the perfectoid Tate ring S_∞ = S_∞⁺[1/t] of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers is perfect, and S_∞ is the tilt of A_∞: there is a unique isomorphism A_∞♭ ≅ S_∞ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) carrying ϖ♭ to a unit multiple of t and inducing the colimit of the α_m modulo ϖ and t, namely A_∞⁺/ϖ = colim A_m⁺/ϖ ≅ colim S_m⁺/t = S_∞⁺/t; under it, Spa(S_∞, S_∞⁺⁺) is the tilt of Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺), and in the global form of the criterion the tilt of X_∞ is the limit of the characteristic-p tower.
hypotheses: The comparison α is given only modulo ϖ^p and t^p (it need not lift).
proofSteps: A_∞⁺/ϖ^p = colim A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ colim S_m⁺/t^p = S_∞⁺/t^p (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (i)).

S_∞⁺ is perfect: Φ: S_∞⁺/t → S_∞⁺/t^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound) and S_∞⁺ is t-adically complete and t-torsion-free, so Frobenius is bijective on S_∞⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

Tilt: A_∞♭⁺ ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} A_∞⁺/ϖ up to almost zero (ECD Lemma 3.10, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); via α this is lim_Φ S_∞⁺/t = S_∞⁺ (perfect and t-complete), compatibly with the rings of integral elements; invert ϖ♭ ↔ t (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: the tilt of X*_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a is the open subset of the perfection X′*perf where |Ha| ≥ |t|^ε, using X′*(p^{-m}ε)/t^{1−ε} = X*(p^{-m}ε)/p^{1−ε} (Theorem III.2.15(i)).
For the compatible-root disc over R, the characteristic-p tower R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ with α_m induced by R⁺/ϖ^p ≅ R♭⁺/(ϖ♭)^p gives the tilt R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ of R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.

sources.match: The tilt identification from the congruence of the two towers.
The characteristic-p side is a perfection.

nodes.title: The perfection of a characteristic-p adic space as a tilde-limit along relative Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser t (more generally a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p with t ∈ k° admitting all p-power roots), (S, S⁺) a complete Tate pair over (k, k°) with S⁺ flat over k° and t-adically complete, and Φ: S → S^{(p)} ≅ S the relative Frobenius over k (an isomorphism of the base, k being perfect). (i) The tower S⁺ →Φ S⁺ →Φ ⋯ (level m carrying the k°-structure twisted by Φ_k^{-m}) is a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with ϖ = t and w_m the canonical base-change isomorphisms (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower, constructor from relative Frobenius); (ii) its completion is S^{perf⁺} := the t-adic completion of colim_Φ S⁺ with S^{perf} = S^{perf⁺}[1/t], a perfect, hence perfectoid, Tate ring; (iii) if S is sheafy, Y^{perf} := Spa(S^{perf}, S^{perf⁺⁺}) ~ lim_Φ Y for Y = Spa(S, S⁺), the maps |Y^{perf}| → |Y| are homeomorphisms, and Y^{perf} is the unique perfectoid space over k with this property; (iv) for an analytic adic space Y over k covered by such affinoids, the Y^{perf} glue to a perfectoid space Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing). The corresponding statement for flat t-adic formal schemes 𝔜: lim_Φ 𝔜 is representable by the perfect flat formal scheme 𝔜^{perf}, locally Spf(R^{perf}), compatibly with generic fibres.
hypotheses: Base perfect of characteristic p so that relative Frobenius is k-linear and the Frobenius twist is isomorphic to the original algebra; S⁺ flat over k°.
proofSteps: (i): relative Frobenius over a perfect base satisfies the source form of the definition: the twist S⁺/t ⊗_{k°/t, Φ} k°/t^p is S⁺/t^p after identifying k°/t ≅ k°/t^p by Frobenius.

(ii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion; perfectness of the completion and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5: in characteristic p, perfectoid = perfect complete Tate).

(iii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers (ii); Frobenius induces homeomorphisms on adic spectra (a valuation is determined by its values on p-th powers), so all transition maps and the projections are homeomorphisms.
(iv) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing, since the construction commutes with rational localisation.
acceptance: Scholze's torsion paper, Definition III.2.18: X′*perf over F_p((t^{1/(p−1)p^∞})) is the tilde-limit of the Siegel space X′* along relative Frobenius.
For Y = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩), Y^{perf} = Spa(k⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, k°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), and the étale topoi of Y^{perf} and Y agree (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers).

sources.match: Statement (iii)-(iv) over the base of the source.

The completion formula (ii).
The formal-scheme version.

nodes.title: Towers of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps have perfectoid tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of perfectoid spaces whose transition maps are affinoid (for every a: j → i and every affinoid open V ⊆ X_i, f_a^{-1}(V) is affinoid; hence qcqs). Then: (i) the limit X := lim_i X_i exists in the category of perfectoid spaces; (ii) X ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), and X represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) for i_0 ∈ I and an affinoid perfectoid open V = Spa(R_{i_0}, R_{i_0}⁺) ⊆ X_{i_0} with preimages V_a = Spa(R_a, R_a⁺), the preimage of V in X is Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_a R_a⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ] (ϖ a compatible pseudouniformiser), and R is perfectoid; (iv) |X| ≅ lim_i |X_i|; (v) if I is ω_1-cofiltered, colim R_a → R and colim R_a⁺ → R⁺ are bijective. This is the easy limit theorem, in which every finite level is already perfectoid; it is distinct from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers, whose finite levels are not perfectoid.
hypotheses: Every X_i perfectoid; affinoid transition maps (as for finite étale or pro-étale towers of affinoids).
proofSteps: Affinoid case: PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4(o), 6.5) gives the limit Spa(R, R⁺), the formula and the homeomorphism; the perfectoidness of (R, R⁺) is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid (each R_a⁺ integral perfectoid by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.20; bijective Frobenius modulo ϖ and ϖ-torsion-freeness pass to the colimit and its completion; Lemmas 3.10(ii) and 3.21), the same argument as PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound with w_m replaced by the inverse Frobenius at each level.
Tilde-limit on affinoids: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{a,0} = R_a⁺.

Global case: cover X_{i_0} by affinoid perfectoids V; affinoid transition maps make every V_a affinoid perfectoid; glue the affinoid limits by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii) (uniqueness on overlaps from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness), which also gives (ii) and (iv).
(v) as in ECD Proposition 6.5 (a Cauchy sequence lives at a finite stage).
acceptance: Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11(2): the finite étale tower X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)∩Γ_1*(p^n)}(ε)_a of perfectoid spaces has the perfectoid tilde-limit X_{Γ_1*(p^∞)}(ε)_a.
A pro-étale G-tower of perfectoid spaces X_j → X with X_∞ = lim X_j (PerfectoidSpaces:P9/profinite-galois-tower in the perfectoid case).

sources.match: The statement in the source's words.

The universal property on affinoids.

nodes.title: Étale base change of residue-field tilde-limits, and bijectivity suffices (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16)
nodes.statement: Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit), i_0 ∈ I and g: Y → X_{i_0} an étale morphism of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces. Put Y_a := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j (a: j → i_0) and Y_X := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X, a perfectoid space étale over X. Then (i) Y_X ~′ lim_a Y_a; (ii) (the remark in the proof) in Definition 7.14, if |X| → lim |X_i| is bijective and the residue-field condition (c) holds, then |X| → lim |X_i| is already a homeomorphism, i.e. X ~′ lim X_i.
hypotheses: X_i and Y qcqs locally noetherian analytic; g étale (Huber's étale = A1's local description, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison).
proofSteps: Existence of Y_X, perfectoid and étale over X: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii), Proposition 7.10).

Bijectivity of |Y_X| → lim_a |Y_a|, fibrewise over x ∈ X with images x_j: points over x are the extensions of the valuation of x to the finite étale k(x)^-algebra obtained from the fibre (étale maps are locally quasi-finite with finite étale fibres over completed residue fields); by (c) and henselian approximation (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^), and the valuation ring k(x)⁺ and its extensions are determined on the dense subfield colim k(x_j); so the fibres correspond.
Residue-field density for points of Y_X: residue fields of Y_X are finite separable over those of X and are the base changes of those of the Y_a, so density is preserved.

Homeomorphism (ii): Scholze refers to Huber's Remark 2.4.3 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). A route through public inputs: over an affinoid perfectoid W ⊆ X the map W → lim |X_i| is spectral (W qc, X_i qs); spectral bijections are homeomorphisms for the constructible topologies (Stacks Lemma 5.23.3 and 5.24.5), and generalising maps of spectral spaces that are surjective are quotient maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient); generalisations of an analytic point are its vertical generalisations, i.e. valuation rings between k(x)⁺ and k(x)°, which by (c) correspond to those of colim k(x_j).
acceptance: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for U → X étale, U ×_X X_∞ ~′ lim U ×_X X_i for the universal cover tower.
For an open immersion Y ⊆ X_{i_0}, Y_X is the open subspace φ_{i_0}^{-1}(Y) (compare PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction).

sources.match: Statement (i).
Statement (ii).
Spectrality of lim |X_i| used in (ii).

nodes.title: Qcqs étale spaces over a residue-field tilde-limit descend to a finite level
nodes.statement: Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit with all X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} → X_{ét,qcqs} between qcqs étale adic spaces over the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), and likewise 2-colim_i (X_i)_{fét} → X_{fét}; (ii) a finite family of morphisms (Z^k_i → Y_i)_k in (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} is jointly surjective after base change to X if and only if it is so after base change to some X_j. This is the perfectoid-limit analogue of ECD Proposition 6.4(i)-(ii) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects), with the X_i locally noetherian instead of affinoid perfectoid.
hypotheses: X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid; ~′ (hence also ~).
proofSteps: Finite étale over neighbourhoods of a point: for x ∈ X, 2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(U) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^) (Berkeley Lemma 7.4.6, via k(x)^⁺ = the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U ∋ x} O⁺(U) and Theorem 7.4.8; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), and the same at x_j ∈ X_j; by (c), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^) (the colimit of the k(x_j)^ is dense in k(x)^ and topologically henselian; finite étale algebras are finitely presented). Hence a finite étale cover of a neighbourhood of x is, near x, pulled back from a neighbourhood of some x_j, uniquely up to shrinking.

Faithfulness and fullness: as in ECD Proposition 6.4(ii) — graphs of maps between étale spaces are quasicompact open immersions (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal); two quasicompact opens of Z_i = Y_i ×_{X_i} Y′_i with the same preimage in Z_X agree in some Z_j, because |Z_X| → lim |Z_j| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change) and quasicompact opens of a limit of spectral spaces descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces); morphisms whose base change is an isomorphism become isomorphisms at a finite stage (surjectivity of f and of Δ_f descend).

Essential surjectivity: a qcqs étale Y → X is covered by finitely many pieces that are rational subsets of finite étale covers of rational subsets of X (local structure, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); quasicompact opens descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 through |X| ≅ lim |X_i|), finite étale covers descend by the first step and quasi-compactness, and the pieces glue at a finite stage by full faithfulness (X qcqs).

(ii): images of étale maps are open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); joint surjectivity is an equality of quasicompact opens, which descends by Stacks Lemma 5.24.6(3) and the surjectivity of |Y_X| → lim |Y_j|.
acceptance: For the compatible-root disc tower over a perfectoid field K, every finite étale cover of the perfectoid disc is pulled back from some K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ (the disc's finite étale site is the 2-colimit).

For the universal pro-finite-étale tower of a connected affinoid X over Q_p, the limit X_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, proof of Theorem 4.9, citing Lemma 7.5(i) of Scholze 2012).

sources.match: Finite étale maps descend by henselian approximation (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).
The graph argument for fullness.
The essential-surjectivity argument.
Finite étale algebras over completed colimits of complete Tate rings.

nodes.title: Tilde-limits X ~ lim X_i of noetherian adic spaces and the comparison of etale topoi
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; no perfectoid base field is assumed, and the X_i may lie over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) while X lies over a perfectoid field), X a perfectoid space and X ~′ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit; this holds whenever X ~ lim X_i, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) |X| is a spectral space and X is qcqs (Scholze 2012 Remark 7.15); (ii) (Theorem 7.17) the étale topos X_ét^~ of the perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space) is the projective limit of the fibred topos (X_{i,ét}^~)_i of the étale topoi of the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, equal to Huber's): X_ét^~ is equivalent to the topos of sheaves on the colimit site colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} (objects qcqs étale over some X_i, morphisms the filtered colimits of Hom sets, coverings the families that are coverings at some finite level), compatibly with the pullback morphisms X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~; (iii) (Corollary 7.18) for i_0 ∈ I and a sheaf of abelian groups F_{i_0} on X_{i_0,ét}, with pullbacks F_j to X_{j,ét} (j → i_0) and F to X_ét, the natural map colim_j H^n(X_{j,ét}, F_j) → H^n(X_ét, F) is bijective for all n ≥ 0 (for sheaves of sets, n = 0; for sheaves of groups, n ≤ 1). When X is itself locally noetherian (and not assumed perfectoid), the corresponding statements are Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6, supplied by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity; this node is their perfectoid extension. Corollary 7.19 is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers.
hypotheses: All X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid (its étale site is that of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.11 / ECD Definition 6.2); no base field (Scholze 2012 states the result over a perfectoid field K; Scholze's rigid paper applies it to X_i over Q_p).
Proofs follow Huber [Hub96] Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6 with Scholze's modification; the step through Huber's unpublished text is recorded as a gap, and the steps below use public inputs.
proofSteps: (i): Remark 7.15 via DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces.

(ii): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent identifies X_{ét,qcqs} with the colimit site, including coverings; since X is qcqs, the qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X form a generating subcategory of X_ét stable under fibre products, so X_ét^~ is the topos of the colimit site; a filtered colimit of coherent sites with finite-limit- and covering-preserving pullbacks has as topos the projective limit of the fibred topos (SGA 4 VI.8.2.3; request to DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).

Scholze's modification of Huber's proof: instead of Huber's Corollary 1.7.3, étale maps factor locally as an open immersion followed by a finite étale map (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison on the X_i; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces on X), and finite étale maps descend to a finite level by henselian approximation (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

(iii): cohomology on a projective limit of coherent topoi of sheaves pulled back from a stage is the colimit of the cohomologies (SGA 4 VI.8.7.7, as in Huber's Corollary 2.4.6); on the colimit site this is DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites applied to the filtered colimit of the pulled-back sheaves, the cohomology of each stage being computed on its qcqs étale site.
acceptance: Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim_n Spa K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ and Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩ (compatible-root disc and torus).
Theorem 1.12/8.5's (P^n)^{ad} ~ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad} (Frobenius tower) is the source's application; in this case Cor. 7.19 does not apply but Thm 7.17 does.

Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for the universal cover X_∞ ~ lim X_i of a connected affinoid noetherian X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) (X_i finite étale over X, over Q_p; X_∞ over C_p), H^j(X_{∞,ét}, L) = colim_i H^j(X_{i,ét}, L) for all j ≥ 0 (the use made by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion). The tower satisfies X_∞ ~ lim X_i also in the sectionwise sense, by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit.

Finite étale maps descend by henselian approximation (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

nodes.title: Towers with homeomorphic, purely inseparable transition maps do not change the étale topos (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.19)
nodes.statement: In the situation of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (X ~′ lim X_i, X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic, X perfectoid), assume that every transition map X_j → X_i induces a homeomorphism |X_j| → |X_i| and purely inseparable extensions of completed residue fields. Then for every i the pullback X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~ is an equivalence of topoi; in particular H^n(X_ét, F) = H^n(X_{i,ét}, F_i) for every abelian sheaf F_i on X_{i,ét} with pullback F.
hypotheses: Transition maps homeomorphisms on underlying spaces with purely inseparable residue-field extensions (a universal-homeomorphism condition, typically relative Frobenius in characteristic p).
proofSteps: For such a transition map, pullback X_{i,ét}^~ → X_{j,ét}^~ is an equivalence: Scholze refers to the remark after Huber's Proposition 2.3.7 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). This is the adic analogue of the topological invariance of the étale site (SGA 4 VIII.1.1).
The projective limit of a system of equivalences of topoi is equivalent to each member (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (ii)).
acceptance: Perfection: for Y an analytic adic space of characteristic p locally noetherian over a perfect field, Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y along relative Frobenius (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit), and Y^{perf}_ét ≃ Y_ét.

Non-example: the Frobenius tower T ↦ T^p of P^n in characteristic 0 (Scholze 2012 Theorem 8.5) has non-inseparable residue extensions; there only the limit statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison applies.

The proof, by reference to Huber.

nodes.title: Finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring with residue field k. There is a filtered direct system of finite flat R-algebras R_i such that each (R_i, mR_i) is a regular local ring and (lim→ R_i, m·lim→ R_i) is a regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field. If k is separably closed of characteristic p > 0, the R_i may be chosen of p-power rank over R. The colimit is Noetherian; it is not claimed to be complete.
hypotheses: R complete regular local, of any characteristic. The proof uses the three Cohen presentations: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (equal characteristic); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ with W a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p (p ∈ m∖m²); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (p ∈ m²).

Reuse Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing at the pin; do not reconstruct the regular-local-ring predicate. The Cohen presentations and the required regularity/normality, power-series, quotient and filtered-colimit comparison theorems remain supplier obligations (gap).
The p-power clause needs k separably closed: then k̄/k is purely inseparable, and its finite subextensions have p-power degree.
proofSteps: Equal characteristic: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (Matsumura 29.7). Let k_i range over the finite subextensions of k̄/k and put R_i := k_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, free of rank [k_i : k] over R. The m-adic completion of lim→ R_i is k̄⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, so lim→ R_i is Noetherian (Stacks 033E, 05UU, 00MK), hence a regular local ring.

Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m∖m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧. There is an integral extension W′/W of discrete valuation rings with uniformizer p and residue field k̄ (Matsumura, proof of 29.1). With W_i ranging over the finite discrete valuation ring subextensions of W′/W, put R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧; as before, the colimit has completion Ŵ′⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and is regular local.

Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (Matsumura 29.3 and the proof of 29.8(ii)). Each R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) is a finite flat R-algebra and a regular local ring. By the previous case lim→ W_i⟦x⟧ is regular local with regular system of parameters (p, x_1, …, x_n), so lim→ R_i is regular local with regular system of parameters (x_1, …, x_n).
p-power ranks: in all three cases rank_R R_i = [k_i : k] (= [W_i : W]); if k is separably closed of characteristic p, this is a power of p.
acceptance: Non-example: the colimit is not complete. For R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧ the colimit is lim→ 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧, whose completion 𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧ is strictly larger.
The p-power clause needs k separably closed: for k = 𝔽_p the stages 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧ have rank n.
Ramified case: R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = ℤ_p[√p] has p ∈ m², R_i = W(𝔽_{p^i})[√p] with i ranging over the positive integers ordered by divisibility, and the colimit is regular with parameter x = √p.

nodes.title: Finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field k, and W := W(k). There is a tower {R_m}_{m≥0} of finite flat R-algebras R_m of p-power rank over R, each a regular local ring, such that the p-adic completion R̂_∞ of R_∞ := lim→_m R_m is perfectoid (integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5, so R̂_∞[1/p] is a perfectoid Tate ring). Explicitly: if p ∈ m∖m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and R_m := W[p^{1/p^m}]⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧; if p ∈ m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² and R_m := W⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧/(p − f). The finite stages are not perfectoid, and R_∞ is not complete.
hypotheses: k perfect, so W ≅ W(k) in the Cohen presentations of P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower; mixed characteristic (0, p).

The criterion used is Česnavičius's Lemma 4.7: for a p-torsion-free ring S with (ϖ^p) = (p) for some ϖ ∈ S, if S is integrally closed in S[1/p] then x ↦ x^p : S/ϖ → S/p is injective, and if moreover every element of S/p is a p-th power then the p-adic completion of S is perfectoid. PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 route 7 plans that lemma at PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, which is not upstream of P7, so step 1 proves the instance needed here.
proofSteps: Criterion. If x ∈ S and x^p = ϖ^p s with s ∈ S, then x/ϖ ∈ S[1/ϖ] = S[1/p] satisfies (x/ϖ)^p = s, so x/ϖ ∈ S by integral closedness, that is x ∈ ϖS. Since Ŝ/ϖ ≅ S/ϖ and Ŝ/p ≅ S/p, Frobenius Ŝ/ϖ → Ŝ/p is bijective, and Ŝ is integral perfectoid; P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid gives the Tate ring.

Each R_m is regular local and finite free of p-power rank over R: in the first case it is a power series ring over the discrete valuation ring W[p^{1/p^m}] (rank p^{m(n+1)}), and in the second it is the quotient of the regular ring W⟦x^{1/p^m}⟧ by p − f, which is not in the square of its maximal ideal (rank p^{mn}). Being regular, each R_m is a normal domain, so R_∞ is a normal domain, integrally closed in R_∞[1/p], and p-torsion free.
p ∈ m∖m²: take ϖ := p^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, since k is perfect and p and the x_i have compatible p-power roots in R_∞. Apply step 1.

p ∈ m²: by step 1 it suffices to find u ∈ R_∞^× with up a p-th power in R_∞, and then ϖ := (up)^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power and p ∈ m_∞², so p = Σ_i (s_i^p + p t_i)(s′_i^p + p t′_i) with s_i, s′_i ∈ m_∞ and t_i, t′_i ∈ R_∞. Hence p = s^p + pt with s, t ∈ m_∞, and u := 1 − t is a unit of the local ring R_∞ (Česnavičius follows Shimomoto's argument, [Shi16, 4.9]).
acceptance: R = ℤ_p (n = 0): R_m = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}], and R̂_∞ is the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}], a perfectoid ring.

Non-example, R = ℤ_p: for m ≥ 1, R_m/p ≅ 𝔽_p[T]/(T^{p^m}) and T is not a p-th power, so Frobenius is not surjective. At m = 0, R_0 = ℤ_p and Frobenius on R_0/p = 𝔽_p IS surjective, but no ϖ ∈ ℤ_p has (ϖ^p)=(p), since p·v_p(ϖ)=1 is impossible. Thus every finite stage in this example fails the perfectoid criterion, for different reasons at stage zero and positive stages.
The residue field must be perfect: k is a quotient of R_∞/p, so if every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, every element of k is one.
The completion is p-adic. R_∞ is not complete, and its m_∞-adic topology is not the one used.

Effective faithfully flat descent for modules and for commutative algebras along a faithfully flat ring map A → B: the functor from A-modules (A-algebras) to B-modules (B-algebras) with descent data (isomorphism p₂*N ≅ p₁*N over B ⊗_A B satisfying the cocycle condition) is an equivalence, with descent of flatness, finite generation, finite presentation, finite projectivity and (weak) étaleness. Mathlib has comonadicity of extension of scalars (`comonadicExtendScalars`) and the Amitsur equalizer for rings, but not the descent-data formulation; PerfectoidSpaces:P0 transports this statement to almost modules and almost algebras along A_!! → B_!!.

(A) Complete Hausdorff Tate rings with their power-bounded subring A°, topologically nilpotent ideal A°°, bounded sets, pseudo-uniformizers, pairs of definition and the open mapping theorem over a Tate ring, as already pinned in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing, powerBoundedSubring, topologicallyNilpotentIdeal, IsBounded, IsPseudoUniformizer, PairOfDefinition, IsTateRing.isOpenMap), together with the anchor's restricted power series A⟨X⟩ (restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion) and completion of Huber rings. (C) Completion of Tate rings with its rings of definition: for a Tate ring A with ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ (ϖ a pseudouniformiser), the completion Â is a complete Tate ring with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion Â₀ and Â = Â₀[ϖ⁻¹]; the colimit topology on a filtered colimit of Tate rings with compatible rings of definition (colim A_{i,0} a ring of definition) and its completion; ϖ-adic completeness of the rings of definition of a complete Tate ring. (B) (a) Uniform and stably uniform complete Tate pairs (Hansen–Kedlaya Definitions 2.3 and 3.13) and the pair-level Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem that a stably uniform complete Tate pair is sheafy (Layer 4.2), consumed for perfectoid pairs; (b) the all-degree exactness of the augmented Čech complex of O_X for every finite rational covering of every rational subset of a complete strongly noetherian Tate pair (Layer 4.1), consumed for reduced affinoid algebras over a perfectoid field of characteristic p. (D) The Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem: a stably uniform complete Tate Huber pair is sheafy (used through AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy for the strong sheafiness of perfectoid Tate rings), and the Tate acyclicity of O on rational coverings of a sheafy Tate affinoid (used through AdicSpacesPartII:R3 for gluing finite projective modules).

The Layer 6.1 package: a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field F of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, A_inf = W(𝒪_F) with pair of definition (A_inf, (p,[ϖ])) and its (p,[ϖ])-adic completeness and separatedness. P1 proves that F is a perfectoid field equal to its tilt and that A_inf = W(F♭+) with the same completeness statement (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring), and needs the anchor objects to be stated for a Tau Ceti nonarchimedean field so that the comparison is an identification of declarations.

For a commutative nonarchimedean Banach ring A (or a uniform Banach algebra over a nonarchimedean field): the Berkovich spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms is nonempty for A ≠ 0; f ∈ A is a unit iff α(f) ≠ 0 for all α ∈ M(A) (Berkovich Theorem 1.2.1, Corollary 1.2.4); and the spectral seminorm satisfies |f|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(f) (Berkovich Theorem 1.3.1). These are the inputs of Kedlaya's Theorem 3.7 (Banach fields). The same maximum formula for an arbitrary nonarchimedean Banach ring B (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21: the spectral seminorm of B equals the supremum of α over the Gel'fand spectrum M(B), attained since M(B) is compact) is used to pass between pointwise and global forms of the sharp approximation lemma for perfectoid Tate rings of any characteristic.

(A) (a) The category of adic spaces (objects of Huber's category 𝒱 locally isomorphic to Spa of a sheafy Huber pair) as a Lean category in which Mathlib's `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`, `CategoryTheory.Over`, `HasPullbacks` and `IsPullback` can be stated; (b) open adic subspaces (U, O_X|_U, (v_x)) with the universal property of open immersions (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(2)) and the existence, for open affinoid U, V and x ∈ U ∩ V, of an open W ∋ x rational in both (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3)); (c) gluing of adic spaces along open subspaces and gluing of morphisms (morphisms form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24); (d) Wedhorn Proposition 8.25 (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1): for an adic space X and a complete sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺), Hom(X, Spa(A, A⁺)) ≅ Hom((A, A⁺), (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X))) naturally; (e) the discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) as an object. PerfectoidSpaces P2 defines perfectoid spaces as a full subcategory of this category and introduces no second carrier. (b) The universal property of affinoid adic spaces: for an adic space W and a complete sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺), morphisms W → Spa(A, A⁺) correspond to morphisms of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (O_W(W), O⁺_W(W)) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1). (c) Open subspaces X|_U with the universal property that a morphism Z → X factors (uniquely) through X|_U iff |Z| lands in U; gluing of morphisms along open covers. (d) Closed immersions defined affinoid-locally by quotient pairs with closed ideal and sheafy quotient, independent of the cover (Layer 5.1). (D) The category of adic spaces with its open subspaces and gluing along open subspaces (Layer 5.1 and 5.3), of which perfectoid spaces form a full subcategory (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space): the limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces is formed in this category, and qcqs étale spaces descended piece by piece are glued along quasicompact open subspaces at a finite stage. (E) Analytic adic spaces with their structure sheaves, open subspaces and gluing along open subspaces, and the description of morphisms into an affinoid adic space: for an adic space Y and a sheafy complete Huber pair (A, A⁺), Hom(Y, Spa(A, A⁺)) = Hom((A, A⁺), (O(Y), O⁺(Y))) (continuous maps of pairs). Used to glue perfectoid tilde-limits and to construct maps into them.

(B) The cofinality form of continuity for Tate rings (Wedhorn Remark 7.11(1), the content of the proof of Theorem 7.10 that Layer 1.5 plans and Tau Ceti proves as `ValuationSpectrum.cont_eq_spvOfIdeal_inter_setOfPred_forall_vlt_one`): for a Tate ring A with ring of definition A₀ and pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A₀, a valuation v on A is continuous if and only if v(ϖ) is cofinal in the value group Γ_v; together with v(A⁺) ≤ 1 this characterises the points of Spa(A, A⁺). (C) The valuation spectrum Spv A of a commutative ring as the type of valuative relations on A, with a point determined by its relation vle (extensionality), and the adic spectrum Spa(A, A⁺) as a subset of Spv A. The pinned tree already contains exactly this (TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum, TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.ext', TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa); P6 uses it only to bound #Spa(A, A⁺) ≤ 2^{#A·#A} (ECD proof of Proposition 4.4) and asks for no further Layer 1 object. The general Huber tilde-limit predicate (topology and affinoid density as separate conditions, Huber Definition 2.4.2) stated for a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces whose transition maps are quasicompact and quasiseparated (the X_i themselves not required qcqs; Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1 generality) and a compatible analytic adic space X that need not be qcqs or locally noetherian, so that PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit is its restriction to perfectoid X; together with Huber's Corollary 2.4.6 for locally noetherian X, against which the perfectoid comparison of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison is stated as compatible.

Projective limits of coherent topoi (SGA 4 VI.8.2.3, VI.8.7.3 and VI.8.7.7): for a filtered colimit of coherent sites whose transition functors preserve finite limits and coverings, the topos of the colimit site is the projective limit of the fibred topos, and for sheaves (of sets, groups, abelian groups) pulled back from a stage the cohomology of the limit is the colimit of the cohomologies in degrees 0, ≤ 1, all n respectively.

ECD Proposition 7.23 (arXiv v4 p. 38) gives flatness modulo ϖ for every affinoid perfectoid map to that base, and Proposition 9.3 p. 44 explicitly invokes it. Then L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ with ring of integral elements (L°)^ℓ, but L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ is injective and not surjective: surjectivity would make K° → L° a Galois extension of rings, so L° would be free of rank ℓ over K°, whereas L°/𝔪_K L° = L°/𝔪_L (the value group of K is dense) is the residue field, of dimension 1. The image contains ϖ(L°)^ℓ (almost purity for perfectoid fields), so it is open, hence complete, and it is not integrally closed (it misses the idempotents of L^ℓ). So (L ⊗̂ L, L° ⊗̂ L°) is not a perfectoid pair and the asserted identification of D⁺ fails; the ring statement is unaffected.

The absolute countably-generated presentation of Proposition 6.5 alone does not supply maps Y_j → X when O(X) is too large. sourceIssues.reason: A cutoff cardinal κ of Lemma 4.1 is an uncountable strong limit; if it were regular it would be strongly inaccessible, so the κ of Lemma 4.1 are in general singular (the example κ(ω₁) constructed in its proof has cofinality ω₁ < κ(ω₁)). For singular κ, a ring R with |R| ≥ κ is not a κ-filtered colimit of rings of cardinality < κ: split a subset S ⊆ R of size κ into cf(κ) < κ pieces of size < κ, find a cocone for the stages representing each piece and then one index j receiving all of them; the image of R_j contains S, so |R_j| ≥ κ. Example: S = {0,1}^κ, Y = S × Spa(K, O_K); |C^0(S, K)| = κ^{ℵ₀} = κ (cofinality of κ larger than ω) and Y is κ′-small for κ′ > 2^κ.

sourceIssues.printed: The source characterizes a perfectoid X as κ-small precisely when it has fewer than κ open affinoids U = Spa(A, A+ ) covering it, each with A of cardinality below κ. It concludes closure of κ-small perfectoid spaces under finite products. The proof asserts that such a cover also forces the cardinality of |X| below κ.
sourceIssues.correction: The 'if' direction needs a uniform bound: if X has a cover by fewer than κ open affinoids Spa(A_j, A_j⁺) with sup_j #A_j < κ (automatic for finite covers, for covers indexed by fewer than cf κ sets, and for every cover when κ is regular), then X is κ-small; without the uniform bound only 'every open affinoid ring has cardinality < κ' follows. Likewise fibre products X ×_Z Y are κ-small when X and Y are uniformly κ-small (κ'-small for one κ' < κ), in particular when they are quasicompact, but not in general.
sourceIssues.reason: For the specific construction κ = κ(ω₁) in the proof of Lemma 4.1, κ has cofinality ω₁ and exceeds ω₁, hence is singular. Being a supremum of a µ-sequence alone does not show singularity for every possible ordinal µ. With perfectoid fields K_α (α < ω₁), #K_α < κ cofinal in κ (completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm), the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs over the K_α is covered by ω₁ < κ affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ but has at least κ points (the classical points of each disc), so it is not κ-small. Similarly X = ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°), with the K_α ⊇ L transcendental over a perfectoid field L, is κ-small (ℵ₁ points, every open affinoid a finite union of components), but X ×_{Spa L} X is not: Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) has at least λ_α points, distinguished by |x_β ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_β|.

review.reason: The counterexamples work for kappa(omega_1), whose singularity follows from the strictly increasing construction in Lemma 4.1. A disjoint union of discs over fields with cardinalities cofinal in that cutoff defeats the asserted cover criterion. For the fiber-product assertion, a disjoint union of one-point field spectra is small while its self-product over a fixed field has unboundedly many points. For example, Gauss-norm-preserving substitutions x_beta to x_beta+1, fixing the other variables, give distinct graph-valuations on the tensor products. The review narrowed the original claim about all cutoffs; the uniformly bounded replacement still requires the full node audit.
